HOVILPRI ® (pritelivir), a novel oral helicase-primase inhibitor represents the first FDA approved HSV therapy with a novel mechanism of action in nearly 30 years. 1-3 
Approval is supported by results from the pivotal Phase 3 PRIOH-1 trial, in which HOVILPRI demonstrated statistically superior complete lesion healing up to day 28. By Day 28, 63% of HOVILPRI-treated participants achieved complete lesion healing compared with 34% of participants receiving Investigator's Choice treatment, corresponding to an adjusted treatment difference of 28.4% (95% CI: 9.6, 47.3; p=0.0047). 1,4 
As an oral therapy, HOVILPRI provides a non-intravenous treatment option for eligible immunocompromised adult patients with refractory (with or without resistance) HSV infection. 1 
Pritelivir was granted Fast Track designation by the FDA along with Breakthrough Therapy designation and the New Drug Application received Priority Review. 5,6 
Asahi Kasei Therapeutics, Inc., the global specialty pharmaceutical business of Tokyo-based Asahi Kasei, with U.S. and European business headquarters in Cary, North Carolina, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved HOVILPRI ® (pritelivir) 100 mg tablets for the treatment of mucocutaneous lesions caused by herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection that is refractory (with or without documented resistance) to treatment with acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir in immunocompromised adults. HOVILPRI, a novel helicase-primase inhibitor, was developed by AiCuris Anti-infective Cures AG, which is now a part of Asahi Kasei Therapeutics. 1,2 
“Today's approval delivers the first FDA-approved treatment for refractory mucocutaneous HSV lesions with a novel mechanism of action in nearly 30 years and marks an important advancement for immunocompromised adults,” said Stacy Wheeler, Chief Executive Officer of Asahi Kasei Therapeutics in the U.S. and Europe. “HOVILPRI offers a new oral treatment option for adult patients with a persistent, difficult-to-treat disease.” 1,3,7-10 
In immunocompetent adults, HSV infection is often asymptomatic or associated with mild disease. In immunocompromised adults, including hematopoietic stem cell and solid organ transplant recipients, people living with HIV, and patients with malignancies or autoimmune and inflammatory conditions, HSV infection can occur more frequently and may be more severe. Refractory HSV infection can result in prolonged and difficult-to-treat mucocutaneous disease. 7-10 Because nucleoside analogue therapies such as acyclovir require activation by the viral thymidine kinase (TK) enzyme, mutations in TK can reduce susceptibility to these treatments in some patients. 2,9 When HSV infection does not improve with nucleoside analogue therapy, available treatment options have often required intravenous administration and may present additional treatment-management challenges for patients and healthcare teams. 8-10 HOVILPRI is a helicase-primase inhibitor with a mechanism of action distinct from nucleoside analogue therapies. 1,2 
The approval is supported by results from PRIOH-1 Part C, the pivotal Phase 3 randomized, open-label, comparator-controlled superiority trial in immunocompromised adults with mucocutaneous HSV infection that was refractory, with or without documented resistance, to acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir. The trial met its primary efficacy endpoint, demonstrating superiority of HOVILPRI over Investigator's Choice treatment, after up to 28 days of treatment. By Day 28, HOVILPRI achieved a significantly higher rate of complete lesion healing vs Investigator's Choice (63% vs 34% respectively, corresponding to an adjusted treatment difference of 28.4% (95% CI: 9.6, 47.3; p=0.0047). Up to day 42, the observed response rates were 82% for HOVILPRI and 42% for Investigator's Choice treatment, corresponding to an adjusted treatment difference of 40.0% (95% CI: 22.7, 57.7). 1,4 
In Part C of the pivotal Phase 3 PRIOH-1 trial, adverse reactions were reported less frequently in participants treated with HOVILPRI compared with Investigator's Choice treatment (22% vs. 54%). Discontinuations due to adverse drug reactions were also less frequent with HOVILPRI compared with Investigator's Choice treatment (2% vs. 20%). The most common adverse reaction was headache, occurring in 6% of patients taking HOVILPRI and 4% of patients taking Investigators Choice. 1 
“In patients with blood cancers or those who have undergone stem cell transplantation, refractory HSV infections can be prolonged, painful, and difficult to treat, while available intravenous treatments carry substantial risks,” said Genovefa Papanicolaou, MD, Clinical Director of Infectious Disease Service at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and Professor at Weill Cornell College of Medicine, and a PRIOH-1 investigator. “In PRIOH-1, pritelivir demonstrated superior lesion healing compared with Investigator’s Choice treatment up to day 28.” 1,4,7-10 
“Refractory HSV can be a serious clinical challenge for immunocompromised adults, a population with limited treatment options,” said Carl Kraus, Chief Medical Officer at Asahi Kasei Therapeutics. “The approval of HOVILPRI reflects years of clinical research in refractory HSV and reinforces our commitment to advancing scientifically differentiated medicines for patients whose conditions remain difficult to treat. We are grateful to the patients, investigators, clinical teams, and scientific community whose contributions made this milestone possible.” 1,4,7-10 
HOVILPRI is expected to be available in the United States before the end of 2026. U.S. Healthcare providers can learn more about HOVILPRI at www.hovilprihcp.com .
About the PRIOH-1 Trial 
PRIOH-1 (NCT03073967 / Eudra-CT 2023-510088-37-00) is a global, controlled, open-label, comparative trial evaluating pritelivir in immunocompromised adults with refractory or resistant HSV infection. The registrational Phase 3 portion (Part C) randomized and treated 101 immunocompromised adults with mucocutaneous HSV infection that was refractory with or without documented resistance to acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir. This included hematopoietic cell and solid organ transplant recipients, patients with malignancies, autoimmune or inflammatory disorders, and people living with HIV. Participants received either oral pritelivir (400 mg loading dose on Day 1 followed by 100 mg once daily) or Investigator's Choice treatment (IV foscarnet, IV/topical cidofovir, or 5% topical imiquimod) for up to 28 days, with treatment extended to 42 days if lesions were improving. Pritelivir met its primary endpoint demonstrating statistically significant superiority in lesion healing up to Day 28 compared with Investigator’s Choice treatment. 1,4 
About Herpes Simplex Virus 
Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) includes two types, HSV-1 and HSV-2, both of which cause lifelong infections; there is no cure. HSV-1 most commonly causes labial herpes, while HSV-2 is the primary cause of genital herpes. Although many people with HSV infection never develop symptoms, the virus can reactivate to cause recurrent, painful lesions and may cause complications in certain cases. 11-12 HSV represents a substantial global public health burden: an estimated 3.8 billion people under the age of 50 (64% of the global population) were infected with HSV-1 in 2020, and approximately 520 million people aged 15 to 49 were living with HSV-2. 11 The disease burden is particularly high in immunocompromised patients, whose weakened immune systems leave them at increased risk of more frequent, more severe, and treatment-refractory HSV infections. 7,9-10 
About HOVILPRI (pritelivir) 
HOVILPRI is an orally administered HSV helicase-primase inhibitor indicated for the treatment of mucocutaneous lesions caused by HSV infection that is refractory, with or without documented resistance, to acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir in immunocompromised adults. HOVILPRI is active against both HSV-1 and HSV-2, including strains resistant to nucleoside analogs and foscarnet. In the pivotal Phase 3 PRIOH-1 trial, HOVILPRI demonstrated statistically significant superiority in lesion healing up to day 28 compared to Investigator's Choice treatment. The most common adverse reaction reported with HOVILPRI was headache. 1-2,4 
INDICATION AND IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION FOR US AUDIENCE
Indication 
HOVILPRI (pritelivir) tablets is indicated in immunocompromised adults for the treatment of mucocutaneous lesions caused by herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection that is refractory (with or without documented resistance) to treatment with acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir.
Important Safety Information 
Warnings and Precautions 
Drug Interactions With Acid-reducing Agents: Concomitant use of HOVILPRI with certain acid-reducing agents may reduce pritelivir exposure, potentially resulting in reduced therapeutic effect and development of resistance. Avoid concomitant use with certain proton pump inhibitors, and stagger concomitant use with H2-receptor antagonists and antacids.
Adverse Reactions: In clinical studies, the adverse reaction (all grades) occurring in more than 5% of participants receiving HOVILPRI was headache, which occurred in 6% and 4% of the HOVILPRI and Investigator’s Choice participants, respectively.
Drug Interactions: 
Pritelivir is a breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) inhibitor. Co-administration of HOVILPRI with a BCRP substrate may increase the plasma concentrations of the BCRP substrate, which may increase the risk of adverse reactions.
Concomitant use of acid-reducing agents may elevate gastric pH and decrease the systemic bioavailability of HOVILPRI, which may reduce its effectiveness or cause drug resistance to HOVILPRI. Avoid concomitant use with esomeprazole or rabeprazole. Avoid concomitant use with omeprazole or lansoprazole at daily doses above 20 mg, or with pantoprazole at daily doses above 40 mg. Take HOVILPRI at least 2 hours before or 12 hours after H2-receptor antagonists. Take HOVILPRI at least 2 hours before or 2 hours after antacids.
Please see full Prescribing Information at https://www.hovilprihcp.com/pdf/prescribing-information.pdf . 
About Asahi Kasei Therapeutics 
Asahi Kasei Therapeutics is the global specialty pharmaceutical business of Tokyo-based Asahi Kasei. We are identifying, developing and commercializing innovative medicines for diseases with significant unmet medical needs. Drawing upon our strong heritage of scientific innovation, we are expanding therapeutic options and helping to positively impact health in immunology, nephrology, transplantation, and infectious diseases. For more information, visit: https://www.aktx.com. 
About Asahi Kasei 
Asahi Kasei is a diversified global company that contributes to life and living for people around the world. Since its foundation in 1922, with businesses in ammonia and cellulose fiber, Asahi Kasei has consistently grown through proactive portfolio transformation to meet the evolving needs of every age. With 50,000 employees worldwide, the company contributes to sustainability by providing solutions to the world’s challenges across its three business sectors: Healthcare, Homes, and Material. For more information, visit https://www.asahi-kasei.com/ .
Asahi Kasei positions Pharmaceuticals as a First Priority business in its medium-term management plan, emphasizing value creation by expanding its research and development activities globally to deliver innovative therapeutic options worldwide.

title: Applied Materials Unveils $5 Billion EPIC Center in Silicon Valley to Accelerate Semiconductor Innovation for the AI Era

content_text:
Applied Materials Unveils $5 Billion EPIC Center in Silicon Valley to Accelerate Semiconductor Innovation for the AI Era
Oct 12, 2026 at 4:30 PM EDT
PDF Version 
$5 billion  investment creates the world’s largest semiconductor equipment and process technology R&D facility 
Purpose-built to accelerate the path from breakthrough innovation to high-volume manufacturing of next-generation chipmaking technologies 
Leading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and research universities have committed to develop inside EPIC 
 
SUNNYVALE, Calif. ,  Oct. 12, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --  Applied Materials, Inc. , the leader in materials engineering for the semiconductor industry, today unveiled its Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization (EPIC) Center, a  $5 billion  capital investment* to build the world’s largest facility dedicated to collaborative semiconductor process technology and manufacturing equipment R&D. Inside the EPIC Center, leading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and university researchers will work side by side with Applied’s scientists and engineers to accelerate the pace of chip innovation for the AI era.
“As AI infrastructure scales, the demands of high-performance computing are driving unprecedented complexity across the chipmaking roadmap,” said  Gary Dickerson , President and CEO of Applied Materials. “To win the race for AI leadership, our industry must rethink and re-engineer how we collaborate to develop and commercialize the next generation of semiconductor technologies. At EPIC, the world’s leading chipmakers, system designers, equipment partners and researchers will work side by side with our teams to accelerate the path from breakthrough materials innovation to high-volume manufacturing faster than ever before.”
Purpose-Built to Accelerate Innovation and Commercialization 
Unveiled today at Applied’s  Sunnyvale, California , campus, the EPIC Center represents one of the most complex R&D construction projects in the world. The 600,000-square-foot structure houses nearly four acres of advanced cleanroom space and required more than six million construction hours to complete. Its foundation holds enough concrete to fill 34 Olympic-sized swimming pools, and its steel-reinforced structure holds enough steel to build two  Eiffel Towers . Thirty-four roof trusses cover the cleanrooms, each spanning nearly 300 feet in length and weighing as much as 12 school buses.
EPIC is designed to reinvent the R&D model the industry has relied on for decades. In the traditional model, foundational materials research happens in one environment, equipment and process development in another, and process integration and pilot production in a third, with a careful handoff at every phase. The EPIC Center is designed to remove these handoffs, putting the people who invent the materials, build the equipment, and make the chips together in a state-of-the-art facility purpose-built for commercialization.
EPIC is founded on a simple conviction: the technologies the AI era demands are too complex and too consequential for any one company to invent alone. The EPIC Center opens with a founding roster that spans the AI technology stack. Founding partners TSMC, Intel, SK hynix, Micron and Samsung Electronics are joined by innovation partners Broadcom, Advantest, SCREEN, KIOXIA, and Besi; and by research partners  Arizona State University ,  Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute ,  Stanford University ,  UC Berkeley , and  UCLA Samueli School of Engineering . Each partner brings its own roadmap challenges and engineers into the facility, working in tight, secure learning cycles alongside Applied teams. Over time, additional companies and organizations are expected to join the EPIC ecosystem.
Leaders from many of the EPIC Center partner companies attended the unveiling event, getting a first glimpse inside the facility. The day started with a summit hosted by Dr.  Prabu Raja , President of the  Semiconductor Products Group  at Applied Materials, where R&D leaders from top semiconductor design, manufacturing and equipment companies discussed key challenges facing growth and progress in the global chip industry.
“Materials innovation has outgrown serial development – at today’s atomic-scale dimensions, many materials and materials interfaces behave in entirely new ways, and making them work at industry scale demands coordinated development and integrated solutions,” said Dr.  Prabu Raja . “EPIC is the only place where materials, process technology and equipment will be innovated in parallel, which increases the success rate of new materials and technologies. Because our customers’ own engineers help optimize the technology before it ever reaches their factory, what leaves EPIC arrives at the fab ready to ramp to high performance and high yield sooner.”
Applied expects the EPIC operating model to deliver returns on both sides of the partnerships. Chipmakers gain earliest access to next-generation materials and equipment, shorter learning cycles and a faster path to volume production. Applied gains visibility across several generations of emerging technology challenges, informing where the company directs its R&D investments to create value for customers and have its systems and services designed in.
Supporting Quotes from Industry and Academic Leaders 
“For three decades, TSMC and Applied Materials have grown together – pushing the boundaries of semiconductor technology through every major transition. Thirty years ago, the leading-edge production node was 350 nanometers. Today, it is 2 nanometers. Working hand-in-hand with the industry, we have shrunk features 175-fold. As chipmaking complexity grows exponentially, our partnership is more vital than ever. Beyond 2nm, collaborating with Applied gives us early access to the disruptive equipment technologies that define the future. This fast-tracks the leap from R&D to high-volume manufacturing for the energy-efficient AI architectures of tomorrow – including new architecture, low-resistance wiring, and advanced packaging. We are proud to be a founding partner of EPIC, accelerating the innovations that will power AI from the data center to the edge.” – Dr.  C.C. Wei , Chairman and CEO of TSMC 
“AI is creating a multi-trillion-dollar opportunity for the semiconductor industry. To capture it, we need continued innovation in transistors, interconnects and advanced packaging. At Intel, we see a path to more than a trillion transistors in a package by 2030. As architectures become more complex and R&D costs continue to rise, we need to move faster and work more closely with our equipment partners. EPIC gives our teams the opportunity to work side by side with Applied on materials and process innovation – helping us accelerate development, improve R&D efficiency and bring new technologies to market faster.” –  Lip-Bu Tan , CEO, Intel 
“Data-intensive AI workloads are driving massive demand for high-performance memory and storage, and innovation in materials and process technology is a critical enabler of next-generation memory. As a founding partner of EPIC, Micron will work side by side with Applied Materials to accelerate innovation and bring next-generation memory technologies from research to high-volume manufacturing at scale.” –  Sanjay Mehrotra , Chairman and CEO, Micron Technology 
“The defining challenge of AI computing is moving data fast enough to keep increasingly powerful processors fully utilized, and meeting that challenge requires memory with far greater bandwidth, speed and capacity. At EPIC, SK hynix and Applied will bring together our leadership in advanced memory with Applied’s leadership in materials engineering and semiconductor manufacturing technology to address major inflections across HBM, DRAM and NAND, and accelerate memory innovation for the AI era.” – Nohjung Kwak, President and CEO of SK hynix 
“Samsung takes an end-to-end view of AI-era computing – across leading-edge logic, memory and advanced packaging. Applied Materials brings uniquely broad process equipment leadership across all three domains, and at EPIC together we will develop, iterate and deploy breakthrough technologies faster than ever, at the pace AI scaling demands.” – Jaihyuk Song, Chief Technology Officer (CTO) of Device Solutions Division, Samsung Electronics 
“The next frontier of AI will be defined by how seamlessly the industry can integrate vast amounts of compute, memory and connectivity into high-performance systems, and that depends on breakthrough advances in advanced packaging. As an innovation partner at EPIC, Broadcom can engage earlier with Applied’s foundational technologies and manufacturing capabilities, connecting future system requirements to the packaging innovations needed to realize them and accelerating the path from concept to commercialization.” –  Charlie Kawwas , Ph.D., President of  Semiconductor Solutions Group , Broadcom 
“Future performance improvements will depend on advanced 3D architectures and heterogeneous integration. As these technologies converge, it becomes increasingly important to connect insights from front-end process development with those from back-end test and measurement. EPIC breaks down these traditional barriers by bringing together Applied Materials’ leadership in materials engineering and process control with Advantest's leadership in semiconductor test and measurement, including capabilities enabled through the Advantest Innovation Center. Together, we are helping the world’s leading semiconductor manufacturers improve yield, accelerate production ramps, and bring next-generation AI systems to market faster.” –  Doug Lefever , Representative Director and Group CEO, Advantest Corporation 
“At EPIC, we have a unique opportunity to co-optimize the critical wet and dry processes behind next-generation chip architectures. We can together accelerate the innovations required to master increasingly complex 3D devices and advanced packaging structures. By driving tighter process integration with materials engineering, we can help chipmakers unlock higher yields, faster production ramps, and the manufacturing scale required for the AI future.” –  Masato Goto , President and CEO, SCREEN Holdings Co., Ltd. 
“AI is making the world increasingly data-driven, and future breakthroughs will depend on memory, logic, and interconnect technologies working seamlessly within integrated systems. We believe the EPIC Center provides a powerful platform for collaboration across technology domains. By working closely with Applied Materials engineers and other partners, we can accelerate the development of next-generation memory technologies.” –  Hideshi Miyajima , Ph.D., Managing Executive Officer and Chief Technology Officer,  KIOXIA Corporation 
“The future of AI depends not only on more powerful chips, but on the chip-to-chip interconnects that drive performance, bandwidth and power efficiency. Besi and Applied recognized early that hybrid bonding would be foundational to next-generation AI systems, and by combining Besi’s leadership in precision die-to-wafer bonding with Applied’s leadership in front-end processing, we are advancing hybrid bonding technology to enable future high-performance 3D integrated devices. EPIC extends that model of high-velocity co-innovation across the ecosystem, accelerating the technologies that will shape future AI systems.” –  Richard Blickman , President and CEO, BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi) 
“ASU has developed a very strong working relationship with Applied Materials through the Materials-to-Fab Center at  ASU Research Park , and we are excited to dig deeper into this partnership at the EPIC Center, where researchers, engineers and manufacturers converge to accelerate bold ideas from the lab to breakthroughs in the fab. EPIC will also serve as a cornerstone for the semiconductor talent pipeline and by working alongside Applied’s scientists and engineers, our students will gain the systems-level perspective needed to drive the future of AI innovation.” –  Michael Crow , President,  Arizona State University 
“UC Berkeley has helped shape microelectronics from its earliest days, advancing the research and talent that continue to propel the semiconductor industry, and our collaboration with Applied Materials is a great example of how academia and industry must work together to meet the scale and opportunity of what’s ahead. The EPIC platform gives our researchers access to the same cutting-edge capabilities used by the world’s leading chipmakers, within a manufacturing-relevant environment, so ideas can be tested, refined and transformed much faster into the semiconductor breakthroughs that will advance the frontier of AI.” –  Rich Lyons , Chancellor,  UC Berkeley 
“Many of the technologies powering today’s AI revolution began in university labs years, often decades, before they transformed the world. As computing demand increases, we must accelerate the pace at which new semiconductor materials, devices and integration technologies move from discovery to deployment. As an inaugural research partner at the EPIC Center, RPI’s students and researchers gain access to world-class experts and a direct pathway to test and validate academic advances in real-world production environments – a powerful blueprint for high-velocity industry-academia collaboration in the AI era.” –  Martin Schmidt , President of RPI 
“The explosive growth of AI is pushing semiconductor technology researchers to find new ways to increase energy efficiency of semiconductor chips. Opportunities abound in discovering new materials and inventing new devices. Experimentation demands faster cycles of innovation and closer collaboration across the ecosystem. Beyond the existing broad research engagement between  Stanford  faculty and Applied Materials, the EPIC Center presents an additional opportunity that enables our students and researchers to engage directly with industry-scale tools and experts, accelerating discovery while gaining the industry-relevant experience needed to lead future advances in semiconductor manufacturing.” –  H.S. Philip Wong , Willard R. and  Inez Kerr Bell Professor  in the  School of Engineering ,  Stanford University 
“Accelerating semiconductor innovation in the new era of AI requires transformative collaboration between universities and industry partners more than ever before. UCLA has a long history of pioneering semiconductor research and innovation, and our collaboration with Applied Materials at the EPIC Center builds on that legacy by bringing together university research and industry expertise to advance the chip technologies that will define the future of computing while preparing the next generation of engineers.” – Ah-Hyung “Alissa” Park, Ronald and  Valerie Sugar Dean  of UCLA Samueli 
*Capital spending is expected to scale over time to approximately $5 billion as customer projects commence. 
Forward-Looking Statements 
This press release contains forward-looking statements, including those regarding Applied’s investment and growth strategies, the development of new materials and technologies, industry outlook and technology requirements, the plans and expectations for the EPIC Center, and other statements that are not historical facts. These statements and their underlying assumptions are subject to risks and uncertainties and are not guarantees of future performance. Factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by such statements include, without limitation: the demand for semiconductors and customers’ technology requirements; the ability to develop new and innovative technologies; the ability to obtain and protect intellectual property rights in key technologies; the ability to achieve the objectives of the EPIC Center; and other risks and uncertainties described in Applied’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including Applied’s most recent Forms 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K. All forward-looking statements are based on management’s current estimates, projections and assumptions, and Applied assumes no obligation to update them.
About the EPIC Center 
The EPIC Center (Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization) is Applied Materials’ flagship R&D facility in Silicon Valley, designed to compress the timeline from early-stage materials research to high-volume semiconductor manufacturing. By bringing chipmakers, equipment partners and university researchers into the same building as Applied’s scientists and engineers, EPIC enables parallel rather than sequential development of materials, equipment and process technology, shortening learning cycles and accelerating the commercialization of the innovations that will power the AI era. Learn more at www.appliedmaterials.com/us/en/epic.html .
About Applied Materials 
Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT) is the leader in materials engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor and advanced display in the world. The technology we create is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation chips. At Applied, we push the boundaries of science and engineering to deliver material innovation that changes the world. Learn more at www.appliedmaterials.com .

Danaher Announces Appointments of Daniel Comas and Robert Hershberg to Board of Directors
WASHINGTON , Oct. 12, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- Danaher Corporation (NYSE: DHR) ("Danaher" or "the Company") today announced the appointment of Daniel L. Comas and Robert Hershberg, M.D., Ph.D., to the Danaher Board of Directors on October 9, 2026. Dr. Hershberg has also been appointed to the Company's Science and Technology Committee. Alan G. Spoon will not stand for reelection at Danaher's 2027 Annual Meeting of Shareholders, retiring from the Board of Directors at that time.
Danaher has expanded the size of its Board from 11 to 13 directors to accommodate these appointments. Danaher's Nominating & Governance Committee also continues to evaluate Board composition as part of its regular governance and refreshment processes.
"Danaher has long benefited from a Board that brings together diverse experiences and perspectives relevant to our strategy and businesses," said Steven M. Rales, Chairman of the Danaher Board of Directors. "Today's appointments reflect our commitment to maintaining a Board with the expertise and experience needed to support Danaher's long-term growth and value creation."
"Dan and Rob each bring highly complementary experience that will further strengthen the Board," Mr. Rales continued. "Dan's deep knowledge of Danaher, the Danaher Business System and our approach to strategy and capital allocation will be very valuable to the Company. Rob adds exceptional scientific, clinical and biopharmaceutical expertise, along with a proven record of advancing innovation that improves patient outcomes. We are delighted to welcome them both to the Board."
Mr. Rales continued, "On behalf of the Board, I'd also like to thank Alan for his contributions and commitment to Danaher and our shareholders during his years of service as a director. We are grateful for the role he has played in the Company's growth and success."
Separately, Danaher's co-founders, Steven and Mitchell Rales, have each waived their right to 500,000 restricted stock units from the awards granted to them on August 4, 2026.
About Daniel L. Comas 
Mr. Comas joined Danaher in 1991 and served as Executive Vice President from April 2005 through December 2020, including as Chief Financial Officer from April 2005 through December 2018. During his tenure, Mr. Comas held various roles with responsibility for corporate development, treasury, finance and risk management. From January 2021 through March 2024, he served in a non-executive capacity as a senior advisor to Danaher, and following his retirement from the Company in March 2024, he served as a consultant to the Company through September 2026. He has also served as a director of Fortive Corporation since March 2021 and Veralto Corporation since September 2023.
About Robert Hershberg, M.D., Ph.D. 
Dr. Hershberg served as President, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of HilleVax, Inc. from March 2020 through September 2025. Before joining HilleVax, he held senior executive roles at Celgene Corporation, including Executive Vice President and Chief Scientific Officer. He also serves as a Senior Advisor to Frazier Life Sciences and as a director of Adaptive Biotechnologies Corporation and Recursion Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
About Danaher

title: Le sport, moteur de la diversité et de l’inclusion chez Veolia
source: Veolia - Financial Press Releases / Financial Press Releases RSS
query: https://www.veolia.com/en/rss-site-updates
content_text:
Sport: A Driving Force for Diversity and Inclusion at Veolia
News listing 
09 Oct. 2026 
At Veolia, diversity is also something we experience through movement. Through two sporting events, the Course de la Diversité and E-Run for Diversity, Group employees come together to champion diversity and inclusion, share a collective experience and promote physical activity. Once again this year, these initiatives brought together employees from numerous Veolia countries and entities around shared values: inclusion, solidarity, sharing and physical health prevention. 
Two Events, One Shared Purpose
The Course de la Diversité (Diversity Run) in Paris and E-Run for Diversity offer two different formats but share the same ambition:  bringing employees together through sport to promote diversity and inclusion .
The  Course de la Diversité (Diversity Run) is a unifying event that gives employees the opportunity to come together and run side by side, sending a powerful message: diversity in backgrounds, career paths and experiences is a strength for the collective.
The  E-Run for Diversity , meanwhile, offers a connected, international dimension. Everyone can take part from wherever they live or work, contributing at their own pace to a global initiative that brings together Veolia's countries and entities.
Together, these two events provide different opportunities to  get active, share experiences and build connections , making diversity and inclusion something that is experienced in practice.
Record-Breaking Participation
This momentum is particularly evident in the E-Run for Diversity figures. As the global virtual running challenge draws to a close, this year's edition has set a  new participation record , with more than 400 additional registrations compared with last year.
Key figures
6,225 Veolia employees taking part worldwide this month (E-Run and Course de la Diversité events)
4,940 Participants in the E-Run
80 Veolia countries and entities involved (E-Run and Course de la Diversité events)
+ 900 participants compared to the 2025 edition
Nearly 4,000 employees came together in person and online to take on this challenge,  getting active, sharing experiences and supporting diversity and inclusion through sport , while promoting physical health prevention.
Sport as a Way to Build Connections
Beyond performance, these two events are above all about  the power of collective action . Taking part in sport brings together employees from different backgrounds, professions and career paths through a shared experience. It encourages interaction, mutual support and teamwork, while building bridges between teams and entities.
Both the Course de la Diversité and the E-Run for Diversity embody a fundamental belief:  diversity is at its strongest when everyone can find their place and contribute to the collective .
These initiatives also support the prevention of physical, mental and social health issues by encouraging everyone to incorporate more movement and physical activity into their daily lives.
Thank You to Everyone! 
A huge thank you to  everyone who took part in the Course de la Diversité and E-Run for Diversity , as well as to all those who helped make these two events possible. Through their commitment, Veolia employees have once again demonstrated that sport can be a powerful driver of connection, inclusion and shared experiences .
The race is now over, but the momentum continues:  making diversity a collective strength and enabling everyone to move forward together .

title: Hexagon to acquire Rocscience, closing the loop between real-world monitoring and advanced simulation 09 Oct 2026
query: https://investors.hexagon.com/en/
content_text:
Hexagon to acquire Rocscience, closing the loop between real-world monitoring and advanced simulation 
9 October 2026
Hexagon AB today announced that it has signed an agreement to acquire Rocscience, a leading provider of geotechnical and engineering analysis software, from TA Associates and Rocscience’s founders and management. Rocscience will become part of the Radar & Monitoring Division within Hexagon’s Infrastructure & Geospatial Business Area.
Customers in mining and infrastructure require early understanding of geological risks, fast intervention, and continuous optimisation to improve safety and productivity. Rocscience, headquartered in Toronto, Canada, helps engineers model how rock, soil and structures behave under different conditions, analyse slope stability and ground movement, and assess how tunnels, dams and other critical infrastructure assets are likely to perform over time. Its software is used by mining, civil engineering and energy customers in around 125 countries to evaluate risk, improve safety and support confident decision-making, and its AI-assisted workflows, including a natural-language interface, make advanced engineering modelling and analysis more accessible and efficient.
Hexagon and Rocscience have complementary technologies. Hexagon’s sensors, such as its radar monitoring solutions, capture and measure conditions in the physical world continuously; Rocscience’s models help customers understand and predict how the ground and structures will behave. Together, they break down the traditional barrier between observation-based actions and model-based decisions, creating a continuous feedback loop in which live sensor data automatically informs, updates and calibrates engineering models from design through construction and operations. For customers, this means earlier detection of emerging risks, faster intervention, reduced analysis time, and improved safety and productivity.
“Rocscience has an exceptionally strong team that has built a proven business with outstanding customer satisfaction. Its software is complementary to our sensor and monitoring businesses in mining, and increasingly in civil and infrastructure applications,” said Henning Sandfort, President, Infrastructure & Geospatial, Hexagon AB. “By connecting what our sensors measure with how Rocscience’s models predict, we can help customers move from data capture to informed action with far greater confidence. We are excited to welcome the global Rocscience team to Infrastructure & Geospatial and to Hexagon.”
Rocscience is expected to deliver revenue approaching USD 50 million in calendar year 2026, with annual recurring revenue equivalent to over 80 per cent of revenue and strong growth rates. The acquisition is expected to be accretive to Hexagon's net income from closing, with EBITAC margins above 40%. Closing is subject to customary conditions and is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. The transaction values Rocscience at an enterprise value of USD 535 million on a cash-free, debt-free basis.

From aerospace & defence, automotive, construction, general manufacturing, to mining and more, we provide the confidence that customers rely on to build, navigate, and innovate. 
Hexagon (Nasdaq Stockholm: HEXA B) has approximately 16,000 employees in 50 countries and net sales of approximately 3.7bn EUR.

Asahi Kasei Therapeutics, Inc., the global specialty pharmaceutical business of Tokyo-based Asahi Kasei, today announced that the first patient has been dosed in a randomized Phase 2a clinical trial ( NCT07503561 ) evaluating AIC468, a novel antiviral antisense oligonucleotide (ASO), in adult kidney transplant recipients with BK virus (BKV) infection. The investigational program was developed by Aicuris Anti-infective Cures AG (Aicuris), which is now part of Asahi Kasei Therapeutics .
“BK virus reactivation, while relatively harmless in immunocompetent people, remains a major complication for kidney transplant recipients, as reactivation of the virus can lead to graft dysfunction and BK nephropathy,” said Carl Kraus, MD, Chief Medical Officer of Asahi Kasei Therapeutics. “For transplant patients and their families, this means a high risk of losing the transplanted kidney. Following encouraging Phase 1 data in healthy volunteers, dosing the first patient in this study represents an important step toward developing a targeted antiviral therapy for a community with no approved treatment options. Our goal is to help protect transplanted organs and improve long-term outcomes for these patients.”
The randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2a trial is part of a Phase 2/3 program designed to evaluate safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetic profile in adult patients with BKV infection after kidney transplantation across multiple dose levels as assessed by frequency and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs). Progression into Phase 2a is supported by favorable Phase 1 safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetic data .
About BKV 
BKV is a ubiquitous human polyomavirus that is typically acquired in early childhood and persists lifelong without symptoms in more than 90% of the adult population. In immunocompromised individuals, such as organ transplant recipients, BKV can reactivate, leading to serious health issues. In kidney transplant patients, BKV reactivation in the transplanted kidney can cause BK virus-associated nephropathy (BKVAN), affecting up to 10% of recipients and potentially resulting in graft loss. Current management involves reducing immunosuppressive therapy, which increases the risk of graft rejection. Despite its prevalence, there is no approved antiviral treatment specifically for BKV.
About AIC468 
AIC468 is an antiviral antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) in clinical development for the treatment of BK virus replication in kidney transplant recipients. The candidate inhibits viral replication in infected cells by modulating splicing of the BKV early coding pre‑mRNA, thereby preventing formation of the mRNA encoding the essential BKV master regulator protein, large T antigen. This innovative approach has already demonstrated potent antiviral activity along with a favorable pharmacokinetic and safety profile in preclinical studies and in a Phase 1 clinical trial in healthy volunteers.
About Asahi Kasei Therapeutics 
Asahi Kasei Therapeutics is the global specialty pharmaceutical business of Tokyo-based Asahi Kasei. We are identifying, developing, and commercializing innovative medicines for diseases with significant unmet medical needs. Drawing upon our strong heritage of scientific innovation, we are expanding therapeutic options and helping to positively impact health in immunology, nephrology, transplantation, and infectious diseases. For more information, visit: www.aktx.com/ .
About Asahi Kasei 
Asahi Kasei is a diversified global company that contributes to life and living for people around the world. Since its foundation in 1922, with businesses in ammonia and cellulose fiber, Asahi Kasei has consistently grown through proactive portfolio transformation to meet the evolving needs of every age. With 50,000 employees worldwide, the company contributes to sustainability by providing solutions to the world’s challenges across its three business sectors: Healthcare, Homes, and Material. For more information, visit https://www.asahi-kasei.com/ .

title: Applied Materials and UCLA Engineering Accelerate Semiconductor Innovation at the EPIC Center
query: https://ir.appliedmaterials.com/rss.xml
content_text:
Applied Materials and UCLA Engineering Accelerate Semiconductor Innovation at the EPIC Center
Oct 8, 2026 at 4:05 PM EDT
PDF Version 
R&D programs to focus on speeding up the commercialization pipeline so chip technology moves from breakthrough research to full-scale manufacturing faster 
Collaborative work at the state-of-the-art facility in Silicon Valley pairs UCLA’s semiconductor research strength with Applied’s cutting-edge chipmaking equipment and process integration expertise 
SANTA CLARA, Calif. , Oct. 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Applied Materials, Inc. today announced that the UCLA Samueli School of Engineering will join the company’s EPIC Center in Silicon Valley as a research partner. Together with Applied’s scientists and engineers, UCLA researchers will work to solve semiconductor materials and integration challenges with a focus on shortening the time it takes to bring breakthrough research to commercialization.
“As the industry races to bring new AI chip technologies to market, the EPIC Center will play a pivotal role by convening the industry’s top innovators in a collaborative environment designed to accelerate the path from breakthrough research to full-scale manufacturing,” said Dr. Prabu Raja , President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials. “UCLA has a long history of semiconductor technology innovation and Applied looks forward to welcoming their researchers to the EPIC Center where together we will work to solve the industry’s toughest challenges.”
The EPIC Center aims to accelerate chip R&D by bridging the gap between traditional academic innovation and industrial-scale development. UCLA researchers will have access to advanced chipmaking tools so that new ideas can be validated and tested in a commercial fab environment, thereby shortening the path from concept to production.
UCLA Samueli brings extensive expertise across semiconductor devices, materials, electronics and computing. In 1991, Henry Samueli co-founded Broadcom Corporation while teaching at UCLA . The school is also home to the Center for Heterogeneous Integration and Performance Scaling (CHIPS) Lab , which brings together researchers across disciplines to advance semiconductor technologies and address challenges in chip design, manufacturing and integration.
By collaborating at the EPIC Center, Applied Materials and UCLA will focus R&D programs on the semiconductor industry’s most critical challenges in areas including 3D chip scaling, advanced packaging and the discovery of new materials for improving energy-efficient AI compute performance. The work will complement and extend the efforts of UCLA’s Semiconductor Hub , which Applied joined as a co-founding member earlier this year. Applied’s ongoing commitment to strengthen the ties between industry and academia is aimed at empowering the next generation of engineers and researchers to bring semiconductor breakthroughs to market faster.
“Accelerating semiconductor innovation in the new era of AI requires transformative collaboration between universities and industry partners more than ever before,” said Ah-Hyung “Alissa” Park, Ronald and Valerie Sugar Dean of UCLA Samueli. “UCLA has a long history of pioneering semiconductor research and innovation, and this collaboration builds on that legacy by bringing together university research and industry expertise to advance the chip technologies that will define the future of computing while preparing the next generation of engineers.”
Applied’s new EPIC (Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization) Center in Silicon Valley represents the largest-ever U.S . investment in advanced semiconductor equipment R&D. The center is designed from the ground up to dramatically reduce the time it takes to commercialize breakthrough technologies from early-stage research to full-scale manufacturing. The facility is on track to become operational in 2026. Visit the EPIC Center website to learn more.

About Applied Materials 
Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT) is the leader in materials engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor and advanced display in the world. The technology we create is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation chips. At Applied, we push the boundaries of science and engineering to deliver material innovation that changes the world. Learn more at www.appliedmaterials.com .

title: TOPPAN to Participate in ‘Rapidus CORE’ Global Ecosystem Framework
query: https://www.holdings.toppan.com/en/news/
content_text:
TOPPAN to Participate in ‘Rapidus CORE’ Global Ecosystem Framework
Offering input on cutting-edge semiconductors as a Design Solution Associate to contribute to LSI design and development
Tweet 
Tokyo – October 8, 2026 – TOPPAN Inc. (TOPPAN), a TOPPAN Group company and wholly owned subsidiary of TOPPAN Holdings Inc. (TYO: 7911), will participate as a Design Solution Associate in the Rapidus Collaborative Open Rapid Ecosystem (Rapidus CORE)—a global ecosystem framework for the development and mass production of cutting-edge semiconductors to be established by Rapidus Corporation (Rapidus).
Background & Objectives
In recent years, driven by the rapid growth of AI, high-performance computing, and automated driving technologies, global demand has surged for cutting-edge logic semiconductors that deliver both exceptional processing power and high energy efficiency. Consequently, semiconductor manufacturing processes are transitioning to next-generation nodes, starting with the 2 nm generation. However, as process miniaturization advances, Large-Scale Integration (LSI) design has become extraordinarily complex. Increased risks in manufacturing lead to costly redesigns and heavier verification workloads, driving up development costs and lengthening time-to-market. Addressing these challenges requires advanced design solutions that seamlessly bridge design and manufacturing, alongside open collaborative frameworks.
To drive innovation across the entire semiconductor value chain—from design to front-end and back-end processes—and to accelerate next-generation LSI development by creating partner-driven value beyond traditional supply chain boundaries, Rapidus has launched Rapidus CORE, a global ecosystem framework.
As part of the initial rollout of Rapidus CORE, Rapidus announced Design Solution Associates, a group of design-related companies in which TOPPAN will participate. Design Solution Associates connect customers with Rapidus, providing specialized engineering resources and technical expertise to facilitate the rapid launch of semiconductor development. This collaborative model strengthens support systems from design through manufacturing tailored to diverse customer needs.
Some of TOPPAN’s core strengths are its expertise built over many years in LSI design technology and the optimization of Electronic Design Automation (EDA) environments. In particular, TOPPAN possesses extensive technical know-how in complex design solutions required for advanced process nodes, including low-power design, timing closure addressing Process, Voltage, Temperature (PVT) variations, and high-speed interface implementation.
By joining Rapidus CORE as a Design Solution Associate, TOPPAN will offer end-to-end support for Rapidus customers—from initial specification analysis to circuit design, layout, and physical verification. In doing so, TOPPAN will help significantly reduce the design complexity, cost, and risks associated with cutting-edge process nodes, contributing to establishing a sustainable semiconductor ecosystem.
Future Goals
In addition to contributing to establishing a sustainable ecosystem for next-generation semiconductors, through participation in Rapidus CORE, TOPPAN will contribute to creating new value as well as resolving societal issues by leveraging cutting-edge semiconductor technology.

Established in Tokyo in 1900, the TOPPAN Group is a leading and diversified global provider committed to delivering sustainable, integrated solutions in fields including printing, communications, security, packaging, décor materials, electronics, and digital transformation. The TOPPAN Group’s global team of more than 50,000 employees offers optimal solutions enabled by industry-leading expertise and technologies to address the diverse challenges of every business sector and society and contribute to the achievement of shared sustainability goals.

title: TOPPAN at Hydrogen Technology World Expo 2026
query: https://www.holdings.toppan.com/en/news/
content_text:
TOPPAN at Hydrogen Technology World Expo 2026
Unveiling performance data for upgraded CCMs and MEAs ideal for green hydrogen production using renewable energy
Tweet 
Tokyo – October 8, 2026 –TOPPAN Holdings Inc. (TYO: 7911) (TOPPAN Holdings) announced its upcoming participation at the Hydrogen Technology World Expo scheduled to be held in Hamburg, Germany, from October 20 to 22. 
As one of Europe’s leading hydrogen technology related events, Hydrogen Technology World Expo enjoys participation from a broad spectrum of companies across the hydrogen supply chain. The TOPPAN Holdings booth (no. 7G48) will present high-performance and high-quality electrode components (CCMs and MEAs) that can be applied in various processes involved in the production, storage, distribution, and utilization of hydrogen.
Background
Countries and regions around the world are advancing measures to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050, including renewable energy use and initiatives to enable a hydrogen society. There are high expectations for hydrogen as an energy source because it is generated from an abundant resource in the form of water and no CO 2 is emitted when used.
For the practical use of hydrogen in society, Catalyst Coated Membranes (CCMs) and Membrane Electrode Assemblies (MEAs) are critical components that determine the efficiency and economic performance of hydrogen-related applications. To this end, TOPPAN Holdings has been conducting CCM and MEA research and development since 2004 to address challenges related to performance and durability. Building on these efforts, TOPPAN aims to expand its provision of CCMs and MEAs to Europe and other markets throughout the world.
Main Solutions on Show
The booth will showcase high-performance, high-quality CCMs and MEAs that are fabricated using proprietary materials, a sheet-to-sheet process and double-sided direct coating technique developed by TOPPAN Holdings.
① CCMs for water electrolysis
Alongside a 600×800 mm CCM display, TOPPAN will unveil for the first time the core specifications of its upgraded CCMs. TOPPAN Holdings' CCMs feature high durability against voltage fluctuations, making them ideally suited for water electrolysis powered by renewable energy and contributing to the expanded adoption of green hydrogen.
TOPPAN Holdings is advancing the development of large-area CCMs in the 1.5 m × 2.5 m class. Adopting these large-area CCMs is expected to lower both capital expenditure (CAPEX) and operational expenditure (OPEX) by reducing the required number of CCM sheets and auxiliary equipment, while also contributing to lower power consumption.
② MEAs for fuel cells
TOPPAN Holdings will present five- and seven-layer MEAs stacked with subgaskets 1 and GDLs 2 that employ the TOPPAN Holding’s proprietary catalyst layer design technology. By utilizing patented proprietary materials, the technology achieves both high voltage retention performance and superior durability, even under high-load operating conditions. Consequently, applications that were previously restricted to low-load operation to preserve durability can now achieve higher power output through high-load operation, directly meeting the needs of customers seeking high-output solutions.
③ Reaction Enhancement Plate (REP)
The Reaction Enhancement Plate (REP) developed by TOPPAN Holdings is a metallic plate featuring precision micro-slits. Integrating it into a fuel cell stack increases overall system power output without requiring modifications to the MEA. At this exhibition, TOPPAN Holdings will display the REP alongside a mockup of the fuel cell stack used during testing and reveal evaluation data demonstrating its power enhancement performance for the first time.

title: 10/07/2026 Health Care Evonik wins CPHI Pharma Award 2026 for Self Driving Labs Evonik has won the 2026 CPHI Pharma Award in the “Digital Transformation” category for its Self Driving Labs. The globally available CDMO service combines artificial intelligence, automation and chemical expertise in a closed-loop platform that autonomously designs, executes and evaluates experiments for active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) process development.
query: https://www.evonik.com/en/media.html
content_text:
Evonik wins CPHI Pharma Award 2026 for Self Driving Labs
Winner in the “Digital Transformation” category
Autonomous platform combines AI, automation and chemical expertise for API process development
Industrial use cases show up to 100 autonomous experiments per day and overnight optimization
Evonik has won the 2026 CPHI Pharma Award in the “Digital Transformation” category for its Self Driving Labs. The globally available CDMO service combines artificial intelligence, automation and chemical expertise in a closed-loop platform that autonomously designs, executes and evaluates experiments for active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) process development.
“The CPHI award recognizes how Self Driving Labs turns AI into practical value for pharmaceutical customers,” said Daniel Fricker, Head of the Drug Substance product line at Evonik. “By reaching robust process conditions faster and generating richer data from the outset, we can help customers shorten development timelines, use expert resources more effectively and make better-informed scale-up decisions.”
Developing manufacturing processes for APIs is becoming more complex as pipelines expand beyond small molecules to modalities such as peptides and oligonucleotides. Conventional process development relies on sequential, manual experiments that can take weeks, produce limited analytical data and depend heavily on expert judgement. Once a process has advanced into later clinical phases, changes can also become more difficult to implement without adding cost, time and risk.
Self Driving Labs digitalizes the workflow from experiment design and execution to data capture, analysis and decision-making. Continuous processing platforms, interchangeable and 3D-printed reactors, high-throughput experimentation, process analytical technology and automated chromatography are connected through a secure orchestration layer. A Bayesian optimization algorithm evaluates results in real time and selects the next experiment, while Evonik’s AI-based user interface “AIChemBuddy” gives scientists transparency, traceability and control.
Self Driving Labs helps customers develop robust processes faster, improve reproducibility and reduce the risk of costly late-stage changes. The technology is being deployed globally for new development projects and the optimization of existing products.
The annual CPHI Excellence in Pharma Awards were established in 2004 to celebrate cross-industry innovators driving the industry forward. This year’s award was presented to Evonik at the CPHI pharmaceutical trade show in Milan on October 6, 2026. In previous years, Evonik has won in the category “Finished Formulation” for its EUDRACAP® colon functional capsules , in the category “Sustainability” for its plant-based squalene, PhytoSquene® and in the category “Packaging and Drug Delivery” for a polymer-based drug delivery system for mRNA and nucleic acid delivery .
Evonik Health Care is a global CDMO for active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and intermediates, supporting pharmaceutical companies with process development, scale-up and manufacturing from clinical development through commercial supply. Its Drug Substance capabilities are part of a broader Health Care portfolio that includes advanced drug delivery solutions for oral and parenteral drug products, as well as growth platforms for lipid-based mRNA and gene delivery and cell culture solutions for biopharma applications.
The Self Driving Labs project was led by Evonik's Competence Center for Simulation & Additive Manufacturing (SAM 3D) and funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action. We would like to thank all contributors and partners for their valuable support throughout the project. 
Further information:
Evonik's product & service portfolio for drug substance 
Evonik: Leading beyond chemistry
Evonik goes beyond the boundaries of chemistry with its combination of innovative strength and leading technological expertise. The global chemical company, headquartered in Essen, Germany, is active in more than 100 countries and generated sales of €14.1 billion and earnings (adjusted EBITDA) of €1.9 billion in 2025. The common motivation of the approximately 31,000 employees: to provide customers with a decisive competitive advantage with tailor-made products and solutions as a superforce for industry, thereby improving people's lives. In all markets. Every day.
About Custom Solutions
The Custom Solutions segment focuses on innovation-driven, tailor-made solutions for customers in specific growth markets. These solutions include additives for coatings, adhesives and sealants, polyurethane foams and lubricants, catalysts, and ingredients for the cosmetics, cleaning and pharmaceutical industries. In 2025, the segment generated sales of €5.4 billion with around 9,500 employees.

title: Skyworks Si829x Isolated Safety Gate Driver Qualified and Ready for Customer Evaluation
query: https://investors.skyworksinc.com/rss.xml
content_text:
Skyworks Si829x Isolated Safety Gate Driver Qualified and Ready for Customer Evaluation
Si829x platform with ProVCD™ technology moves from development to pre-production release for EV traction inverters
IRVINE, Calif., Oct. 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Skyworks Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq: SWKS), an innovator of high-performance analog and mixed-signal semiconductors, today announced that its Si829x isolated safety gate driver with ProVCD™ technology has completed AEC-Q100 automotive qualification and is ready for advanced prototyping. Samples, tools, user guides, and application notes are available now. Designed for scalable, high-performance inverter architectures, the Si829x supports both SiC FETs and IGBTs while helping customers improve efficiency, simplify system design, and reduce system cost in applications ranging from automotive drivetrains to safety-critical electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) systems.
AEC-Q100 Qualified and Ready for Evaluation 
With AEC-Q100 qualification completed, the Si829x is now positioned to support customers for initial product evaluation through pre-production prototypes. Samples are available today, giving customers a qualified, prototype-ready path to design-in.
The Si829x was designed to support customer functional safety system designs rated up to ASIL D, subject to system-level implementation and validation, to deliver the robustness required for EV traction inverters and other safety critical motor control applications. Its integrated protection features include:
Extensive diagnostic fault coverage, notification and management
Comprehensive safety mechanisms including power-up self-checks and safe state enforcement – a functional safety manual is available today
Advanced isolation technology certified by multiple independent organizations for enhanced safety and reliability 
With applications in battery electric vehicles, hybrid electric vehicles, eAgriculture, eTrucking, robotaxis, and exciting new segments like eVTOL aircraft, Si829x is a comprehensive choice among isolated gate drivers for safety-critical advanced propulsion systems.
Full Documentation and Development Tools Now Available 
Alongside qualification, Skyworks has prepared the complete technical resource set for the Si829x, including datasheet, technical reference manual, functional safety manual and application notes. This resource set, available under NDA, gives design teams comprehensive technical documentation to evaluate, integrate and validate the part.
Skyworks has also released customer-facing development tools, including two evaluation board kits, companion GUI software and complex device driver (CDD) software, designed to shorten development cycles and reduce time-to-market.
A New Approach to Gate Drive Control 
Unlike conventional voltage-mode gate drivers, the Si829x uses ProVCD™, which is Skyworks’ second-generation variable current drive that delivers high resolution gate waveform shaping and cycle-by-cycle control through a digital interface. This approach enables:
Precise 15 Amp 3-phase turn-on and turn-off current waveform control
Switching-loss reductions of up to 44% in Skyworks testing, compared with voltage-mode gate drive
Reduced electromagnetic interference (EMI) and filtering requirements
Improved thermal efficiency through multiple packaging options
Smaller PCB footprint and potential system-level cost savings
Together, these benefits allow manufacturers to increase inverter efficiency while simplifying system design and accelerating development cycles.
“Si829x gives customers a qualified path from evaluation to advanced prototypes,” said Mario Battello, vice president of product line management at Skyworks. “The ProVCD™ platform combines software-configurable performance with the safety, isolation and design flexibility needed to standardize inverter designs for EVs, eVTOL, and eAgriculture, and accelerate development for high power motor applications like datacenter cooling and AI power supplies.”
Platform Scalability and Design Flexibility 
The Si829x is designed as a configurable platform, allowing engineers to adjust gate drive parameters through software rather than fixed hardware components. This configurability supports:
Design reuse across multiple vehicle platforms
Faster development and validation cycles
Greater flexibility to optimize performance, efficiency and cost

AVerMedia and Stereolabs Accelerate AI Vision Deployment with NVIDIA JetPack 7.2
October 7, 2026
General
Unified integration delivers faster time to market, broad camera compatibility, and more efficient use of memory across Jetson Orin and Thor modules
TAIPEI, Taiwan & PARIS--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 7, 2026-- AVerMedia Technologies, Inc. and Stereolabs , an Ouster company, today announced NVIDIA JetPack 7.2 support across all Stereolabs ZED X GMSL cameras and AVerMedia’s NVIDIA Jetson carrier boards, offering robotics and edge AI developers a faster and more efficient path from development to production.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261007896664/en/
AVerMedia and Stereolabs Accelerate AI Vision Deployment with NVIDIA JetPack 7.2
The collaboration combines AVerMedia’s NVIDIA Jetson carrier-board and Board Support Package (BSP) engineering expertise with Stereolabs’ unified ZED X driver architecture. With this approach, AVerMedia can adapt the hardware-specific device tree and generate drivers for the JetPack and Jetson Linux versions required by customers, reducing the repeated exchanges previously required for each hardware or software update.
This collaboration allows AVerMedia hardware development and Stereolabs software releases to progress in parallel, shortening validation cycles and giving customers greater control over product schedules.
The unified workflow allows Stereolabs to focus on camera firmware, ISP performance, and ZED SDK capabilities, while AVerMedia manages the carrier-board-specific integration and validation required for production deployment.
More AI Capability from Available Jetson Memory
Memory is a critical resource in embedded AI systems, particularly when multiple camera streams, perception models, and robotics applications must run simultaneously on a single Jetson module.
NVIDIA JetPack 7.2 introduces Jetson agent skills that help developers optimize memory usage across the software stack. These agent-driven workflows can tune bootloader carveouts, optimize kernel memory reservations, streamline user-space services, and improve inference memory usage. These optimizations free up critical memory for vision processing and AI workloads, enabling richer applications on smaller memory footprints and lowering total cost of ownership.
Key Customer Benefits:
Faster time to market: Hardware modifications and software releases can be integrated and validated more efficiently.
Broad compatibility: NVIDIA JetPack 7.2 supports all Stereolabs cameras across AVerMedia’s NVIDIA Jetson carrier-board portfolio, including Jetson Orin and Jetson Thor platforms.
More efficient memory utilization: Developers can make more memory available for camera processing, AI models, and robotics applications.
Greater software control: Reproducible Debian packages provide traceability of the driver, device tree, installation flow, and kernel code used in production.
Simplified lifecycle management: Drivers can be regenerated for required JetPack and Linux versions, supporting long-term maintenance, compliance, and product updates.
“By anchoring the platform-specific integration work with AVerMedia, where we’re doubling down on both companies’ hardware expertise, both teams can develop in parallel and respond to customer requirements more quickly,” said Ihsane Debbache , VP of Engineering at Stereolabs. “This integration gives developers a more efficient path to deploying Stereolabs ZED vision across AVerMedia Jetson platforms.”
NVIDIA JetPack 7.2 also provides official Yocto support, giving developers greater control over reproducible, production-ready software images for Jetson Orin and Jetson Thor platforms.
“Customers need both faster integration and more efficient use of their computing resources,” said Alex Liu , Vice President of AVerMedia. “By combining Stereolabs’ vision technology and AVerMedia’s BSP and hardware engineering expertise, we can help customers reduce integration risk, make better use of available Jetson memory, and deploy more capable AI vision systems faster.”
Ongoing support and transition to NVIDIA JetPack 7.2 will be available through AVerMedia support form .
About AVerMedia Technologies, Inc.
AVerMedia Technologies, Inc. is a leading global provider of application-ready Edge AI turnkey solutions, recognized for its expertise in video and audio technologies. AVerMedia offers customized, fully integrated hardware and software solutions designed to accelerate AI deployments across various industries, including smart cities, robotics, and industrial automation. AVerMedia is dedicated to delivering cutting-edge AI inference solutions that enable businesses to scale AI effectively and reliably at the edge.
About Stereolabs
Stereolabs , a wholly owned subsidiary of Ouster, Inc. (Nasdaq: OUST), is a leader of 3D vision and depth perception for Physical AI. Its ZED camera family and ZED SDK platform provide real-time depth sensing, spatial mapping, and AI-powered object understanding for robotics, industrial automation, and smart spaces.

Danaher Accelerates Life Sciences Research with New AI-powered Autonomous Lab
Helping researchers to move from discovery to breakthrough up to 8x faster by combining AI, automation and innovation from across Danaher's ecosystem of industry-leading technologies 
WASHINGTON , Oct. 7, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- Danaher Corporation (NYSE: DHR) today announced plans to launch its first AI-powered autonomous lab, designed to help researchers develop custom antibodies and other molecular tools faster and more efficiently. Expected to operate at scale in early 2027, the lab will combine artificial intelligence, robotics and technologies from several Danaher operating companies in one connected workflow. It is the first step in a broader Danaher initiative to create smart instruments, integrated workflows and autonomous labs that accelerate scientific research . 
Danaher's first AI-powered autonomous lab is designed to deliver:
Speed: Up to 8x faster discovery of affinity reagents, helping researchers get from idea to breakthrough sooner
Scale: Unlocking up to a tenfold increase in annual reagent generation, from tens to hundreds of reagents per year as the lab scales
Quality: Each design built in the lab would also be verified, tested and fed back to improve the next, without trading speed for scientific rigor
Sustainability: Over time, this approach is expected to complement traditional immunization-based methods used in the discovery of antibodies and other research tools
"The autonomous lab reflects the kind of progress Danaher is uniquely positioned to deliver," said Julie Sawyer Montgomery, President and Chief Executive Officer of Danaher. "By applying our science, technology and culture of continuous improvement, we can help turn promising ideas into validated systems faster. It is an important step toward a future where AI, automation and intelligent systems dramatically accelerate the journey from discovery to impact."
Based at Abcam, a Danaher company, the lab uses AI to help create new affinity reagents, including antibodies, then builds and tests each one, feeding every result back into the model to improve the next design. The lab brings together industry-leading technologies and expertise from several Danaher operating companies, including Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, Cytiva, Genedata, Integrated DNA Technologies, and Molecular Devices, in one connected workflow. The device orchestration and robotic automation is the result of collaborative work with Automata *. This continuous design-make-test-learn loop can run in a fraction of the time it takes today, without trading speed for scientific rigor. This approach applies the same test-and-verify discipline of continuous improvement long used across Danaher operations to an AI-enabled laboratory environment. The lab is set to be an early proof point for how Danaher's smart instruments, AI-ready data, and expert agentic systems can accelerate scientific discovery and medical progress.
"This lab represents a new model for scientific discovery, where AI, automation and human expertise work together in a continuous learning cycle," said JC Gutierrez-Ramos, Senior Vice President and Chief Science Officer of Danaher. "Speed is what supercharges that cycle. Every result sharpens the next design, so the faster each loop runs, the faster discovery compounds. The lab is designed to deliver up to eight times faster progress from idea to validated reagent and up to a tenfold increase in reagent generation, while scientists continue to make the key decisions. That frees them to focus on the complex scientific challenges where human insight matters most."
The lab is an example of a broader program across Danaher intended to create a fleet of smart instruments that are easier to integrate and control programmatically, produce AI-ready data, and include expert-level agentic systems designed to simplify operation, improve data quality and generate deeper insights. These intelligent devices can then be connected to create integrated workflows and autonomous labs that execute design-make-test-learn cycles. The approach also supports a shift toward more predictive and standardized research workflows, with models helping prioritize the most promising designs before they are made and robotics supporting more consistent experimentation.
The platform reflects an important milestone in the Company's continued investment in connected science at a global scale: technologies designed to help researchers move from scientific question to validated answer with greater speed, consistency and confidence.
