content_text:
Infineon opens new backend manufacturing hub in Thailand adding resilient capacity for future growth
Business & Financial Press
Oct 01, 2026 
New backend manufacturing hub strengthens and further diversifies Infineon's global production network 
Strategic investment reinforces Thailand's growing semiconductor ecosystem and talent development, creating up to 1,000 highly skilled jobs 
Designed for phased expansion, Bangkok has the potential to become one of Infineon's largest backend manufacturing sites over time 
Bangkok, Thailand, 01 October 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) officially inaugurated its new backend manufacturing site in Bangkok, Samut Prakan, together with Anutin Charnvirakul, Prime Minister of Thailand and Alexander Gorski, Chief Operations Officer of Infineon Technologies. The site strengthens and further diversifies the company's global manufacturing footprint while adding capacity for future growth. Strategically located in the heart of Southeast Asia, the site reinforces Infineon's ability to serve customers worldwide at a time when long-term semiconductor demand continues to grow, driven by digitalization, electrification and the energy transition.
Built for future growth, the facility can scale up to five modules, giving Bangkok the potential to become one of Infineon's largest backend manufacturing sites over time. As a strategic addition to Infineon's globally diversified manufacturing network, the site complements the ongoing expansion of Infineon's frontend manufacturing capacities.
"What makes Bangkok such an important addition to our global manufacturing footprint is its unique combination of location and growth potential," says Alexander Gorski, Chief Operations Officer of Infineon Technologies. "We are establishing a new hub in the heart of Southeast Asia, surrounded by a fast-growing ecosystem and with excellent access to global logistics. This helps us further diversify our manufacturing network across regions and serve our customers with resilient capacity and great flexibility. We have built the Bangkok site with the future in mind. Starting with Module A, the site can grow to up to five modules over time, giving us unique scalability to support future growth."
"Infineon's new backend manufacturing site in Bangkok, Samut Prakan, is a strong vote of confidence in Thailand's future as a leading semiconductor location," says Anutin Charnvirakul, Prime Minister of Thailand. "Together, we are advancing Thailand's semiconductor ecosystem, strengthening our role in the global value chain and creating new opportunities and highly skilled jobs for future generations. We welcome Infineon's long-term engagement and look forward to deepening our cooperation."
A long-term investment in Thailand's semiconductor ecosystem 
Thailand's commitment to building a strong semiconductor ecosystem, guided by its national technology strategy, is creating new momentum for advanced manufacturing and technology-driven growth in the region. Thailand offers excellent connections throughout Southeast Asia, proximity to key customer markets and a long-standing semiconductor manufacturing heritage. The Bangkok site builds on local expertise, established partnerships and a highly skilled workforce while contributing to the further development of Thailand's flourishing semiconductor ecosystem.
The site currently employs around 350 people and is expected to grow to approximately 1,000 employees as the first building (Module A) ramps up. Beyond manufacturing, Infineon supports talent development through collaborations with universities, educational institutions and industry partners.
Expanding capabilities for complex, high-value semiconductor solutions 
The Bangkok site combines advanced automation, scalable design and a digital manufacturing backbone to support efficient, stable and high-quality production at scale. Built as a greenfield site, the facility leverages proven expertise from Infineon’s established backend manufacturing locations while providing the flexibility to adapt to evolving customer requirements, new technologies and large production volumes.
Equipped with advanced cleanroom, assembly and test capabilities, all supported by a high level of automation, the Bangkok site covers the full spectrum of semiconductor backend processes as well as wafer test. This unique combination strengthens its role within Infineon’s manufacturing network and enables increasingly complex, high-value semiconductor solutions for applications across the automotive, industrial and energy infrastructure, contributing directly to technologies that drive electrification, energy efficiency and digitalization worldwide.
Sustainability built in from the ground up 
The Bangkok site runs on 100 percent green electricity, incorporates water recycling and rainwater collection systems and is equipped with solar modules that generate renewable energy on site. Together, these measures support resource-efficient manufacturing and contribute to Infineon’s strategic priority of continuously reducing its carbon footprint across the entire value chain.

content_text:
Infineon completes acquisition of C2i Semiconductors to expand innovation capabilities in AI data center power management solutions
Business & Financial Press
Oct 05, 2026 
Acquisition strengthens Infineon’s leadership in power solutions for AI data centers and accelerates software-defined power architectures from grid to core 
C2i Semiconductors adds highly differentiated expertise in intelligent digital power management, multiphase controllers and system-level power architectures, including next-generation vertical power delivery solutions 
Transaction expands Infineon’s innovation footprint in India and further strengthens its global R&D capabilities 
C2i Semiconductors’ team joins Infineon’s Power Systems division 
Munich, Germany and Bengaluru, India, 5 October 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) today announced the completion of its acquisition of C2i Semiconductors, a Bengaluru-based technology company specializing in software-defined multiphase controllers and smart power stages for AI data center applications. C2i Semiconductors’ technology complements Infineon’s leading portfolio of power semiconductors and power systems, enabling intelligent and scalable power delivery architectures from grid to core for AI servers and high-performance computing platforms. The acquisition further strengthens Infineon’s leadership in power solutions for AI data centers, expands its engineering capabilities in India and reinforces the country’s role as a strategic innovation hub. With the completion of the transaction, the C2i Semiconductors team becomes part of Infineon’s Power Systems division.
“Completing this acquisition marks an important milestone for our AI power business and our innovation activities in India,” said Adam White, President of Infineon’s Power Systems division. “C2i Semiconductors brings exceptional expertise in software-defined power management and system-level power architectures, backed by a highly experienced engineering team. By combining these capabilities with Infineon’s semiconductor technologies, application know-how, manufacturing capabilities and global customer reach, we will accelerate innovation in power delivery solutions for AI data centers and create significant value for our customers. I am delighted to welcome the C2i team to Infineon.”
Software-defined power solutions combine advanced power semiconductors with intelligent digital control and software algorithms to optimize power conversion, regulation and system performance in real time. As increasingly powerful AI processors create highly dynamic and rapidly changing power demands, power delivery systems must respond faster and more precisely to sudden load fluctuations while maintaining efficiency and system stability. By adding intelligence to the power delivery architecture, software-defined solutions can help improve efficiency, reduce power losses and support the increasing power density requirements of next-generation AI processors.
The acquisition combines C2i Semiconductors’ digital power expertise with Infineon’s global scale, application know-how and broad portfolio of power semiconductors, including silicon, silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN) technologies, as well as vertical power delivery solutions. Together, the teams will accelerate the development of more intelligent, efficient and scalable power delivery solutions for AI infrastructure, including future Substrate Integrated Voltage Regulators (SIVR).
C2i Semiconductors adds expertise in software-defined power management, multiphase controllers, smart power stages, digital control technologies and system-level power architectures. The combination strengthens Infineon’s capabilities across the entire power path from grid to core and supports the development of next-generation power solutions for AI servers and high-performance computing platforms.
The acquisition also adds highly specialized engineering expertise to Infineon’s global R&D network and further strengthens its innovation capabilities in India. The combined team will contribute to reinforcing Bengaluru’s role as an important innovation location for digital power technologies and to accelerating the development of next-generation power solutions for AI infrastructure. Infineon currently employs approximately 2,800 people across multiple locations in India.
About Infineon
Infineon Technologies AG is a global semiconductor leader in power systems and IoT. Infineon drives decarbonization and digitalization with its products and solutions. The Company had around 57,000 employees worldwide (end of September 2025) and generated revenue of about €14.7 billion in the 2025 fiscal year (ending 30 September). Infineon is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: IFX) and in the USA on the OTCQX International over-the-counter market (ticker symbol: IFNNY).

content_text:
Annual report 2025
The fiscal year 2025 was marked by various challenges for Jenoptik, particularly from the semiconductor equipment and automotive markets. Nevertheless, we have continued to focus on our relevant growth potentials in our core markets of semiconductors, medical technology, metrology and smart mobility, and we look to the future with optimism thanks to our strong growth platforms. 
Overview over the fiscal year 2025
Jenoptik performed well overall in a challenging market environment in 2025.
Despite a 6 percent decline in revenue , we were able to maintain our profitability at a good level, with an EBITDA margin of 18.4 percent, thanks to cost reduction measures implemented early on.
We succeeded in further improving key balance sheet and financial ratios. The Group increased its equity ratio to around 60 percent, and free cash flow before interest and taxes rose by approximately 50 million euros.
The Executive Board and Supervisory Board will propose a dividend  payout of 0.40 euros per share to the Annual General Meeting.
The Group’s organizational structure has been realigned more closely with our growth areas of semiconductors, medical technology, metrology, and smart mobility.
With the opening of the new fab  for innovative micro-optics in Dresden, Germany, an important foundation was laid to realize further growth potential in this area.
Our approach to sustainability : As an “enabler,” we use our expertise and innovative products to make an important contribution to overcome social and climate challenges, enable customers worldwide to contribute more efficiently and sustainably to conserving resources and protecting the climate.
Outlook : We expect to return to a growth path in fiscal year 2026.

title: Monsanto unanimously wins first Roundup™ trial since U.S. Supreme Court decision
query: https://www.bayer.com/media/en-us/
content_text:
Monsanto unanimously wins first Roundup™ trial since U.S. Supreme Court decision
Summary
Missouri verdict demonstrates that plaintiffs could not prove their claims following the U.S. Supreme Court’s landmark decision in Durnell 
St. Louis, October 29, 2026 – A Missouri Circuit Court jury today reached a unanimous defense verdict in favor of Monsanto in the three-plaintiff case of Theresa Aretino, et al. v. Monsanto Company , the first Roundup™ trial to take place since the U.S. Supreme Court’s landmark ruling in Monsanto v. Durnell . The jury found for Monsanto on the design defect, fraud and negligence claims that each of the three plaintiffs pursued at trial following the Supreme Court’s favorable decision in Durnell, which preempted their failure-to-warn claims. 
“We are pleased with the jury’s favorable verdict for Monsanto validating our belief that there is no evidence to prove design defect, fraud or negligence claims in the Roundup™ litigation,” said Bill Dodero, U.S. General Counsel and Global Head of Litigation. “This verdict should send a strong signal that plaintiffs who wish to pursue claims in the court system following the Durnell ruling will face significant challenges both in demonstrating they have viable claims and putting forth the necessary evidence to prove them in court.” 
The first trial following Durnell 
In June 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court issued a landmark ruling in the Durnell Roundup™ case, affirming that the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) expressly preempts state law claims based on failure-to-warn theories when the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has made a definitive determination on product safety. These claims have been a central theory in the Roundup™ litigation to date. With failure-to-warn claims no longer available, the Aretino plaintiffs pursued design defect and negligence claims. The verdict marks the first time a court has tested the sufficiency of evidence to support design defect and negligence claims at trial in the post- Durnell landscape. 
Glyphosate’s safety 
Glyphosate remains one of the most studied agricultural tools in history. The overwhelming weight of scientific evidence and the consensus of regulatory bodies and their scientific assessments worldwide support the safety of glyphosate-based herbicides when used as directed. The U.S. EPA has repeatedly and unequivocally determined that glyphosate is not likely to be carcinogenic and has consistently approved Roundup™ labels that contain no cancer warnings. 
The company will continue to back the safety of its glyphosate-based herbicides – critical tools that farmers rely on to produce affordable food and feed the world – and will vigorously defend its products in any remaining litigation.

title: Arkema’s product carbon footprint calculation methodology certification by TÜV RHEINLAND is renewed and extended
query: https://www.arkema.com/global/en/media/newsroom/
content_text:
Arkema’s product carbon footprint calculation methodology certification by TÜV RHEINLAND is renewed and extended
Download the PDF 
Arkema is proud to announce that the certification according to the ISO 14067:2018 standard of its product carbon footprint (PCF) calculation methodology has been renewed and extended to Together for Sustainability - Guideline version 3.0 - December 2024 by TÜV Rheinland.
The TÜV Rheinland certification confirms that the PCF methodology used for calculating individual PCF shared with customers is robust and in accordance with the ISO 14067:2018 standard and now with Together for Sustainability - The Product Carbon Footprint Guideline for the Chemical Industry, version 3.0 - December 2024.
The calculation scope is “cradle to gate”. The calculation is notably based on Arkema’s internal site-specific data, primary raw material data received from suppliers as well as external secondary databases. Both manual and automated calculations accessible through ARKEMA proprietary digital tool are covered. The extension of the certification to the compliance to TfS guidelines ensures full alignment of Arkema with its peers within the chemical and material science sectors. It also strengthens Arkema’s commitments towards full transparency regarding its carbon footprint assessment methodologies .
About TÜV Rheinland: 
150 years of making the world a safer place: TÜV Rheinland is one of the world’s leading providers of testing and inspection services. Its highly qualified experts test technical systems and products, enable innovation, and assist companies in their transition toward greater sustainability. They train professionals across numerous fields and certify management systems to international standards. In doing so, TÜV Rheinland contributes to a safer and better future for everyone. Since 2006, TÜV Rheinland has been a signatory to the UN Global Compact, which promotes sustainability and combats corruption.

title: Arkema showcases its innovative materials for higher-performance, more sustainable sport at ISPO 2026
query: https://www.arkema.com/global/en/media/newsroom/
content_text:
Arkema showcases its innovative materials for higher-performance , more sustainable sport at ISPO 2026
Download the PDF 
On 4 and 5 November in Amsterdam, Arkema will present its latest innovations in high-performance materials for sports equipment, footwear, technical textiles and accessories. The Group will highlight its Pebax ® EVA+ range for midsole foams, as well as its partnership with Movmenta in connected footwear.
As partner to the world’s leading sports brands for several decades, Arkema develops specialty materials renowned for their lightness, energy return, durability and performance. At the show, the Group will demonstrate how these materials help reconcile two key industry requirements: enhancing performance and accelerating the transition to more circular solutions.
Pebax ® EVA+: a new generation of foams for sports footwear
The Pebax ® EVA+ range , a new generation of compounds, is designed for midsole foams in running, trail, hiking and safety footwear. These grades are compatible with conventional EVA processes. They enhance foam performance while allowing manufacturers to keep their existing equipment. The Pebax ® EVA+ range thus offers a balance between performance, ease of processing and cost competitiveness.
Meet us at Booth 6B12
Towards connected running shoes with Movmenta 
Arkema will also present its partnership with Movmenta , which created SOLLO, an ultra-lightweight, battery-free smart sensor integrated into running shoes. This innovative solution gives athletes access to real-time performance data by tracking foam wear over time.
A comprehensive portfolio for the sports industry
Visitors will be able to discover the Group’s materials for sports applications:
Pebax ® elastomers , the benchmark for lightness and energy return
Rilsan ® PA11 , a high-performance bio-based polyamide with a low carbon footprint* for sports equipment and technical textiles
Rilsan ® Clear transparent polyamides , for optical and protective equipment
Platamid ® adhesive solutions , for footwear and technical textile assembly
Arkema will also present its circular economy initiatives under its Virtucycle ® program , dedicated to the recycling of high-performance materials.
*Compared with an equivalent fossil-based long-chain polyamide, based on the IPCC 2021 GWP100 cradle-to-gate indicator (including biogenic CO₂ uptake), in accordance with ISO 14067.

Sport and leisure

At the Board of Directors meeting held on October 30, 2026, Tokyo Electron Limited (TEL) resolved to establish a
facility for the repurchase of its own shares under the provisions of its Articles of Incorporation pursuant to
paragraph 1, Article 459 of the Companies Act, as follows.
1. Reason for Establishing Share Repurchase Facility
TEL intends to establish a share repurchase facility to enable flexible repurchases of its own shares in accordance
with its capital policy, taking into account its current cash position as well as growth investment capital aimed at
medium- to long-term profit growth.
2. Details of the Share Repurchase Facility
1) Type of shares to be repurchased: Shares of common stock
2) Total number of shares to be repurchased: Up to 25 million shares
(Equivalent to 1.1% of outstanding shares excluding treasury stock)
3) Total purchase amount for share repurchase: Up to 150 billion yen
4) Period of repurchase: From November 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027
5) Method of repurchase (planned): Market purchase through the Tokyo Stock Exchange based on
a discretionary trading contract
(Note) Depending on market conditions and other factors, it is possible that no share repurchase, or a share repurchase of only a portion
of the above, will be carried out.
(Reference) Status of treasury stock as of September 30, 2026
Number of outstanding shares (Excluding treasury stock): 2,269,837,310 shares
Number of treasury shares : 70,326,355 shares
*TEL implemented a 5-for-1 common stock split on October 1, 2026. The above share numbers are presented on the assumption that
the stock split had been implemented on September 30, 2026.
Treasury stock excludes the Company shares owned by the executive compensation Board Incentive Plan (BIP) trust account and the
share-delivering Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) trust account.

content_text:
MilliporeSigma Opens €300 Million Asia-Pacific Bioprocessing Center in Daejeon 
MilliporeSigma opened a €300 million Daejeon center, expanding regional capacity and access to critical bioprocessing materials. 
Subscribe
Share 
Icons revealed to the left 
29 Oct 2026 
| 
Burlington, Massachusetts, United States of America 
The company’s largest life science investment in Asia-Pacific to date expands regional manufacturing capacity 
Integrated digital systems support automated data capture and end-to-end batch traceability 
Advances the company’s in-region-for-region strategy, bringing critical products closer to customers across Asia-Pacific 
State-of-the-art facility designed to eliminate on-site fossil-fuel use and improve energy and water efficiency 
MilliporeSigma, the U.S. and Canada Life Science business of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, today announced the opening of a new Asia-Pacific Bioprocessing Production Center in Daejeon, South Korea. The center represents an investment of more than €300 million, the company’s largest Life Science investment in Asia-Pacific to date.
The 44,500-square-meter site expands the company’s regional manufacturing capacity for critical materials and solutions used in the development and production of biologic medicines. It gives biopharmaceutical manufacturers across Asia-Pacific closer access to the materials and solutions needed to develop and produce biologic medicines.
"Reliable access to critical materials is essential at every stage of biologics manufacturing,” said Jean-Charles Wirth, Member of the Executive Board and CEO, Life Science of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. “Daejeon brings advanced production closer to biopharma manufacturers across Asia-Pacific, giving them greater supply confidence, as they move from development to commercial scale. The center adds the regional capacity customers need and delivers the quality and consistency they expect from us.”
From Daejeon, the company will supply bioprocessing products used from early process development through commercial-scale manufacturing. These include cell culture media in dry powder and liquid formats, including pre-GMP small-scale custom products through imMEDIAte ADVANTAGE®, process liquids and ready-to-use cleaning-in-place solutions; and single-use sterile sampling solutions based on the NovaSeptum® Sterile Sampling System. Together, they help customers accelerate development, scale production, maintain controlled manufacturing environments and reduce contamination risk. Cell culture media and process liquids will use animal-component-free raw materials and be manufactured to consistent global quality standards.
“The completion of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany’s Asia-Pacific Bioprocessing Production Center, a world-leading bioscience company, marks a historic turning point in Daejeon’s rise as a global bio hub—not just for Korea, but for the world." said Tae-Jeong Heo, Mayor of Daejeon. “We will provide our full support to ensure that Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany’s foundational technologies at the Daedeok Innopolis and the capabilities of the local community can be brought together seamlessly. We will focus the city’s resources on building a world-class global bio ecosystem through close collaboration among industry, academia, research institutions, and hospitals.”
The center’s integrated digital ecosystem is designed to support automated data capture and end-to-end batch traceability, increasing process transparency and supporting quality management and regulatory compliance.
The facility is designed to eliminate the use of fossil fuels on-site while increasing energy and water efficiency through the use of solar power, a heat-pump system, energy recovery in air handling units, and rainwater reuse.
The Daejeon center is a key part of the company’s in-region-for-region strategy. It builds on recent investments across the company’s global network, including BioReliance® drug product testing in Darmstadt, Germany, and filtration manufacturing in Blarney, Ireland. Across this network, the company is bringing critical products and services closer to customers while applying consistent global quality standards.

Arkema welcomes table tennis player Prithika Pavade to its team of athletes
Arkema is proud to announce the arrival of Prithika Pavade, a rising star in French table tennis, to Team Arkema. Signed with the Group through 2028, she joins a group of elite athletes from diverse backgrounds and disciplines who share Arkema’s values: solidarity, performance, simplicity, accountability, and inclusion.
At 22, Prithika Pavade has already been competing at the highest international level for several years. After representing France at the 2024 Paris Olympic Games, she recently won the bronze medal in women’s singles at the 2026 European Championships, confirming her place among Europe’s top players.
A left-hander, she stands out for her resolutely offensive style of play, based on speed and taking the initiative. This approach has enabled her to reach No. 33 in the world (as of October 2026). She even has her own racket model, developed with the GEWO brand to complement her playing style. She is a member of the Saint-Denis US 93 club. 
Her achievements: 
French Women’s Singles Champion (2022 and 2026)
French Women’s Doubles Champion (2022 and 2023)
French Mixed Doubles Champion (2023 and 2026)
Bronze medalist at the European Team Championships (2023)
Bronze medal at the World Team Championships (2024)
Participated in the Paris Olympic Games (2024)
Bronze medalist at the European Women’s Singles Championships (2026)
A team Arkema with diverse backgrounds
Prithika Pavade joins a group of athletes with whom Arkema renewed its partnerships in November 2025 for three years:
Clara Mateo , international soccer player, Paris FC player, and Arkema employee
Pauline Déroulède , wheelchair tennis player, three-time French champion, and representative of France at the Paris Paralympic Games
Alexis Hanquinquant , a para-triathlete and two-time Paralympic gold medalist in Tokyo and Paris

Hydro breaks ground on new press in Cressona, Pennsylvania
On October 27, Hydro marked the start of construction of a new 5,900 tonne indirect extrusion press line at Cressona, Pennsylvania. The USD 53.5 million investment will modernize production capabilities and strengthen Hydro's North American manufacturing footprint, with operations expected to commence in the first quarter of 2028.
From left to right: Rep. Jamie Barton, Pennsylvania House of Representatives, 124th District; Joseph Yutko, PE, Sr. Director Project Engineering, Hydro; Mike Hammer, VP & General Manager, Central Region, Hydro; Jeff Lehman, BUP President, Extrusion North America, Hydro; Michael Shay, District Director, Congressman Dan Meuser's Office; Rep. Tim Twardzik, Pennsylvania House of Representatives, 123rd District; Larry Padora, Schuylkill County Board of Commissioners; Jason Reilly, Vice President, Distribution & Regional Sales, Hydro (Photo: Art Clagett/Simone Associates) 
This indirect extrusion press investment marks the latest step in Hydro’s strategic modernization efforts in North America. The investment will replace equipment from the 1950’s, bringing with it Industry 4.0 technology, advanced automation, increased energy efficiency and best in class safety performance.
“We are extremely proud of this new equipment and the additional capabilities it brings to Hydro Cressona . This project will improve efficiency, enhance product quality and expand our indirect extrusion capacity to serve the growing needs of our key customers,” says Mike Hammer, Vice President & General Manager of Hydro Extrusion North America’s Industrial and Distribution Region.
Demand for indirect extrusions continues to grow in the commercial transportation , automotive , and electrical markets , where customers increasingly require high performance profiles with consistent dimensions, superior grain structure, and consistent mechanical properties. With this expanded indirect extrusion capacity, Hydro is well positioned to capitalize on these trends.
Investing in American competitiveness
Hydro has a robust presence in the United States, with nearly 6,000 employees and 19 production sites across 14 states. With plans to invest more than USD 800 million over the next five years, the company has raised concerns about the impact of U.S. tariff policy on the competitiveness of domestic manufacturing. Extrusion presses and other specialized equipment produced only in Europe are currently subject to elevated and frequently changing tariffs that increase costs and drive uncertainty. 
"This investment is about much more than a new piece of equipment. It is about Cressona, our employees, our customers and the future of manufacturing in North America. Cressona continues to serve as the keystone of our North American operations, and we’ve invested more than USD 150 million in the site over the past three years. We remain fiercely committed to investing in our U.S. operations, but the aluminium industry needs more nuanced trade policies that do not increase the cost of capital equipment and hinder industrial growth,” says Jeff Lehman, Business Unit President, Extrusion North America.
Hydro's Extrusion plant in Cressona, Pennsylvania, USA is one of the largest facilities of its kind in the world. (Photo: Hydro) 
About Hydro Cressona
Hydro’s facility in Cressona, Pennsylvania , was originally built in 1942 by the U.S. government and is the largest aluminium extrusion site in the western hemisphere, with~15.8 hectares (148,000 square meters) under roof. The site has more than 1,200 employees, nine extrusion presses, three extrusion ingot casting units, extensive fabrication capabilities and a distribution warehouse.
What is an indirect extrusion press?
Aluminium extrusion shapes heated aluminium by forcing it through a die to create a specific profile. In conventional direct extrusion, the aluminium billet moves toward a stationary die. In indirect extrusion, the die instead moves into the billet, reducing friction between the billet and the container.
The process can provide more consistent dimensions, grain structure, and mechanical properties, making it well suited to demanding applications where consistency and product performance are important. At Hydro Cressona, demand for indirect extrusions is growing in markets including commercial transportation, automotive and electrical. Indirect extrusion is a specialized process, while direct extrusion remains the more commonly used method for producing aluminium profiles.

What does Nobel Prize-winning science have to do with Umicore? The connection lies in turning fundamental chemistry into practical applications. The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry recognized research that advances our understanding of how molecules can be created with greater precision.
That journey from fundamental chemistry to practical application is also relevant to Umicore. Within Precious Metals Chemistry , we support customers and research partners working on complex chemical transformations where catalyst performance and selectivity are important considerations.
At the heart of this year’s Nobel Prize: chirality
Some molecules can exist in two forms that are mirror images of each other, much like our left and right hands. This property is known as chirality. Although these forms share the same chemical composition, they can behave differently in biological and chemical systems.
This difference can have important consequences. In pharmaceuticals, for example, one form of a molecule may provide the desired therapeutic effect, while its mirror image may be less active or even cause unwanted side effects. Understanding and controlling chirality has therefore become an important aspect of modern chemistry.
What role do catalysts play?
A catalyst helps a chemical reaction take place without being consumed in the process. It can also help steer the reaction towards the product chemists want to make.
Asymmetric catalysis enables chemists to selectively produce desired molecular structures and has expanded the possibilities for designing increasingly complex molecules.
The research recognized by this year’s Nobel Prize advanced scientific understanding of asymmetric synthesis and contributed to the development of catalytic approaches that are now widely used in pharmaceutical, fine chemical and specialty chemical applications.
This is also where the connection with Umicore Precious Metals Chemistry becomes tangible. Pharmaceuticals are one of the sectors served by the business, which provides specialized catalysts and reagents used in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs).
From scientific discovery to industrial application
Turning scientific advances into practical applications requires deep expertise across chemistry and materials technology. At Umicore, we bring together capabilities in catalysis, materials science and process technologies to translate that knowledge into solutions for complex industrial applications. That ability to connect science with technology and industrial know-how is how innovation can ultimately deliver value for industry and society.

What does Nobel Prize-winning science have to do with Umicore? The connection lies in turning fundamental chemistry into practical applications. The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry recognized research that advances our understanding of how molecules can be created with greater precision.
That journey from fundamental chemistry to practical application is also relevant to Umicore. Within Precious Metals Chemistry , we support customers and research partners working on complex chemical transformations where catalyst performance and selectivity are important considerations.
At the heart of this year’s Nobel Prize: chirality
Some molecules can exist in two forms that are mirror images of each other, much like our left and right hands. This property is known as chirality. Although these forms share the same chemical composition, they can behave differently in biological and chemical systems.
This difference can have important consequences. In pharmaceuticals, for example, one form of a molecule may provide the desired therapeutic effect, while its mirror image may be less active or even cause unwanted side effects. Understanding and controlling chirality has therefore become an important aspect of modern chemistry.
What role do catalysts play?
A catalyst helps a chemical reaction take place without being consumed in the process. It can also help steer the reaction towards the product chemists want to make.
Asymmetric catalysis enables chemists to selectively produce desired molecular structures and has expanded the possibilities for designing increasingly complex molecules.
The research recognized by this year’s Nobel Prize advanced scientific understanding of asymmetric synthesis and contributed to the development of catalytic approaches that are now widely used in pharmaceutical, fine chemical and specialty chemical applications.
This is also where the connection with Umicore Precious Metals Chemistry becomes tangible. Pharmaceuticals are one of the sectors served by the business, which provides specialized catalysts and reagents used in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs).
From scientific discovery to industrial application
Turning scientific advances into practical applications requires deep expertise across chemistry and materials technology. At Umicore, we bring together capabilities in catalysis, materials science and process technologies to translate that knowledge into solutions for complex industrial applications. That ability to connect science with technology and industrial know-how is how innovation can ultimately deliver value for industry and society.

Scientific breakthroughs in asymmetric catalysis continue to support innovation in areas ranging from healthcare and agriculture to advanced materials and specialty ingredients.
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry is a reminder of the lasting value of fundamental scientific research and of the impact it can have when scientific discovery finds its way into practical applications.

Text in:
Umicore today inaugurated Zilverbos and the connecting road next to its site in Hoboken, together with Cathy Berx, Governor of the Province of Antwerp, Koen Kennis, Alderman for Mobility of the City of Antwerp, the Hoboken district, the Municipality of Hemiksem and other partners. 
Both projects bring an important change to the historically evolved interface between industrial activities and the surrounding residential area. Zilverbos is the green zone that creates greater distance between the industrial site and the Moretusburg residential neighbourhood. The connecting road between Moretusburg and Hemiksem provides a safer and clearer separation between public traffic and the industrial activities on the site.
Both projects are the result of years of preparation and collaboration with the City of Antwerp, the Hoboken district and other partners. Since 2020, Umicore has invested approximately €125 million in the two projects combined.
“With Zilverbos and the connecting road, historically evolved situations around the site have been structurally addressed. Umicore in Hoboken has played an important industrial role for generations, and with that comes our responsibility for the environment in which we operate. We know that these projects have significantly changed the neighbourhood in recent years. We are grateful to residents for their patience and involvement throughout this process,” said Johan Ramharter, Site Director Umicore Hoboken.
Where residential areas, public traffic and industrial activities were located very close to one another for many years, both projects create greater distance and a clearer separation between the site and its surroundings. They form part of Umicore’s broader efforts to further reduce the impact of its activities on the surrounding environment, in cooperation with public authorities and local partners.
Johan Ramharter
Green zone named Zilverbos
During the inauguration, the name of the green zone was announced: Zilverbos. The name has been placed on the new insect hotel at the north-eastern corner of the site. Zilverbos comprises around 11,000 native trees and shrubs across five hectares and will gradually develop further into a wooded area in Moretusburg. The area is not open to the public and has no recreational function.
Zilverbos creates a structural spatial separation between residential areas and industry. The Umicore site dates back to 1887. As industrial and residential development continued, the site and residential area gradually came closer together over time. In Curiestraat, for example, homes were still being built in 1958 just a few metres from the industrial site.
The zone forms part of Umicore’s environmental improvement projects in Hoboken aimed at further reducing exposure to lead and other metals. The twice-yearly blood lead measurements were among the factors underpinning the development of the green zone.
To create the zone, from 2020 onwards Umicore offered residents in the area closest to the site the opportunity to sell their homes voluntarily. In total, 186 homes were acquired. Four homes were retained and integrated into the new surroundings.
“Residential areas and industry both fulfil an important role in our society. The challenge is to enable them to coexist in a responsible way. The green zone, now Zilverbos, contributes to this by literally creating more distance between residential areas and industry. In this way, it gives concrete shape to a future-oriented and balanced development of the area,” said Cathy Berx, Governor of the Province of Antwerp.
The name Zilverbos emerged from proposals by local residents, employees of the Umicore site in Hoboken and the Heemkundige Kring Hoboken. The name refers to “de Zilver”, as the plant and its predecessors have been known locally for generations, thereby linking the industrial history of the location with its new green setting.
New connecting road makes traffic safer and clearer
Together with Zilverbos, the approximately two-kilometre-long connecting road between Moretusburg and Hemiksem was inaugurated. The connecting road is expected to open to traffic on 16 November 2026. Umicore made 3.7 hectares of its own land available for the project.
The connecting road provides a structural solution to a historically evolved situation. Part of Adolf Greinerstraat still runs through the site, where public traffic, cyclists and pedestrians share the route with industrial traffic. After the connecting road opens, this section will be closed as a public road and incorporated into the Umicore site. The new road, with a four-metre-wide segregated two-way cycle path alongside it, directs public traffic along the site and thus provides a clear and safe separation of traffic flows. Both have been integrated into the surroundings, with landscaping and facilities for the collection and infiltration of rainwater.
Umicore developed and financed the connecting road in cooperation with the City of Antwerp and the Hoboken district. The City and the district oversee, among other things, alignment with urban policy, the quality of the execution and safety for the different road users.
“With this connecting road, we are making traffic flows around the industrial area safer and clearer. Cyclists will have a separate and comfortable connection, while public and industrial traffic will no longer get in each other’s way. This project shows what targeted cooperation between a company, the City and the district can concretely deliver for mobility, accessibility and quality of life,” said Koen Kennis, Alderman for Mobility of the City of Antwerp.
The Umicore site in Hoboken recycles hundreds of thousands of tonnes of complex recyclable materials each year and recovers 17 different valuable metals from them, including critical metals that are essential to European industry. Gold, silver, platinum, palladium and rhodium, among others, find their way back into applications that are part of our daily lives and our economy after recycling, from electronics to mobility and advanced technologies. By recovering these metals and bringing them back into circulation, Umicore contributes to a more circular and resilient supply of raw materials in Europe.

title: Asundexian first Factor XIa inhibitor approved in China for stroke risk reduction after priority review

content_text:
Asundexian first Factor XIa inhibitor approved in China for stroke risk reduction after priority review
Not intended for U.S. and UK Media
Summary
With this approval, asundexian will become the first Factor XIa inhibitor (FXIa) available in China, to reduce the risk of stroke in adults after a non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack / Regulatory approval follows the China’s Center of Drug Evaluation’s Priority Review designation and is based on positive data from the pivotal, global Phase III OCEANIC-STROKE study / Stroke is the leading cause of death and disability in China

Pharmaceutical Tablet Production at Bayer
2026-0184-2
Pharmaceutical Tablet Production at Bayer

Berlin, October 26, 2026 – Bayer announced today that China’s National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) has granted marketing authorization for asundexian, under the brand name Sunharbo ® . Asundexian, 50 mg, a selective, once-daily oral Factor XIa inhibitor (FXIa), is indicated to reduce the risk of stroke in adults after a non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA). Sunharbo ® (asundexian) is the first FXIa inhibitor approved worldwide. 
In China, stroke is the leading cause of death and disability. Between 2010 and 2021, the prevalence of ischemic stroke increased by 10% to more than 20 million ischemic stroke cases in China. Globally, approximately 1 in 10 non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke survivors experience another stroke within one year, even with available secondary stroke prevention strategies. 
“With the approval of asundexian, we have reached an important milestone and are proud soon to be able to offer physicians in China a new treatment option for stroke survivors after a non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or high‑risk transient ischemic attack. This enables us to address an unmet need with limited therapeutic advances over the past two decades," said Christian Rommel, Ph.D., Global Head of Research and Development at Bayer`s Pharmaceuticals Division. "We are working with stakeholders and medical communities to support equitable and timely access for eligible patients in China." 
Asundexian has been submitted for marketing authorization in additional markets around the world. These applications are currently under review, while Bayer continues to work with health authorities worldwide to bring asundexian to patients in other regions. 
Key Clinical Trial Findings Supporting Approval 
The approval by China’s National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) is based on positive data from the pivotal, global Phase III OCEANIC-STROKE study, the first successfully completed Phase III study of a Factor XIa inhibitor in combination with dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) / single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) demonstrating superiority in reducing ischemic stroke, compared to DAPT/SAPT alone. The incidence of all bleeding events was similar between the two treatment groups, in patients after a non-cardioembolic stroke or high-risk TIA. Key findings demonstrated: 
Asundexian 50 mg in combination with DAPT/SAPT, significantly reduced ischemic stroke by 26% in patients after a non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA), compared to DAPT/SAPT alone. 
The incidence of all bleeding events was similar between the two treatment groups. 
Treatment effect for the primary endpoint was consistent across key subgroups (including age, sex, type of index event, non-cardioembolic stroke subtypes, stroke severity, and planned antiplatelet therapy) supporting its potential use across a broad patient population. 
The full results from OCEANIC-STROKE have been published in The New England Journal of Medicine 
About OCEANIC-STROKE 
The Phase III OCEANIC-STROKE study investigated the efficacy and safety of the selective, once-daily oral Factor XIa inhibitor asundexian 50 mg in combination with DAPT/SAPT, compared to DAPT/SAPT alone, for risk reduction of ischemic stroke in patients after a non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA). OCEANIC-STROKE is a multicenter, international, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, parallel group and event-driven study, that randomized 12,327 participants worldwide. The primary efficacy endpoint was time to ischemic stroke; the primary safety endpoint was ISTH (International Society on Thrombosis and Hemostasis) major bleeding. 
About FXIa Inhibitors and Asundexian 
Factor XIa (FXIa) is a protein in the blood coagulation pathway with different roles in hemostasis and thrombosis. FXIa is thought to contribute to the formation of pathological thrombus growth and vessel blockage. However, FXIa has a minor role in the formation of a hemostatic plug that seals the leak at the site of vessel injury. 
Asundexian is the first approved FXIa inhibitor worldwide. It selectively inhibits FXIa, allowing to reduce pathological clot formation, with similar incidence of all bleeding events between the two treatment groups, by uncoupling hemostasis from pathological thrombosis. 
About Bayer’s Commitment in Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Medicine 
Bayer is a leader in cardiology and is advancing a portfolio of innovative treatments in cardiovascular (CV) and cerebrovascular diseases of high unmet medical need. The company has set a clear focus on developing therapies to treat such diseases (e.g. stroke, heart failure, cardiomyopathies, and chronic kidney disease) and it is our ambition to take a leading role in the care of patients with these diseases. Bayer is actively shaping the future of cardiology and neurology with a robust and diversified pipeline, strategically positioned to address critical unmet needs and drive significant long-term value. Bayer’s portfolio already includes several innovative products and compounds in various stages of preclinical and clinical development. 
About Bayer 
Bayer is a global enterprise with core competencies in the life science fields of health care and nutrition. In line with its mission, “Health for all, Hunger for none,” the company’s products and services are designed to support efforts to master major challenges presented by a growing and aging global population and create value through innovation and growth. The Bayer brand stands for trust, reliability and quality throughout the world. In fiscal 2025, the Group employed around 88,000 people and had sales of 45.6 billion euros. title: Two-Year Data of Pimicotinib Demonstrated Durable Tumor Control and Sustained ...

content_text:
Two-Year Data of Pimicotinib Demonstrated Durable Tumor Control and Sustained Improvement in TGCT Symptoms and Joint Function 
The company announced today new two-year follow up results from the Phase 3 MANEUVER study evaluating pimicotinib in patients with TGCT. 
Share 
Icons revealed to the left 
26 Oct 2026 
| 
Darmstadt, Germany 
Improvements in symptoms of pain, stiffness, and range of motion were sustained through two years 
Tumor responses remained robust 1 and durable 2 
Not intended for UK-based media 
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, a leading science and technology company, today announced new two-year follow up results from the Phase 3 MANEUVER study evaluating pimicotinib in patients with tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT). The study showed that among patients initially randomized to pimicotinib, improvements in symptoms and joint function were observed as early as Week 5, sustained through two years, and continued to improve over time. Tumor responses remained robust 1 and durable, 2 and the safety profile was consistent with previous analyses. The findings are being presented today in the Sarcoma poster session at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 (Presentation # 3747P). 
"For people living with TGCT, the impact of the disease is often felt through persistent limitations in mobility, physical function and the ability to carry out everyday activities," said Vinod Ravi, MD, MS, MBA, Department of Sarcoma Medical Oncology, Division of Cancer Medicine, UT MD Anderson, an investigator on the MANEUVER trial. "What is encouraging about these two-year findings is the consistency of improvements, not only in the durability of tumor response, but across the symptoms and functional outcomes that matter to patients. Together with the observed safety profile, these results provide important insight into the potential for pimicotinib to deliver meaningful benefit over time."
The new analysis in patients initially randomized to pimicotinib found that at Week 97, mean changes from baseline were 19.6% in range of motion, -3.9 in stiffness (as measured by the Worst Stiffness Numeric Scale Rating), -3.1 in pain (as measured by the Brief Pain Inventory worst pain rating) and +7.4 in physical function (as measured by the patient-reported PROMIS-PF scale).
Tumor responses also remained robust 1 and durable 2 through two years. Objective Response Rate (ORR) by blinded independent review committee (BICR) per RECIST v1.1 was 76.2% (95% CI: 63.8, 86.0), remaining unchanged from the one-year analysis, while ORR per BIRC based on tumor volume score (TVS) increased from 74.6% at one year to 77.8% (95% CI: 65.5, 87.3) at two years. Median duration of response was not reached at the time of analysis, and median treatment duration was 22.6 months (range: 1.8-33.6 months) at the March 1, 2026 data cutoff. Fifty-four percent of patients initially randomized to pimicotinib remained on treatment at two years.
In MANEUVER, pimicotinib was well-tolerated, with no evidence of cholestatic hepatotoxicity or hair/skin hypopigmentation. During the randomized, double-blind treatment phase of the trial, treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) leading to treatment discontinuation occurred in one patient (1.6%) treated with pimicotinib; TEAEs leading to dose reduction occurred in 7.9% (n=5) of pimicotinib-treated patients.
"These two-year findings add to the growing body of evidence from the MANEUVER study demonstrating the potential for pimicotinib to meaningfully address some of the burden of TGCT," said David Weinreich, MD, MBA, Global Head of R&D and Chief Medical Officer for the Healthcare business of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. “The sustained improvements observed across symptoms, physical function and tumor control reinforce the potential of pimicotinib to address aspects of TGCT that can affect patients every day. These results add to our evolving understanding of the long-term benefit that pimicotinib may provide for people living with this debilitating rare tumor."
TGCT is a rare, locally aggressive tumor occurring in or around the joints leading to progressive worsening of symptoms including pain and reduced mobility of the affected joint, significantly impacting physical function in what is typically an otherwise healthy and young adult population. Patient-reported experiences indicate that up to half of people with TGCT may initially receive an incorrect diagnosis, which can delay appropriate disease management. 3 If left untreated or in recurrent cases, TGCT may result in cumulative morbidity and irreversible damage to the bone, joint and surrounding tissues.
Pimicotinib was approved in China by the China National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) in December 2025 and in Canada by Health Canada in June 2026 for the treatment of adult patients with symptomatic TGCT. A regulatory application is currently under review by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and other regulatory agencies.
1 54% ORR as assessed by BIRC based on RECIST v1.1 at week 25 vs. 3% with placebo; p 2 The majority (77%) of patients with response at 25 weeks maintained this clinical benefit after an additional 12 months of treatment.
3 Stern S, et al. Localized and diffuse tenosynovial giant cell tumor: real-world results from a patient observational registry. Future Oncol . 2025;21(12):1501-1510.

About MANEUVER 
The pivotal, global Phase 3 MANEUVER study is a three-part, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to assess the efficacy and safety of pimicotinib in patients with TGCT who were eligible for systemic therapy and have not received prior anti-CSF-1/CSF-1R therapy.
The ongoing study is being conducted by Abbisko Therapeutics and enrolled patients globally in U.S., Canada and Europe (n=49) and China (n=45).
In the double-blind Part 1, 94 patients were randomized 2:1 to receive either 50 mg QD of pimicotinib (n=63) or placebo (n=31) for 24 weeks. In addition to the primary endpoint of ORR at week 25, as measured by RECIST v1.1 by BICR, secondary endpoints include tumor volume score (TVS), relative range of motion, stiffness by Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), pain by Brief Pain Inventory (BPI), and physical function measured by Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS-PF).
After the double-blind Part 1, all eligible patients from either arm could continue to the open-label Part 2 and receive up to 24 weeks of pimicotinib treatment. Patients who completed Part 2 could then enter the open-label extension phase (Part 3) for extended treatment and safety follow-up.
About Pimicotinib (ABSK021) 
Pimicotinib, developed by Abbisko Therapeutics, is a novel, orally administered, selective and potent small-molecule inhibitor of CSF-1R. Pimicotinib has been approved for the treatment of adult patients with symptomatic TGCT for which surgical resection will potentially cause functional limitation or relatively severe morbidity by China National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) and Health Canada. It has been granted breakthrough therapy designation (BTD) for the treatment of inoperable TGCT by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and priority medicine (PRIME) designation from the European Medicines Agency (EMA). title: Darolutamide plus ADT and radiation therapy reduces risk of metastasis or death by 58% in prostate cancer patients at high risk of recurrence
query: https://www.bayer.com/media/en-us/
content_text:
Darolutamide plus ADT and radiation therapy reduces risk of metastasis or death by 58% in prostate cancer patients at high risk of recurrence
Not intended for U.S. and UK Media
Summary
Interim analysis results from the Phase III trial DASL-HiCaP show a 58% reduction in the risk of metastasis or death in the combined primary endpoint of metastasis-free survival (MFS-CI) with darolutamide versus placebo, in addition to androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and radiation therapy / Four-year metastasis-free survival rate in trial reached 95% with darolutamide compared to 88% with placebo, alongside secondary endpoint improvements and a safety profile consistent with previous studies / Results will be presented as a late-breaking abstract in a Presidential Symposium at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026
Berlin, October 24, 2026 – New late-breaking data to be presented today at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 will show that adding Bayer’s androgen receptor inhibitor (ARi), darolutamide, to standard-of-care androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and locoregional radiation therapy (RT), significantly improves metastasis-free survival based on conventional imaging (MFS-CI) in prostate cancer patients with high risk of recurrence compared to placebo. Darolutamide is currently not approved for this treatment setting. These data will be presented at Presidential Symposium I at the ESMO Congress 2026 (LBA4, Saturday 24 October, 16:30 CET). 
At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the interim analysis demonstrated a 58% reduction in the risk of metastasis or death with darolutamide plus ADT and RT compared with placebo plus ADT and RT (hazard ratio [HR] 0.42; 95% CI: 0.27–0.66; p=0.0001). The 4-year metastasis-free survival rate was 95% for patients receiving darolutamide compared with 88% for those receiving placebo. 
“Prostate cancer patients at a high risk of relapse face a considerable risk of recurrence and metastatic spread, making early, highly effective intervention vital,” said Dr. Tamim Niazi, Associate Professor of Oncology at McGill University, Radiation Oncologist at the Jewish General Hospital in Montreal, Canada. and Co-Lead Investigator of the study. “The clear improvement in metastasis-free survival seen in interim results from the DASL-HiCaP trial highlights the potential of adding darolutamide to standard androgen deprivation therapy and radiation therapy to help prevent or delay disease progression in patients who are at high risk of progression despite receiving primary curative therapy.” 
Secondary endpoints also showed consistent positive trends with darolutamide, with a 53% reduction in the risk of prostate-specific antigen progression free survival (PSA-PFS; HR 0.47; 95% CI: 0.33–0.67), and a 4-year PSA-PFS rate of 91% versus 83% with placebo. Prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS) and overall survival (OS) hazard ratios were 0.58 (95% CI: 0.17–1.97; 99% vs 99% at 4 years) and 0.88 (95% CI: 0.49–1.59; 97% vs 95% at 4 years), respectively, with follow-up ongoing. 
The safety profile of darolutamide was consistent with its known tolerability, with adverse events being similar to the placebo group. Proportions of patients experiencing Grade ≥2 adverse events of special interest for darolutamide versus placebo were: fatigue/asthenia (14% vs 10%), hypertension (7% vs 9%), fractures (2% vs 3%), and cardiac events (3% vs 3%). Any Grade ≥3 adverse event occurred in 43% of patients in the darolutamide group versus 36% in the placebo group. 
"These new data highlight the potential of darolutamide to make a meaningful difference for patients earlier in the course of their prostate cancer,” said Christine Roth, Executive Vice President, Global Product Strategy and Commercialization at Bayer’s Pharmaceuticals Division. “By advancing darolutamide into earlier disease settings, we aim to reach more patients across the prostate cancer care continuum. We are proud to support ANZUP, the Sydney Clinical Trials Centre, CCTG and international partners in research as we work together with the potential to improve outcomes for men living with prostate cancer.” 
Follow-up of participants is continuing to provide further information on longer-term outcomes, including overall survival. 
About the DASL-HiCaP trial (ANZUP1801) 
The DASL-HiCaP trial is an investigator-initiated, randomized, placebo-controlled, Phase III trial (NCT04136353) evaluating darolutamide added to standard-of-care ADT and locoregional radiation therapy in prostate cancer patients at high risk of recurrence. 
DASL-HiCaP was conducted in collaboration with the University of Sydney and ANZUP Clinical Trials Group and is the fourth Phase III trial for darolutamide. Following ARAMIS, ARASENS, and ARANOTE, which demonstrated darolutamide’s efficacy and safety in advanced prostate cancer, DASL-HiCaP represents the first Phase III study of darolutamide in early prostate cancer. 
A total of 1,106 participants across Australia, New Zealand, Canada, the United States, Ireland and the United Kingdom were randomized 1:1 to receive darolutamide (600 mg twice daily) or matching placebo for 96 weeks, combined with an LHRH analog for 96 weeks and RT to the prostate/prostate bed and pelvic lymph nodes. 
The primary endpoint was metastasis-free survival based on conventional imaging (MFS-CI). Secondary endpoints included prostate-specific antigen progression free survival (PSA-PFS), prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS), and overall survival (OS). The protocol specified an interim analysis after 87 MFS-CI events; follow-up is ongoing to evaluate long-term overall survival. 
About the Sydney Clinical Trials Centre 
The Sydney Clinical Trials Centre is a flagship research centre of the Faculty of Medicine and Health at the University of Sydney that designs and manages clinical trials. This includes responsibility for study coordination, monitoring, data acquisition and management and statistical analysis. The Sydney Clinical Trials Centre has health economics, biostatistics, systematic reviews and biomarker teams that work with trial data and inform healthcare providers about best practice. For further details, please visit its website at https://www.ctc.usyd.edu.au 
About ANZUP Clinical Trials Group 
ANZUP ( https://www.anzup.org.au ) is the leading cancer-cooperative trials group bringing together all of the professional disciplines and groups involved in researching and treating urogenital cancers to conduct high-quality cancer research. ANZUP’s mission is to improve the lives of people affected by bladder, kidney, testicular, penile, and prostate cancers, towards our vision of living life without fear of cancer. ANZUP identifies gaps in evidence and areas of clinical need, collaborates with the best clinicians and researchers in genitourinary cancer and communicates frequently and effectively with the broader community along the way. ANZUP receives valuable infrastructure support from the Australian Government through Cancer Australia and research funding from Prostate Cancer Foundation of Australia. 
About Prostate Cancer 
Prostate cancer is the second most common cancer and the fourth most common cause of cancer death in men worldwide. Over 1.5 million men are diagnosed with prostate cancer each year and almost 420,000 die from the disease worldwide. By 2040, prostate cancer diagnoses are projected to increase to 2.9 million. 
Standard therapy for prostate cancer patients at high risk of recurrence combines radiation therapy with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT). However, despite this approach, a significant proportion of patients experience treatment failure, local recurrence, or distant metastases. Intensifying therapy early with an advanced androgen receptor inhibitor aims to improve long-term disease control and delay metastatic progression. 
About darolutamide (Nubeqa™) 
Darolutamide is an oral ARi with a distinct chemical structure that binds with high affinity to the androgen receptor and exhibits a strong antagonistic effect against the androgen receptor inhibiting the receptor function and growth of prostate cancer cells. Additionally, preclinical models and neuroimaging data in healthy humans support darolutamide's low potential for blood-brain barrier penetration and low potential for clinically relevant drug-drug interactions. 
Darolutamide, under the brand name Nubeqa™ plus androgen deprivation therapy (ADT), is already approved in more than 85 markets around the world, including the US, EU and China. It is approved for the treatment of adult patients with mHSPC without docetaxel in 75 markets and with docetaxel in more than 85 countries, and for adult patients with nmCRPC at high risk of developing metastatic disease in more than 85 countries. 
Darolutamide is developed jointly by Bayer and Orion Corporation, a globally operating Finnish pharmaceutical company. 
Darolutamide demonstrated efficacy and tolerability in pivotal Phase 3 studies, supporting its indications in nmCRPC and mHSPC with and without chemotherapy, with a favorable safety profile that offers an advancement in treatment management for physicians and patients. 
A robust clinical development program is underway investigating darolutamide across various stages of prostate cancer. Current ongoing trials include the Phase III ARASTEP trial evaluating the efficacy of darolutamide plus ADT compared to ADT alone in hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (HSPC), in patients with high-risk biochemical recurrence (BCR) who have no evidence of metastatic disease by conventional imaging and a positive PSMA PET/CT at baseline. 
About Prostate Cancer at Bayer 
Bayer is committed to delivering science for a better life by advancing a portfolio of innovative treatments. The company has the passion and determination to develop new medicines that help improve and extend the lives of people living with cancer. Prostate cancer is the second most commonly diagnosed cancer in men and a key area of focus for Bayer. The company’s franchise includes two products on the market (Nubeqa™ and Xofigo™) and several compounds in development. Bayer is focused on addressing the unique needs of patients with prostate cancer, providing treatments that extend their lives throughout the different stages of the disease and allowing them to continue with their everyday activities, so that patients can live longer, better lives.

Bayer is a global enterprise with core competencies in the life science fields of health care and nutrition. source: Norsk Hydro - News Subscription / Investor News Subscription
