Eli Lilly LLY reported 39% revenue growth and 7% non-GAAP earnings-per-share growth, including acquisition costs. Management raised 2026 revenue guidance to $91.5 billion at the midpoint (from $86 billion) and trimmed non-GAAP EPS guidance to $35.50 at the midpoint from $36, accounting for acquisitions.
Why it matters: Lilly shares rose 6% intraday on Oct. 29 as investors processed another quarter of remarkably strong revenue and underlying earnings growth.
Obesity drug Zepbound’s rapid uptake as part of the new Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program and deeper demand for obesity drugs in the cash-pay market internationally look like the biggest sources of this outperformance.
The bottom line: We’re maintaining our $980 per share fair value estimate for wide-moat Lilly. While we see momentum around the shares due to strong performance and rotation out of other sectors, we think market prices have risen above Lilly’s fundamental value.
Our near- and long-term revenue projections are well ahead of consensus. We’ve raised our 2026 revenue forecast from $90.4 billion to $92.7 billion, reflecting 42% sales growth this year, but our changes didn’t significantly alter our valuation.
While acquisitions are masking underlying operating leverage in 2026, we expect revenue growth to fall back to earth (18% growth) in 2027, which looks more in line with operating expense growth and less likely to drive operating leverage.
Coming up: International expansion of oral GLP-1 Foundayo should accelerate as it gains approval in more markets (potentially broader European approval this year), and US diabetes approval would also allow Lilly to point to more favorable data relative to Novo’s.
We’re watching 2027 data in oncology (Inluriyo, early-stage breast cancer) and neurology (Kisunla, cognitively unimpaired Alzheimer’s patients diagnosed via blood test) for confidence in Lilly’s long-term growth trajectory outside of diabetes and obesity.

Rio Tinto Opens Two Argentine Lithium Projects Worth US$1.4 Billion
Written by Giann Liguid 
| 
Edited by 
Georgia Williams
Oct. 29, 2026 11:46AM PST
The company plans to invest approximately US$4 billion in growth capital across its Argentine lithium operations and expects to spend around 70 percent of it with local suppliers.
Tigarto / Adobe Stock 
Rio Tinto (ASX:RIO,NYSE:RIO,LSE:RIO) opened two lithium operations in Argentina's Catamarca province on Thursday (October 29), which is touted to add 25,000 metric tons of annual lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) capacity once fully ramped up. 
To date, Rio Tinto has invested roughly US$1.4 billion in the Fénix 1B expansion and the new Sal de Vida operation. Both reached first production ahead of plan in the second quarter and are now ramping up.
Fénix began operating in 1997 as Argentina's first commercial lithium operation. The 1B expansion adds 10,000 metric tons of annual LCE capacity there, which raises the operation's total target to about 40,000 metric tons. Sal de Vida sits roughly 20 kilometers northeast of Fénix and targets 15,000 metric tons a year.
CEO Simon Trott linked the two projects to Rio Tinto's global target of 200,000 metric tons of annual LCE production capacity by 2028.
"Our focus now is on safely ramping up production, delivering reliable, high-quality lithium to our customers, and creating lasting value for our shareholders and Argentina," Trott said.
In Salta, Rio Tinto is building the US$2.5 billion Rincon project, which targets approximately 60,000 metric tons of annual battery-grade lithium carbonate capacity. 
In March, the company secured a US$1.175 billion financing package for Rincon from four lenders. 
Construction at Rincon started in 2025. Rio Tinto expects first production in 2028, followed by a three-year ramp-up to full capacity running across an expected lifespan of 40 years.
Outside Argentina, Rio Tinto took majority control of Nemaska Lithium (TSX:NMX) in Québec in February this year with a 53.9 percent stake and assumed direct management of the company. The Québec government holds the remaining 46.1 percent through Investissement Québec.
Rio Tinto said it plans to invest more than US$300 million in its Québec lithium business this year.

Rio Tinto Opens Two Argentine Lithium Projects Backed by $1.4 Billion
Rio Tinto has launched two lithium ventures in Argentina, underpinned by a total commitment of $1.4 billion, as the mining group accelerates its push into battery metals. The Fénix 1B expansion and the Sal de Vida operation, both located in Catamarca province, commenced first production during the second quarter of 2026, ahead of schedule, and are currently increasing output.
Once running at full capacity, the pair will contribute 25,000 tonnes of yearly lithium carbonate equivalent capacity, according to the company. At an inauguration event attended by President Javier Milei and Catamarca Governor Raúl Jalil, Rio Tinto chief executive Simon Trott said the developments draw on almost thirty years of lithium output in the province and the skills of the firm's Argentine employees. He also referenced the company's worldwide ambition of reaching 200,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent annual capacity by 2028.
Project Details
The $530-million Fénix 1B expansion contributes 10,000 tonnes of yearly capacity, raising the site's overall target to about 40,000 tonnes. Fénix started producing in 1997, becoming Argentina's first commercial lithium operation. Rio Tinto is evaluating a further expansion, with an investment decision anticipated in 2028 or 2029.
Sal de Vida, a new lithium carbonate facility situated roughly 20 km northeast of Fénix, is designed for 15,000 tonnes per year. Its initial phase required an investment of $374 million.
Both operations belong to an integrated production hub in the Salar del Hombre Muerto, whose combined resource base stands at approximately 19 million tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent. Running the sites jointly enables infrastructure sharing, efficiency gains and efforts to lower water use. Fénix employs direct lithium extraction, whereas Sal de Vida uses conventional evaporation ponds.
Counting Fénix, Sal de Vida and Olaroz, Rio Tinto's nominal lithium capacity in Argentina totals roughly 100,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent per year. Its wider Argentine holdings include a 66.5% interest in Olaroz and complete ownership of the Rincón project, which extends across Catamarca, Jujuy and Salta provinces.
Market Context
Argentina is projected to generate around 172,700 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent in 2026, a 48% rise over the prior year and over five times the 2018 figure. Between January and August 2026, lithium exports brought in $1.467 billion, up 190.5% compared with the same period twelve months earlier.
Rio Tinto intends to direct close to 70% of its planned $4 billion in Argentine lithium growth capital toward local suppliers. The spending dovetails with Milei's push to draw foreign investment via market-friendly reforms and the Large Investment Incentive Regime, which grants tax, legal and foreign-exchange advantages for 30 years to eligible projects exceeding $200 million in value.
Benchmark Mineral Intelligence projects worldwide lithium demand climbing from 2 million tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent in 2026 to 7 million tonnes by 2050, chiefly on electric vehicle and energy storage growth. Argentina's Mining Secretariat anticipates the country may surpass Chile in lithium output by 2029 and achieve yearly production of 573,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent by 2035.

Merck outlines 2027 as ‘another year of investment’ despite recent clinical wins
By
Angus Liu 
Oct 29, 2026 11:23am 
Merck 
Earnings 
Keytruda 
sac-TMT 
Merck ramps up R&D and commercial investments to secure its post-Keytruda future. (Photo by Kena Betancur/Getty Images)
Even as a wave of clinical trial wins bolsters its momentum, Merck & Co. is prioritizing ongoing pipeline and commercial expansions over near-term margin growth, hoping to gird its long-term prospects past Keytruda's loss of exclusivity.
For 2027, “we see it as another year of investment, as we invest behind our expansive pipeline and our new product launches to drive long-term growth,” Merck’s CFO Caroline Litchfield said on the company’s third-quarter earnings call Thursday.
Litchfield made the comment in response to a question about whether Merck has seen enough R&D progress recently that the company may start to turn its attention to earnings growth as it looks beyond 2030.
At least for 2027, Merck expects underlying operating expenses to increase at a mid- to high-single-digit rate, “reflecting our conviction in the significant opportunity from our expanding pipeline and the growing portfolio of new product launches,” Litchfield said.
“We will continue to invest in value-creating opportunities that drive both near- and long-term growth,” Litchfield said of Merck’s capital allocation plans. “Business development remains an important priority, and we retain financial flexibility within a strong investment-grade credit rating to pursue additional science-driven, value-enhancing transactions.”
One of the key new clinical programs that Merck plans to invest in next year is advancing its PD-1xVEGF bispecific MK-2010, partnered with China’s SBP Group (formerly Sino Biopharmaceutical), into phase 3.
Following “productive discussions” with the FDA and “the totality of data generated to date,” Merck will initiate phase 3 development for MK-2010, including combinations with Kelun-Biotech-partnered TROP2 antibody-drug conjugate sac-TMT, in first-line non-small cell lung cancer in the first half of 2027, Marjorie Green, Merck’s head of oncology global clinical development, told investors during an Oct. 26 event. This plan was confirmed by Merck’s R&D chief Dean Li, M.D., Ph.D., on Thursday’s call.
The decision comes as sac-TMT, used alongside Keytruda, delivered a 51% progression-free survival benefit against Keytruda-chemo in first-line, PD-L1-negative NSCLC in a China phase 3. In parallel, sac-TMT’s first global phase 3 readout, in endometrial cancer, also showed consistent data with previous China results. 
Beyond sac-TMT, positive phase 3 results from Moderna-partnered mRNA cancer vaccine intismeran autogene and diabetic macular edema candidate remigromig drew some recent investor scrutiny. 
On the mRNA immunotherapy specifically, jacked-up investor expectations have overshadowed the otherwise strong data itself. 
During Thursday’s call, Li called the INTerpath-001 melanoma trial “a landmark study in its own right,” citing a comment from Antoni Ribas, M.D., Ph.D., a leading melanoma clinical researcher from the University of California Los Angeles.
“Because of that, we would hope that upon approval that the NCCN guidelines would potentially define this as a new standard of care,” Li said.
Looking into 2027, Merck expects some top-line pressure, as Litchfield flagged the potential for more “moderate” growth thanks to more than $2 billion of negative impact from generic competition affecting Bridion, the Januvia family and Bayer-partnered Adempas.
Keytruda, while still a major pillar of Merck’s business, will “see growth moderating” as it has reached peak penetration in several indications, she said. Total Keytruda sales, including the subcutaneous Keytruda Qlex, reached $8.6 billion during the third quarter, up 6% year over year.
Merck is locked in a patent fight with Halozyme over Keytruda Qlex. An injunction was recently ordered by a Dutch patent court that affects the subcutaneous drug’s rollout in eight European nations. 
The injunction was put in place until a hearing is held, and it “doesn’t speak to the merits of our belief,” Merck’s CEO Rob Davis noted on the call. “We continue to feel very, very good that we have a position both in the U.S. and in Europe.”
Meanwhile, in the vaccines business, Merck’s HPV vaccine Gardasil enjoyed a rally thanks to “favorable public-sector purchasing patterns and higher net pricing” in the U.S., with 14% year-over-year growth to $2 billion, according to an earnings release.
For vaccines overall, Litchfield said a $250 million buy-in from the CDC this year will unwind in 2027.
On other recent launch progress, pulmonary arterial hypertension med Winrevair nearly doubled sales to $694 million in the third quarter, and kidney cancer drug Welireg grew sales by 56% to $307 million. 
Also in the infectious disease department, sales of Merck’s RSV preventive Enflonsia jumped 138% year over year to $187 million as inventory builds ahead of a new RSV season.
For 2026, Merck narrowed the range of its full-year revenue guidance to between $66.8 billion and $67.3 billion.

Bangladesh regime change: Hasina's ouster was planned days before Aug 5, says Yusuf's aide 
Edited by Rajeev Singh / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Oct 29, 2026, 18:17 IST 
Save Comments
Share 
Aa + Text Size Small
Medium
Large
Print 
After Hanisa's ouster, student protest leaders publicly proposed Yunus as the head of an interim govt. 
A journalist working for French news agency Agence France-Presse (AFP) acted as an intermediary between student leaders in Bangladesh and Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus before Sheikh Hasina was forced from power in August 2024, according to a claim by Yunus's former press secretary Shafiqul Alam. In a Facebook post on October 28, Alam alleged that Qadaruddin Shishir, who was then with AFP's fact-checking team in Dhaka, helped arrange initial discussions between Yunus and student leaders who wanted him to head an interim government after Hasina's departure. Alam's account suggests that discussions about who would lead Bangladesh after Hasina had begun before she fled the country on August 5, 2024. Describing how the contact was established, Alam wrote: "When student leaders wanted to reach out to Nobel Laureate Professor Muhammad Yunus and invite him to head the interim government in a post-Hasina scenario, they needed a trusted bridge-builder. Qadaruddin Shishir stepped up to fulfill that critical role." Alam said Shishir managed the discussions discreetly while working alongside him at the AFP bureau in Dhaka. "At the time, Shishir was the editor of AFP Dhaka Fact Check team. Sitting just a yard away from my desk in the AFP Dhaka bureau, he managed this high-stakes operation in complete secrecy. Only a select few trusted individuals knew what was happening. 
It was Shishir who first approached the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize winner on behalf of the student leaders and facilitated the initial talks between the two parties." According to Alam, the initial contact took place two days before Hasina's departure. He claimed the secrecy was essential because the then prime minister's security apparatus could have discovered the discussions. "Hasina would remain in power for two more days, yet her brutal security machine—notorious for mass killings and abductions—never caught a whisper of it. Had they discovered what was happening, Shishir and our entire AFP team would likely have ended up in an Aynaghar (house of mirrors secret prison)." Shafiqul Alam is Yunus's former press secretary.
Aynaghar is the name associated with a secret detention facility in Bangladesh, where allegations of enforced disappearances and torture have been reported. Alam also said Shishir had been collecting video evidence of violence during the crackdown on protesters. "Throughout it all, Shishir remained remarkably cool and composed, even as he quietly started gathering video evidence of the cold-blooded murders being committed by the regime." Yunus took charge after Hasina fled
The student-led protests began in July 2024 as an agitation against government job quotas before escalating into a wider movement against Hasina's government. She fled Bangladesh on August 5 amid the unrest. On August 6, student protest leaders publicly proposed Yunus as the head of an interim administration. He returned to Dhaka from Paris and took office as chief adviser on August 8. The revelations in Alam's post add details about the contacts that preceded Yunus's appointment. They also raise questions about how student leaders prepared for a possible transition of power before Hasina's departure. However, evidence of discussions about a successor does not, by itself, prove that the protests as a whole were planned or controlled by a single group. Alam's account has not independently established the extent of coordination between the student leadership and other actors. Hasina has since accused the Yunus administration of political persecution and failing to hold those responsible for violence accountable. Yunus's interim administration governed Bangladesh until February 2026, when it handed over power following the election of Tarique Rahman as prime minister.

Wolfspeed and BorgWarner sign multiyear SiC agreement
Thursday 29th October 2026
Long-term supply agreement supports BorgWarner’s next-gen 800V SiC inverter platform 
Wolfspeed has announced a multiyear supply agreement for its SiC devices to support BorgWarner’s next-generation 800V SiC-based inverter platform as strategic partner. BorgWarner is using Wolfspeed’s Gen 5 1200V SiC technology in the inverter. 
The agreement builds on the companies’ longstanding collaboration and is designed to provide BorgWarner with consistent, uninterrupted access to Wolfspeed SiC devices.
“Our strategy is to combine our technology leadership with deep, long-term customer partnerships,” said Matthias Buchner, SVP, global sales and chief marketing officer at Wolfspeed.
“Our supply agreement with BorgWarner demonstrates that strategy, bringing together advanced SiC technology, proven quality and reliability, and scaled 200 mm manufacturing capabilities to deliver the performance and supply confidence BorgWarner needs for their next-generation EV platform.”

MilliporeSigma Announces the Opening of €300 Million Asia-Pacific Bioprocessing Production Center in Daejeon, South Korea
MilliporeSigma 
Thu, October 29, 2026 at 7:00 AM CDT 4 min read 
MRK.DE 
+0.67% 
MilliporeSigma Announces the Opening of €300 Million Asia-Pacific Bioprocessing Production Center in Daejeon, South Korea 
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany's Asia-Pacific Bioprocessing Production Center Opening Ceremony Burlington, Massachusetts, Oct. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- 
The company's largest life science investment in Asia-Pacific to date expands regional manufacturing capacity 
Integrated digital systems support automated data capture and end-to-end batch traceability 
Advances the company's in-region-for-region strategy, bringing critical products closer to customers across Asia-Pacific 
State-of-the-art facility designed to eliminate on-site fossil-fuel use and improve energy and water efficiency 
Burlington, Massachusetts, October 29, 2026 – MilliporeSigma, the U.S. and Canada Life Science business of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, today announced the opening of a new Asia-Pacific Bioprocessing Production Center in Daejeon, South Korea. The center represents an investment of more than €300 million, the company's largest Life Science investment in Asia-Pacific to date. 
The 44,500-square-meter site expands the company's regional manufacturing capacity for critical materials and solutions used in the development and production of biologic medicines. It gives biopharmaceutical manufacturers across Asia-Pacific closer access to the materials and solutions needed to develop and produce biologic medicines.
"Reliable access to critical materials is essential at every stage of biologics manufacturing," said Jean-Charles Wirth, Member of the Executive Board and CEO, Life Science of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. "Daejeon brings advanced production closer to biopharma manufacturers across Asia-Pacific, giving them greater supply confidence, as they move from development to commercial scale. The center adds the regional capacity customers need and delivers the quality and consistency they expect from us."
From Daejeon, the company will supply bioprocessing products used from early process development through commercial-scale manufacturing. These include cell culture media in dry powder and liquid formats, including pre-GMP small-scale custom products through imMEDIAte ADVANTAGE®, process liquids and ready-to-use cleaning-in-place solutions; and single-use sterile sampling solutions based on the NovaSeptum® Sterile Sampling System. Together, they help customers accelerate development, scale production, maintain controlled manufacturing environments and reduce contamination risk. Cell culture media and process liquids will use animal-component-free raw materials and be manufactured to consistent global quality standards. 
Story Continues 
"The completion of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany's Asia-Pacific Bioprocessing Production Center, a world-leading bioscience company, marks a historic turning point in Daejeon's rise as a global bio hub—not just for Korea, but for the world." said Tae-Jeong Heo, Mayor of Daejeon. "We will provide our full support to ensure that Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany's foundational technologies at the Daedeok Innopolis and the capabilities of the local community can be brought together seamlessly. We will focus the city's resources on building a world-class global bio ecosystem through close collaboration among industry, academia, research institutions, and hospitals." 
The center's integrated digital ecosystem is designed to support automated data capture and end-to-end batch traceability, increasing process transparency and supporting quality management and regulatory compliance.
The facility is designed to eliminate the use of fossil fuels on-site while increasing energy and water efficiency through the use of solar power, a heat-pump system, energy recovery in air handling units, and rainwater reuse. 
The Daejeon center is a key part of the company's in-region-for-region strategy. It builds on recent investments across the company's global network, including BioReliance® drug product testing in Darmstadt, Germany, and filtration manufacturing in Blarney, Ireland. Across this network, the company is bringing critical products and services closer to customers while applying consistent global quality standards. 
About the Life Science business of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany 
The Life Science business of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, which operates as MilliporeSigma in the U.S. and Canada, has more than 27,000 employees and more than 55 total manufacturing and testing sites worldwide, with a portfolio of more than 300,000 products focused on scientific discovery, biomanufacturing and testing services. Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, a leading science and technology company, operates across healthcare, life science and electronics. 
More than 62,000 employees work to make a positive difference to millions of people's lives every day by creating more joyful and sustainable ways to live. From providing products and services that accelerate drug development and manufacturing as well as discovering unique ways to treat the most challenging diseases to enabling the intelligence of devices – the company is everywhere. In 2025, Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, generated sales of € 21.1 billion in 65 countries. 
The company holds the global rights to the name and trademark "Merck" internationally. The only exceptions are the United States and Canada, where the business sectors of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, operate as MilliporeSigma in life science, EMD Serono in healthcare and EMD Electronics in electronics. Since its founding in 1668, scientific exploration and responsible entrepreneurship have been key to the company's technological and scientific advances. To this day, the founding family remains the majority owner of the publicly listed company. For more information about Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, visit www.emdgroup.com .

GE HealthCare raises 2026 outlook after positive Q3
In Q3, GE HealthCare reported notable growth in PDx, a segment it moved to strengthen earlier this month with the $945m acquisition of SOFIE Biosciences.
Ross Law 
October 29, 2026 
Share
Copy Link

GE HealthCare’s PDx segment saw the largest YoY growth at over 13%
Credit: PixelBiss/Shutterstock.com 
GE HealthCare has reported revenues of $5.5bn in Q3, with notable year-over-year (YoY) growth in its pharmaceutical diagnostics (PDx) segment, prompting the company to raise its 2026 outlook.
With Q3 revenues indicative of a 7.2% rise YoY, the imaging giant now expects 2026 earnings to fall in the $4.95 to $5.05 per share range, up from $4.80 to $5 as previously outlined.

Releasing its Q3 results ahead of market open on 28 October, GE HealthCare’s stock on the Nasdaq exchange opened at $76 per share, an uptick of almost 7% from $71.11 previously. GE HealthCare has a market cap of $34.25bn.
As usual, the majority of revenue in the quarter emanated from GE HealthCare’s core advanced imaging solutions (AIS) segment at around $3.8bn. This was followed by pharmaceutical diagnostics (PDx) and patient care solutions at $846m and $793m, respectively.
Regarding segment growth, however, PDx achieved the highest YoY growth margin at 13%, with patient care and AIS rising by 8.5% and 6.1% YoY, respectively.
Growth in PDx, a segment comprised of contrast media and radiopharmaceutical imaging agents including GE HealthCare’s myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI), Flyrcado, follows its agreement to acquire contract manufacturing organisation (CMO) SOFIE Biosciences for $945m earlier this month. Flyrcado obtained US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval in September 2024 and is manufactured by SOFIE.
Upon the acquisition’s announcement, GE HealthCare said the move was anticipated to drive patient access to novel radiopharmaceuticals via the inheritance of SOFIE’s US network of 15 CMO sites and its theranostics-focused contract development and manufacturing organisation (CDMO) site, and give it the ability to participate in other high-growth areas outside its own product portfolio. Radiopharma is a fast-growing area within the wider healthcare space due to its ability to precisely target complex cancers. 
Reflecting on its forward-looking ambitions for PDx, GE HealthCare’s president and CEO, Peter Arduini, noted during an earnings call that the segment has delivered at “least high single-digit growth” for “five straight quarters”.
“We are investing in strengthening our supply chain and manufacturing capabilities and expanding where we can create value,” Arduini said.
“Managing diseases often requires imaging at several points along the patient journey. From diagnosis to treatment to monitoring. Our agents are used in many of those imaging scans. Because each scan uses a dose, PDx revenue is recurring and grows with patient volume,” Arduni continued.
GE HealthCare’s SOFIE acquisition gives rise to potential market tension
While GE HealthCare’s acquisition of SOFIE has largely been read by market observers as a move to protect supply for Flycado, GlobalData analysts highlight that the deal “deepens” an unusually complicated relationship within the nuclear imaging space.
GlobalData analysts note that GE HealthCare and Lantheus are competitors, though GE HealthCare licenses one of its key products from Lantheus. And once the SOFIE deal closes in H1 2027, GE HealthCare will also manufacture some of Lantheus’s most important products.
Flyrcado began as a Lantheus asset before GE HealthCare licensed it in 2017, and Lantheus still receives royalties on its US sales. GlobalData analysts note that SOFIE manufactures Flyrcado and two Lantheus agents, Neuraceq and Pylarify, which together generated more than $1bn in sales in 2025. Regarding market dynamic tensions, analysts highlight that when SOFIE joins GE HealthCare, each company (GE HealthCare and Lantheus) will have a financial stake in the other’s products.

Merck tops quarterly estimates, hikes profit outlook as new Keytruda form shows strength
Published Thu, Oct 29 2026 6:31 AM EDT Updated Thu, Oct 29 2026 7:24 AM EDT 
Annika Kim Constantino @annikakimc 
WATCH LIVE 
Key Points
Merck topped third-quarter estimates and hiked its adjusted profit outlook. 
The company's immunotherapy Keytruda, including a newer injectable form of the drug called Qlex, posted stronger-than-expected sales. 
That new version of the drug raked in $830 million in sales for the period – the highest in a quarter since it launched in 2025. 
In this article
MRK 
Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT 
The exterior view of the entrance to Merck headquarters in Rahway, New Jersey, on Feb. 5, 2024.
Spencer Platt | Getty Images
Merck on Thursday topped third-quarter estimates and hiked its adjusted profit outlook, as its immunotherapy Keytruda, including a newer injectable form of the drug, showed stronger-than-expected sales. 
The pharmaceutical giant now expects adjusted earnings to be between $2.77 and $2.82 per share. That adjusted profit outlook is up from a previous range of $2.66 to $2.76 per share. The guidance now includes a one-time charge of $400 million, or 12 cents per share, related to its licensing agreement with the Chinese cancer drugmaker SciBrunch.
Merck also narrowed the low end of its 2026 revenue guidance, now expecting sales between $66.8 billion and $67.3 billion. That compares to a previous outlook of $66.3 billion to $67.3 billion. 
The company has been on a deal spree as it races to offset generic competition for Keytruda after key patents begin expiring in 2028. 
Merck is also positioning the new form of the drug, Keytruda Qlex, as a cornerstone of its growth strategy. The goal is to transition patients from the original intravenous version to Qlex, considered a more convenient under-the-skin injection. This strategy allows the company to defend its market share and sustain Keytruda's blockbuster sales beyond the original version's loss of exclusivity.
Keytruda raked in $8.60 billion in sales for the quarter, beating the $7.73 billion that analysts were expecting, according to StreetAccount. That includes $830 million in sales for Qlex – the highest seen in a quarter since it launched in 2025. 
Analysts were expecting $649 million in sales, StreetAccount estimates said. The blowout quarter for the shot suggests it could soon eventually be a multibillion-dollar product annually.
Here's what Merck reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: 
Earnings per share: $2.49 adjusted vs. $2.08 expected
Revenue: $18.09 billion vs. $17.31 billion expected
The company posted a net income of $5.07 billion, or $2.04 per share, for the quarter. That compares with net income of $5.79 billion, or $2.32 per share, for the year-earlier period. 
Excluding acquisition and restructuring costs, Merck posted earnings of $2.49 per share for the third quarter.
Merck raked in $18.09 billion in revenue for the quarter, up 5% from the same period a year earlier.
Beyond Keytruda, Merck's newer products also showed strong growth. 
Winrevair, which is used to treat a rare, deadly lung condition, generated $694 million in sales for the quarter, up 93% from the same period a year earlier. Analysts were expecting sales of $645 million. 
Meanwhile, the Gardasil vaccine, which prevents cancers from HPV, a very common sexually transmitted infection, drew about $2 billion in sales due to higher demand in the U.S. That tops the $1.76 billion in sales that analysts were expecting. 
That strong revenue comes after Merck last year grappled with elevated Gardasil inventory and weak demand for the vaccine in China. 
Meanwhile, Merck's animal health business posted $1.68 billion in sales for the third quarter, which came in slightly below analysts' estimates.

content_text:
SCHOTT Poonawalla Renamed SCHOTT Pharma India, Reaffirms Long-Term Commitment to Indian Pharma Market 
Written By : sheeba farhat Published On 2026-10-29T15:46:32+05:30   |   Updated On 29 Oct 2026 3:46 PM IST 
New Delhi: SCHOTT Poonawalla Private Limited will become SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited, marking an important new chapter in the company's journey and strengthening its connection with the global SCHOTT Pharma organization.
The new identity more clearly reflects the India business’s place within SCHOTT Pharma’s global network and its role in advancing high-quality drug containment and delivery solutions for the pharmaceutical and biotech industries. It brings together the company’s strong manufacturing footprint, long-standing customer relationships and deep market expertise in India with SCHOTT Pharma’s global capabilities, innovation and scientific excellence.
For customers, partners and employees, this is a change in name, not a change in commitment. There is no change in ownership, management, employees, business strategy, operations, products, services or existing customer commitments.
The transition reinforces SCHOTT Pharma India’s long-term commitment to customers in India and international markets, while creating a stronger and more consistent connection to the global SCHOTT Pharma brand.
Building on a heritage of more than 140 years, the new identity brings the company’s heritage and future ambition under one global name, reflecting the values that continue to define SCHOTT Pharma: innovation, quality, scientific excellence and trust.
Also Read: TPG to acquire 35% stake in SCHOTT Poonawalla from SII 
SCHOTT Pharma India represents both continuity and progress: the same trusted business, capabilities and relationships, now with an identity that more clearly reflects who we are today and where we are headed.
Roy Joseph, CEO & Managing Director, SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited, said, “SCHOTT Pharma India represents the next chapter of our journey, combining our strength in India with SCHOTT Pharma’s global innovation and expertise. We see significant opportunity to build on our capabilities, deepen collaboration with pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners, and advance drug containment and delivery solutions. As we move forward, our focus remains on growing with our customers and contributing to the safe and reliable delivery of critical therapies to patients worldwide.”
“SCHOTT Pharma India plays a critical role in patient care. With more than 3 billion containers produced annually, this company enables around 7,000 injections to reach patients every minute,” said Dr. Christian Mias, CEO of SCHOTT Pharma AG & Co. KGaA, SCHOTT Pharma India’s major shareholder. “The name change from SCHOTT Poonawalla to SCHOTT Pharma India reinforces our strategic partnership and confirms our long-term commitment to India as a key pharma hub.”
The new identity builds on the company’s strong foundation in India. During the COVID-19 pandemic, its pharmaceutical vials supported more than 4.3 billion vaccine doses worldwide, including 3 billion doses in India. As India’s only manufacturer of glass pre-fillable syringes and sterile formats, the company also strengthens local supply capabilities. Furthermore, the company continues to invest significantly towards manufacturing capacity expansions of pre-fillable syringes and cartridges, strengthening their ability to support the rapidly evolving needs of biologics, biosimilars, GLP-1 based treatments and other advanced injectable therapies.
Looking ahead, SCHOTT Pharma India will focus on expanding capabilities across pharmaceutical drug containment and drug delivery solutions, driving innovation through closer customer collaboration, and strengthening operational excellence and sustainability. These priorities will support the company as it responds to the evolving needs of pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies while contributing to India’s growing role in the global pharmaceutical value chain.
SCHOTT Pharma India is a manufacturer of advanced drug containment and delivery solutions, serving pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies across global markets. Based on innovation in specialty glass and advanced materials, the company offers a comprehensive portfolio of injectable drug containment and delivery products, including vials, cartridges, syringes and ampoules. Manufactured to stringent international quality standards, SCHOTT Pharma India’s solutions enable safe storage of vaccines and biologics. Through continued investment in innovation and operational excellence, and a strong focus on quality, reliability and customer partnership, the company addresses evolving healthcare needs and supports better patient outcomes worldwide.

query: ("Eli Lilly and Company" OR "Eli Lilly") ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Eli Lilly hikes sales outlook, as CEO says there's room for 'dramatic' obesity market expansion
Published Thu, Oct 29 2026 6:13 AM EDT Updated Thu, Oct 29 2026 12:46 PM EDT 
Annika Kim Constantino @annikakimc 
WATCH LIVE 
Key Points
Eli Lilly reported third-quarter earnings and revenue that blew past estimates and hiked its full-year sales outlook.
Demand for its obesity drug Zepbound and diabetes treatment Mounjaro surged again and topped estimates for the quarter.
Despite that strength, sales of its new GLP-1 obesity pill Foundayo, which launched in the U.S. in April, were under Wall Street's expectations for the quarter.
In this article
LLY 
Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT 
watch now 
VIDEO 4:53 04:53 
Eli Lilly CEO Dave Ricks on the obesity market: The room for expansion is dramatic
Squawk on the Street 
Eli Lilly on Thursday reported third-quarter earnings and revenue that blew past estimates and hiked its full-year sales outlook, as demand for its blockbuster weight loss drug Zepbound and diabetes treatment Mounjaro soared again. 
Despite that strength, sales of its new GLP-1 obesity pill Foundayo, which launched in the U.S. in April, were under Wall Street's expectations for the quarter.
The pharmaceutical giant now expects 2026 revenue to come in between $91 billion and $92 billion, up from a previous guidance of $85 billion to $87 billion. 
Lilly projects its full-year adjusted earnings will be between $35 and $36 per share, which compares with a previous outlook of $35.50 to $36.50 per share. The company said it raised the underlying profit guidance by $4.07 per share at the midpoint, but noted that it is offset by $4.57 per share in charges tied to deals in the quarter.
The company's shares rose about 7% on Thursday. 
Lilly's massive diabetes and obesity windfall – and market share lead over chief rival Novo – shows no signs of slowing down, even as the company grapples with lower net prices in the U.S. The pharma giant is converting its massive profits into a deal-making spree, most recently striking an agreement to buy Merida Biosciences to develop a new class of treatments for serious autoimmune and allergic diseases. 
Here's what Eli Lilly reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: 
Earnings per share: $7.48 adjusted vs. $6.26 expected
Revenue: $24.40 billion vs. $22.61 billion expected
Resilient demand for Zepbound and Mounjaro has helped fuel several strong quarters for Lilly despite lower prices for the medications in the U.S., which came after a drug pricing deal struck with the Trump administration last year. In a release, Lilly also pointed to expanded U.S. coverage for obesity care, referring to Medicare's decision to start covering GLP-1s for weight loss in July under a temporary pilot program. 
"This is a program that's really working," Lilly CEO Dave Ricks said on CNBC's " Squawk on the Street ." "We're pleased with the early uptake and access, and I think doctors and patients are as well."
Mounjaro's worldwide revenue rose 65% to $10.72 billion for the quarter, including U.S. sales of about $5 billion. That surpassed the $10.10 billion in worldwide sales and $4.79 billion in U.S. revenue that analysts were expecting for the quarter, according to StreetAccount.
Mounjaro notably saw strength internationally, with sales outside the U.S. jumping 93%.
Zepbound, which entered the market roughly three years ago, posted $5.35 billion in revenue for the third quarter. That's up 49% from the year-earlier period, as demand for the drug also rose while realized prices dropped. The vast majority of those sales came from the U.S. 
Analysts were expecting $5.09 billion in global sales for Zepbound, including $4.99 billion from the U.S., according to StreetAccount.
The Eli Lilly logo appears on the company’s office in San Diego, California, Nov. 21, 2025.
Mike Blake | Reuters
Lilly's newly launched obesity pill, Foundayo, which won U.S. approval in April, took in $184 million in sales for the third quarter. That fell under analyst forecasts of around $229 million in sales, StreetAccount estimates showed. 
It marks the second earnings report that includes revenue from the GLP-1 pill, which is competing head-to-head with a rival oral drug from Novo that launched in January. 
Total U.S. prescriptions for Foundayo and the number of new Foundayo patients in the third quarter doubled from the previous quarter, Lilly CFO Lucas Montarces said during a Thursday earnings call. Around 4 in 10 patients starting an oral obesity medicine choose Foundayo, he added.
Lilly expects Foundayo to win U.S. approval for Type 2 diabetes in the fourth quarter.
Lilly is working to maintain its dominance in the booming market for GLP-1 drugs, with the company holding 63% share of the U.S. obesity and diabetes drug market in the third quarter, according to an earnings presentation on Thursday. Novo's market share in the quarter was 36.6%. 
During the earnings call, Montarces said 7 out of 10 U.S. prescriptions for injectable obesity and diabetes drugs in the third quarter were for a Lilly medicine. 
Ricks told CNBC that he estimates 3% to 10% of eligible patients access obesity care in the U.S., but said the "room for expansion here of this market is dramatic." Lilly is at the front of that push, he added. 
Internationally, Lilly held 58.4% share of the market, while Novo had 41.6%, the presentation said. 
Eli Lilly's revenue in the U.S. climbed 34% to $15.1 billion. Lilly said it saw a 41% increase in volume — or the number of prescriptions or units sold — for its products, primarily for Mounjaro and Zepbound. That was partially offset by a 7% decrease in realized prices, primarily driven by Zepbound. 
Lilly's quarter was also boosted by a sales-based milestone payout of $410 million for its Type 2 diabetes medication Jardiance, related to the company's collaboration with Boehringer Ingelheim.
Sales outside the U.S. jumped 47% to $9.3 billion, propelled by a 76% surge in volume and partly offset by a 29% drop in realized prices. 
The pharmaceutical giant booked net income of $6.45 billion, or $7.22 per share, for the third quarter, which includes the $4.57 per share deal charges. That compares with net income of $5.58 billion, or $6.21 per share, a year earlier. 
Excluding one-time items associated with the value of intangible assets and other adjustments, Eli Lilly posted earnings of $7.48 per share for the third quarter.

content_text:
Rio Tinto celebrates opening of US$1.4 billion lithium projects in Argentina
The official opening of Rio Tinto’s Fénix 1B expansion and Sal de Vida operation in Catamarca marks a major milestone for Argentina's lithium industry, following a combined investment of around US$1.4 billion.
Both projects achieved first production in 2Q26 ahead of plan and are now ramping up production. They will add 25 000 tpy of lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) capacity once fully ramped up, strengthening Rio Tinto’s standing and Argentina’s position as a leading supplier of lithium for global markets.
The celebrations included a visit to Fénix by President Milei and Governor Jalil, hosted by Simon Trott, and an inauguration event recognising both projects with national and provincial authorities, employees, suppliers, and representatives of local and Indigenous communities.
President of Argentina Javier Milei said: “The expansion of the Fénix project is a historic milestone that demonstrates the potential of Argentina’s mining sector. This was made possible by the country once again creating incentives for the production of resources that are essential to the modern world.
“We are proud that a company of this scale once again sees Argentina as a reliable partner and is investing in our country, validating the decisions we have taken over the past few years.”
Rio Tinto Chief Executive Simon Trott said: “Today is a proud moment for Rio Tinto and an important milestone for Argentina’s lithium industry, as we grow our position as a leading global supplier. It was a privilege to welcome President Milei, Governor Jalil and national and provincial authorities, and I thank them for joining us to recognise the work behind Fénix 1B and Sal de Vida.
“These two projects build on nearly three decades of lithium production in Catamarca and the expertise of our Argentine workforce. They demonstrate our industry-leading project delivery capability, as we execute with discipline towards our global target of 200 000 tonnes lithium carbonate equivalent annual production capacity by 2028.
“The delivery of these projects reflects the dedication of our people, the capabilities of Argentine suppliers and our partnerships with local communities and governments. Our focus now is on safely ramping up production, delivering reliable, high-quality lithium to our customers, and creating lasting value for our shareholders and Argentina.”
Fénix began operations in 1997 as Argentina’s first commercial lithium operation. The Fénix 1B expansion adds 10,000 tonnes of annual LCE capacity to the existing operation, increasing its total target of annual LCE capacity to approximately 40 000 t.
Sal de Vida is a new lithium carbonate operation located approximately 20 kilometres northeast of Fénix, with a target of annual LCE capacity of 15 000 t.
The projects form part of Rio Tinto’s growing lithium business in Argentina, which includes operations and projects across Catamarca, Jujuy and Salta, including the Rincon lithium project.
Rio Tinto’s growth in Argentina is strengthening the country’s supplier network. Around 70% of the approximately US$4 billion in growth capital to be invested across our lithium operations in Argentina is expected to be spent with local suppliers.

[Shin-Etsu FY2026 Q2 Earnings Call] Japan's Shin-Etsu Chemical Posts Record Q2 Operating Profit of ¥212.1 Billion, Up 27% on AI Demand; Electronic Materials Running at Full Capacity, Full-Year Forecast Unchanged
Add preferred source 
Shin-Etsu Chemical reported consolidated results for the April-September 2026 period, with revenue of ¥1.4206 trillion (up 10.6% year-on-year) and operating profit of ¥385.9 billion (up 15.6%), marking substantial growth on both lines. Operating profit for the July-September quarter alone rose 27% year-on-year to ¥212.1 billion, a record for any quarter. Driven by expanding AI-related investment, the Electronic Materials segment generated revenue of ¥577.7 billion (up 16%) and operating profit of ¥218.9 billion (up 28%), accounting for more than half of segment profit, with production running at full capacity. President Yasuhiko Saito said top executives at customer companies are requesting additional supply, and that the company is working on capacity expansion and pricing terms. Meanwhile, softening PVC market conditions pushed Lifestyle Environment Materials operating profit down 16% to ¥86.2 billion. The full-year forecast targets record revenue of ¥2.7 trillion and operating profit of ¥700 billion, but was left unchanged after the assumed exchange rates were revised toward a stronger yen. Capital investment was raised to ¥380 billion to accelerate response to AI-related demand.
Key Elements 
Shin-Etsu Chemical Yasuhiko Saito Toshiyuki Kasahara Electronic Materials Lifestyle Environment Materials Functional Materials PVC Semiconductor Lithography Materials Silicone Shin-Etsu Polymer AI-Related Investment Share Buyback 100th Anniversary Commemorative Dividend ROE DOE 
Japan's Shin-Etsu Chemical Posts Record Q2 Operating Profit of ¥212.1 Billion, Up 27% on AI Demand; Electronic Materials Running at Full Capacity, Full-Year Forecast Unchanged
Shin-Etsu Chemical's consolidated results for the second quarter of fiscal 2026 (April-September 2026), announced on October 27, 2026, showed substantial growth on both revenue and profit lines: revenue of ¥1.4206 trillion (up 10.6% year-on-year), operating profit of ¥385.9 billion (up 15.6%), ordinary profit of ¥415.1 billion (up 13.0%), and interim net profit attributable to owners of the parent of ¥286.9 billion (up 11.3%). Operating profit for the July-September quarter alone rose 27% year-on-year to ¥212.1 billion, a record for any quarter, with the profit margin improving 1 point from a year earlier to 27.2%.
Financial Highlights
Item Apr-Sep 2026 Year-Earlier Period Change 
Revenue ¥1.4206 trillion ¥1.2842 trillion +10.6% 
Operating Profit ¥385.9 billion ¥333.8 billion +15.6% 
Ordinary Profit ¥415.1 billion ¥367.3 billion +13.0% 
Interim Net Profit ¥286.9 billion ¥257.8 billion +11.3% 
Interim EPS ¥155.71 ¥136.59 +14.0% 
Operating Margin 27.2% 26.0% +1.2pt 
ROIC (annualized) 16.9% 15.9% +1.0pt 
ROE (annualized) 12.8% 11.6% +1.2pt 
(Year-earlier figures back-calculated from percentage changes)
Electronic Materials Generates More Than Half of Profit
The Electronic Materials segment drove results. Revenue came to ¥577.7 billion (up 16% year-on-year) and operating profit to ¥218.9 billion (up 28%), accounting for more than half of segment profit. Historic expansion of AI-related investment for data centers sent demand for semiconductor materials surging, and with supply tightening for some products, the company implemented precise supply responses and price revisions.
President Yasuhiko Saito said at the briefing that "expansion of the AI-related market is driving demand, other fields are also recovering broadly, and our electronic materials production is running at full capacity." He added that "the top executives of customers I have met and held meetings with recently are all requesting additional supply and making future supply volumes a priority." He made clear the company intends to pursue capacity expansion and price pass-through simultaneously: "Responding will require investment, so not only for wafers but for many of the items we handle, we are working on the necessary investment and on setting prices and other terms to support it."
On magnetic materials, he said the company is working with customers on urgent measures to minimize the use of heavy rare earths while diversifying procurement across multiple raw material suppliers.
By Segment: Functional Materials Profit Up 31%, Lifestyle Environment Materials Down 16%
Segment Revenue YoY Operating Profit YoY 
Electronic Materials ¥577.7 billion +16% ¥218.9 billion +28% 
Lifestyle Environment Materials ¥522.1 billion +4% ¥86.2 billion -16% 
Functional Materials ¥245.6 billion +11% ¥63.2 billion +31% 
Processing, Trading & Technical Services ¥75.1 billion +12% ¥17.4 billion +28% 
The Functional Materials segment posted a large profit increase, with operating profit of ¥63.2 billion (up 31%), on sales growth of high-value-added products. "Our policy of dramatically growing functional and specialty products is unchanged, and we are concentrating on that. The results are showing up in a rise in the overall average unit price, which is leading to improved profitability," Saito said. Cellulose for pharmaceutical formulations also grew.
Meanwhile, the Lifestyle Environment Materials segment saw operating profit fall 16% to ¥86.2 billion on softening PVC market conditions. In the United States, domestic PVC sales volume in July-September rose 7% year-on-year according to industry statistics, but market prices fell 3 cents per pound in July. They held firm afterward, and Saito said the price increase announced in October is "expected to go through, even if not in full." "From our perspective, this month's sales pace in the U.S. is on par with September, and the outlook for November is not bad," he said, offering a cautious but positive view. In overseas markets, the company also pushed through a price increase in July, after which prices fluctuated, but "now we are able to raise prices," he said. Caustic soda market conditions are relatively stable.
Processing, Trading & Technical Services grew on solid demand for containers related to semiconductor wafers, with revenue of ¥75.1 billion (up 12%) and operating profit of ¥17.4 billion (up 28%).
By Region: Overseas Sales Account for 78%
Region Revenue Share 
Japan ¥312.3 billion 22% 
United States ¥362.9 billion 26% 
Asia & Oceania ¥486.6 billion 34% 
Europe ¥152.3 billion 11% 
Overseas Total ¥1.1083 trillion 78% 
Asia & Oceania accounted for 34% of the total, making it the largest market, of which China was ¥138.1 billion.
Full-Year Forecast Unchanged; Exchange Rate Assumptions Revised Toward Stronger Yen
The full-year forecast targets record results: revenue of ¥2.7 trillion (up 4.9% from the prior year), operating profit of ¥700 billion (up 10.2%), ordinary profit of ¥770 billion (up 8.7%), and net profit of ¥525 billion (up 10.7%). The forecast was left unchanged from July.
Item Full-Year Forecast YoY 
Revenue ¥2.7 trillion +4.9% 
Operating Profit ¥700 billion +10.2% 
Ordinary Profit ¥770 billion +8.7% 
Net Profit ¥525 billion +10.7% 
Net EPS ¥286 +13.2% 
Operating Margin 25.9% +1.2pt 
Notably, the company left its earnings forecast unchanged even as it revised its assumed exchange rates for October onward toward a stronger yen — around ¥157 to the dollar (previously around ¥160) and around ¥176 to the euro (previously around ¥180). Exchange-rate sensitivity is ¥3.6 billion in annual ordinary profit for each ¥1 move in the dollar and ¥200 million for each ¥1 move in the euro (a weaker yen is positive). The company is absorbing the profit drag from the stronger-yen revision through the strength of real demand, centered on electronic materials.
"The full-year forecast has been left unchanged, but we are working to grow earnings so as to meet your expectations. We will also pay even closer attention to crude oil price trends and their impact, and respond in a timely manner," Saito said.
Capital Investment Raised to ¥380 Billion
Capital investment was revised upward from the previous forecast to ¥380 billion. Toshiyuki Kasahara, Executive Officer in charge of accounting, said this is "mainly because progress on investment plans has moved forward." Depreciation is projected at ¥240 billion.
Major projects include semiconductor lithography materials (Isesaki, ¥83 billion, to be completed in the first half of 2026), high-performance silicone products (Gunma, Takefu and Naoetsu, ¥80 billion), and expansion of a PVC raw material plant in the United States ($3.4 billion, scheduled for completion at the end of 2030). The company is accelerating capacity expansion to meet AI-related demand, centered on electronic materials.
Shareholder Returns and Finances
The interim dividend was ¥78 (ordinary ¥58 plus a ¥20 commemorative dividend marking the company's 100th anniversary). The annual dividend is planned at ¥136 (ordinary ¥116 plus ¥20 commemorative), with a payout ratio of 47.6% and a DOE of 5.5%. A ¥250 billion share buyback was completed, raising the number of treasury shares to 169.26 million. The equity ratio fell to 75.6%, but ROE rose to 12.8% on an annualized basis, indicating improved capital efficiency.
On the balance sheet, long-term borrowings increased by ¥161.1 billion during the first half. Kasahara explained that the company "responded to robust funding needs for capital investment and shareholder returns by preserving high-yield dollar funds on hand and borrowing yen funds." Net cash on hand after deducting borrowings fell by about ¥72 billion from the end of the prior fiscal year to about ¥1.35 trillion.
Operating cash flow expanded to ¥410.7 billion (¥347.0 billion a year earlier).
Q&A: Questions Focus on Durability of AI Demand and Price Pass-Through
At the briefing, questions came in succession about the durability of AI-related demand and progress on the accompanying price pass-through. Asked how long the supply tightness in electronic materials would last, Saito repeatedly noted that "customer top executives are making supply volumes a priority," indicating his view that demand will continue for the time being. On setting price terms, he limited himself to saying the company is "working on the necessary investment and on setting prices and other terms to support it," without mentioning specific increase amounts or timing.
On the U.S. PVC market, while saying the October price increase is "expected to go through, even if not in full," he acknowledged that domestic sales volume in July-September declined from April-June, suggesting a cautious stance on the pace of recovery.
Summary
Shin-Etsu Chemical's second quarter saw electronic materials running at full capacity on the tailwind of AI-related investment, achieving record quarterly operating profit. Although the full-year forecast was left unchanged, holding it steady after revising exchange-rate assumptions toward a stronger yen can be read as a sign of management's confidence in the strength of real demand. The accelerated execution of capital investment and the upward revision to ¥380 billion are a stepping stone toward medium- and long-term growth. Going forward, the focus will be on when Lifestyle Environment Materials recovers amid continued softening of PVC market conditions, and on progress in price pass-through for electronic materials.

content_text:
Q3 2026 Results: Air Liquide accelerates, driven by sales growth and the launch of its strategic plan
Paris, France, 
October 29, 2026 
Press Releases
Group
Sales growth , driven notably by growth in Electronics and Industrial Merchant 
Record investments  since the beginning of 2026, strengthening a record backlog 
Execution of the first €1 billion share buyback tranche by the end of 2026 
2026 and 2027 outlook confirmed 
Commenting on sales in the 3 rd quarter of 2026, François Jackow, Chief Executive Officer of the Air Liquide Group , stated: 
“On October 5th, with the unveiling of BEYOND, our strategic plan through 2030, we opened a new chapter. Our ambition is clear: reach the next frontier in lasting value creation by accelerating operational performance, capturing all profitable growth opportunities, and evolving our capital allocation program to boost shareholder returns. 
BEYOND is already being implemented by our teams worldwide . Our third quarter is a perfect illustration, delivering robust performance driven by the momentum of our sales and investments in growth markets. As a reflection of our deep conviction in our strategic roadmap and our commitment to accelerating performance, we are announcing today the launch of the first €1 billion tranche of our share buyback program, to be completed by the end of December . 
Reaching nearly €7.3 billion as of September 30, 2026, our revenue is up +4.3% excluding currency and energy impacts and +3% on a comparable basis. Gas & Services activities (1) grew by +3.6% on a comparable basis, particularly in Industrial Merchant , which rose +5%, confirming a steady growth since the beginning of the year. Electronics  also acted as a key driver with a strong +12% increase, boosted by sustained semiconductors’ demand for AI, for which our carrier gases and advanced materials are essential. Geographically, Asia-Pacific  and the Americas stood out, advancing by +7% and +6% respectively on a comparable basis. The key development this quarter is the acceleration of volume growth in Electronics and Industrial Merchant segments, going beyond positive pricing effects. While subject to fluctuations in this volatile environment, this is a very positive sign. 
Concurrently, the Group continues to enhance its operational performance, achieving €441 million in efficiencies through the end of September. Our investments have reached new heights. Standing at €1.25 billion this quarter, investment decisions total more than €4.1 billion since the beginning of the year. Our investments in Electronics have almost doubled in just nine months compared to the full year 2025. This momentum propels our ongoing investments to an unprecedented level of €6.2 billion. » 
Air Liquide is therefore confident in its ability to increase its operating margin by +100 basis points (2) and to deliver recurring net profit growth, at constant exchange rates in 2026 (3) . 
The Group is also confident in its ability to improve its margin by +100 basis points (4) in 2027. This brings its total objective to +560 basis points over the 2022-2027 period.” 
Highlights 
“BEYOND” STRATEGIC PLAN 
Accelerating the Group’s lasting value creation with its new 2030 strategic plan. It embodies Air Liquide’s ambition to expand in the highest-potential markets and turn major global structural shifts into opportunities. 
This ambition targets three key objectives : 
A compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of +10% (±2%) over the period in recurring net Earnings per Share (5) , ensuring ambitious and profitable growth ; 
A recurring ROCE (6) above 11% in 2030, while maintaining a significant increase in industrial investments over the period, ensuring lasting value creation; 
And a confirmed environmental commitment , pursuing a 33% reduction in CO 2 emissions ( 7 ) by 2035 compared to 2020, ensuring a sustained societal commitment. 
In order to achieve the recurring EPS objective, three complementary levers will be flexibly deployed: 
A compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of +5% (±1%) (8) over the period in sales , outpacing industrial production by a factor of 2 to 3, 
A margin improvement of +400 to +600 basis points over the period (9) , 
A capital allocation of over €40 billion over the period (10) , made possible by the increased profitability initiated during the ADVANCE plan. More than half of this will be dedicated to higher industrial investments, bolt-on and strategic acquisitions. In addition, a significantly higher return for both institutional and individual shareholders will be ensured by combining a sustained, regular dividend growth policy with the launch for the first time of a 4 billion euros share buyback program by the end of 2028 (11) . 
Attention to all stakeholders - from customers to employees, shareholders to local communities - is reinforced with specific measures for each in the BEYOND plan, built on three pillars: Listen & Care , Growth , Performance . 
CORPORATE 
Successful issuance of a €2 billion multi-tranche bond on the Euro market, very significantly oversubscribed by investors. This new transaction reflects investor confidence in the implementation of the BEYOND strategic plan for 2030. The funds raised will support the Group's capital allocation and drive the development of the activities in future growth markets. 
Creation of a research chair “Artificial Intelligence for chemistry and through chemistry” by Air Liquide, the Ecole normale supérieure (ENS-PSL) and the ENS Foundation. 
ELECTRONICS 
Japan : To support market momentum in semiconductors and AI, more than €170 million invested to support a leading semiconductor manufacturer in the expansion of its manufacturing capabilities, notably an existing logic chip production facility. Air Liquide will build, own, and operate several production units to supply large volumes of ultra-pure gases. 
In the United States , the Group supports the expansion of its customers' sites.  In Idaho , more than USD 150 million invested to build, own and operate a new industrial gas production plant. The plant will produce large volumes of essential gases to manufacture advanced memory chips to meet the surging demand for AI in the U.S. and global markets. 
And supporting SK hynix in Indiana , USA : Investment of more than USD 170 million to build, own and operate two new industrial gas production units. They will supply ultra-pure gases  to SK hynix's first US site. 
INDUSTRY & ENERGY TRANSITION 
Texas, United States of America : More than USD 200 million invested in a new low-carbon gas production facility to support the development of the chemical industry in this US state. Air Liquide is strengthening its production capacity at its long-standing partner Oxea 's site in Bay City.  
Footnotes: 
[1] Representing over 97% of Air Liquide's revenue. 
[2] Excluding energy impact and the amortization of intangible assets recognized as part of Purchase Price Allocation following DIG Airgas acquisition. 
[3] Recurring net profit excluding exceptional and significant transactions that have no impact on the operating income recurring. 
[4] Excluding energy impact. See definitions in the appendix of the Capital Markets Day presentation available on the Air Liquide Group website. 
[5] Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of recurring net Earnings Per Share from year-end 2025 to year-end 2030 at 2025 exchange rates, see assumptions and new definitions in the appendix of the Capital Markets Day presentation available on the Air Liquide Group website. 
[6] Recurring ROCE excluding strategic acquisitions defined as presented at the Capital Markets Day, see definitions in the appendix of the Capital Markets Day presentation available on the Air Liquide Group website. 
[7] Reduction in Scope 1 and 2 CO 2 emissions compared to the 2020 baseline year, based on scenarios compatible with a 1.5°C trajectory. 
[8] This lever is calculated as a CAGR end of 2025 to end of 2030 at 2025 FX and Energy price; it includes the scope effect of acquisitions. See definitions in the appendix of the Capital Markets Day presentation available on the Air Liquide Group website. 
[9] This lever is calculated as the sum of yearly operating margin improvements at the energy price of the previous year, over the period 2026-2030. See definitions in the appendix of the Capital Markets Day presentation available on the Air Liquide Group website. 
[10] Sum of investments, acquisitions, dividends and shares buyback programs over the period 2026-2030; Includes bolt-on and DIG acquisitions but no other strategic acquisitions. 
[11] The Board of Directors has approved a €4 billion share buyback program through the end of 2028.

Sumitomo Chemical India Ltd (BOM:542920) (Q2 2027) Earnings Call Highlights: Stable H1 Revenue ...
GuruFocus News

SUMICHEM.NS 
+1.97% 
542920 
This article first appeared on GuruFocus . 
Q2 Revenue: Rs. 907 crore, down 2% YoY (from Rs. 930 crore in Q2 FY26). 
H1 Revenue: Rs. 1,971 crore, down 1% YoY. 
Q2 Gross Margin: 40.7%, down 240 bps YoY; improved 149 bps QoQ vs Q1 FY27. 
H1 Gross Margin: 39.9% vs 40.4% last year. 
Q2 EBITDA: Rs. 187 crore, down 15%; EBITDA margin 20.5%, down 297 bps YoY. 
H1 EBITDA Margin: 21.3% vs 22% last year. 
Q2 Net Profit: Rs. 157 crore, down 11% YoY; net profit margin 17.3%. 
H1 Net Profit: Rs. 372 crore, up 5% from Rs. 356 crore; net profit margin 18.9%, up 96 bps. 
H1 EPS: Rs. 7.45 vs Rs. 7.1 last year. 
H1 PBT (before exceptional): Rs. 472 crore, broadly in line with Rs. 478 crore last year; including Rs. 26.9 crore exceptional insurance income, PBT was Rs. 498 crore, up 4%. 
Q2 Domestic Revenue: Rs. 774 crore, up 2% YoY; H1 domestic revenue broadly stable at Rs. 1,657 crore. 
Q2 Exports: Rs. 127 crore, down 23% YoY (shipment timing to Japan and South America); H1 exports stable at Rs. 300 crore. 
Branded Products Share: 79% of domestic revenue; 41% of export revenue in H1 vs 34% last year. 
Q2 Sales Volumes: Fell by high single-digit percentage due to adverse weather. 
Product Category Performance (Q2): Insecticides down 9%, herbicides down 6%, fungicides down 6%; metal phosphides up 13%, PGRs up 9%, animal nutrition and environmental health together up 18%. 
H1 Product Mix: Insecticides Rs. 733 crore (38% of revenue, down 4%); herbicides Rs. 488 crore (25%, down 6%); metal phosphides Rs. 186 crore (up 18%); animal nutrition and environmental health Rs. 207 crore (up 14%); PGRs stable at Rs. 179 crore; fungicides Rs. 156 crore (down 7%). 
H1 Revenue Split: Generic products 72%, specialty products 28%; domestic 85%, exports 15%. 
Q2 Operating Expenses: Employee expenses Rs. 70 crore and other operating expenses Rs. 113 crore, both largely flat YoY. 
Cash & Liquid Investments: Approximately Rs. 2,523 crore as of September 30, 2026, up from Rs. 2,113 crore in March 2026; balance sheet essentially debt free. 
Net Cash from Operations (H1): Rs. 447 crore vs Rs. 435 crore in H1 FY26. 
Collections (H1): About Rs. 2,231 crore vs Rs. 2,277 crore last year. 
Trade Receivables: Rs. 887 crore as of September 2026 vs Rs. 903 crore a year ago.

Release Date: October 27, 2026 
For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript . 
Positive Points 
Sumitomo Chemical India Ltd ( BOM:542920 ) maintained stable H1 FY27 revenue at Rs. 1,971 crore despite the weakest monsoon since 2015, demonstrating resilience. 
Key brands like Flumioxazin, Meshi, Excalia Max, and others grew 22% in H1, outperforming the market. 
The company launched two proprietary products, Top Grain and Helibax, with Top Grain being the first global commercial launch in India. 
Exports of branded products increased to 41% of export revenue from 34% last year, improving product mix. 
Sumitomo Chemical India Ltd ( BOM:542920 ) remains debt-free with cash and liquid investments of approximately Rs. 2,523 crore, providing financial flexibility. 
Negative Points 
H1 FY27 was one of the most difficult for the Indian agrochemical industry due to erratic monsoon, with a 13% rainfall deficit, impacting demand. 
Q2 FY27 revenue declined 2% YoY to Rs. 907 crore, with volumes falling high single-digit due to lower consumption. 
EBITDA margin contracted by 297 bps YoY to 20.5% in Q2 FY27 due to high-cost inventory. 
Exports declined 23% YoY in Q2 FY27 to Rs. 127 crore due to timing of shipments and overstocking at parent company. 
Inventory days increased to 115 days as of September 2026 from 95 days last year, due to higher costs and lower sales. 
Q & A Highlights 
Q : Could you share an update on the semiconductor chemicals opportunity and whether Sumitomo Chemical India (the listed entity) will have a role in it? A : Kunal Mittal (Executive Vice President) said the parent, Sumitomo Chemical Japan, runs a global semiconductor business through its ICTM sector and is looking at India with keen interest. An MOU has been signed between the parent and a leading Indian semiconductor player building India's first fabrication plant, expected to be operational in one to two years. However, the Indian listed entity has not signed any MOU, and its specific role is still being discussed at a strategic level. He added that the company will not make speculative announcements and will inform shareholders once discussions reach a firm, mature stage. 
Q : How did H1 FY27 pan out given the weak monsoon, and what is the outlook for H2? A : Dr. Suresh Ramachandran (Managing Director) said H1 FY27 was one of the toughest first halves for the Indian agrochemical industry in over a decade, with a 13% monsoon deficit (the weakest since 2015) and a declared drought year. Despite this, revenue was broadly stable at Rs. 1,971 crore (down 1%), with key brands growing about 22%. For H2, he flagged three challenges: a potentially strong El Nino peaking around December, reservoir levels about 25% lower than last year, and a large southern soil-moisture shortfall. Positives include firming commodity prices, a better grape season, and normal wheat and mustard expectations. The goal is to grow over last year where the market allows while protecting profitability. 
Q : What drove the Q2 margin decline, and how do you see margins in H2? A : Kunal Mittal (Executive Vice President) explained that Q1 benefited from low-cost opening inventory, while Q2 absorbed inventory bought at higher cost between April and June. Q2 gross margin was 40.7% (down 240 bps) and EBITDA margin 20.5% (down 297 bps); H1 gross margin was 39.9% and EBITDA margin 21.3%, broadly in line with historical levels. Inventory costs largely normalized by the end of Q2. For H2, he expects margins in the normal historical range, with no significant adverse impact expected, and noted operating leverage should help as revenue scales. 
Q : What is the "Good to Great" transformation initiative, and what does it aim to achieve financially? A : Dr. Suresh Ramachandran (Managing Director) said the program, launched after the new management took over on September 1, 2026, is built on five pillars: people and performance culture, operational excellence, technology, data/digital/automation, and cross-functional collaboration. It stemmed from internal feedback that the company is "good" but needs to become "great" to differentiate itself amid competition. Some initiatives will yield financial benefits and others qualitative ones; the team is crunching data and expects to set a financial goal in the near future. Cash deployment for new segments is a separate, board-level matter. 
Q : Why has Q2 export revenue fallen 23%, and what is the outlook for exports? A : Dr. Suresh Ramachandran (Managing Director) attributed the Q2 export decline mainly to overstocking and ongoing inventory liquidation of parent-company molecules in Japan, while third-party exports to Africa, Europe, and Brazil grew. H1 exports were stable at Rs. 300 crore, with Africa, South America, Asia, and Europe each growing 15%19%, and the branded share of exports rose to 41% from 34%. Kunal Mittal (Executive Vice President) said the Japan softness is expected to be a this-year phenomenon, with normalization next year, and that the Tarapur CapEx is domestic-focused rather than export-oriented. 
Q : What is the status of the Dahej greenfield CapEx and other expansion projects? A : Kunal Mittal (Executive Vice President) said the ~Rs. 150 crore Dahej project, a dedicated facility for an intermediate for one blockbuster herbicide (not multipurpose), is on track for commercial production in Q2 FY28-29 (roughly JulyOctober 2028), with payback under five years and margins in line with company levels. Two Tarapur CapEx projects of Rs. 10 crore each (Rs. 20 crore total) will add three to four products, with the first completing this fiscal and the second by FY28. Dahej is envisioned as a long-term greenfield site for four or five parent blockbuster products, with further projects to be announced as approved. 
Q : With about Rs. 2,500 crore of cash, why not return capital to shareholders or acquire distressed brands? A : Kunal Mittal (Executive Vice President) said the company believes attractive growth opportunities exist in India's fast-growing agro market and does not want to forgo future growth by returning cash now, though the board will keep the option open if no use emerges. On acquisitions, he said the company looks at opportunities but will act only where there is strategic rationalesuch as new geography, distribution, or segmentsnot merely because smaller players face financial stress. Several strategic bases are already covered, but the company remains open to deploying funds for the right opportunity. 
Q : What is the opportunity from the paraquat ban, and how is the innovation pipeline shaping up? A : Dr. Suresh Ramachandran (Managing Director) said the government's recent ban on paraquat creates a vacuum that other molecules, including glyphosate, can fill, though the outcome will unfold over coming months and years. On innovation, he said India is now a first-tier country alongside Japan, the US, Europe, and Brazil for testing and launching parent moleculesTop Grain, a biostimulant from Sumitomo Biorational, had its world-first commercial launch in India. Kunal Mittal (Executive Vice President) said the innovation turnover index is in the high single digits (9%10%), with one to two specialty molecules expected annually plus generational combinations. 
Q : How are inventory and working capital trending, and do you expect sales returns or provisions in H2? A : Kunal Mittal (Executive Vice President) said net working capital rose to 76 days from 55 days, driven by inventory days increasing to 115 from 95 due to higher inventory cost and softer Q2 liquidation.
