HyProMag USA Completes Pre-Feasibility Study for Three-Plant Rare Earth Magnet Expansion
HyProMag USA LLC has completed a pre-feasibility study assessing a possible expansion of its proposed rare earth magnet manufacturing platform in the United States beyond its first plant in Northlake, Texas, according to Mining.com. The Northlake facility is in detailed engineering, with commissioning of its first phase expected in mid-2028. 
The company is developing rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing operations aimed at building a secure domestic supply chain for neodymium iron boron magnets, which it describes as essential components for defense systems, robotics, electric vehicles, advanced electronics and AI infrastructure.
Three-Plant Expansion Concept
The study evaluates a phased strategy involving three new regional production plants supported by a centralized manufacturing, finishing and technology hub. The hub would produce commercial NdFeB magnet products in the U.S. from both end-of-life recycled feedstock and primary alloy material.
Combined with the Northlake facility, the platform targets total salable material production of roughly 6,000 metric tons per year by 2034, an increase of 4,474 metric tons per year above current production. The 2034 output would comprise approximately 4,192 metric tons of magnets, 1,305 metric tons of magnetic NdFeB alloy powder and 503 metric tons of other salable material.
Economics Exclude Northlake
The study's economics cover the three new plants and the Central Texas hub only, and do not include the Northlake facility, whose value is excluded from the results. For the three new plants, the study envisions post-tax net present value of $1.85 billion to $2.1 billion, a post-tax internal rate of return of 31% to 36% and a profitability index of approximately 2.8x to 3.3x. Those figures rest on forecast prices and a Class 3 capital cost estimate of approximately $656 million to $623 million, with payback of 3 years and 2.3 years respectively.
For the first plant under the study in 2030, all-in sustaining cost is estimated at approximately $41.6 per kg to $37.4 per kg of finished NdFeB products sold, including downstream processing and finishing such as plating and epoxy coating. Based on forecast market prices and product mix, the weighted average realized all-in selling price in 2030 is estimated at approximately $100.5 per kg.
The combined post-tax net present value of the proposed Northlake facility and the potential plants covered by the study is estimated at $2.6 billion to $2.8 billion. The updated post-tax net present value for Northlake is approximately $723 million, based on forecast prices and a capital cost estimate of approximately $167 million.
Executive Commentary
Chief executive Julian Treger said in a news release that the study confirms the opportunity to establish a significant domestic rare earth magnet manufacturing platform in the United States. He said the study demonstrates robust economics and a pathway to producing higher-value NdFeB magnet products for strategically important sectors including advanced manufacturing, energy, defense and AI-driven technologies. He also said the platform is designed with flexibility to use primary alloy feedstock alongside recycled materials, which the company sees as supporting supply chain resilience and long-term operational competitiveness.

South Korea's East-West Power Weighs Rescue Role in Anma Offshore Wind After Equis Exit
Add preferred source 
South Korea's Korea East-West Power has begun reviewing a potential equity investment in the 532 MW Anma Offshore Wind project off Yeonggwang, South Jeolla Province, after Singapore-based Equis was left stranded by the collapse of its controlling-stake sale talks. The state-owned utility plans to send requests for proposals to accounting firms soon to select advisers, examining structures including buying existing shares, subscribing to new shares and taking over shareholder loans. It says it has a stake as a counterparty to the project's renewable energy certificate (REC) sales contract and needs to assess whether the project can be carried out. The project company's borrowings more than doubled to 268.2 billion won (approximately $199.7 million) at the end of last year and it posted an operating loss of 42.6 billion won (approximately $31.7 million), while suppliers including Siemens Gamesa, SK Oceanplant, LS Cable & System and CS Wind have walked away.
Key Elements 
Korea East-West Power Anma Offshore Wind Equis Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) Korea Midland Power Hoban Industrial Korea Development Bank CS Wind Daemyung Energy Siemens Gamesa SK Oceanplant LS Cable & System Anma Island in Yeonggwang 
South Korea's Korea East-West Power has emerged as a candidate to buy a stake in the Anma Offshore Wind project off Yeonggwang, South Jeolla Province, after Singapore-based investor Equis put its controlling stake up for sale only to see negotiations collapse. Attention is focused on whether a South Korean state-owned power generator will step in as rescuer for the 532 MW project, which faces being stranded as its largest shareholder withdraws and its supply chain falls apart.
According to investment banking sources, East-West Power is reviewing the possibility of acquiring a stake in Anma Offshore Wind. The company will soon send requests for proposals (RFPs) to South Korean and foreign accounting firms to begin selecting advisers. The move is aimed at launching a review of various deal structures, including buying existing shares held by current shareholders, participating in a new share issue, and taking over loans extended by existing shareholders.
The reason East-West Power is eyeing the project is its existing contractual relationship. Anma Offshore Wind was selected in the South Korean government's competitive wind power tender in 2024 and signed a renewable energy certificate (REC) sales contract in September last year. East-West Power is one of the generators, along with Korea Midland Power, that joined the contract. The company says that as a contract counterparty it has an interest in examining how far the project progresses and whether the contract can be fulfilled going forward.
Anma Offshore Wind is a project to build a 532 MW generation complex in waters near Anma Island in Yeonggwang County, South Jeolla Province. The plan centers on installing 38 wind turbines of 14 MW each, with total project cost estimated at about 4.9 trillion won (approximately $3.6 billion). Equis is a Singapore-based investor that develops and invests in energy and infrastructure assets in the Asia-Pacific region, and as of the end of last year it was the largest shareholder with a 78.09% stake in Anma Offshore Wind. The remaining shares are held by Hoban Industrial (6.64%), Korea Development Bank (6.13%), CS Wind (4.38%), Daemyung Energy (4.11%) and Daemyung GC (0.65%).
The background to Equis's sale is cited as the funding burden swollen by project delays and uncertainty over profitability. Because the project site overlaps with a weapons testing area used by the South Korean Agency for Defense Development (ADD), consultations with the South Korean Ministry of National Defense on military operational suitability and procedures for permits to occupy and use public waters dragged on for a long time, pushing back the start of construction and the schedule for closing project financing (PF). Military consultations are said to have been largely resolved since then, but financial costs and project expenses snowballed as permitting was delayed. Industry analysts say securing project viability became difficult as a relatively low bid price was combined with rising PF interest rates and exchange rate volatility.
To recover its investment, Equis had been negotiating a stake sale with Danish offshore wind investor Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) since late last year. However, the two sides reportedly failed to narrow differences over the acquisition price, project costs, repayment of borrowings to the lender group and conditions for financial close. According to foreign media reports, CIP considered withdrawing its investment commitment, citing differences in corporate valuation amid macroeconomic uncertainty, and the $2.5 billion (about 3.4 trillion won) borrowing that Equis was seeking to arrange is also in doubt.
The project company's financial condition has also deteriorated rapidly. Borrowings at the end of last year stood at 268.2 billion won (approximately $199.7 million), more than double the 124.5 billion won (approximately $92.7 million) at the end of the previous year. Over the same period, the operating loss widened to 42.6 billion won (approximately $31.7 million) from 37 billion won (approximately $27.6 million), and the net loss widened to 40.2 billion won (approximately $29.9 million) from 36.2 billion won (approximately $27.0 million). Cash flow from operating activities also posted a net outflow of 50 billion won (approximately $37.2 million) as funds were deployed for acquisitions of tangible assets and other items during the development stage.
Item End-2024 End-2025 
Borrowings 124.5 billion won 268.2 billion won 
Operating loss 37 billion won 42.6 billion won 
Net loss 36.2 billion won 40.2 billion won 
Note: Based on the Anma Offshore Wind project company
The burden of restarting the project has grown further with the departure of the supply chain. Turbine supplier Siemens Gamesa terminated its supply contract in April last year, citing the expiration of the contract period. SK Oceanplant, which had a contract to supply substructures, halted performance at the request of the ordering party, and LS Cable & System's subsea cable supply contract was also canceled. CS Wind has also pulled out of the project.
Whether East-West Power steps in could also affect the landscape of South Korea's offshore wind industry. One of the large offshore wind projects the South Korean government is seeking to foster to expand renewable energy supply simultaneously faces two tasks: replacing its largest shareholder and rebuilding its supply chain. Expectations are that if a state-owned power generator buys a stake, continuity in fulfilling the REC contract can be secured and orders for new turbines, substructures and cables can be placed again. On the other hand, some argue it is inappropriate for a state-owned company to inject funds when project viability has deteriorated, and the due diligence results after advisers are selected are expected to be a watershed.
How the deal structure is designed is also a key issue. Buying Equis's existing shares would require handling existing shareholders' loans and obtaining consent from the lender group, while participating in a new share issue would require consultations with existing shareholders over the size of the capital increase and stake dilution. Whichever card East-West Power chooses, the conditions for financial close on the 4.9 trillion won (approximately $3.6 billion) project will inevitably have to be renegotiated, analysts say.

content_text:
Clinical trials: New mRNA cancer vaccine plus Keytruda sharply improves melanoma survival
The Keytruda-intismeran combination reduced the risk of recurrence or death in patients with high-risk melanoma and may soon become a new treatment option.
By: Todd Neff 
Oct. 28, 2026 
An estimated 112,000 people in the United States will be diagnosed with melanoma this year, and more than 8,500 deaths are expected from the cancer’s spread to other parts of the body. Photo: Getty Images. 
If all goes well, a major advance in preventing the spread of melanoma, the deadliest skin cancer, could be just months away from U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval.
Moderna and Merck announced on Oct. 22 that a major phase 3 clinical trial had tracked with the success of a smaller phase 2 trial whose results the pharmaceutical companies released in early June . Both melanoma trials involved patients who had had cancers surgically removed but were at high risk of those cancers coming back and spreading to other organs.
The clinical trials combined Merck’s pembrolizumab (Keytruda) and Merck and Moderna’s jointly developed intismeran, an investigational, mRNA-based cancer vaccine. The drug combination showed remarkable effectiveness in the phase 3 trial: Patients on it had a 42% lower risk of recurrence or death two years out, the companies say.
Those results build up upon promising phase 2 findings Moderna and Merck announced in August . An average of five years after taking the drug combination for up to a year, those on the combination had a 49% lower chance of recurrence or death than those taking only Keytruda.
What’s new in melanoma research 
A phase 3 trial confirmed the success of an earlier study, whose data showed a 49% lower risk of recurrence or death for patients receiving the Keytruda-intiselimab combination compared with Keytruda alone.
Researchers hope the new mRNA cancer vaccine could become available within months if the FDA follows a review timeline similar to past melanoma immunotherapies.
The promising melanoma treatment targets unique markers on a patient’s tumor to help the immune system find and destroy lingering cancer cells.
Moderna and Merck already are studying the approach in lung, kidney and bladder cancers.
Not long ago, Keytruda alone brought a roughly 40% improvement on those fronts over prior melanoma treatments, said Dr. Theresa Medina , an oncologist specializing in melanoma at UCHealth University of Colorado Hospital . Medina, also an associate professor of medical oncology at University of Colorado Anschutz , led the phase 2 trial site at UCHealth, where about 20 patients participated.
“We’re very excited to have this, hopefully, as a future option,” Medina said.
The National Cancer Institute estimates that there will be about 112,000 new melanoma cases in the United States this year, with more than 8,500 deaths from melanoma’s spread to the lymph nodes, lungs, liver, bones, brain, and elsewhere. Colorado residents are at elevated risk given the thinner atmosphere to filter out ultraviolet rays that can lead to skin cancers.
How the Keytruda-intismeran combination works to fight melanoma 
Both intismeran and Keytruda are immunotherapies. They work by helping the immune system see invaders — in this case, melanoma cancer cells — that use various tricks to hide from it.
Dr. Theresa Medina is an oncologist specializing in melanoma at UCHealth University of Colorado Hospital and an associate professor of medical oncology at the University of Colorado Anschutz. 
Keytruda, which the FDA approved in September 2014, is a checkpoint-inhibitor immunotherapy. Melanoma and other cancer cells avoid immune system detection in part by producing proteins (PD-L1 and PD-L2) that bind to PD-1 receptors on the surface of immune system T cells. Those receptors normally are important “off” switches that stop T cells from attacking the body’s healthy tissue. Cancers exploit that. Keytruda works by binding to those PD-1 receptors before the cancer cells’ diversionary PD-L1 and PD-L2 proteins do. The T cells are then unblindfolded to the cancer cells and, ideally, attack them.
Intismeran works differently. Just as with Moderna’s mRNA coronavirus vaccine, intismeran sends tiny packets of messenger RNA into healthy cells. Those cells then crank out proteins based on the mRNA’s instructions.
With the coronavirus vaccine, those proteins mimic the COVID-19 spike protein . The immune system learns to recognize the vaccine-driven proteins as invaders, so if immune cells encounter an actual coronavirus, they recognize it and attack quickly, reducing the viral burden and the severity of subsequent illness.
The big difference with intismeran is that it’s tailored to the patient. Tissue from a patient’s surgically removed melanoma tumor goes to a lab, where staff sequence the DNA in the tumor. They look for sections of DNA that ultimately lead to the creation of “ neoantigens .” These are proteins that cancer cells produce, but healthy cells don’t, and they end up on the surface of cancer cells. There they act like chemical flags that say, in effect, “I’m a cancer cell.”
How Moderna and Merck target neoantigens with intismeran 
Various types of cancer cells produce thousands of different neoantigens, with a given cancer cell averaging about 150 of them. A key early step in making a patient-tailored batch of intismeran involves taking a snapshot, based on tumor DNA, of up to 34 of the neoantigens that tumor cells might produce.
In a process that takes about six weeks, staff then create millions of mRNA strands that will, once injected, cause the patient’s own healthy cells near the injection site to produce legions of proteins that look just like those up-to-34 different types of tumor-cell neoantigens. As with the coronavirus vaccine, the immune system recognizes the free-floating, mRNA-driven neoantigen proteins as invaders and learns to attack the cancer cells that have the actual neoantigens on their surfaces.
The Keytruda-intismeran combination isn’t the first where scientists have tried to combine Keytruda or Opdivo — another effective checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy — with other drugs, but those trials came up empty, Medina said.
The FDA’s approval decision will hinge on those phase 3 results, Medina said, and potentially also on patient-survival data, which could push approval out years. But there’s precedent for the FDA acting more quickly on a promising drug without that survival-related data: the approvals of Keytruda and Opdivo.
The FDA approved Keytruda, just over six months after Merck filed. Bristol-Myers Squibb waited seven-and-a-half months from their filing to Opdivo’s approval in December 2014.
Since then, the FDA has greenlit Keytruda for more than two dozen types of cancer, and Opdivo for more than a dozen . Merck and Moderna see a similar path for their Keytruda-intismeran combination. They’re already running trials of it for non-small cell lung cancer, kidney cancer, and bladder cancer.
A lot of patients are already asking for this promising melanoma treatment, Medina said.
“I wish it was available now,” she said.

Qualcomm RF Front End Expansion: Beyond Smartphones
Radu Trandafir
Cristiano Amon was excited and proud to announce Qualcomm Technologies’ deep forays into the automotive, Metaverse, PC and edge computing markets at CES 2022, in January.
 
Now we have the chance to hear directly from one of the key business units about Qualcomm’s world beyond mobiles: Christian Block, SVP and General Manager of Qualcomm’s RF Front End (FE) business unit presented how the modem-to-antenna solutions developed initially for smartphones and mobile communications are penetrating other key areas where data exchanges are happening wirelessly: automotive, IoT & edge networking, personal computing, wearables and extended reality (XR), and industrial IoT.
Having a true end-to-end, modem-to-antenna solution and capitalizing on the benefits of having developed class-leading mobile applications with integrated baseband (BB) processors/modems, there is nothing missing from Qualcomm’s portfolio.
Figure 1: Qualcomm’s modem-to-antenna device portfolio coverage (Source: Qualcomm Technologies Inc.) 
The “modem-to antenna” solution is not just a well garnished portfolio of stand-alone components, rather a well thought out, holistic system design, where RF H/W and BB processing together with other algorithms like SmartTransmit 2.0, work seamlessly to deliver their best performance.
Subscribe to TechInsights Blogs
Join our list to get the latest blog posts directly in your email.
There is still room for 3 rd party RF FE components to substitute some of Qualcomm’s own to better suit the OEM’s needs, however, it is to be expected that the Qualcomm modem + transceiver combinations perform at their best when used with the rest of the Qualcomm RF FE family.
Figure 2: The near future is bright, here are the projections for the RF FE business unit for the 2022 to 2024 interval. “In fiscal year 2021, Qualcomm Technologies reached the #1 position in RFFE revenues for handsets.” (Source: Qualcomm Technologies Inc.) 
Even though the specifications for IEEE 802.11be are still with the standards working groups – and it wouldn’t surprise us to learn that the modems are ready to receive updated firmware (F/W) loads to make them compatible with the standard when it will be released, Qualcomm is ready with their 3 rd generation of RF FE components which are being introduced today.
These are LNA – PA combo for WiFi applications, with and without RF shields, designed for 5G coexistence, “complement(ing) Qualcomm® ultraBAW™ filters to allow 5G/Wi-Fi concurrency” and are “purpose-built design(s) for Wi-Fi 6E/7 (to) showcase the Company’s leadership in both wireless technologies” .
Figure 3: Source: Qualcomm Technologies Inc. 
Introducing the 3 rd generation Qualcomm WiFi 6e/7 and Bluetooth RF FE modules: the QXM108x family and QXM1910AQ. “ The modules are designed for a wide array of device segments beyond smartphones – including automotive, XR, PCs, wearables, mobile broadband, IoT, and more .”
Figure 4: Third generation RF FE components Wi-Fi7 ready (Source: Qualcomm Technologies Inc.) 
The newly announced FE modules are expected to launch in H2 2022 but modules are already sampling to customers. These modules can be used “along with Qualcomm Technologies’ client connectivity products, such as Qualcomm® FastConnectTM 7800 Wi-Fi 7/Bluetooth Systems and Snapdragon® 5G Modem-RF Systems – for cutting-edge wireless devices such as those featuring Snapdragon® Connect. Or they can use 3rd party Wi-Fi and Bluetooth chipsets along with the modules.”

content_text:
ON Semiconductor Falls 5%, NXP Semiconductors Drops 4% as Soft Guidance Revives Auto Chip Worries; Skyworks Ticks Up, Qualcomm and Texas Instruments Dip
NXP Semiconductors beat earnings estimates but its cautious outlook sent auto-exposed chipmakers sliding, and the ripple effect is hitting ON Semiconductor harder than NXP itself. Whether that selloff signals a broader auto chip downturn or a buying opportunity depends on…
By David Moadel 
Published October 28, 2026, 1:20pm ET · 3 min read 
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel .
𝕏 
f 
⧉ 
A tangled pile of discarded electronic components visually represents the competitive landscape of the ongoing chip war. As Apple dominates, some of Google's partners might be left with the remnants. © Sebastian_Photography / Shutterstock.com 
Handset-focused peers are a mixed bag today, it seems. Soft guidance from NXP Semiconductors ( NASDAQ:NXPI | NXPI Price Prediction ) is hitting the chipmakers most tied to the auto industry. ON Semiconductor ( NASDAQ:ON ) stock is at $75 in afternoon trading, down 5%, the biggest drop in the group.
NXP stock is at $245, down 4%. Skyworks Solutions ( NASDAQ:SWKS ) stock is at $87, up 1%, moving against the selling in auto-linked chip names.
NXP Pairs a Strong Quarter With a Softer Outlook
After the close on October 27, NXP reported Q3 2026 results that looked strong on their own.
Sales at NXP Semiconductors reached $3.79 billion, up 19% from a year earlier, ahead of Wall Street analysts’ consensus of $3.76 billion. Demand at NXP was broad, too, with management describing growth in every region.
On the bottom line, NXP Semiconductors earned adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $4.20, exceeding Wall Street analysts’ consensus of $4.12. Where NXP disappointed was its outlook for the final quarter of the year.
NXP Semiconductors guided Q4 2026 revenue to $3.75 billion to $3.95 billion, a midpoint of $3.85 billion versus Wall Street analysts’ consensus of $3.86 billion. That shortfall is slight, and the company’s adjusted EPS guide at the midpoint exceeding the consensus of Wall Street analysts, $4.34.
The midpoint of that range implies NXP Semiconductors’ revenue growth slowing to 15% from a year earlier. In Q3, NXP Semiconductors’ automotive business, which makes up more than half of the company’s sales, grew 13%, trailing the company’s overall pace.
TE Connectivity ( NYSE:TEL ) has also named weaker vehicle production as a constraint on its fiscal 2027, adding to concerns about chip demand from carmakers. A new $5 billion addition to NXP Semiconductors’ buyback hasn’t been enough to offset that read.
ON Semiconductor and Skyworks Split on Auto Exposure
ON Semiconductor is trading on a read-across from NXP’s auto numbers. The company sells power chips. These include silicon carbide devices used in electric-vehicle inverters and industrial power conversion, so auto demand carries more weight for it than for most peers. That exposure helps explain why ON Semiconductor is falling harder than NXP itself. Even so, ON Semiconductor stock is up 38% year to date (YTD).
Skyworks is the contrast, selling radio-frequency chips for smartphones, and the iPhone maker is its largest customer. An auto slowdown barely touches that business, and Skyworks stock has gained ground over the past week as well.
Chip funds are moving the same way. The iShares Semiconductor ETF is at $517, up 1%, a sign the selling is concentrated in auto-exposed names. Tech overall is quieter, with the Invesco QQQ Trust at $722, up 0.1%.
Qualcomm ( NASDAQ:QCOM ) stock is at $182, down 1%. Texas Instruments ( NASDAQ:TXN ) is sliding as well, with its stock at $305, down 1%. Handset exposure hasn’t fully protected Qualcomm, which cuts against a perfectly clean split between auto and smartphone chipmakers.
The two stocks are dipping from very different starting points. Since the start of the year, Texas Instruments stock is up 79%. Gains at Qualcomm are more modest, with the stock up 8% YTD. NXP stock is up 14% YTD as well, even after the drop.
What ON Semiconductor’s Next Report Could Reveal
For ON Semiconductor, the question is whether its upcoming quarterly report shows the same auto drag that NXP’s numbers suggested at. On August 3, ON Semiconductor’s management called automotive “very stable with a good outlook,” a view the company’s next results could confirm or revise. A pending acquisition of Synaptics ( NASDAQ:SYNA ) which was revised earlier this month, adds another moving piece to the ON Semiconductor story. For NXP, the risk is a Q4 that lands at the low end of its range if auto demand weakens further.
The bulls can point to NXP’s earnings beat, its expanded buyback and ON Semiconductor’s strong run this year as signs the auto worry may be overdone. The bears, meanwhile, see slower auto growth at NXP as an early warning that could spread to ON Semiconductor and other suppliers to carmakers. Interest rates add one more variable, with the Federal Reserve’s policy decision scheduled for today. For traders, waiting could make sense until ON Semiconductor’s auto outlook becomes clearer.

VCU School of Nursing and VCU Health honored with national award for exemplary academic-practice collaboration
The American Association of Colleges of Nursing recognized the VCU partnership for building strong connections between academics and clinical care.
Share this story
Share on X (Twitter) 
Share on Facebook 
Share on LinkedIn 
Print page 
By Joe Schilling
School of Nursing 
The American Association of Colleges of Nursing has awarded the Virginia Commonwealth University School of Nursing and VCU Health System the prestigious 2026 AACN Exemplary Academic-Practice Partnership Award. This national honor recognizes an integrated model between the two institutions that bridges clinical care, academic inquiry and community health. 
The AACN Exemplary Academic-Practice Partnership Award celebrates member institutions and healthcare systems that demonstrate highly productive, collaborative relationships aligned with the eight AACN/American Organization for Nursing Leadership Guiding Principles and the 2021 AACN Essentials: Core Competencies for Professional Nursing Education. 
In an era marked by nationwide clinical staffing shortages and shifting healthcare demands, the VCU partnership stands out as a national benchmark — proving how a research-intensive urban university and Virginia’s largest safety-net academic health system can build a bidirectional ecosystem where clinical practice informs the classroom, faculty scholarship elevates bedside care and joint initiatives directly improve patient outcomes.
“Earning this award is a significant achievement and reflects the strength of our collaboration with our School of Nursing colleagues,” said Amber Balzer, DNP, director of advanced practice professional development and fellowship for VCU Health. “The application process was extensive and truly a team effort, requiring thoughtful contributions from partners across both organizations.”
The partnership rests on deliberately dismantling traditional academic and clinical silos. VCU Health operates VCU Medical Center , an urban academic medical center, as well as VCU Health Community Memorial Hospital and VCU Health Tappahannock Hospital . Less than three blocks away stands the VCU School of Nursing, a nationally ranked institution educating undergraduate, master’s, Doctor of Nursing Practice and Ph.D. scholars.
Formalized in 2021, the partnership’s executive governance structure includes quarterly strategic sessions among the School of Nursing dean, chief nursing officers, associate chief nursing officers and the associate vice president of advanced practice providers, along with monthly faculty practice assemblies. To ensure alignment across all clinical environments, 70 key stakeholders across 14 focus groups co-designed the shared leadership framework. 
“Quarterly gatherings of our respective leadership teams are crucial to building trust between the School of Nursing and VCU Health and to helping ensure the needs of both institutions are met,” said Patricia Kinser, Ph.D., dean of the VCU School of Nursing.
Central to this collaboration is a bidirectional model: numerous School of Nursing faculty members maintain active clinical practices embedded across VCU Health units. At the same time, the school’s appointment, promotion and tenure guidelines formally recognize clinical practice excellence, allowing five faculty members to earn academic promotion through clinical and scholarly excellence.
“Academic-practice partnerships cannot simply be administrative agreements on paper; they must live and breathe at the bedside and in the lecture hall,” said Lana Sargent , Ph.D., associate dean of practice and community engagement in the School of Nursing. “Our tripartite mission of teaching, scholarship and service works because the exchange is truly bidirectional. When our faculty practice inside a Level I trauma center, they bring current clinical complexities and evidence-based innovations straight back to our students. In turn, our students and scholars analyze real-time health system data to solve operational challenges, advance health equity, and elevate the standard of patient care. We are educating nurses in the exact environment where they will lead and heal.”
The collaboration has transformed nursing workforce development across Central Virginia. Between 2021 and 2026, the undergraduate nursing programs doubled, now training more than 650 undergraduate students, most of whom rotate directly through VCU Health facilities. At the graduate level, 237 health system clinicians have mentored 727 advanced practice students, completing 77,890 clinical hours — including 17,899 hours overseen directly through faculty practice.
To foster retention and career mobility for frontline healthcare workers, the partners established a guaranteed admission pathway into the RN-to-BS for VCU Health System registered nurses holding associate degrees . VCU Health supports these nurses by reimbursing application fees and providing tuition assistance, while the School of Nursing maintains dedicated web portals and streamlined application reviews.
After being hired into the health system, new graduates enter an enterprise-wide nurse residency program that recently earned a 10-year Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education accreditation. With School of Nursing faculty serving on the advisory board and guiding curriculum delivery, the program enrolled 318 nurse residents in CY2025 alone — nearly a third of whom graduated from VCU. The program boasts an 87.1% one-year retention rate (up from 86% in CY2024), with 90.5% of participants successfully advancing to Clinical Nurse II within 24 months, vastly outpacing national retention averages. 
"The AACN Exemplary Academic-Practice Partnership Award is undeniable proof of our shared commitment to measurable outcomes and practice readiness,” said Mary Marshman, DNP, chief nursing officer at VCU Medical Center. “Thanks to this partnership between the School of Nursing and VCU Health, graduates enter our workforce with clinical judgment, hands-on experience, and knowledge of VCU Health nursing practices that ensures they are ready to contribute effectively from day one.”
Beyond workforce numbers, the partnership drives healthcare quality improvement. DNP projects linked directly to health system strategic priorities have expanded from six in spring 2023 to 55 projected through 2027.
These efforts have also led to substantial financial impacts through cost-saving for the health system and increased patient satisfaction metrics. Demonstrating the health system’s commitment to advanced practice leadership, the health system appointed an advanced practice provider as its first associate vice president of quality and safety .
Scholarly dissemination has flourished concurrently. Collaborative teams have produced more than 30 conference presentations, 46 grand rounds sessions, six jointly funded research grants totaling over $128,000 and seven peer-reviewed publications in journals such as the Journal of the American Association of Nurse Practitioners, the American Journal of Critical Care and The American Surgeon.
The partnership’s impact reaches deep into medically underserved communities across the region. Through the Mobile Health and Wellness Program , faculty and nursing students deliver preventive and chronic disease care across eight rural and urban communities.
The 2026 AACN Exemplary Academic-Practice Partnership Award affirms the VCU School of Nursing and VCU Health’s shared vision: an academic-practice model that transforms nursing education into measurable community wellness and bedside excellence.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

Revenues are expected to be $10.15 billion, down 10% from the year-ago quarter. 
Estimate Revisions Trend 
The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 2.02% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period. 
Investors should keep in mind that the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts may not always get reflected in the aggregate change. 
Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction). 
The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier. 
Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only. 
A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

For Qualcomm, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.51%. 
On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #4. 
So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Qualcomm will beat the consensus EPS estimate. 
Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue? 
Analysts often consider to what extent a company has been able to match consensus estimates in the past while calculating their estimates for its future earnings. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number. 
For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Qualcomm would post earnings of $2.22 per share when it actually produced earnings of $2.21, delivering a surprise of -0.45%. 
Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates three times. 
Bottom Line 
An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss. 
That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. Onsemi is in talks to acquire chip startup Ferric for about $1 billion, The Information reported on Oct. 27 local time.
The Information, citing sources, said the deal could be completed within days, though terms could change or the talks could fall through.
The structure of the deal was not disclosed. The Information said it could include terms under which Ferric is paid based on meeting performance targets.
Rival Analog Devices agreed in May to buy Empower Semiconductor, a startup developing devices that improve power efficiency for AI chips, for $1.5 billion.
Onsemi provides semiconductors that manage power for vehicles, factories and AI data centres. As electricity consumption in data centres rises, chip companies are looking for new technologies that can deliver power to chips without power loss, The Information said.
Onsemi posted revenue of $6 billion last year and has recently accelerated efforts to expand its business scope. In October, it agreed to buy listed company Synaptics for $5.7 billion in cash. The Information said the Synaptics deal could allow Onsemi to expand sales of sensors and processors for smart devices.

eBeam Initiatives Review: High-NA EUV, Chiplets, Physical AI and Advanced Packaging Insights
An expert panel discussion covered by Jan Willis of eBeam Initiatives examined large-format masks, equipment investment, high-NA EUV and curvilinear masks. Kevin Rinebold and Andras Vass-Varnai of Siemens discussed the industry's movement toward chiplet-based and heterogeneous design, noting that system technology co-optimization and multiphysics analysis are growing essential for tackling thermal, power and integration bottlenecks.
Sumit Vishwakarma of Synopsys maintained that physical AI systems will call for a new engineering discipline that co-designs and validates interactions among silicon, sensors, software, mechanics and power through a holistic, physics-aware method. Reela Samuel of Cadence noted that with AI increasingly able to generate RTL, propose ECOs, modify constraints or create verification properties, determining whether a design still satisfies its requirements has become more critical than ever.
Alan Chen of Arm explored how source-less microarchitectural analysis can be enabled through an evidence-first harness engineering approach combining indexed workload data, bounded LLM analysis and simulation evidence to improve optimization outcomes. Eric Yu of Keysight explained why tensor parallelism is the first parallelism dimension that any scale-up fabric, whether NVLink or Ethernet, must get right.
Paul Carey of SEMI identified seven themes shaping the MEMS and sensors industry, with markets such as robotics and medical introducing new requirements and opportunities for differentiation. Germain Fenger of Synopsys demonstrated why better models, richer metrology, explainable AI and cross-industry collaboration must converge to extend semiconductor scaling.
Gerard John of Amkor outlined why today's high-performance processors are increasingly systems in their own right. Qingpeng Wang of Lam Research showed how a self-aligned CFET process sequence for SRAM and logic achieves higher performance through larger effective channel width and improved electrostatics at smaller nodes.
Kaladhar Radhakrishnan, Nicolas Butzen and Vishal Javvaji of Intel Foundry dug into how integrated voltage regulators lower current density, deliver higher regulation bandwidth and lessen reliance on large decoupling capacitor networks. Clemens Leichtle of Advantest outlined new photonics test requirements, including fiber alignment, coupling efficiency, polarization management and optical instrumentation.

eBeam Initiatives Review: High-NA EUV, Chiplets, Physical AI and Advanced Packaging Insights
An expert panel discussion covered by Jan Willis of eBeam Initiatives examined large-format masks, equipment investment, high-NA EUV and curvilinear masks. Kevin Rinebold and Andras Vass-Varnai of Siemens discussed the industry's movement toward chiplet-based and heterogeneous design, noting that system technology co-optimization and multiphysics analysis are growing essential for tackling thermal, power and integration bottlenecks.
Sumit Vishwakarma of Synopsys maintained that physical AI systems will call for a new engineering discipline that co-designs and validates interactions among silicon, sensors, software, mechanics and power through a holistic, physics-aware method. Reela Samuel of Cadence noted that with AI increasingly able to generate RTL, propose ECOs, modify constraints or create verification properties, determining whether a design still satisfies its requirements has become more critical than ever.
Alan Chen of Arm explored how source-less microarchitectural analysis can be enabled through an evidence-first harness engineering approach combining indexed workload data, bounded LLM analysis and simulation evidence to improve optimization outcomes. Eric Yu of Keysight explained why tensor parallelism is the first parallelism dimension that any scale-up fabric, whether NVLink or Ethernet, must get right.
Paul Carey of SEMI identified seven themes shaping the MEMS and sensors industry, with markets such as robotics and medical introducing new requirements and opportunities for differentiation. Germain Fenger of Synopsys demonstrated why better models, richer metrology, explainable AI and cross-industry collaboration must converge to extend semiconductor scaling.
Gerard John of Amkor outlined why today's high-performance processors are increasingly systems in their own right. Qingpeng Wang of Lam Research showed how a self-aligned CFET process sequence for SRAM and logic achieves higher performance through larger effective channel width and improved electrostatics at smaller nodes.
Kaladhar Radhakrishnan, Nicolas Butzen and Vishal Javvaji of Intel Foundry dug into how integrated voltage regulators lower current density, deliver higher regulation bandwidth and lessen reliance on large decoupling capacitor networks. Clemens Leichtle of Advantest outlined new photonics test requirements, including fiber alignment, coupling efficiency, polarization management and optical instrumentation.

content_text:
Breaking the Japanese monopoly grip, Korean display industry bets on new OLED technology
By KIM Nami 
5:50 p.m. 
Oct 28, 2026 
Korean companies spend 600 billion won annually on FMM purchases effectively monopolized by Japanese firms… LG Display develops new technology that eliminates the need for FMM
An LG Display-related product is on display at the 'K-Display 2026 Korea Display Industry Exhibition' at COEX in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. /NEWS1 photo by Lee Jong-soo 
Domestic display companies leading the global OLED (organic light-emitting diode) panel market have moved to reduce their dependence on a key component that has been effectively monopolized by Japan through a technological shift. 
They are pursuing both improved panel performance and technological self-reliance not only by domesticating Japanese-made components, but also by developing new processes that do not use the components themselves.
According to the electronics industry on Thursday, Japanese companies account for approximately 90% of the global FMM (fine metal mask) market. An FMM is a component made by drilling tens of millions of microscopic holes smaller than a human hair into a metal sheet thinner than paper. Much like a painter uses a stencil to spray paint, OLED red, green, and blue (RGB) light-emitting materials are deposited through these holes to form pixels.
Domestic companies lead the OLED panel market with approximately 70% market share. Since becoming the first in the world to sell large-size OLED TV panels in 2013, LG Display has expanded its business into monitors and achieved cumulative sales of 50 million large-size OLED panels. However, the supply chain for FMMs, a key component in OLED panel production, is effectively controlled by Japanese companies. Dependence on Japanese-made products is close to 100%.
In particular, Japan's DNP (Dai Nippon Printing) holds approximately 70% of the global FMM market, occupying a near-monopoly position. It is estimated that domestic companies spend at least 60 billion won annually on FMM purchases from DNP alone. An industry official explained that DNP holds the upper hand in supply negotiations based on its high market share and technological capabilities.
Effect of LG Display's FLiPP technology compared to existing FMM process / Graphic by Kim Hyeon-jung 
Japan's influence is also formidable in the raw materials sector for FMMs. 'Invar,' a thin film of iron-nickel alloy that serves as the core material for FMMs, is supplied primarily by Japan's Proterial (formerly Hitachi Metals). 
In the equipment market for depositing light-emitting materials using FMMs, Canon Tokki, a subsidiary of Japan's Canon, also exerts strong influence. A single Canon Tokki deposition machine costs well over 1 trillion won (based on 8.6-generation lines). Japanese companies thus exert strong influence across the entire spectrum of materials, components and equipment that are central to OLED production.
Domestic display companies have begun developing next-generation OLED processes that do not use FMMs in order to change this supply chain structure. A representative technology is 'FLiPP' developed by LG Display. 
FLiPP is a process that forms RGB pixels using photolithography technology, which is used in semiconductor manufacturing, instead of the conventional FMM. It involves depositing organic light-emitting material across the entire substrate and then using light to remove unnecessary parts. Because it does not use an FMM, it can reduce dependence on key Japanese-made components.
The effect on panel performance improvement is also significant. According to LG Display, utilizing FLiPP can raise the aperture ratio from approximately 42% in existing processes to 65%. 
The aperture ratio is the proportion of the total pixel area that actually emits light. As the light-emitting area expands, brightness can be increased by up to 1.6 times or lifespan extended by up to 2.4 times compared to conventional methods. A reduction in power consumption is also expected.
Furthermore, the existing FMM method has a problem where the center of the metal mask sags downward as its size increases. Consequently, the existing FMM method involves the constraint that large glass substrates must be cut for use. In contrast, FLiPP can utilize an entire 8.5-generation mother glass sheet measuring 2.2 meters wide and 2.5 meters long. 
Theoretically, it can produce everything from 1-inch-class smartwatches to ultra-large TVs of 100 inches or more using a single process. Material utilization efficiency can be raised from 40% to 74%.
The significance of FLiPP lies in changing the approach to technological self-reliance itself. It secures a new production process that does not require the component, going beyond merely domesticating components imported from overseas. 
LG Display is first pushing for application in IT products such as laptops and monitors, with plans to expand the scope of application according to future customer demand. Samsung Display is also researching and developing next-generation OLED patterning technology that does not use FMMs.
However, it is expected that new processes will be difficult to completely replace the existing FMM method in the short term. Investment burdens associated with introducing new equipment, securing mass production yields, and stabilizing the process are cited as challenges to be resolved. 
An industry official said, "It will be difficult to introduce non-FMM methods into all OLED production immediately," adding, "Even if the new technology enters the mass production stage, it is highly likely that it will run in parallel with existing FMM processes for a while."

Battery Binder Market to Reach USD 8.44 Billion by 2035, Growing from USD 2.60 Billion in 2025 - SRI
10-28-2026 07:17 AM CET | Chemicals & Materials 
Press release from: Strategic Revenue Insights Inc. 
Battery Binder Market
London, UK - October 2026 | Strategic Revenue Insights Inc. - Electric vehicle battery output, stationary storage build-out, silicon anodes and high-nickel cathodes and water-based and PFAS-free binders are driving strong growth in battery binders.
https://www.strategicrevenueinsights.com/industry/battery-binder-market 
The Battery Binder market was valued at USD 2.60 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 8.44 billion by 2035, growing at a CAGR of 12.5%, according to Strategic Revenue Insights Inc. The report was prepared by lead analyst Lukas Schmidt. The research methodology combines primary interviews with relevant industry stakeholders, including binder and fluoropolymer producers, battery cell manufacturers, electrode material suppliers and automakers, with secondary data across the regions covered by the report.
KEY TAKEAWAYS
Market value is projected to rise from USD 2.60 billion in 2025 to USD 8.44 billion by 2035, at a CAGR of 12.5%.
PVDF is the largest binder type with a 38.00% share, while Polyacrylic Acid and Others is the fastest-growing type at a 16.0% CAGR.
Cathode Binder is the largest electrode segment at 46.00% while Separator Coating Binder grows fastest at 15.5%, Lithium-Ion accounts for 94.00% of demand by chemistry while Solid-State grows fastest at 25.6%, and Electric Vehicles are the largest application at 61.00% while Energy Storage Systems grow fastest at 14.8%.
Asia Pacific is the largest regional market with a 70.00% share, valued at USD 1.82 billion in 2025, and shares the fastest growth rate of 12.7% with North America.
Named market participants include Arkema, Kureha, and Solvay.
Full report access: https://www.strategicrevenueinsights.com/industry/battery-binder-market 
GROWTH DRIVERS AND TRENDS
Electric vehicle battery output is the largest growth driver, adding an estimated 3.6 percentage points to the CAGR, followed by stationary storage build-out at 2.8 points, silicon anodes and high-nickel cathodes at 2.1 points, and water-based and PFAS-free binders at 1.6 points. The source projects the market at USD 4.69 billion in 2030.
Key trends identified in the report include a shift from solvent-based to water-based binders and from simple to specialized binders. Opportunities include water-based cathode binders, binders for silicon-rich anodes, and separator coating binders for safety. 2035 scenarios range from USD 7.00 billion to USD 9.80 billion.
MARKET SEGMENTATION
By type, the market is segmented into PVDF (38.00%), SBR (24.00%), CMC (18.00%), Acrylic (11.00%), and Polyacrylic Acid and Others (9.00%). PVDF is the largest segment with an 11.7% CAGR, and Polyacrylic Acid and Others is the fastest-growing at 16.0%, followed by Acrylic at 13.3%.
By electrode, the market covers Cathode Binder (46.00%), Anode Binder (44.00%), and Separator Coating Binder (10.00%). Cathode Binder is the largest segment with an 11.9% CAGR, and Separator Coating Binder is the fastest-growing at 15.5%.
By battery chemistry, the market includes Lithium-Ion (94.00%), Sodium-Ion (4.00%), and Solid-State (2.00%). Lithium-Ion is the largest segment with an 11.5% CAGR, and Solid-State is the fastest-growing at 25.6%, followed by Sodium-Ion at 20.6%.
By application, the market is divided into Electric Vehicles (61.00%), Consumer Electronics (17.00%), Energy Storage Systems (16.00%), and Industrial (6.00%). Electric Vehicles is the largest segment with a 13.0% CAGR, and Energy Storage Systems is the fastest-growing at 14.8%, while Consumer Electronics is the slowest at 8.3%.
REGIONAL OUTLOOK
The report covers North America, Europe, Asia Pacific, Latin America, and the Middle East and Africa. Asia Pacific is the largest regional market with a 70.00% share, valued at USD 1.82 billion in 2025 and projected to reach USD 6.04 billion by 2035 at a 12.7% CAGR, a rate it shares with North America as the fastest. North America holds 12.00% (USD 312.00 million, rising to USD 1.03 billion), Europe 13.00% (USD 338.00 million, rising to USD 990.37 million) with an 11.3% CAGR, the Middle East and Africa 3.00% (reaching USD 239.00 million) with 11.8%, and Latin America 2.00% (reaching USD 145.67 million) with 10.9%.
COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE
The report profiles Arkema (France, about 12.0% share), which supplies PVDF binder grades for lithium-ion cathodes and separator coatings; Kureha (Japan, 10.0%), which makes PVDF binders for cathodes and has long supplied Japanese and Korean cell makers; Solvay (Belgium, 8.0%), which produces PVDF for cathodes and works on grades for higher-voltage chemistries; Zeon (Japan, 7.0%), which supplies SBR and acrylic binder latexes for anodes and separator coatings; Shandong Huaxia Shenzhou (China, 6.0%), which makes PVDF and related fluoropolymers for Chinese lithium-ion cell producers; and Daikin (Japan, 5.0%), which offers fluoropolymer binders for electrodes and fluorine-based battery materials. LG Chem, Ashland, Resonac and Nippon A&L are also covered.
MARKET RESTRAINTS
Fluorspar and PVDF price swings reduce the CAGR by an estimated 1.7 percentage points, and qualification time subtracts a further 1.2 points. The report also cites PFAS rules on fluoropolymers, Chinese price competition, and dry electrode processes that reduce binder use.

SCHOTT Poonawalla renamed SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited 
The name change takes effect on October 28, 2026, with no changes to ownership, management, operations, products or services
By EP News Bureau on October 28, 2026 
SCHOTT Poonawalla Private Limited will become SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited with effect from October 28, 2026, marking a new chapter in the company’s journey and strengthening its connection with the global SCHOTT Pharma organisation. 
The new identity reflects the India business’s place within SCHOTT Pharma’s global network and its role in advancing drug containment and delivery solutions for the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries. It brings together the company’s manufacturing footprint, customer relationships and market expertise in India with SCHOTT Pharma’s global capabilities, innovation and scientific expertise. 
The company stated that the change is limited to its name and does not affect its ownership, management, employees, business strategy, operations, products, services or existing customer commitments. 
The transition reinforces SCHOTT Pharma India’s commitment to customers in India and international markets, while establishing a consistent connection with the global SCHOTT Pharma brand. 
Building on a heritage of more than 140 years, the new identity brings the company’s heritage and future ambitions under one global name, reflecting SCHOTT Pharma’s values of innovation, quality, scientific expertise and trust. 
Commenting on the development, Roy Joseph, CEO and Managing Director, SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited, said, “SCHOTT Pharma India represents the next chapter of our journey, combining our strength in India with SCHOTT Pharma’s global innovation and expertise. We see significant opportunity to build on our capabilities, deepen collaboration with pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners, and advance drug containment and delivery solutions. As we move forward, our focus remains on growing with our customers and contributing to the safe and reliable delivery of critical therapies to patients worldwide.” 
Dr Christian Mias, CEO of SCHOTT Pharma AG & Co. KGaA, SCHOTT Pharma India’s major shareholder, said, “SCHOTT Pharma India plays a critical role in patient care. With more than 3 billion containers produced annually, this company enables around 7,000 injections to reach patients every minute. The name change from SCHOTT Poonawalla to SCHOTT Pharma India reinforces our strategic partnership and confirms our long-term commitment to India as a key pharma hub.” 
The new identity builds on the company’s operations in India. During the COVID-19 pandemic, its pharmaceutical vials supported more than 4.3 billion vaccine doses worldwide, including 3 billion doses in India. 
As India’s only manufacturer of glass pre-fillable syringes and sterile formats, the company also contributes to local supply capabilities. It continues to invest in manufacturing capacity expansions for pre-fillable syringes and cartridges to support the requirements of biologics, biosimilars, GLP-1-based treatments and other injectable therapies. 
Going forward, SCHOTT Pharma India will focus on expanding its capabilities in pharmaceutical drug containment and delivery solutions, driving innovation through customer collaboration, and strengthening operational excellence and sustainability. These priorities will support the company in responding to the needs of pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies and contribute to India’s role in the global pharmaceutical value chain.

“God bless your hands,” was just one expression of gratitude for medical professionals from Carl R. Darnall Army Medical Center that helped support an Operation Panamanian partnership from late August to early September.
The team, comprising Army ophthalmologists, nurses, operating room technicians and patient administrators , performed more than 100 cataract surgeries at Hospital San Miguel Arcángel, helping Panamanians regain their vision and improve their quality of life.
Maj. Cameron Maxon and Maj. Shyam Patel, anesthesiologists; and Maj. Matthew Ricci, an ophthalmologist, represented the CRDAMC team
“From the surgeon’s standpoint, one of the main difficulties was the severity of the cataracts we were seeing,” said Ricci. “The cataracts were more severe than most we see in the United States, which made surgery more technically challenging.”
The collaboration with our Army nursing and anesthesia team and the local nurses and anesthesiologists made things easy for us and allowed us to focus solely on performing surgery, he added.
“Overall, it was an exceptional experience,” said Patel. “We made an impact on over 100 people directly, bonded with the local anesthesiologists and shared our various experiences and expertise.”
Cataracts, a clouding of the eye’s lens that can cause blurred vision and blindness, can significantly affect a person’s ability to perform everyday activities. Through the partnership program, the Army medical team provided surgical care to patients whose vision had been impaired by the condition for many years.
“Though not involved in the post-operative care as an anesthesiologist, I heard of all the gratitude from the various other ophthalmologists,” said Patel. “During the first week, one of the doctors informed me that a patient started crying as she was able to see for the first time in over 10 years. She was able to see her grandkids for the first time.”
Maxon, a father of three, felt the entire mission was defined as a success after treating a mother who had developed severe cataracts while undergoing chemotherapy for cancer. “A mother with children the same age as mine, hadn’t seen one of her children since they were an infant. Another child she hadn’t seen since birth,” said Maxon. “She said she could never thank us enough for restoring her vision and letting her finally see her babies.”
The mission demonstrated the value of collaboration among medical professionals and strengthened the partnership through the delivery of specialized care to the Panamanian community.
The team navigated a minor language barrier, a new environment, and new or unfamiliar equipment. By combining their expertise alongside local medical partners, the team demonstrated they were medically ready to perform cataract surgeries in a challenging environment, enhance their medical skills and support international medical cooperation.

[News] Applied Materials to Double BESI Stake to 20% on Hybrid Bonding Demand, Pending U.S. Antitrust Review
2026-10-27 
Semiconductors 
editor 
Applied Materials is strengthening its position in advanced chip packaging as demand for AI-related semiconductor technologies continues to grow. According to Reuters , the U.S. semiconductor equipment maker plans to increase its stake in Dutch company BE Semiconductor Industries (BESI) from 9% to approximately 20%, deepening a partnership focused on advanced packaging technologies for AI chips.
Applied Materials, BESI’s largest shareholder since acquiring a 9% stake in April 2025, has entered into an accelerated share purchase agreement to acquire additional shares in the company, subject to U.S. antitrust review. The company said it does not intend to increase its stake beyond approximately 20% or seek representation on BESI’s board.
The expanded partnership will focus on next-generation chip interconnect and packaging technologies for AI semiconductors. Applied Materials and BESI have collaborated on hybrid bonding technology since 2020, Reuters notes. According to ijiwei , BESI holds approximately 70% of the global hybrid bonding equipment market.
BESI’s Hybrid Bonding Technology Gains Momentum
Hybrid bonding directly joins copper interconnects and dielectric layers without conventional bumps, enabling denser connections between chips. According to Chosun Biz , the companies have jointly developed Kinex, an integrated die-to-wafer hybrid bonding system that combines Applied Materials’ expertise in etching, planarization, deposition and inspection with BESI’s precision die placement and assembly technologies.
BESI is a leading supplier of hybrid bonding equipment. As noted by ijiwei, its flagship Datacon 8800 CHAMEO ultra plus AC system offers alignment accuracy of 100 nanometers and throughput of up to 2,000 cycles per hour (CPH), highlighting the technology’s potential for high-volume manufacturing.
Demand for the technology is gaining momentum. Reuters reported on October 22 that BESI’s third-quarter orders rose 96% year over year to €342.6 million, while hybrid bonding equipment orders in the first nine months of 2026 more than doubled compared with the full-year 2025 level. BESI ‘s latest earnings release further shows that its hybrid bonding customer base has expanded to 23, with cumulative equipment demand exceeding 215 systems.

Corning Earnings: Another Step Forward While Shares Stay Attractive
For us, this is a moaty, diversified technology leader with strong AI exposure at a discount.
William Kerwin, CFA
Oct 27, 2026 
Share 
John Greim/LightRocket via Getty Securities in This Article
Corning Inc
(GLW)
Key Morningstar Metrics for Corning
Fair Value Estimate 
: $155.00
Morningstar Rating 
: ★★★★
Morningstar Economic Moat Rating 
: Narrow
Morningstar Uncertainty Rating 
: High
What We Thought of Corning’s Earnings
Corning GLW reported solid third-quarter results above the top end of guidance and guided to continued fourth-quarter growth. Non-GAAP sales rose 19% year over year to $5.1 billion, and generative AI sales doubled. Non-GAAP operating margin rose 310 basis points year over year to 22.7%.
Why it matters: Corning is well on track to its attractive “Springboard” targets. We like the firm’s consistent execution, growth, and margin expansion since unveiling Springboard three years ago. Its diversified portfolio and centralized cost advantage set it up well to achieve targets through 2030.
Optical fiber for AI leads Corning’s growth, and we continue to be impressed with the firm’s ability to rapidly increase its supply to capitalize on demand. Furthermore, Corning’s ability to derisk capital spending with co-investment by customers should please investors.
We expect optical growth to endure at a high level through 2030, and we believe it may even continue to accelerate. We see longer-term upside from scale-up networking and co-packaged optics, which make up no revenue today.
The bottom line: We maintain our $155 fair value estimate for narrow-moat Corning, and shares look attractive. Shares sold off 4% early intraday, with some market nitpicks about costs and consensus expectations. We focus on the long-term runway, which looks very positive.
Our model comes in ahead of Corning’s 2030 Springboard target, which calls for exiting 2030 with $40 billion in annualized sales. We model closer to $45 billion. We expect scale-up networking to drive upside, but we like Corning’s position even if we end up being aggressive here.
Shares are down 50% from late June. We did see exuberance priced into Corning at the peak, but now we think the market has oversold to the downside. For us, this is a moaty, diversified technology leader with strong AI exposure at a discount.

Switched On: Scenes from the World’s First High-Altitude Hybrid Electric Flight
October 27, 2026
| by Jay Stowe
Share
Related Topics
Technology 
Performance 
“We are proud to say: ‘We did it,’” said Mohamed Ali, GE Aerospace’s president and CEO of Commercial Engines & Services, at the Farnborough International Airshow this past summer. 
Ali was referring to a new chapter in aviation history. GE Aerospace was announcing to the world that it had partnered with NASA, BETA Technologies, and Boeing to complete the world’s first high-altitude  hybrid electric  flight — reaching altitude levels above 30,000 feet — during flight tests over Plattsburgh, New York, in May 2026.
“This is not a lab experiment or a one-off prototype,” Ali went on to note, referring to the Saab 340B aircraft that had been modified for use in NASA’s Electrified Powertrain Flight Demonstration (EPFD) project. “It’s a meaningful step forward for future propulsion, and it helps validate hybrid electric technology as a credible path for the next-generation engine.”
These photos show the EPFD aircraft on the ground and in flight, along with the GE Aerospace and BETA Technologies teams in action.
 
While hybrid electric vehicles are now a common sight on roads around the world, sustained hybrid electric flight has been elusive. For the past five years,  Christine Andrews has been leading a team at GE Aerospace that aimed to prove out a high-performing, scalable hybrid electric propulsion solution. The data they’ve amassed, along with the test records, show that hybrid electric flight is well on its way to becoming a reality. And they’re getting closer to a point where the technology can be scaled across engine architectures. “I think most people would love to say they were part of a team that achieved a world first in their field,” says Andrews, GE Aerospace’s executive hybrid electric systems leader. “We’re doing it consistently. We’ve got a team that has really built a strong bond and has a relentless prioritization and focus on advancing hybrid electric technology.”
 
The right side of the EPFD aircraft was modified for flight tests with a hybrid electric system that fits inside an inverted nacelle, providing extra ventilation. The system includes GE Aerospace-developed motor/generators, power converters and inverters, controllers,  Avio Aero * gearboxes,  Dowty * propellers,  Unison * heat exchangers, torque sensing, and engine harnesses, and a CT7 turboprop engine. BAE Systems provided the batteries used for the test flight and Boeing subsidiary Aurora Flight Sciences supplied the complete nacelle.
 
Andrews’ team is mapping out uncharted aviation territory each time they do hybrid electric testing at a higher altitude or for a longer duration. They successfully  completed ground tests  of a megawatt-class hybrid electric engine system earlier this year at Peebles Test Operation in southwestern Ohio as part of NASA’s EPFD project. The ground tests simulated various flight phases (such as taxi, takeoff, climb, and cruise) and yielded higher power output and higher voltage than competing hybrid electric offerings. During the flight test campaign, the modified aircraft flew for more than two hours in a single flight, one of the aviation industry’s longest hybrid electric flights to date. “It’s been exhilarating for us,” says Andrews, standing at center with team members from BETA Technologies and GE Aerospace. The company’s 747 Flying Test Bed (FTB) is parked behind the group on the tarmac. 
 
GE Aerospace took one of its first major steps in the development of hybrid electric flight in 2013 when it opened its Electrical Power Integrated Systems Center ( EPISCenter ) with the University of Dayton, where it has made great strides in testing and simulated power transfers. In 2022, the  EPFD project successfully demonstrated  a multi-kilovolt, megawatt-power-class power transfer at a simulated altitude of 45,000 feet at the NASA Electric Aircraft Testbed facility near Sandusky, Ohio. “This proves that we are altitude ready,” Ali said at the time. “Next is to prove that we are flight ready.” That proof finally came this May with the help of (from left) Nick Wilson, chief engineer of the advanced system team and test pilot at BETA Technologies; Chris Caputo, head of flight operations and test pilot at BETA Technologies; and Jon Ohman, chief test pilot at GE Aerospace. 
 
The hybrid electric engine system in the EPFD aircraft combines an electric powertrain with a traditional gas turbine to optimize power management during different phases of operation. Hybrid electric systems are highly compatible with different fuel types and advanced aircraft engine architectures like Open Fan, which GE Aerospace is developing through  CFM International’s RISE program .** “The EPFD program is the first and only program of its type to fly at commercial grade altitudes in hybrid mode,” says Andrews, standing here with (from left) BETA Technologies test pilots Chris Caputo and Nick Wilson. “We’re able to pull power off of the batteries as well as recharge the batteries in flight.” “It allows us to do more with the aircraft,” adds Wilson. “It changes the way we operate the aircraft. It allows us to be more efficient.”
 
From his seat at the controls of  GE Aerospace’s 747 Flying Test Bed , Jon Ohman has helped test a variety of engines, including the CFM LEAP***, GEnx, GE9X, and Passport. Throughout the EPFD campaign, the FTB has served as a “logistics enabler,” Ohman says, helping to provide guidance and support during its test flight, as well as transport team members and equipment as the EPFD completed the world’s first hybrid electric flight across the Atlantic Ocean to the Farnborough International Airshow in July. “The FTB demonstrates, along with the Saab 340B, GE Aerospace’s commitment to furthering the technological development of the next generation of turbofan engines,” he adds. “The FTB is critical to the safe operation of our engines in operation. That’s because when we put a developmental engine on the FTB, we put them through their paces in all conditions of operability to ensure that we don’t find any surprises when that engine is on a commercial air flight with the paying public on board.”
 
The 747 Flying Test Bed is based at GE Aerospace’s  Flight Test Operations facility  in Victorville, California, where the Flight Test Operations (FTO) team has worked closely with Andrews’ team on the integration of hybrid electric technology into the modified Saab 340B aircraft. In preparation for the hybrid electric test flight in May, the engineering and test teams addressed heat management, lower atmospheric pressures, and power density using flightworthy components that meet higher safety and reliability requirements than typical test hardware. During the flight tests, the electric powertrain helped successfully power the propeller and generated power to the battery. “When we look back at history, all hybrid beginnings will have started with proving this very first hybrid electric flight at commercial grade altitudes,” says Andrews.
 
 
* Avio Aero, Dowty, and Unison are GE Aerospace companies. 
** Revolutionary Innovation for Sustainable Engines (RISE) is a technology demonstration program of CFM International, a 50-50 joint company between GE Aerospace and Safran Aircraft Engines. It is not a product offered for commercial sale. 
*** The CFM LEAP engine is produced by CFM International.
