content_text:
Anduril expanding into laptop manufacturing in partnership with Qualcomm 
The companies plan to market the tech to government and military customers, among other potential buyers. 
By 
Jon Harper 
October 27, 2026 
Listen to this article
0:00
Learn more. 
This feature uses an automated voice, which may result in occasional errors in pronunciation, tone, or sentiment.
(Image courtesy of Anduril) 
Defense technology company Anduril, best known for building drones and AI-enabled software for the military, is branching out into a new product manufacturing business: laptops.
The company on Tuesday announced the launch of a computer initiative, dubbed BlueChip, in partnership with wireless tech giant Qualcomm.
Anduril has already developed “functional prototypes” of the laptops, according to a press release. Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X Series will provide the core computing capabilities for the devices, including “general-purpose processing, graphics, and on-device AI.”
The companies plan to begin taking orders next year.
Advertisement 
The firms touted BlueChip as an effort to boost manufacturing in America and reduce the nation’s reliance on foreign supply chains.
“The United States pioneered personal computing and continues to lead the world in designing advanced technology, but decades of offshoring have left America dependent on foreign manufacturers for the computers and components that power everything from personal devices to critical government infrastructure. This dependence creates a national security vulnerability. Conflict or disruptions to overseas supply chains could limit access to essential computing hardware and undermine America’s ability to sustain production when it matters most,” company officials wrote in the press release.
The organizations plan to market the tech to government and military customers, among other potential buyers.
“It might sound crazy for a company like Anduril to be doing something like this,” Anduril co-founder and leader Palmer Luckey told reporters ahead of the official announcement.
However, he suggested that the BlueChip product line isn’t far outside of Anduril’s wheelhouse.
Advertisement 
“What we’ve been doing at Anduril, including with Qualcomm, is not actually very different from building a computer. You look at any of our autonomous drones, we’ve got a CPU, a GPU, memory, storage, mainboard, battery, sensors, wireless radios. It’s basically all the same stuff you’d have in any computer. The only difference is the shape and that it has a screen and a keyboard. Even on the display side, actually, we have a number of drones that have status screens, so it’s really not all that different,” he said.
During a call with reporters ahead of the announcement, Luckey declined to say what the production targets are for the new laptops.
“We’re not sharing any quantities yet. We’re gonna have a lot more to announce next year. I think it’s really, really tough right now to announce these things. To be totally candid, we’re in an unprecedented time, as it were, for building computers given … the AI explosion, and so we’re not going into full-rate production until next year. We’re in very early prototyping production. Like, we have a very small line put together, very small quantities of these right now to build out the manufacturing process. But I’m not going to know quantities until we have a little more clarity on the manufacturing side, the vendor supply chain side. There’s a lot of moving pieces,” he said.
Anduril plans to use its Arsenal-1 facility in Ohio — where it’s also building autonomous drones for the Air Force’s Collaborative Combat Aircraft program — for BlueChip manufacturing.
Cristiano Amon, president and CEO of Qualcomm, told reporters during the call that chips for the laptops will be made at a TSMC facility in Arizona.
Advertisement 
Luckey added that the companies also have “some stuff going on” in California related to the effort, though he didn’t provide details.
“There’s certainly going to end up being other facilities. This is another one of those things where it’s still in flux, exactly which facility is going to do which step. So, I can’t get into as much detail as I’d like,” he said.
Luckey noted that, while the laptop will be the first product in the BlueChip line, the companies’ vision is to expand the offerings and it’s “very likely” that some of those will be made at other facilities.
Currently, the laptop’s bill of materials is about 90% from the U.S. and allies, according to Luckey. The aim is to eventually get that number up to 100%.
Regarding the workforce, the Anduril boss said he’s been “diverting some of our best people to this project for quite some time,” including those who worked on some of the other offerings that the company is better known for, such as attack drones.
Advertisement 
The U.S. government has not yet provided any subsidies or contracts to Anduril and Qualcomm to develop the laptops, according to Luckey, who noted that the companies have been putting their own R&D dollars into the initiative. He did not disclose how much money is being invested in the effort to get to full-rate production.
“I’d say the worst case here is that this is going to be a low-volume laptop for critical industries and government … that desperately need something like this to exist. That is a healthy business for Android to run, even if it doesn’t get bigger. I happen to believe it’s going to be much, much, much bigger,” he told reporters.
Amon noted the AI boom that’s unfolding across the economy.
“I think when you look at how AI is evolving, computers are also becoming token machines,” he said. “In addition to what you do with a laptop, it’s going to run models, it’s going to be part of this entire compute fabric that’s going to be running AI. And you’re going to have different ecosystems and needs for [the tech] across different industries. It’s very possible that you’re going to have certain industries … in addition to the federal government, that will want devices. They have different kinds of requirements and compliance with security and across the supply chain. … So, I think this could create an interesting opportunity when you think about the addressable market. It’s just a different world going forward when you think about the role of PCs.”
Luckey added that the chips in the new laptop are “extremely good” for AI inference.
Advertisement 
“Maybe not training large models, but on the inference side, they’re fantastic. And so, I’ve been using my BlueChip laptop to do a whole bunch of local model work where … I don’t want to — and actually am not allowed to — send certain information out into the cloud. And so having devices that can do a really good job of onboard AI inference running local models is actually really, really important,” he told reporters.
The BlueChip systems are designed for potential military customers.
“This is aimed squarely at the defense side of things as the pace-setting element of the design because it’s the most stringent part of the design. So basically I have to design for the military users because they’re the ones that are going to be beating these things up the most. They have the most stringent security requirements, the most stringent environmental requirements, shock and vibration, all of that,” Luckey said.
For the average individual consumer, the price tag for the extra-rugged devices might not be cost competitive with other laptop offerings on the market, he suggested.
Anduril has been testing out the BlueChip tech with multiple operating systems, Luckey noted.
Advertisement 
“As of right now, we have it running Windows and two particular flavors of Linux that are very popular with the U.S. military to make sure that all the drivers work, make sure that all the applications work,” he said.
One of the applications that has been integrated into the BlueChip system is Anduril’s Lattice software platform that serves as the backbone for some of the military’s high-priority modernization initiatives, such as Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2).
“It’s critical that we be able to run Lattice, both the version that processes locally and the version that commands and controls systems that are processing at the edge with Lattice,” Luckey said.

Infineon to establish Europe's first volume 300mm GaN facility
Tuesday 27th October 2026
€1.1 billion investment in the Villach site Austria to become global competence centre for power semiconductors 
Infineon is establishing the world’s first high-volume manufacturing facility for next-generation GaN power semiconductors on 300mm wafers in Europe. As part of the project, Infineon will invest around €1.1 billion in its existing cleanroom facilities at the Villach site in Austria by 2034.
Production is scheduled to start by the end of 2027. Infineon’s investment addresses the rapidly growing demand for high-performance power supply solutions. GaN enables significant efficiency gains in numerous applications, such as AI data centres, energy infrastructure, e-mobility, robotics and consumer electronics.  
'By establishing high-volume manufacturing on 300mm wafers, we will be the first company in the world to bring GaN power electronics into volume production,” says Jochen Hanebeck, CEO of Infineon Technologies AG. “In doing so, we are paving the way for the widespread use of GaN in a wide range of key applications in areas such as artificial intelligence, energy infrastructure, e- mobility and robotics. This new, state-of-the-art manufacturing facility translates innovation leadership into direct customer benefits.” 
Christian Stocker, Federal Chancellor of the Republic of Austria: “With Infineon’s billion-euro investment, we are witnessing one of the largest single investments in the history of Austria’s high- tech industry. This is not only a strong commitment to Austria as a business location but also helps ensure that the future of the semiconductor industry will not be shaped solely in Asia or the United States, but also in Austria and Europe."
The investment is being supported under the European Chips Act. The European Commission approved €319 million in state aid. The formal funding commitment by the Austrian Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, Energy and Tourism is expected within the stipulated time limits.

HyProMag Outlines Three-Plant Expansion to Quadruple US Rare Earth Magnet Output
HyProMag , a scrap recycler, has outlined a scenario involving three plants that would quadruple its rare earth magnet production, Mining Weekly reports. The HyProMag USA subsidiary of TSX-V- and Aim-listed Mkango Magnetic Materials has finished an independent prefeasibility study on potentially expanding its planned US rare earth magnet manufacturing platform beyond its initial Northlake, Texas, plant. 
The Northlake facility is in detailed engineering, with Phase 1 commissioning targeted for mid-2028. The study assesses a phased build-out to three regional production plants backed by a centralised manufacturing, finishing and technology hub called the Central Texas Hub, making commercial neodymium-iron-boron magnet products in the US from end-of-life recycled feedstock and primary alloy material.
Alongside the Northlake Texas facility, the platform aims for total saleable material of roughly 6 000 t/y by 2034, which is 4 474 t/y more than the standalone Northlake scenario. Mkango expects HyProMag's total magnetic material production by 2034 to reach 4 192 t/y of magnets, 1 305 t/y of magnetic NdFeB alloy powder and 503 t/y of other saleable material.
The study draws on engineering and development work already completed for the Northlake facility and sets out how HyProMag could evolve from a Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap-enabled magnet recycler into a fully integrated producer of commercial rare earth magnet products for US customers. HyProMag considers the platform to combine the cost advantages and operational flexibility of recycled and primary alloy feedstocks, offering a flexible and scalable route to magnet manufacturing. The company could also benefit from potential future access to primary sourced feedstock from Mkango under certain supply rights.
The study examined three new production plants in South Carolina, Nevada and a second Texas location, which would run alongside the Northlake facility. Each plant is meant to process feedstock, operate the HPMS process and produce unfinished sintered NdFeB blocks, which could then be moved to the Central Texas Hub for advanced manufacturing and finishing.
A key finding was optimisation of the manufacturing configuration to raise output of higher-value NdFeB magnet products. The study outlines a potential four-fold rise in US magnet production capacity, from 1 048 t/y of NdFeB magnets at Northlake Texas alone to about 4 192 t/y across four plants by 2034. The plants are designed to recover and reprocess manufacturing residues, including magnet machining end cuts through the HPMS process, maximising use of rare earth materials.
The study assessed two development options based on modular production systems. In the first, the plants use recycled feedstock only, applying HPMS recycling of magnet scrap to produce NdFeB alloy powder, sintered magnet blocks and finished magnets. The second envisions recycled and primary feedstocks, with additional capital expenditure to support primary NdFeB alloy as a feedstock.
Case 1 delivered the strongest project economics with an after-tax net present value of $2.06-billion, an internal rate of return of 36% and a payback period of 2.3 years, for a capital cost of $623-million. Case 2 showed a net present value of $1.8-billion, an internal rate of return of 31% and a payback period of three years, for a capital cost of $656-million. The combined after-tax net present value range of the proposed Northlake facility and the potential study plants is estimated between $2.6-billion and $2.8-billion.
Mkango said the study demonstrates robust economics and a pathway to producing higher-value NdFeB magnet products for strategically important sectors. HyProMag founder Allan Walton said the platform's objective has always been to demonstrate that HPMS technology can recover rare earth magnetic materials and convert them into high-performance commercial magnet products, and that the study outlines a pathway to scaling that capability through an integrated manufacturing platform incorporating magnet production, finishing and product qualification. He added that the enhanced production configuration would support manufacture of a broader range of commercial magnet products for demanding industrial applications, while finishing, quality assurance and product development capabilities provide a foundation for continued product optimisation and customer qualification.

Boeing says it won't significantly ramp up 737 Max production until late 2027
Published Tue, Oct 27 2026 7:00 AM EDT Updated Tue, Oct 27 2026 4:32 PM EDT 
Leslie Josephs @lesliejosephs 
WATCH LIVE 
Key Points
Boeing narrowed its loss in the third quarter after defense sales rose.
The company beat revenue expectations but posted a bigger loss per share than expected.
Boeing also said it was targeting a production increase of its best-selling 737 Max aircraft in the second half of 2027.
In this article
BA 
Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT 
VIDEO 6:41 06:41 
Watch CNBC's full interview with Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg
Boeing doesn't expect to significantly ramp up output of its best-selling 737 Max aircraft until the second half of 2027 as it grapples with a slower-than-expected pace of wing production.
CEO Kelly Ortberg said Tuesday on the company's quarterly earnings call that Boeing is targeting a production rate of 52 planes a month in the second half of 2027. It has been manufacturing about 47 of its 737 Max planes a month.
Ortberg had told investors last month that the production stabilize was taking a "little bit longer" than expected because of the wings production pace.
Boeing stock fell 10% in trading Tuesday.
"I know everybody wants us to go faster, but we're going to do it right," Ortberg told CNBC's Phil LeBeau in an interview Tuesday.
Ortberg reiterated the company's priority in stabilizing production on Tuesday.
"Looking ahead, expectations are rising, and they should," Ortberg said in a note to staff on Tuesday. "That means elevating our performance through lean, productivity and efficiency improvements in our day-to-day work while upholding our high levels of safety and quality."
Aircraft production and deliveries are key to Boeing's recovery since the bulk of an aircraft's price is paid when the customer receives it.
Third-quarter earnings
The company also reported Tuesday that it narrowed its losses in the third quarter, thanks to a boost from its defense unit.
For the three months ended Sept. 30, Boeing reported a net loss of $116 million, or 26 cents a share, compared with a $5.34 billion loss, or $7.14 per share, a year earlier. Adjusting for one-time items, the company posted a loss of 34 cents a share. A year earlier, Boeing had taken a nearly $5 billion charge on its long-delayed 777X aircraft program.
Revenue climbed 4% on the year to $24.19 billion. Free cash flow rose to $464 million from $238 million in the third quarter of 2025.
The company's defense unit revenue jumped 15% in the third quarter from a year earlier to $7.94 billion.
Here's what Boeing reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street analysts expected, according to consensus estimates from LSEG:
Loss per share: 34 cents adjusted vs. a loss of 21 cents expected
Revenue: $24.19 billion vs $23.84 billion expected.
Boeing delivered 161 commercial airplanes in the third quarter, one more jet than a year earlier. 
Revenue in the all-important commercial aircraft business fell 3% to $10.72 billion. The unit had a negative operating margin of 6.5% because of a "less favorable delivery mix, higher projected costs associated with future production rate adjustments and higher estimated supply chain costs," Boeing said.
Ortberg told staff in a memo that the manufacturer has "more work to do."
Certification wins
The manufacturer had some wins lately. The U.S. Navy tapped Boeing to develop its next-generation fighter jet.
And the Federal Aviation Administration last week signed off on the 737 Max 10 , the largest in the Max family. That followed the approval of the 737 Max 7 in August and marked the final certifications for the aircraft line.

Infineon establishing first high-volume fab for GaN power semiconductors on 300mm wafers in Europe
Infineon Technologies AG of Munich, Germany is establishing the world’s first high-volume manufacturing facility for gallium nitride (GaN) power semiconductors on 300mm wafers in Europe. As part of the project, the firm will invest about €1.1bn in its existing cleanroom facilities at the site in Villach, Austria by 2034. Leveraging both the existing and upgraded infrastructure will enable efficient and cost-effective expansion of manufacturing capacity, it is reckoned. Production is scheduled to start by the end of 2027. 
Infineon’s investment addresses the rapidly growing demand for high-performance power supply solutions, as gallium nitride enables significant efficiency gains in applications such as AI data centers, energy infrastructure, e-mobility, robotics and consumer electronics. 
Picture: Infineon’s site in Villach, Austria. 
Two years ago, Infineon achieved the milestone of processing the world’s first 300mm GaN wafers. Compared with 200mm wafers, the 300mm diameter enables the production of 2.3 times as many chips per wafer. Infineon is now transferring this more efficient technology to the first high-volume manufacturing facility serving customers. 
“This substantial investment shows our clear commitment to strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem and Europe’s technological sovereignty. By establishing high-volume manufacturing on 300mm wafers, we will be the first company in the world to bring gallium nitride power electronics into volume production,” says Infineon’s CEO Jochen Hanebeck. “In doing so, we are paving the way for the widespread use of gallium nitride in a wide range of key applications in areas such as artificial intelligence, energy infrastructure, e-mobility and robotics,” he adds. 
“We are witnessing one of the largest single investments in the history of Austria’s high-tech industry,” states Christian Stocker, Federal Chancellor of the Republic of Austria. “This is not only a strong commitment to Austria as a business location but also helps ensure that the future of the semiconductor industry will not be shaped solely in Asia or the USA, but also in Austria and Europe,” he adds. 
“Europe currently accounts for only around 10% of global chip production… We must also manufacture this key technology in Europe,” says Wolfgang Hattmannsdorfer, Austrian Federal Minister for Economic Affairs. “Austria is already a leader in energy-efficient chips. Relative to our population, we rank first in the EU in business R&D spending in the semiconductor sector. With our industrial strategy, we intend to build on this lead and not only research new technologies but also manufacture them on an industrial scale,” he adds. “Every job in the chip industry can provide six additional jobs across the broader economy. That is why we intend to support Infineon’s new chip production with up to €319m — subject to clear funding criteria for the location. This will ensure that public funds strengthen value creation and jobs in Austria over the long term.” 
The investment is being supported under the European Chips Act. The European Commission has approved the €319m in state aid. The formal funding commitment by the Austrian Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, Energy and Tourism is expected within the stipulated time limits.
“Competitiveness and technological sovereignty emerge where excellent research is translated into industrial value creation. This is precisely where our flagship project comes in. From Austria, we are bringing innovation into industrial application, strengthening our technological leadership and securing highly skilled jobs,” says Infineon Technologies Austria AG’s CEO Sabine Herlitschka. “The entire Austrian semiconductor ecosystem benefits — from research organizations and universities to industrial partners. We are thus sustainably strengthening Europe’s competitiveness and strategic autonomy in microelectronics.”
Infineon reckons that the investment strengthens Villach’s role as a global competence center for power electronics and new semiconductor materials. Infineon Austria currently employs about 5800 people, including 4800 at the Villach site (as of end-September 2025). Together with universities, research institutions, start-ups and industry partners, Infineon forms the core of a microelectronics ecosystem in southern Austria. The establishment of the new 300mm GaN manufacturing facility is also expected to create synergies with the power electronics R&D activities in Villach.

Applied Materials Raises BE Semiconductor Stake to 20%, Deepening AI Advanced Packaging Push; Deal Awaits U.S. Antitrust Review
Add preferred source 2 
Applied Materials announced it will raise its stake in Dutch packaging equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries from 9% to approximately 20%, having signed an accelerated share purchase agreement, with the deal still pending U.S. antitrust review. Applied Materials became BE Semiconductor's largest shareholder after first taking a stake in April 2025, and the increased holding is aimed at AI chip advanced packaging. The two companies have collaborated on hybrid bonding technology since 2020 and have jointly developed the Kinex integrated die-to-wafer system. Applied Materials said it does not intend to push its stake above 20% or seek board seats. BE Semiconductor holds roughly 70% of the global hybrid bonding equipment market, with third-quarter orders up 96% year over year, and hybrid bonding equipment orders in the first nine months of 2026 already more than double the full-year 2025 level.
Key Elements 
Applied Materials BE Semiconductor Industries hybrid bonding EPIC Center Prabh Raja ASML Kinex Piotech 
U.S. semiconductor equipment giant Applied Materials announced Monday that it will raise its stake in Dutch packaging equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries (BESI) from the current 9% to approximately 20%, deepening cooperation between the two companies in advanced packaging for artificial intelligence (AI) chips. The increased holding has been signed under an accelerated share purchase agreement but still requires U.S. antitrust review.
Applied Materials became the largest shareholder of the Dutch company after first taking a 9% stake in April 2025. At that time, BE Semiconductor had a market value of about $13 billion. Under the plan, the stake will approach 20% once the increase is completed. However, Applied Materials made clear that at this stage it does not intend to push its holding above 20% or seek seats on BE Semiconductor's board, indicating that this is a long-term strategic investment centered on technology cooperation rather than a move toward a full acquisition.
The expanded cooperation focuses on next-generation chip interconnection and packaging technology, with the goal of supporting the next generation of AI semiconductors. The two companies have jointly invested in hybrid bonding process development since 2020, a technology regarded as a key link in advanced packaging and mainly used for high-performance chips.
Hybrid bonding is characterized by directly bonding copper interconnects and dielectric layers without the need for traditional bumps, allowing a substantial increase in connection density between chips. The two companies have jointly developed the Kinex integrated die-to-wafer hybrid bonding system, combining Applied Materials' expertise in etching, planarization, deposition and inspection with BE Semiconductor's technology in high-precision die placement and assembly. BE Semiconductor also recently formally joined Applied Materials' newly established chip equipment research organization, the EPIC Center.
Prabh Raja, president of Applied Materials' Semiconductor Products Group, said in a statement: "We look forward to further deepening our strategic collaboration with Besi to deliver the innovative products and technologies customers need to scale AI systems."
From a market structure perspective, BE Semiconductor holds a critical position in the advanced packaging equipment sector. According to market data, BE Semiconductor accounts for about 70% of the global hybrid bonding equipment market. Its flagship model, the Datacon 8800 CHAMEO ultra plus AC, achieves alignment accuracy of up to 100 nanometers and a throughput of up to 2,000 cycles per hour, with volume production potential.
Demand-side momentum is also strengthening. BE Semiconductor's third-quarter orders surged 96% year over year to €342.6 million (approximately $382.0 million); hybrid bonding equipment orders in the first nine months of 2026 were already more than double the full-year 2025 level. The company's latest financial report shows that its hybrid bonding customer base has expanded to 23 companies, with cumulative equipment demand exceeding 215 units.
It is worth noting that last week the market briefly worried that Dutch semiconductor equipment leader ASML might become a competitor to BE Semiconductor in the hybrid bonding arena, which BE Semiconductor has denied. Against the backdrop of advanced packaging becoming key to the AI chip computing power race, alliances and competitive-cooperative relationships among equipment makers are rapidly intensifying.
On the other hand, Chinese equipment makers are also catching up in hybrid bonding technology. China's Piotech recorded hybrid bonding equipment revenue of CNY 136 million (approximately $20.4 million) in 2025, up 41.92% year over year, and has secured repeat orders for wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding systems, meaning that this niche market previously dominated by a small number of vendors is gradually seeing new suppliers emerge.
For investors, the most direct significance of this deal is that Applied Materials is betting its resources on the "back-end" packaging link of AI chips. As advancing Moore's Law becomes increasingly difficult, improvements in chip performance increasingly depend on advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration, and hybrid bonding is one of the highest-barrier technologies in this area. By tying up with BE Semiconductor through a stake purchase rather than an acquisition, Applied Materials can share technology and customers while avoiding the operational risks and regulatory resistance of full integration.
However, the deal still must pass U.S. antitrust review, and the timetable and conditions remain uncertain. Applied Materials has also stated that it will not pursue board seats or increase its stake further, and whether the cooperation can be translated into substantive orders and revenue contribution will be a key focus for the market going forward.

CoTec Holdings Corp. Notes HyProMag USA Pre-Feasibility Study Outlining Future Expansion Options to Quadruple Planned U.S. Rare Earth Magnet Capacity, Indicating an Incremental Post-Tax NPV of Up to US$2.1 billion
Investing News Network 
October 27, 2026 
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 27, 2026 / CoTec Holdings Corp. ( TSXV:CTH )(OTCQX:CTHCF) ("CoTec" or the "Company") notes the press release issued yesterday October 26, 2026, by its joint venture, HyProMag USA LLC ("HyProMag USA"), announcing the completion of an independent Pre-Feasibility Study (" PFS " or the "Study") undertaken by PegasusTSI Inc. and BBA USA Inc. evaluating the potential expansion of HyProMag USA's proposed U.S. rare earth magnet manufacturing platform beyond its first plant in Northlake, Texas (the "Northlake Texas Facility"), which is in detailed engineering, with Phase 1 commissioning expected in mid-2028.
CoTec Holdings: HyProMag USA PFS Outlines 4x U.S. Magnet Capacity youtube.com 
The PFS evaluates a three-plant[i] phased expansion strategy: three new regional production plants, supported by a centralized manufacturing, finishing and technology hub (the " Central Texas Hub "), to produce commercial neodymium iron boron ("NdFeB") magnet products in the United States from both end-of-life recycled feedstock and primary alloy material. Together with the Northlake Texas Facility[ii], the platform targets total salable material production of approximately 6,000 metric tons per year by 2034, an increase of 4,474 metric tons per year above production from the Northlake Texas Facility.
Annual total magnetic material production in 2034 from HyProMag USA would comprise approximately 4,192 metric tons of magnets, 1,305 metric tons of magnetic NdFeB alloy powder and 503 metric tons of other salable material. The PFS economics listed below cover the three new plants, including the Central Texas Hub only; they do not include the Northlake Texas Facility, whose value is not included in the PFS results.
The Study builds upon the engineering and development work completed for the Northlake Texas Facility and outlines a pathway for HyProMag USA to develop from a Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap ("HPMS")[iii] enabled magnet recycler into a fully integrated producer of commercial rare earth magnet products for U.S. customers.
HyProMag USA believes the platform combines the cost advantages and operational flexibility of both end-of-life recycled feedstock and primary alloy feedstocks, providing a flexible and scalable pathway to magnet manufacturing.
HyProMag USA may also benefit from potential future access to primary sourced feedstock from Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited ("Mkango") pursuant to certain Mkango supply rights to HyProMag USA.
Highlights 
The PFS evaluated two development options, both based on modular production systems: Case 1 - Recycled feedstock only: HPMS recycling of magnet scrap to produce NdFeB alloy powder, sintered magnet blocks, finished and packaged magnets; and 
Case 2 - Recycled and primary feedstock: as Case 1, with the additional capex to support primary NdFeB alloy as a feedstock to produce NdFeB alloy powder, sintered magnet blocks, finished and packaged magnets. 
Project economics with a post-tax NPV [iv] , [v] of US$1,854 million (Case 2) to US$2,062 million (Case 1) for the three new plants (excluding the Northlake Texas Facility), post-tax IRR of 31% (Case 2) to 36% (Case 1) and a Profitability Index (post-tax NPV divided by capital cost) of approximately 2.8x to 3.3x, based on forecast prices [vi] and a Class 3 AACE [vii] capital cost estimate of approximately US$656 million (Case 2) to US$623 million (Case 1), respectively, with a payback of 3 years (Case 2) and 2.3 years (Case 1). 
Competitive Manufacturing Costs. For the first PFS Plant in 2030, the PFS estimates an All-In Sustaining Cost ("AISC") of approximately US$41.6 per kg ( Case 2 ) to US$37.4 per kg ( Case 1 ) of finished NdFeB products sold. AISC includes all downstream processing and finishing costs, including plating and epoxy coating. Based on forecast market prices and the forecast product mix, the weighted average realized all-in selling price in 2030 is estimated at approximately US$100.5 per kg, supporting strong margins and attractive project returns.
Combined HyProMag USA platform value: The combined post-tax NPV range of the proposed Northlake Texas Facility and the potential PFS plants is estimated at US$2.6 billion to US$2.8 billion. 
The staged approach for the Northlake Texas Facility: [viii] Updated post-tax NPV of approximately US$723 [ix] , [x] , [xi] , [xii] million based on forecast prices and a capital cost estimate of approximately US$167 million [xiii] , increased due to the phased construction approach and the finalization of equipment orders. The reduction from the post-tax NPV of approximately US$797 million announced on June 22, 2026, reflects the later construction timetable, the higher capital costs and updated operating cost assumptions consistent with the PFS. 
Potential fourfold increase in U.S. magnet producing capacity: from approximately 1,048 metric tons per year of salable NdFeB magnets at the Northlake Texas Facility to approximately 4,192 metric tons per year across four plants by 2034. Phase 1 of the Northlake Texas Facility is expected to be commissioned in mid-2028. 
Integrated alloy processing and centralized finishing: The Central Texas Hub is expected to incorporate Vacuum Induction Melting ("VIM") and strip-casting operations, allowing the platform to process NdFeB alloy, provide magnet plating, passivation, coating, quality assurance and customer qualification for all plants. 
Higher-value magnet production: The production configuration would incorporate grain boundary diffusion ("GBD") capability, which would significantly increase the proportion of higher-value NdFeB magnet products. High-grade magnet production would increase from approximately 10% to 20% of total magnet output, supporting enhanced product mix, market access and project economics. 
Low-carbon production: supported by a previously completed carbon footprint of approximately 2.35 kg CO₂-eq per kilogram of NdFeB sintered block product for the Northlake Texas Facility[xiv] . 
Commercial qualification pathway: Product performance data and customer validation are underway with potential U.S. offtake customers, with the support of the HyProMag Group. 
Additional revenue opportunities: The platform would provide future opportunities for third-party magnet finishing activities, supporting enhanced utilization of manufacturing infrastructure and potential additional revenue streams. 
The platform is expected to play a key role in re-establishing domestic NdFeB magnet manufacturing: in the United States, creating approximately 300 jobs across Texas, South Carolina, and Nevada, in addition to the 100 positions at the Northlake Texas Facility.
Independent PFS: completed by PegasusTSI Inc. and BBA USA Inc. with support from HyProMag's international teams and the University of Birmingham, UK. Subject to ongoing review, the expansion strategy is expected to progress to a Feasibility Study at the appropriate time. 
Julian Treger, Chief Executive Officer of CoTec, commented : "This Pre-Feasibility Study confirms the opportunity to establish a significant domestic rare earth magnet manufacturing platform in the United States. The Study demonstrates robust economics and a pathway to producing higher-value NdFeB magnet products for strategically important sectors including advanced manufacturing, energy, defense and AI-driven technologies. Importantly, the platform is designed with the flexibility to utilize primary alloy feedstock alongside recycled materials, providing greater supply chain resilience and supporting long-term operational competitiveness. The results highlight the platform's potential to create substantial long-term value while strengthening the U.S. rare earth magnet supply chain." 
Professor Allan Walton, Founder of HyProMag and Head of the Magnetic Materials Group at the University of Birmingham, commented: "The objective of the HyProMag platform has always been to demonstrate that HPMS technology can recover rare earth magnetic materials and convert them into high-performance commercial magnet products. The PFS outlines a pathway to scaling that capability through an integrated manufacturing platform incorporating magnet production, finishing and product qualification. Importantly, the enhanced production configuration would support the manufacture of a broader range of commercial magnet products for demanding industrial applications, while the inclusion of finishing, quality assurance and product development capabilities provides a foundation for continued product optimization and customer qualification." 
Platform Configuration 
The PFS assessed three new production plants in South Carolina, Nevada and a second location in Texas, which would operate alongside the Northlake Texas Facility. Each plant is intended to process feedstock, operate HPMS and produce unfinished sintered NdFeB blocks.
The Central Texas Hub, located within the second Texas plant, is expected to incorporate alloy processing (VIM and strip-casting), GBD, machining, plating, passivation, epoxy coating, quality assurance, product qualification and technology development capabilities.
Under the proposed configuration, unfinished sintered blocks produced from South Carolina, Nevada and the second facility in Texas would be transferred to the Central Texas Hub for advanced manufacturing and finishing. The Central Texas Hub is also designed to support future partnerships with specialist manufacturing and finishing providers, enabling the efficient scaling of advanced magnet production capability.
Higher-Value Magnet Production 
A key outcome of the PFS was the optimization of the manufacturing configuration to increase production of higher-value NdFeB magnet products. This enhanced product mix would be supported by further incorporation of GBD technology, which enables the production of higher-performance magnet grades required for demanding applications across medical, industrial automation, robotics, energy infrastructure and advanced manufacturing markets.
The increased proportion of higher-value magnet products would broaden exposure to premium end-use applications and is expected to support improved revenues, stronger operating margins and enhanced overall project returns.
Recycling of Magnet End Cuts By-Products 
The PFS plants are designed to recover and reprocess manufacturing residues, including magnet machining end cuts, through the HPMS process, maximizing the use of rare earth materials. This integrated approach would support both production flexibility and the circular manufacturing characteristics of the HyProMag platform.
Integrated Manufacturing Platform 
The Central Texas Hub is expected to create operating synergies through shared infrastructure and integrated processing capabilities. The Study indicates that the combination of integrated alloy processing, magnet manufacturing, finishing operations and flexible feedstock sourcing has the potential to support a competitive cost position for domestically manufactured rare earth magnet products. HyProMag USA believes these advantages will support the supply of U.S. manufactured magnets at competitive prices while providing customers with the benefits of domestic supply-chain security, traceability and low-carbon production.
The Central Texas Hub is also expected to evolve into an advanced manufacturing, product qualification and technology development center serving the broader manufacturing platform. In addition to supporting HyProMag USA production, the facility would provide future opportunities to support third-party magnet finishing activities, creating the potential for additional revenue streams and improved utilization of manufacturing infrastructure.
The proposed technology and product development center would leverage expertise from the wider HyProMag Group and the University of Birmingham's Magnetic Materials Group, supporting development, qualification and optimization of commercial magnet products.
Flexible Feedstock Platform 
A key outcome of the independent PFS is the flexibility of a manufacturing platform capable of utilizing both recycled NdFeB materials and primary alloy feedstocks. This flexible sourcing model is expected to enhance supply-chain resilience, support production growth and provide the ability to optimize raw material inputs in response to market conditions and customer requirements. HPMS technology provides the foundation for processing recycled magnetic materials and integrating them into the broader manufacturing platform.
Advancing Commercial Magnet Qualification with HyProMag Group 
Commercial magnet qualification activities continue across the wider HyProMag Group in the United Kingdom and Germany. These activities are expected to support qualification of future U.S.-produced magnet products, accelerate customer onboarding and reduce commercialization risk as the U.S. manufacturing platform expands. HyProMag USA believes this provides a meaningful advantage by allowing future U.S. operations to build upon existing technical and commercial progress rather than initiating qualification programs from a standing start.
About HyProMag USA 
HyProMag USA is developing advanced rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing operations to establish a secure domestic U.S. supply chain for NdFeB magnets, essential components for AI infrastructure, defense systems, robotics, electric vehicles, and advanced electronics. Leveraging the revolutionary HPMS technology, developed over 15 years with over US$100 million in R&D investment, HyProMag USA is designed to deliver faster magnet-to-magnet short-loop recycling that uses 88% less energy and reduces carbon emissions by 85% compared to conventional methods. HPMS accepts a wide range of magnet-bearing feedstocks - including end-of-life EV motors, data-center and industrial equipment, consumer electronics, and manufacturing scrap - enabling recovery of magnet-grade material without chemical processing.
Ownership 
HyProMag USA LLC is owned 50:50 by CoTec and HyProMag Limited. HyProMag Limited is 100% owned by Maginito Limited, which is owned 79.4% by Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) and 20.6% by CoTec.
For more information on HyProMag USA, please visit www.hypromagusa.com 
About CoTec 
CoTec Holdings Corp. ( TSXV:CTH )(OTCQX:CTHCF) is redefining the future of resource extraction and recycling. Focused on rare earth magnets and strategic materials, CoTec integrates breakthrough technologies with strategic assets to unlock secure, sustainable, and low-cost supply chains.
CoTec's mission is clear: accelerate the energy transition while strengthening strategic mineral supply chains for the countries we operate in. By investing in and deploying disruptive technologies, the Company delivers capital-efficient, scalable solutions that transform marginal assets, tailings, waste streams, and recycled products into high-value critical minerals.
From its HyProMag USA magnet recycling joint venture in Texas, to iron tailings reprocessing and reclamation in Québec, to next-generation copper and iron solutions backed by global majors, CoTec is building a diversified portfolio with long-term growth, rapid cash flow potential, and high barriers to entry. The result is a differentiated platform at the intersection of technology, sustainability, and strategic materials.
For more information, please visit www.cotec.ca

content_text:
AVL and VisIC move GaN traction inverter from test bench to vehicle demonstrator
Posted October 26, 2026 by Chris Ruoff & filed under Newswire , The Tech . 
Gallium nitride (GaN) semiconductor developer VisIC Technologies and mobility technology company AVL have integrated VisIC’s D³GaN power modules into the traction inverter of an AVL vehicle demonstrator.
The demonstrator, a platform for evaluating electric propulsion technologies, combines the GaN inverter with an e-axle, power electronics and vehicle control technologies. The project includes technology from AVL, NXP Semiconductors and VisIC.
The companies say that in earlier WLTC drive-cycle testing on AVL’s e-motor test bench in Germany, an inverter using VisIC’s D³GaN technology achieved 99.67% efficiency at 10 kHz and more than 99.8% at 5 kHz. They say the inverter showed an improvement over comparable SiC inverters and a reduction in inverter energy losses of more than 60% under the tested conditions. The inverter was developed with an NXP driver, AVL’s PI850e Inverter Development Platform and AVL control software.
VisIC’s D³GaN technology is designed to combine low switching and conduction losses with high power density for high-power automotive applications. Reducing switching losses during partial-load operation can improve inverter efficiency and reduce cooling requirements.
AVL and VisIC previously announced plans to extend VisIC’s GaN-on-silicon platform toward 800 V power modules for higher-voltage battery and drivetrain systems. The companies say the GaN-on-silicon approach can use established silicon manufacturing infrastructure and is compatible with 200 mm and 300 mm silicon foundries.
“Bringing D³GaN from the test bench into a fully operational vehicle is an important milestone for high-power GaN,” said Tamara Baksht, CEO of VisIC Technologies. “The AVL demonstrator shows that GaN is no longer limited to discussing future potential. We can demonstrate the technology in the traction inverter of a real electric vehicle and show automotive manufacturers what higher efficiency, lower losses and higher power density can mean at system level.”
“Integrating a GaN traction inverter into a vehicle demonstrator is an important step in understanding the opportunities and challenges of bringing this technology into future automotive applications,” said Mathias Deiml, Technical Lead GaN Inverter Development at AVL Software and Functions.
Source: VisIC Technologies

(See the video above for Jay's complete chart breakdown.) This week we want to game plan how to trade a stock after it reports earnings. Trading a stock before it reports can be a bit of a gamble. However, using the charts we see potential pathways that will enable us to take advantage of a reaction to those results with price being our guide. The stock in question is Corning , the specialty electronic, glass optics and components maker reports on Tuesday. Shares have given investors quite the ride this year. They are up 40% YTD but ~50% off their peak. However, we see a set-up giving traders a good near-term opportunity. Let's break it down on the charts. We are seeing a rounded topping formation that is at a critical level of support. This $120 area has held on two prior occasions and is being tested again. Based on this level we see three scenarios from which we can profit while minimizing risk. Trade scenario 1: The stock reacts positively to earnings and gaps higher Buy the gap higher if it's below $145. Set stops $2/$3 below that opening gap depending on your risk tolerance. Upward momentum should continue to $150/$155 and meet resistance there. That coincides with the 50 and 200-day moving averages — the stock should be sold there. If shares gap to that $150 level on the open, then a short play may be in order as that old support should be resistance and the gap could retrace 1/3 to ½ of that initial move. Trade scenario 2: No Major Reaction — support at $120/$125 holds Buy the small dip and look for a recovery rally to the $145 level. Use $118 as your stop as a break lower could see an accelerated move into the gap towards $105. Trade scenario 3: Stock Gaps Lower As seen on the short-term daily chart look for minor support at $100/$105 Buyers should step in at the level from its breakout in early 2026 As seen on the longer-term weekly chart, watch for longer-term support at the $90/$95 range. Any sizable gap lower would send shares into oversold territory and a snapback rally is expected As we head into what could be a very volatile time we have laid out the trading game plan. While the $120 level could dictate the longer-term path and health of the stock, it gives the trader a key area to watch and react to where price may head after its report. Shares have traded lower after each of its last four reports and our technical levels have been able to guide us to profits. We don't know which way it may break, but we will be ready to react once it does. —Jay Woods with Chase Games Jay Woods is the Chief Market Strategist at Freedom Capital Markets. By Ernest Hoffman 
Published :

The Leading News Source in Precious Metals
Kitco NEWS has a diverse team of journalists reporting on the economy, stock markets, commodities, cryptocurrencies, mining and metals with accuracy and objectivity. Our goal is to help people make informed market decisions through in-depth reporting, daily market roundups, interviews with prominent industry figures, comprehensive coverage (often exclusive) of important industry events and analyses of market-affecting developments.
(Kitco News) – Gold prices are being stymied by rising oil prices even as they gain support from falling real yields, while the world’s largest primary silver producer saw output slide over the first three quarters of 2026, according to precious metals analysts at Heraeus.
In their latest update, the analysts noted that gold prices are trapped between rising oil prices and falling Treasury yields.
“Brent crude has climbed back above $110/bbl following renewed Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, while Iran’s floating oil stocks, which had continued to supply Chinese refiners despite the US blockade, ran out in mid-October,” they noted. “Oil for delivery in a year’s time is trading around $89/bbl, suggesting the market sees a significant short-term risk premium along with disruption lasting into next year. For gold, elevated near-term oil prices continue to raise inflation risks and keep a December Fed rate hike firmly priced in, offsetting the traditional safe-haven support from geopolitical uncertainty.”
The analysts said that while the decline in Treasury yields has counteracted some of the impacts of rising oil, it hasn’t been enough to boost gold prices. “The 10-year yield has retreated towards 5.0%, from around 5.35% earlier this month, as concerns over stretched AI valuations, heavy financing requirements and returns on investment have driven investors towards government bonds,” they wrote. “The inflation-protected (TIPS) real yield has also reduced from above 2.9%, down to nearly 2.6%.”
“Lower yields reduce the opportunity cost of holding gold, but Treasuries are also competing directly for safe-haven flows at yields that remain historically high while the dollar remains elevated,” the analysts said. “The gold price has consequently slipped back towards $4,000/oz despite the bond rally. A sustained easing in oil prices alongside lower Treasury yields would provide a more supportive combination for gold, whereas continued strength in Brent crude would keep the inflation and interest-rate headwinds in place.”
And Russia continued to sell off its gold reserves to mitigate the pressure on its federal budget. “The Central Bank of Russia sold approximately 6 tonnes in September, its 10th consecutive month of sales, taking its reserves to around 2,260 tonnes and their lowest level since 2019,” they noted. “Holdings have fallen by around 62 tonnes since December, already more than the net decline of around 50 tonnes in 1998, the year of Russia’s financial crisis.”
“Between January and August, 170 tonnes of net central bank buying was reported, despite selling by Russia and Turkey, the analysts said. “Russia remains an exception to the broader trend of central-bank accumulation, with its need to mobilise reserve assets increasingly outweighing the incentive to hold gold.”
Spot gold continued to trade not far from session highs just before the North American market open, and last traded at $4,012.31 per ounce for a gain of 0.41% on the daily chart.
Turning to silver, Heraeus analysts pointed out that Fresnillo’s silver production dipped in the third quarter.
“Attributable silver production totalled 10.3 moz, down 5.5% quarter-on-quarter from 10.9 moz and 11.6% year-on-year from 11.7 moz,” they noted. “Lower grades at Juanicipio, Saucito and San Julián contributed to the decline, while the year-on-year comparison was also affected by the end of the Silverstream contribution. Juanicipio was particularly weak, with attributable silver output falling by 26% year-on-year to 1.8 moz, although production at the Fresnillo mine increased by 5% to 2.5 moz.”
The world's largest primary silver miner produced 32.4 million ounces in the first nine months of the year, a drop of 11.5% from the same period last year. “With full-year guidance remaining at 42.0- 46.5 moz, 9.6 moz is required in Q4 to reach the lower end of the range,” they said. “At that level, Fresnillo’s output would be equivalent to around 5% of global mined silver supply, which totalled 846.6 moz in 2025.”
Looking at the price action, Heraeus analysts pointed out that the silver price dropped below $55 per ounce, breaching the lows recorded in July. “This leaves silver over 20% below its late-August rebound high near $70/oz as the previous week's recovery was short-lived,” they said. “If the move below $55/oz is sustained, it would mark a further deterioration in the price trend. Below this, the $50/oz psychological level provides the next obvious support band.”
Silver was giving back its early gains on Monday morning as prices slid back below $54 per ounce on the session.
Spot silver last traded at $53.770 per ounce for a loss of 0.24% on the daily chart.

Enphase Energy and Infineon Announce World’s First 900 V GaN Bidirectional Switch Devices for AI Data Center Solid-State Transformers
Enphase Energy, Inc.

ENPH 
IFX.DE 
IFNNF

Enphase Energy, Inc. FREMONT, Calif., Oct. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Enphase Energy, Inc. (NASDAQ: ENPH), a global energy technology company, and Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) today announced that Enphase will deploy the world's first 900 V gallium nitride (GaN) monolithic bidirectional switch (BDS) devices, designed to operate in Enphase solid-state transformer power modules. The devices extend GaN technology to 900 V while retaining the high-frequency switching capabilities that enable compact, efficient power conversion. 
Enphase has pioneered the system-level development and demonstration, building on more than 10 years of in-house research into GaN power conversion, with device technology and engineering expertise from Infineon. Enphase is among the first to bring 650 V GaN BDS devices into volume production power electronics, and GaN HEMT technology is already operating in Enphase IQ9™ Microinverters deployed in the field. Extending that work with Infineon beyond 650 V, using Infineon's CoolGaN™ bidirectional switch portfolio, opens the door further to medium-voltage systems. 
The 900 V GaN devices allow Enphase to continue using components rated below 1 kV, expanding the design options towards high-performance power conversion typically governed by silicon carbide (SiC). This supports a single-stage architecture with high-frequency switching, low electromagnetic interference (EMI), and fewer points of failure. Switching at such high frequency shrinks the transformers and other magnetics needed in the power stage, cutting size, weight, and cost. 
Higher-voltage switches within that low-voltage envelope change the economics of power conversion. In a solid-state transformer, a medium-voltage input can be handled by fewer inverters connected in series while retaining the low switching losses and intrinsic bidirectionality of GaN BDS. Fewer building blocks means lower system-level losses at the same input current, fewer components in the power path, and a lower total switch count. On the DC side, higher-voltage unidirectional switch (UDS) devices allow power to be generated at a unipolar 800 volts rather than split +/-400 V buses, and support future 1,500 VDC bus architectures through split +/-750 V generation with fewer switches and lower bridge losses. 
The technology is particularly relevant to the Enphase IQ ® Solid-State Transformer (IQ SST), the company's solid-state transformer platform for AI data centers, where power density, efficiency, and uptime drive the economics of every megawatt deployed. The same devices are expected to benefit commercial solar inverters by enabling three-phase, line-to-line designs for 480 V applications in the United States and 400 V applications elsewhere, again with fewer switches, lower losses, and lower cost. 
Story Continues 
"Enphase asks more of our technology than almost anyone, and medium-voltage solid-state transformers are exactly where high-voltage GaN proves its value," said Johannes Schoiswohl, senior vice president and head of GaN Systems Business Line at Infineon. "Moving past 650 V lets system designers strip cost and loss out of the architecture rather than optimizing around it." 
"GaN is not new to us. It has been running in Enphase IQ9 Microinverters in the field, and that field data is why we trust it in a megawatt-class system," said Hans van Antwerpen, senior vice president and chief technology officer at Enphase Energy. "Moving to 900 V gives us more voltage headroom without giving up high-frequency switching, and it allows us to stay with components rated below 1 kV while reducing the number of converters in the system. Fewer parts in the power path means higher efficiency and fewer things that can fail." 
The 900 V GaN BDS devices have been successfully tested and are now being integrated into IQ SST development builds, with production qualification expected to follow. Learn more about the use of GaN in Enphase products in its white paper. 
About Enphase Energy, Inc. 
Enphase Energy is a global energy technology company advancing intelligent power systems for homes, businesses, and next-generation AI data centers. The company designs semiconductor-based energy technologies spanning solar, batteries, EV charging, energy management, and virtual power plants, and is developing solid-state transformer technology to address the rapidly growing power demands of AI data centers. Based in Fremont, California, Enphase is the world's leading supplier of microinverter-based solar and battery systems. The company revolutionized the solar industry with its microinverter technology and has shipped approximately 89.4 million microinverters, with approximately 5.3 million Enphase-based systems deployed in more than 165 countries. Enphase products enable people to harness the sun to make, use, save, and sell their own power, all controlled through the Enphase App. For more information, visit https://enphase.com/ .

Exclusive: Veolia sells R&E to Bricks Capital in deal worth about W70b
by An Hyo-jung,Park Ji-young 
Published : Oct. 26, 2026 - 15:43:01
View Korean Original
Link copied!
Acquirer: Bricks Capital; deal size about 70 billion won
Firm expands resource-recycling portfolio with high-margin acquisition
R&E, a company specializing in recycling artificial marble waste. [R&E website] 
Global environmental services firm Veolia Industrial Development Korea is selling R&E, a company that recycles artificial marble waste.
According to investment banking industry sources, Veolia signed a share purchase agreement Monday to sell its entire 100 percent stake in R&E to private equity fund manager Bricks Capital. The deal is valued at around 70 billion won ($52.9 million).
Veolia appointed BDA Partners as the sale manager earlier this year and formally launched the divestiture process, selecting Bricks Capital as the preferred bidder in late July. The final contract was signed roughly three months after that designation.
Veolia first acquired a 60 percent stake in R&E in 2019, securing management control, and later bought the remaining 40 percent to make it a wholly owned subsidiary. The deal marks a full exit from the investment approximately seven years after the initial acquisition.
The preliminary bidding round drew competition from three to five financial and strategic investors. R&E's appeal lay in its established share of the artificial marble waste recycling market and its operating profit margin of around 20 percent.
R&E operates a distinctive dual-revenue business model. It first collects processing fees when it takes in waste generated during the manufacturing and fabrication of artificial marble. It then subjects that waste to high-temperature crushing and pyrolysis to produce recycled methyl methacrylate (rMMA) and alumina, which it sells for a second stream of revenue. The structure lets the company capture the benefits of both waste treatment and recycled materials manufacturing simultaneously.
On the production side, R&E operates its main factory in Changwon, South Gyeongsang Province, along with facilities in Oksan, North Chungcheong Province, and Haman, South Gyeongsang Province. It sources raw materials through a network of major domestic manufacturers and fabricators, commanding the bulk of the artificial marble waste processing market and holding relevant technology patents.
Recent financial results, however, show signs of strain. Sales grew only marginally, from 13.5 billion won in 2024 to 13.7 billion won in 2025, while operating profit fell from 3.1 billion won to 2.8 billion won over the same period. Cash flow from operating activities also declined, dropping from 3.45 billion won in 2024 to 2.31 billion won in 2025.
Bricks Capital, which is acquiring R&E, is a young private equity fund manager founded in 2022. It is co-led by Kim Sae-han-sol, who built hands-on experience in the battery and electric vehicle industry at LG Energy Solution and Apple, and Kang Hun-gu, who comes from Goldman Sachs and IMM Private Equity. The firm operates out of Seoul and Silicon Valley, focusing on advanced manufacturing and sustainable industries.
With North American battery technology companies Sion Power and Mitra Chem already in its portfolio, Bricks Capital is using the R&E acquisition to extend its investment reach from batteries and advanced materials into the eco-friendly resource-recycling sector. The move signals the firm's intent to build a stronger foundation for broader investment in recycled materials.

Polypropylene Battery Separator Market to Reach US$28.31 Billion by 2035 as Capacity and Coating Investments Advance
10-25-2026 02:54 PM CET | Chemicals & Materials 
Press release from: DataM intelligence 4 Market Research LLP 
Regional production plans and new separator designs are sharpening competition around supply reliability, safety performance and customer qualification.
The global polypropylene battery separator market was valued at US$6.53 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach US$28.31 billion by 2035, growing at a CAGR of 15.8% from 2026 to 2035, according to DataM Intelligence. Lithium-ion batteries accounted for 72.5% of the market in 2025. Asia-Pacific held a 64.89% share, while North America is forecast to be the fastest-growing region. 
Battery separators must keep the electrodes apart while allowing ions to pass through the electrolyte. For polypropylene (PP) separators, competitive performance increasingly depends on film thickness, pore structure, mechanical strength, coating quality and consistency across production runs. Cell manufacturers qualify separators for particular chemistries and formats, so expanding capacity alone does not guarantee sales. Suppliers must meet customer specifications and demonstrate reliable output at scale.

Recent Developments
- Japan updated its battery industry strategy: In June 2026, METI cited structural oversupply and supply-chain risks, while highlighting energy-storage requirements associated with advanced power demand, including AI data centers. The strategy adds supply resilience and cost discipline to Japan's battery-industry priorities. 
- SEMCORP reported results for new separator designs: In June, the company said cells using its pure-polyolefin and polyolefin/ceramic-coated separators passed impact and hot-box tests and retained more than 91% capacity after 1,000 cycles in its evaluations. These are company-reported test results. 
- Asahi Kasei opened a coating line in North Carolina: The company held an August 20 ceremony for a new wet-process Hipore separator coating line at its existing Celgard facility, adding North American coating and supply capabilities. 
- SEMCORP began production at a Phase II line in Yuxi: On August 30, SEMCORP announced that the first production line of the project had been commissioned, starting a new capacity ramp-up phase. 
- ENTEK continued development of its Indiana separator plant: The company lists a Phase I capacity deployment of 700 million square metres and targets a Q4 2026 start of production. These remain company project targets, with commercial output dependent on construction, commissioning and qualification. 
- Sumitomo Chemical consolidated its PERVIO separator operations: The company's restructuring plan called for production at Ohe Works to cease and manufacturing functions to move to subsidiary SSLM by the end of March 2026. The change illustrates how established Japanese suppliers are adjusting their production footprints in a competitive market. 
United States & Japan Market Opportunities
United States: 
The clearest opportunity is to qualify local separator production and coating for battery manufacturers seeking closer supply and technical support. Asahi Kasei's North Carolina line adds coating capability at an established site, while ENTEK's Indiana project is aimed at wet-process separator manufacturing. Their different approaches show that the domestic opportunity spans new film production, coating, equipment, quality control and testing. The commercial test will be how quickly each line reaches reliable output and passes customer qualification. 
Japan: 
Japan's established battery-material companies can compete through separator engineering, coatings and close technical work with cell and automotive manufacturers. METI's revised battery strategy brings supply-chain risk and storage needs into the policy discussion. Meanwhile, Sumitomo Chemical's PERVIO reorganization reflects pressure to streamline production. Companies assessing Japanese opportunities should weigh customer access and local technical collaboration against the cost and utilization of maintaining multiple manufacturing sites. 
Market Segmentation
DataM Intelligence segments the market by thickness, layer, battery type, technology, end user and region. Thickness categories include below 20 μm, 20-50 μm, 50-100 μm and above 100 μm. Layer categories include single-layer, multilayer, microporous and other structures. Battery types include lithium-ion, lead-acid and others; technology includes dry and wet processes. End users span energy and power, electronics, automotive, telecommunications, aerospace and defense, medical and other markets. 
Segment Analysis: Lithium-Ion Batteries
Lithium-ion batteries accounted for 72.5% of the market in 2025, supported by separator use across EVs, energy storage and consumer electronics. This segment is not a uniform product market: cell makers set separator requirements around chemistry, electrode design, electrolyte, charging profile and form factor. That makes customer qualification and product consistency central to competition. 
The opportunity lies in supplying qualified separator grades that meet cell-specific performance targets. Automotive programs put particular weight on safety, durability and stable supply over long production cycles. Electronics customers may prioritize compact cell design and energy density, while stationary storage applications emphasize dependable operation over extended cycling. Suppliers that can adapt thickness, pore structure and coating to these requirements may win a broader range of programs, but each new grade can add testing and manufacturing complexity.
Battery chemistry changes can also shift requirements. A separator design suited to one cell architecture may not automatically transfer to another. Product development and capacity planning therefore depend on close collaboration with cell manufacturers-not simply forecasts of overall lithium-ion production.

Segment Analysis: Dry and Wet Technologies
The market includes dry-process and wet-process separators, but the two processes should not be treated as interchangeable. Dry processing is associated with PP separators and forms pores through stretching and related film-manufacturing steps. Its commercial appeal can include a simpler process route and cost-efficient production, with product value depending on pore uniformity, mechanical strength, film thickness and fit with the battery design.
Wet processing uses a different pore-forming route and is widely associated with PE separator products. ENTEK, for example, describes its lithium-ion separators as wet-process, biaxially oriented PE products, offered in coated and uncoated formats. It also identifies thickness, air permeability and porosity as characteristics that can be tailored with customers. This distinction matters when assessing the PP market: competitors may operate across the broader polyolefin separator sector without every product being made from polypropylene. 
Technology selection depends on the target cell's performance needs and manufacturing economics. Cell makers evaluate separator properties, coating compatibility, yield, operating cost and production-line fit. Suppliers, in turn, need to demonstrate repeatable quality and adequate scale. New plants and coating lines may widen the regional supply base, but their commercial value depends on qualified output-not announced nameplate capacity alone.
Company Profiles
- Asahi Kasei Corporation - Asahi Kasei supplies wet-process Hipore and dry-process Celgard lithium-ion separators. Celgard offers single- and multilayer configurations, different film thicknesses and widths, and optional functional coatings. The company's North Carolina coating line adds local processing for Hipore products at an existing Celgard site, giving it a combined product and manufacturing footprint in North America. 
- ENTEK International - ENTEK manufactures wet-process, biaxially oriented PE separators for lithium-ion batteries, with coated and uncoated options. Its product specifications can be customized around thickness, air permeability and porosity. The company is building a large Indiana facility, with a stated Phase I capacity deployment of 700 million m2 and a Q4 2026 production target. Its U.S. expansion will depend on commissioning and customer qualification. 
- SEMCORP - SEMCORP's lithium-ion separator business combines product development with large-scale manufacturing. Its recent updates include evaluations of pure-polyolefin and ceramic-coated designs, as well as the commissioning of a Phase II production line at Yuxi. Together, these developments highlight its focus on functional coatings, battery performance and capacity expansion. 
- Toray Industries - Toray's film portfolio includes SETELA battery separator film for lithium-ion batteries and TORAYFAN polypropylene film. The company identifies SETELA as a microporous film used in batteries for mobile devices and EVs. Its separator R&D includes product functionality, quality improvement, manufacturing-process development and cost reduction. 
- Sumitomo Chemical - Sumitomo Chemical markets PERVIO lithium-ion battery separators. It announced a reorganization of the business that consolidated manufacturing and related functions at subsidiary SSLM, with production at Ohe Works scheduled to end by March 2026. The restructuring reflects the need to align production sites and operating costs with customer demand and competitive conditions.

Samsung's Exynos processor (Samsung Electronics) 
Samsung Electronics' next-generation Exynos 2700 mobile processor scored nearly 20 percent higher than Qualcomm's top-end Snapdragon chip in an internal multicore CPU test, ahead of its expected debut in the Galaxy S27 series early next year.
The results came from recent in-house benchmark tests comparing the Exynos 2700 with Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, which powers Xiaomi's 18 Pro Max, according to industry sources Sunday.
In Geekbench 6.5, the Exynos 2700 posted a multicore CPU score of around 13,000, compared with roughly 11,000 for Qualcomm's Extreme chip. The Samsung processor also scored about 15 percent higher in Geekbench 7.0 multicore tests.
Qualcomm has introduced two versions of its latest flagship mobile chipset: the top-end Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and the standard Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6. The Extreme variant powers the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max, while the standard version is used in the Xiaomi 18 Pro.
Against the standard Snapdragon chip, the Exynos 2700 scored 44 percent higher in Geekbench 6.5 multicore tests and 36 percent higher in Geekbench 7.0.
The Samsung chip also outperformed Qualcomm's Extreme model in graphics tests, which measure capabilities important for gaming and video playback.
In a test of peak graphics performance under demanding gaming conditions using advanced graphics technologies, the Exynos 2700 scored about 20 percent higher than the Qualcomm chip. It also held a roughly 5 percent lead in a separate test measuring basic graphics processing capabilities in high-end 3D games.
Samsung's System LSI business designs the Exynos family of mobile processors, which handle core computing and graphics tasks in smartphones. The previous-generation Exynos 2600 powers select Galaxy S26 models and the Galaxy Z Flip8.
The Exynos 2700 is expected to be manufactured using Samsung's second-generation 2-nanometer foundry process, known as SF2P. The chip is also expected to feature an upgraded heat path block, packaging technology designed to improve heat dissipation and performance.
"Development of the Exynos 2700 is on track, with the aim of having it used in flagship models," Park Yong-in, president and head of system LSI business, said at a management briefing in June.
