Park Kwang-sun, president of Applied Materials Korea, poses for a commemorative photo at the 19th Semiconductor Day ceremony held at the Grand InterContinental Seoul Parnas in Gangnam, Seoul, on Oct. 21. (Photo: Applied Materials Korea) 
Applied Materials Korea received an Industrial Service Medal in recognition of its contributions to strengthening South Korea's semiconductor industry competitiveness.
Park Kwang-sun, president of Applied Materials Korea, received the medal at the 19th Semiconductor Day ceremony held at the Grand InterContinental Seoul Parnas in Gangnam, Seoul, on Oct. 21.
Applied Materials Korea said the award recognized its efforts to expand the global technology innovation ecosystem and strengthen collaboration on next-generation semiconductor research and development (R&D). Park has promoted cooperation among domestic customers and suppliers and led efforts to build industry networks.
Applied Materials Korea is establishing the Applied Collaboration Center Korea in Osan, Gyeonggi Province, as a regional hub. The center will expand collaboration with major domestic customers and suppliers, supporting activities from early-stage R&D to mass-production validation. It aims to develop local talent and strengthen the competitiveness of South Korea's semiconductor ecosystem.
The company also invests in domestic startups. Applied Materials Korea works with approximately 100 local suppliers. It has established a $50 million fund with Korea Venture Investment Corp. (KVIC) to support promising domestic startups. The company also organizes technology symposiums and site visit programs for university students and provides semiconductor simulation software to university research laboratories.
Semiconductor Day was established by the Korea Semiconductor Industry Association in 2008. Each year, the association recognizes individuals who have contributed to strengthening the competitiveness of South Korea's semiconductor industry.

LOS ANGELES, United States: QY Research has recently published a research report titled, "Global Ultra-high Purity Aluminum Sputtering Target Market Insights - Industry Share, Sales Projections, and Demand Outlook 2026-2032". The report offers an industry-standard and a highly authentic research study on the global Ultra-high Purity Aluminum Sputtering Target market. With qualitative and quantitative analysis, it throws light on some of the crucial factors contributing to the growth of the global Ultra-high Purity Aluminum Sputtering Target market. As part of a study on market dynamics, it also explains factors affecting the global market growth. The authors of the report have provided a broad competitive assessment, detailed regional study, and other different types of research studies to give a complete analysis of the global Ultra-high Purity Aluminum Sputtering Target market. The report can be used as an effective tool for finding new ways of growth and ensuring lasting success in the global Ultra-high Purity Aluminum Sputtering Target market.

Get PDF Sample Copy of Report: (Including Full TOC, List of Tables & Figures, Chart) @ https://www.qyresearch.in/request-sample/chemical-material-global-ultra-high-purity-aluminum-sputtering-target-market-insights-industry-share-sales-projections-and-demand-outlook-2026-2032 
Ultra-high-purity aluminum sputtering targets are essential base materials used in thin-film processes for semiconductors, flat-panel displays, and solar cells, with demand steadily increasing as metallization structures become more complex in advanced manufacturing nodes. These products are defined by purity levels ranging from 4N (≥99.99%) to 6N, and the industry's core technical barriers lie in ultra-high-purity refining, impurity control, grain refinement, and uniformity management for large-size targets. The global market is dominated by a small number of suppliers capable of ultra-high-purity metal refining and precision processing. Asia-Pacific is the largest consumption region, accounting for about 89% of global demand, with China alone holding approximately 49%, reflecting a highly concentrated regional structure.
In terms of product structure, purity grades include 4N, 4N5, 5N, 5N5, and 6N. Among them, 5N is the dominant category with roughly 65% market share, followed by 5N5 at around 18%. Different purity levels correspond to different process nodes and film performance requirements; higher purity demands stricter control over impurities, oxide inclusions, grain size uniformity, and particle contamination. By application, semiconductors account for the largest share at about 49%, mainly for metal interconnects, electrodes, and barrier/adhesion layers; flat-panel displays account for about 36.5%, primarily for pixel electrodes and reflective layers; solar-related applications constitute a smaller but steadily growing segment.
Regarding cost structure, ultra-high-purity aluminum feedstock represents a high proportion of total costs, typically 45%-55%; processing costs-including annealing, hot rolling, cold rolling, extrusion, and precision machining-represent 30%-40%; the remainder consists of labor, inspection, and depreciation. Typical single-line capacity ranges from 150 to 300 tons per year, with capacity expansion constrained by investments in high-purity refining equipment and strict quality-control systems. Industry-wide gross margins generally remain around 25%-35%, with higher margins achievable for higher-purity and higher-uniformity products. Upstream suppliers include ultra-high-purity aluminum producers and specialized refining-technology providers, while downstream users include wafer fabs, display manufacturers, and solar module producers.
The competitive landscape is clearly oligopolistic, led by global suppliers such as Sumitomo Chemical, Konfoong Materials International (KFMI), Linde, TOSOH, and Honeywell. Sumitomo Chemical is the market leader with approximately 22% global share. Chinese manufacturers have established strong competitiveness in the 4N5-5N range and are advancing steadily in 5N5-6N grades, while Japanese and U.S. suppliers continue to lead in ultra-high-purity refining and large-size target uniformity. The tightly integrated supply chain and long customer qualification cycles contribute to high industry stickiness and entry barriers.
Looking ahead, as advanced nodes require increasingly stringent control of film purity, particle levels, and thickness uniformity, ultra-high-purity aluminum targets will further develop toward higher purity, larger dimensions, fewer defects, and tighter compositional homogeneity. The growing use of combined PVD-ALD processes, larger wafer sizes, and greater penetration of OLED and high-end display technologies will continue to drive market expansion. At the same time, localization and supply-chain security concerns-particularly in Asia and especially in China-will accelerate capacity growth and technological upgrading in the region.

Investing.com -- British measurement firm Renishaw said on Thursday first-quarter revenue jumped 47% to a record £251.8 million, driven by demand from semiconductor and aerospace customers, but stopped short of raising its full-year guidance. 
Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list » 
The figure for the three months to Sept 30 was 47% higher than a weak comparator a year earlier and 3% above the fourth quarter of the last financial year, the company said in an unaudited trading update. 
At constant exchange rates, which strip out currency moves, revenue rose 48% from the previous year. 
Renishaw said it continues to expect "strong progress on revenue and operating margin for FY2027 as a whole." Revenue grew in all three business segments and all three regions. 
Position Measurement revenue rose 84% to a record £96.0 million from £52.1 million a year earlier, driven by demand for open optical and laser encoders used in semiconductor manufacturing equipment. 
Revenue was 17% above the fourth quarter. The order book grew further in the quarter, and Renishaw is investing in more production capacity for those products. It also saw rising demand for encoders for harsh environments in automation, robotics and space applications. 
Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks » 
Industrial Metrology revenue rose 28% to £130.8 million from £102 million a year earlier, and was 9% above the fourth quarter, on demand for five-axis coordinate measuring machines and shop-floor gauging systems, with a growing order book. 
Sales of sensors to machine tool and measuring machine makers also improved after a flat FY2026, with stronger sales into aerospace and defence, energy and consumer electronics. 
Specialised Technologies revenue rose 50% to £25 million from £16.7 million, led by additive manufacturing systems sold to aerospace and defence and medical customers. 
Revenue was below the £42.7 million of the fourth quarter, as expected, after what the company called an "exceptionally strong" period. 
The order book has strengthened. Spectroscopy revenue was marginally lower than a year earlier, though its order book also strengthened. Renishaw said the sale of its neurological business continues. 
Demand from semiconductor, aerospace and defence customers remains strong, and is now complemented by wider automation investment in other industries, the company said.

It is working to expand its supply chain and production capacity while remaining "mindful of the cyclical nature of demand over the medium term."

title: Latest information on a possible combination of BASF and Evonik - BASF – United States
query: "Evonik Industries" ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Latest information on a possible combination of BASF and Evonik 
In recent weeks, there has been extensive reporting on the potential combination of BASF and Evonik – particularly in the Ruhr region, Evonik’s home.  
In this video, Markus Kamieth, CEO of BASF, explains why BASF is seeking a combination with Evonik – and what opportunities he sees arising from it. He specifically addresses the employees of Evonik and the people of the Ruhr region.
Downloads
Download Transcript 
Download Video (719 MB) 
Transcript of Markus Kamieth’s statement
“A strong chemical industry in Germany is the right response to global competition.” 
These days, many are asking questions. About BASF. About Evonik. About the future of the chemical industry in Germany. And especially in the Ruhr region.
I was born in Dinslaken and studied in Essen. My father worked underground for 35 years in the mines. I come from North Rhine-Westphalia. So, I understand the questions people are asking when they hear that BASF wants to join forces with Evonik. For employees, the most important question is, of course: What does this mean for my job?
And I can assure you that: First: BASF would take over the existing site agreements. This means that compulsory redundancies, would remain ruled out until 2032. Collective bargaining agreements and the social partnership would remain untouched. And we would continue to invest in training young people.
Second: Essen and North Rhine-Westphalia would remain important locations. With at least one Board member based there, as well as the leadership of business and functional units. We would look at which joint activities could be managed from Essen. And we want to strengthen North Rhine-Westphalia as a location for research and development.
Third, Evonik plans to sell Syneqt, the chemical park operator. Our approach is more open: We believe that we could continue to operate the parks in Marl and Wesseling ourselves as well. The sale currently planned by Evonik will affect approximately 3,500 jobs in North Rhine-Westphalia.
The Ruhr region has been through many transformations before. The mines are gone. The steel industry has become smaller. And yet the region has constantly reinvented itself. This is exactly the kind of ability the chemical industry needs today and in the future.
Our industry is changing faster than ever before. In particular, competitors from Asia and the Middle East are becoming stronger and stronger. The Evonik team is doing an excellent job. But our industry has been facing strong headwinds for years. And those headwinds are getting stronger.
At BASF, we also have to deal with these difficult conditions. We are doing our own homework. Since two years, our “Winning Ways” strategy takes effect. Now we want to take the next step. Together with Evonik.
Both BASF and Evonik are strong players in specialty chemicals. In innovative, customer-focused solutions with global market access. But BASF’s strengths also lie in its Verbund. In integrated value chains with access to key building blocks in every region of the world. The products and strengths of both companies complement each other extremely well.
Evonik currently has to purchase certain feedstocks. Through BASF’s Verbund, these could be sourced more cost-effectively, more directly, and more reliably from within the company. On top of that come advantages in procurement, infrastructure, and research. Size and financial strength are real advantages, including for the sites in North Rhine-Westphalia.
The chemical industry is consolidating, one way or another. The question is: Do we shape this ourselves? As German companies, with our values, our model of co-determination and our social partnership? Or do we wait until European chemical companies are overtaken in global competition or increasingly acquired by foreign investors? A combination of BASF and Evonik would be a strong German response to global competition.
The coalition agreement of the federal government sets out the goal of making Germany the most innovative chemical industry location in the world. This is the opportunity. This is also an opportunity for the RAG Foundation. It has already announced that it intends to reduce its stake in Evonik. This is important in order to continue to fulfill the foundation’s purpose as effectively as possible in the future.
The Foundation is responsible for securing the long-term funding of the perpetual obligations of the mining industry. In concrete terms: making sure that water will still be pumped out of old shafts in the future. And that no home in the Ruhr region will subside.
Above all, however, this is an opportunity for Evonik to create value for all shareholders. And together with us, to build a globally successful chemical company that is even stronger. One that preserves jobs in Germany. One that is better equipped to compete globally.
We are ready to enter into talks. Because we want to shape the future together. However, we will not pursue a merger at any price. We owe this not only to our shareholders but also to our employees. But we’re approaching this with the confidence that, together, we can build something that is stronger than the two companies on their own.
This is what it comes down to: Think smaller alone, or think bigger together. A strong chemical industry in Germany is the right response to global competition. Let’s make it happen together. It’s worth it.
Important Notice 
This video is for information purposes only. It is neither an offer to purchase nor a solicitation of an offer to sell any shares or other securities of Evonik Industries AG ("Evonik"). Should BASF SE ("BASF") make a public offer for securities of Evonik, its terms and further provisions would be set out only in a formal offer document.

content_text:
Solvay cuts 2026 guidance as Middle East conflict hits Q3 earnings
Solvay now expects full-year underlying EBITDA of €720 million to €740 million
By ICN Bureau | October 22, 2026 
Belgian chemical group Solvay has lowered its full-year 2026 financial guidance after the Middle East conflict and the continued shutdown of a peroxide plant in Saudi Arabia hit its third-quarter performance.
 
The company reported preliminary third-quarter underlying EBITDA of €173 million on underlying net sales of €1.03 billion, with free cash flow to Solvay shareholders from continuing operations reaching €54 million.
 
Solvay now expects full-year underlying EBITDA of €720 million to €740 million and free cash flow of €120 million to €150 million, excluding any potential revenue or recovery measures linked to its Saudi operations for the remainder of the year.
 
The conflict in the Middle East reduced underlying EBITDA by approximately €25 million in the third quarter, following a negative impact of around €20 million in the second quarter, the company said.
 
The continued shutdown of the peroxide plant at the Sadara complex in Jubail, Saudi Arabia, accounted for nearly €15 million of the third-quarter EBITDA hit.
 
Solvay operates in Jubail through a joint venture with Sadara, which is majority-owned by Saudi Aramco. The company said it is exploring options to limit the financial damage, with contractual mechanisms in place that are designed to recover lost profitability.
 
The revised free cash flow target of €120 million to €150 million for 2026 is net of approximately €90 million in transformation expenses.
 
Despite the disruption, Solvay said it remains committed to its transformation programme, with a continued focus on cash generation and meeting its cost-saving targets.
 
The latest outlook underscores the financial pressure facing the group as geopolitical instability disrupts operations and weighs on earnings.
 
Solvay said it would not comment further before releasing its full third-quarter results on November 4, citing an ongoing quiet period.
 
Under the updated guidance, Solvay expects: Underlying EBITDA: €720 million to €740 million. Free cash flow to Solvay shareholders from continuing operations: €120 million to €150 million, after approximately €90 million in transformation expenses.
 
The figures are preliminary and remain subject to completion of the company's quarter-end closing process.

title: Sumitomo Chemical deepens India semiconductor push with Tata Electronics pact - Indiatimes
query: "Sumitomo Chemical" ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Sumitomo Chemical deepens India semiconductor push with Tata Electronics pact 
Sumitomo Chemical has signed an MoU with Tata Electronics to explore collaboration in semiconductor fabrication and materials supply, including a possible chemicals facility in India. The move reflects growing interest from upstream suppliers in India’s chip ambitions, where reliable access to high-purity chemicals and photoresists could shape future manufacturing capacity. 
ETChemicals 
Published On Oct 21, 2026 at 12:04 PM IST
Read by 2812 Professionals
Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook 
Bookmark 
India’s semiconductor ambitions are increasingly drawing in global materials suppliers, not just chip designers and fabricators. In a move that underlines that shift, Sumitomo Chemical has signed a memorandum of understanding with Tata Electronics to examine a possible collaboration in semiconductor fabrication and the supporting supply chain , according to specchemonline.com . 
The agreement is significant because semiconductor manufacturing depends on a tightly controlled ecosystem of chemicals, photoresists and high-purity inputs. Any serious effort to localise chip production in India will need those upstream materials to be available reliably, at scale and with consistent quality. That is the business opportunity Sumitomo Chemical appears to be targeting through the Tata partnership. 
What the agreement is meant to cover 
The companies plan to study specific steps that could help create a stable materials supply system for semiconductor manufacturing. One possibility being explored is the establishment of a semiconductor chemicals facility in India, which would give the Japanese supplier a local foothold in a market that is still building out its chip ecosystem. 
The MoU does not amount to a final investment decision, but it signals intent. For Tata Electronics , which is building its semiconductor ambitions in India, a dependable materials partner could be as important as equipment, talent and policy support. For Sumitomo Chemical, the arrangement offers a way to align with a customer base that may grow as India pushes harder into advanced electronics manufacturing. 
Why materials matter more than ever 
Semiconductor fabrication is often discussed through the lens of fabs, foundries and government incentives, but the industry is equally dependent on specialist materials. Photoresists and high-purity chemicals are essential in the patterning and processing steps that allow chips to be manufactured at advanced nodes. Supply disruptions in these inputs can quickly ripple through production schedules and yield outcomes. 
That is why localisation efforts are increasingly extending beyond assembly and packaging. Countries seeking to build semiconductor resilience are now looking at the full stack, including the chemicals that enable chipmaking in the first place. A domestic or regional supply base can reduce logistics risk, shorten lead times and improve control over quality assurance. 
Sumitomo Chemical is betting on semiconductor growth 
The semiconductor materials business has been positioned as a priority inside Sumitomo Chemical’s ICT and Mobility Solutions segment, which the Japanese group views as one of its growth engines. The company has built a reputation in advanced photoresists and semiconductor chemicals, particularly high-purity products used in demanding fabrication environments. 
Over the past few years, the company has expanded semiconductor chemicals capacity in Japan and South Korea while also setting up a new base in Texas. Earlier this year, it acquired Asia Union Electronic Chemical , which operates facilities in Taiwan and Nevada. The company has also started work at advanced high-purity chemical centres in Japan and South Korea, where it is developing new processes and recycling technologies. 
That sequence of investments suggests a broader strategy: deepen presence in major semiconductor geographies while improving supply resilience and technical capabilities. The India move fits that pattern, especially as chip manufacturing becomes more geographically diversified in response to geopolitical and supply chain concerns. 
India’s chip ecosystem is attracting upstream players 
India has spent the past few years trying to move from policy ambition to industrial execution in semiconductors . The country’s appeal is no longer limited to final-stage electronics assembly. Global suppliers are beginning to evaluate whether India can support the specialised materials and process infrastructure needed for chip fabrication. 
That shift matters because semiconductor projects are rarely built in isolation. A viable ecosystem requires chemical suppliers, gas suppliers, wafer handling, cleanroom services, logistics providers and a skilled technical workforce. The presence of a company such as Sumitomo Chemical would be a signal that India is moving closer to that broader industrial base. 
For Tata Electronics, the partnership could help strengthen its supply chain planning at a time when semiconductor manufacturing is becoming a strategic priority for large industrial groups in India. For Sumitomo Chemical, the arrangement could open a pathway into a market that combines scale potential with policy support for electronics manufacturing. 
Regional competition is also intensifying 
The India discussion comes as Japanese chemical companies continue to expand in other Asian semiconductor hubs. Another Japanese player, Nissan Chemical , has separately set up a wholly owned subsidiary in Zhangjiagang in Jiangsu province, China. That unit will manufacture anti-reflective coatings used in photoresists and multilayer semiconductor materials. 
Nissan Chemical has said demand for semiconductors in China has continued to rise, helped by digitalisation and other structural factors, while customers are also seeking more resilient supply chains. The parallel expansion by Japanese suppliers in China and India highlights a broader industry trend: materials companies are following chip manufacturing demand wherever it is likely to concentrate next. 
For India, the challenge will be to convert interest into durable industrial capacity. A materials facility, if it goes ahead, would not by itself create a complete semiconductor supply chain. But it would be an important marker of confidence, showing that upstream global suppliers are willing to commit capital and know-how to the country’s chip ambitions. 
The Tata Electronics tie-up therefore sits at the intersection of manufacturing policy, supply chain resilience and long-term industrial strategy. If the exploratory talks lead to a concrete project, it could become one of the more telling examples of how India’s semiconductor push is beginning to draw in the chemicals businesses that underpin the sector’s real economics.

ABB Robotics has launched its first fully integrated, camera-based Physical AI solution for logistics applications in the fashion industry.
ABB Robotics is launching its first end-to-end physical-AI solution for industrial applications: the Fashion Inductor and AI Robot Trainer. (Image: ABB Robotics) 
By integrating the AI Robot Trainer into the Fashion Inductor feature package, ABB Robotics aims to help system integrators implement, scale, and continuously optimize AI-powered applications for fashion logistics with less effort and risk.
“Physical AI is fundamentally changing what robots can do in industrial applications,” emphasizes Craig McDonnell, head of the Industries business line at ABB Robotics. “Some of the greatest potential of Physical AI lies in applications that, due to their high variability, have been difficult to automate until now.”
Designed to Meet the Demands of Fashion Logistics
The Fashion Inductor was developed specifically to meet the demands and accommodate the wide variety of the fashion and apparel logistics sector, where products, packaging, and operating conditions are constantly changing. Even today, the system is designed to enable high-performance sorting and separation under real-world logistics conditions—with a throughput of up to 1,300 items per hour per cell and a grasping accuracy of more than 99.5 percent. This is made possible by ABB Robotics’ AI-powered automatic path planning, the robots’ high motion precision, and the image processing technology developed specifically for this application.
Physical AI Features Reduce Effort by 75 Percent
The AI Robot Trainer adds camera-based Physical AI features designed to reduce development and commissioning efforts by up to 75 percent. The solution includes pre-trained AI models for image processing—specifically tailored to applications in fashion and apparel logistics—as well as application-specific tools and features for quickly retraining the models. This is intended to enable system integrators to implement applications without specialized AI expertise, adapt them to changing requirements, and continuously optimize them.
AI Robot Trainer Enables a Closed-Loop Workflow
The AI models are not only developed but also continuously optimized throughout the robot system’s entire lifecycle and adapted to real-world performance requirements and changing operating conditions. The AI Robot Trainer enables fast and structured retraining tailored to the specific robot cell within a so-called closed-loop workflow. In this process, the system monitors the robot’s performance, detects deviations, generates new training data for the models, and feeds improvements directly back to the robot.

Sony Semiconductor Solutions Announces 1 mm Square Image Sensor for Medical Single-Use Endoscopes, Featuring Industry's First*¹5 m Digital Transmission and High Image Quality
PR Newswire 
October 21, 2026 4 min read 
Providing stable transmission of high-definition images for thin endoscopes 
ATSUGI, Japan, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sony Semiconductor Solutions Corporation (Sony) today announced the upcoming release of the IMX742, a CMOS image sensor with approximately 0.51 effective megapixels*2 for medical single-use endoscopes. This sensor is the industry's first*1 to support digital output and data transmission through a 5 m*3 cable. 
IMX742 CMOS image sensor for single-use endoscopes
Model name
IMX742 1/17.7-type CMOS image sensor with approximately 0.51 effective megapixels for single-use endoscopes Demand for disposable, single-use endoscopes is growing in the medical field to help prevent infections and reduce the burden of endoscope reprocessing and managing equipment after use. Cameras on such endoscopes require not only compact sensors that are compatible with today's increasingly small diameter insertion parts but also improved basic performance such as high image quality and stable signal transmission. 
By miniaturizing peripheral circuits, including the A/D converter (analog-to-digital conversion circuit), and using proprietary bi-directional communication technology to transmit control and video signals via the same cable, the IMX742 combines approximately 0.51 effective megapixels with a compact 1 mm-square sensor size. Furthermore, digitizing image signals on the sensor enables low-noise imaging at a high frame rate of 60 fps, with stable transmission via a 5 m cable, providing clear images for endoscopic visualization. These features will contribute to the miniaturization and improved image quality of thin endoscope cameras used in bronchoscopes and ureteroscopes. 
Sony has provided image sensors for reusable endoscopes and will expand its offerings to single-use endoscope applications, for which demand continues to rise, thereby contributing to the realization of endoscope systems designed to meet needs for reduced invasiveness and improved operability and visibility. 
Model name: IMX742 1/17.7-type CMOS image sensor with approximately 0.51 effective megapixels for single-use endoscopes. Sample shipment date (planned) November 2026. 
*1 Among CMOS image sensors for medical endoscopes. According to Sony research (as of announcement on October 22, 2026).
*2 Based on the image sensor effective pixel specification method.
*3 Transmission distance confirmed in a Sony evaluation environment using an AWG44 cable. 
Main Features 
Achieving high resolution and digital output in a compact 1 mm-square sensor 
The new sensor combines approximately 0.51 effective megapixels and digital output in a compact 1 mm-square sensor suitable for thin endoscopes.
Digital output requires the A/D converter to be integrated into the sensor, making sensor miniaturization more challenging. This product miniaturizes peripheral circuits, including the A/D converter, while preserving sufficient area for the pixel array, thereby achieving both high resolution and digital output in a compact sensor.
Additionally, it uses Sony's proprietary bi-directional communication technology to enable both the control and video signals to be transmitted via the same cable while keeping the number of sensor pins to six.
These features contribute to the further miniaturization and improved image quality of thin endoscopes, including bronchoscopes and ureteroscopes. 
Stable transmission of high-quality 60 fps images on a 5 m cable 
The new sensor outputs image signals digitized on the sensor, enabling lower-noise imaging in low-light environments compared with analog output. This provides high visibility in dark areas inside the body, even when the sensor is used in thin endoscopes equipped with compact LED light sources that offer limited brightness. It also supports a high frame rate of 60 fps, enabling smooth video display that keeps pace with rapid movement during diagnosis and treatment.
Additionally, outputting a digital signal enables stable video transmission, which makes it possible to configure a system using a 5 m-long cable.
With all these features, the new sensor supports stable image acquisition in thin endoscopes and increased flexibility in cable routing and system configuration, contributing to the realization of endoscope systems that support smoother observation.

Published : Oct. 22, 2026 - 10:27:43

Link copied!

Tech Reporter
Covers Korean companies at the center of global chips, AI and consumer technology, from Samsung and SK hynix to Apple suppliers

Merck Electronics CEO sees Korea as key market as company braces for potential doubling of chip materials demand
Benjamin Hein, CEO of Merck's Electronics business, speaks during a press conference in Seoul on Wednesday. (Merck Korea) 
German science and technology company Merck opened a new semiconductor materials plant in South Korea on Thursday, expanding local production of molybdenum as chipmakers adopt the metal for increasingly advanced memory chips.
The facility in Eumseong, North Chungcheong Province, will produce molybdenum dioxide dichloride, a chemical used to deposit ultrathin metal films during chip manufacturing. It will supply customers in Korea and elsewhere in Asia.
Benjamin Hein, CEO of Merck's Electronics business, described Korea as among the top three markets for semiconductor materials during a press conference in Seoul on Wednesday.
"What if the demand for semiconductor materials and solutions doubles within the next five years? Are we ready? We want to be ready," Hein said.
The plant will initially focus on materials for advanced 3D NAND flash memory, which increases storage capacity by stacking memory cells vertically.
Merck's Eumseong plant in North Chungcheong Province, where the German company opened a new molybdenum production facility for advanced semiconductor manufacturing on Thursday (Merck Korea) 
Samsung Electronics began using molybdenum in its ninth-generation V-NAND in 2024, while SK hynix has reportedly been preparing to introduce the metal in its next-generation 375-layer NAND.
Molybdenum offers an alternative to tungsten, whose electrical resistance becomes increasingly problematic as chipmakers shrink components and stack more layers. It can also reduce the need for barrier films that occupy valuable space inside microscopic structures.
Bing Han, executive vice president and head of Merck's Thin Films business, said adoption was beginning with NAND, with DRAM and logic chips expected to follow. "Eventually more of the smaller features will all move to Moly," Han said, while acknowledging that the pace of adoption depends on individual customers.
Merck will combine precursor production in Eumseong with chemical delivery systems manufactured at its Ansan facility in Gyeonggi Province. The company says the integrated system can use more than 99 percent of the material loaded into its containers, potentially reducing waste and manufacturing costs.
"Local for local is everything," Han said. "You can have the best offering, but you have to have your best offering in the right location."
The expansion forms part of Merck's 600 million euro ($674 million) investment program announced in 2021. Merck disclosed plans for the molybdenum facility in February, but declined to reveal its investment cost or production capacity.
Hein also identified advanced packaging, which combines multiple chips into increasingly complex systems, as another growth area. He said manufacturers face an immediate shortage of packaging capacity, with further technological changes expected over the next three to five years.
"On advanced packaging, short term, there is simply not enough capacity," he said. "So on the immediate, it is about debottlenecking."

The Korea Toray Science Foundation has selected Professor Kim Sang-kyu of KAIST’s Department of Chemistry and Professor Kim Yoon-hee of Gyeongsang National University’s Department of Chemistry as recipients of the ninth Toray Science and Technology Awards.
The foundation said it held the awards ceremony at Seoul Garden Hotel on Oct. 21, attended by approximately 150 guests, including award recipients, academics, industry representatives and students. The two professors, recognized for their research achievements in chemistry and materials science, each received a prize of 100 million won.
Five early-career researchers were selected for the foundation’s fellowship program: Song In-taek, professor of chemistry and physics at DGIST; Hong Seung-yoon, professor of chemistry at Seoul National University; Kim Hyung-jun, professor of chemical and biomolecular engineering at Sogang University; Chun Dong-won, professor of materials science and engineering at POSTECH; and Ham Dong-hyo, professor of chemical engineering at Hanyang University. Each will receive 150 million won in research funding over three years.
Since its establishment in 2018, the Korea Toray Science Foundation has selected 18 science and technology award recipients and 40 fellowship researchers. The foundation also provides annual scholarships to university students majoring in science and engineering, supporting a total of 255 students through the second semester of 2026.

Danaher Q3 Earnings Call Highlights
4 minutos de lectura 
DHR 
The Often-Missed Corner of Healthcare That Wall Street Is Loving 
Danaher DHR reported third-quarter 2026 results that exceeded its expectations, citing improved market conditions, commercial execution and operational performance across its Biotechnology, Life Sciences and Diagnostics businesses. 
Sales totaled $6.6 billion for the quarter. Core revenue growth excluding respiratory testing revenue was 5.5%, accelerating 100 basis points from the second quarter. Respiratory revenue created an approximately 250-basis-point headwind, resulting in reported core revenue growth of 3%. 
An AI Play Hiding in Plain Sight: A Look at Johnson Controls 
Adjusted operating profit margin rose 110 basis points to 29%, aided primarily by operational execution and a modest benefit from tariff refunds received during the quarter. Adjusted diluted earnings per share increased about 11.5% to $2.11. The company generated $1.6 billion of free cash flow in the quarter and $4 billion through the first nine months of the year. 
New CEO Outlines Growth Priorities 
President and Chief Executive Officer Julie Sawyer Montgomery, in her first earnings call as CEO, said the company’s objective is to become the “defining leader in Life Sciences and Diagnostics” by gaining share more consistently, delivering profitable growth and helping customers improve patient outcomes. 
3 Stocks Offering Strong Value and Stability 
Montgomery said Danaher’s focus is shifting from portfolio reshaping toward generating more growth from its existing businesses. She outlined four strategic priorities: commercial excellence, innovation, talent and disciplined capital allocation. 
The company’s most immediate opportunity is commercial execution, according to Montgomery. She said Danaher intends to preserve the customer intimacy and accountability of its operating-company structure while making it easier for customers to access capabilities across the broader organization. 
In Diagnostics, she said coordinated engagement by leaders from different businesses with major customers has created “several hundred millions of dollars of opportunity” in a short period. Montgomery said Danaher views higher core growth, profitable core growth and “unambiguous share gain” as the measures of progress. 
Montgomery also emphasized artificial intelligence as an opportunity both internally and for customers. Danaher recently announced an AI-powered autonomous laboratory at Abcam that combines AI, robotics and technologies from Cytiva, Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, Genedata, IDT and Molecular Devices. The company said the connected design, make and test workflow is designed to help researchers move from an idea to a validated reagent up to eight times faster and produce up to 10 times higher volume than existing models. 
The company also announced a collaboration with NVIDIA focused on connecting Danaher instruments, automation and software with NVIDIA AI and advanced-computing capabilities. Montgomery said the company is also working with Anthropic on standards intended to make instruments easier to connect with other agents and instruments. 
Segment Performance 
Biotechnology core revenue increased 5% in the third quarter. Bioprocessing revenue grew toward the upper end of the mid-single-digit range, exceeding the company’s expectations. Consumables increased mid-single digits, led by upstream consumables, while equipment revenue grew low single digits. Bioprocessing orders increased in the mid-teens, led by upstream consumables and reagents. 
Chief Financial Officer Matt Gugino said Danaher maintained its expectation for mid-single-digit bioprocessing core revenue growth for the full year. He said the company continues to view bioprocessing as a long-term high-single-digit growth business, supported by commercial production activity and a pipeline of new programs. 
Life Sciences core revenue rose 4.5%. Pall’s applied filtration business grew mid-single digits, driven by aerospace and microelectronics demand. Life Sciences instruments also increased mid-single digits, with SCIEX benefiting from pharma and biopharma demand, improving U.S. academic spending and momentum for products including the ZenoTOF 8600. 
Beckman Coulter Life Sciences reported strong performance, including increased demand for AI-enabled automation solutions and services. Collectively, Life Sciences consumables businesses grew low single digits, with IDT benefiting from molecular residual disease and next-generation sequencing products, while Abcam experienced improving academic demand and traction with pharma and biopharma customers. 
Diagnostics core revenue excluding respiratory testing increased 7%. Respiratory revenue represented an approximately 650-basis-point headwind, leaving total segment core growth of 50 basis points. Clinical Diagnostics businesses grew mid-single digits, led by Leica Biosystems’ momentum in digital pathology and advanced staining. Beckman Coulter Diagnostics delivered its highest core-growth quarter in more than two years, according to the company. 
Cepheid’s non-respiratory molecular diagnostics business grew low double digits, driven by group A strep, virology and sexual-health assays. Respiratory revenue was approximately $350 million, declining year over year due mainly to lower global infection rates, though it was modestly above the company’s expectations as customers purchased ahead of the respiratory season. 
Outlook and Capital Deployment 
For the fourth quarter, Danaher expects core revenue growth excluding respiratory revenue of 4% to 5%. Respiratory revenue is expected to be an approximately 150-basis-point headwind, while adjusted operating profit margin is projected at about 29.5%. 
The company increased its full-year 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $8.57 to $8.62, from a prior range of $8.45 to $8.60. Gugino said the new range reflects third-quarter outperformance and represents double-digit year-over-year EPS growth. 
For 2027, Danaher said it views 4% to 5% core revenue growth excluding respiratory revenue as the appropriate starting point based on current market conditions, though formal guidance will be provided in January. The company is using $1.5 billion in respiratory revenue as its planning assumption for both 2026 and as a starting point for 2027, while noting that seasonal flu variability can affect that figure. 
On acquisitions, Montgomery said M&A remains Danaher’s preferred capital-allocation approach and that the company will continue to seek strategically compounding transactions under its established investment criteria. She said Masimo and StatLab, which Leica Biosystems acquired in early fourth quarter, are examples of acquisitions intended to strengthen the Diagnostics platform rather than signal a broader move into medical technology. 
Masimo delivered high-single-digit revenue growth in its first full quarter as part of Danaher, according to Montgomery. She said integration is progressing with cost-savings and commercial-synergy opportunities, while Masimo recently received FDA clearance for its smartSET platform to help detect atrial fibrillation. 
Danaher also said reshoring activity in bioprocessing is currently centered on brownfield projects, while larger greenfield projects remain largely in planning stages. Montgomery said the company sees the opportunity as potentially reaching $1 billion in the U.S., with the more significant revenue impact expected to begin in 2028 and develop over several years. 
About Danaher DHR 
Danaher Corporation DHR is a global science and technology company that develops products, services and solutions for the life sciences, biotechnology and diagnostics markets. Its offerings help researchers, pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, healthcare providers and other organizations conduct scientific research, develop and manufacture medicines, and diagnose disease. 
The company operates through businesses that provide bioprocessing equipment and technologies, laboratory instruments, consumables, analytical tools and clinical diagnostic systems.

Corning to invest $585M, add 414 jobs in Wilmington expansion 
Corning Inc. will invest $585 million at its Wilmington campus and add 414 jobs over the next five years, expanding one of the world’s largest optical fiber man 
By Hannah Hall 
Published : Oct. 21, 2026 at 10:31 AM EDT 
Share 
Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google 
WILMINGTON, N.C. (WECT) - Corning Inc. will invest $585 million at its Wilmington campus and add 414 jobs over the next five years, expanding one of the world’s largest optical fiber manufacturing plants.
The New York-based company announced the expansion Wednesday after the Wilmington City Council and New Hanover County Commissioners approved a package of incentives earlier this week to expand its operations. 
“We’re proud to expand our presence in Wilmington, where Corning made history with the world’s first optical fiber manufacturing plant and where our people continue to make the fiber that is critical to next-generation networks,” said John McGirr, senior vice president and general manager of Corning Optical Fiber and Cable.
NHC Commissioners approve incentive for Corning Inc. to expand in Wilmington 
Wilmington council backs $2 million deal to sweeten odds of landing Corning expansion 
Wilmington competed with several other locations for the project, known as “Project Pearl 2.” The project will supply fiber for next-generation networks and support long-term customer agreements, according to Corning.
The new jobs are expected to pay an average salary of more than $85,000 a year, and the company said the expansion will add more than $35 million in annual payroll for the region.
“Corning has been part of New Hanover County for decades, and when a company with that track record is ready to grow, this Board wants that growth to happen here,” said LeAnn Pierce, Chair of the New Hanover County Board of Commissioners. “Those are good paychecks for families in our community. The grant is tied to those jobs and that investment, and that is exactly how it should work.”
The company has maintained a civic commitment to the Wilmington area for 60 years, partnering with Cape Fear Community College on the Corning Technician Pipeline Program and investing in STEM education in local schools.
“It’s impossible to overstate how important this company is to Greater Wilmington,” said Scott Satterfield, CEO of Wilmington Business Development.

title: Toray develops polyester-nylon fiber with recycled content - Recycling Today
query: ("Toray" OR "Toray Industries") (Korea OR Korean) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Toray develops polyester-nylon fiber with recycled content
The company says both the polyester and nylon components of its new fiber incorporate recycled materials.
Photo courtesy of Toray 
Posted by
Chris Voloschuk, Associate Editor 
Published October 21, 2026
Listen to article 
/ 
Toray Industries Inc. recently announced it had developed a polyester-nylon fiber containing at least 93 percent recycled content by mass, based on the total weight of the raw yarn.
The Japan-based company says the percentage applies to the newly developed raw yarn and does not represent the recycled content of the finished fabric or garment. It says the breakthrough drew on technologies the company cultivated through its &+ (and plus) recycled fiber brand, adding that the polyester and nylon components of the fiber incorporate recycled materials.
Composite fibers can provide added functionality, sophisticated textures and subtle visual effects, Toray says, but combining different polymers makes it difficult to use high proportions of recycled materials while maintaining consistent quality. The company says it tapped into its expertise in polymer design and composite spinning to overcome the challenge and achieve a product containing at least 93 percent recycled content by mass, and it plans to verify the technology’s viability for mass production and continue research to increase recycled content in composite fibers.
“The fashion industry is showing increasing interest in material containing recycled content,” Toray says. “Materials for high-end and luxury applications must also deliver exceptional aesthetic qualities, including appearance, tailoring and drape, texture and durability.”
These considerations prompted Toray to create Artirosa CX, which it says incorporates the newly developed fiber. The company notes that the recycled content in each Artirosa CX fabric may vary depending on its composition.
The company says Artirosa CX features a “dense, finely textured surface and a crisp, sophisticated feel,” adding that fabric design and finishing also can impart practical properties like waterproofing, durable water repellency and wind resistance. 
“Rather than emphasizing the distinctive appearance typical of conventional functional materials, Artirosa CX refines that look into an elegant, sophisticated texture,” Toray says. “The result is a cleaner, more contemporary urban aesthetic.”
Toray says it intends to market Artirosa CX for wide-ranging applications, including men’s and women’s outerwear, urban outdoor wear and premium casual wear. The company expects to launch the product in late-2027 and is targeting initial year sales of 200,000 meters (around 218,722 yards) of material.

Thermo Fisher posts higher third-quarter revenue and earnings as margins improve
Proactive 
October 21, 2026 2 min read 
TMO 
TN8 
Thermo Fisher posts higher third-quarter revenue and earnings as margins improve Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc ( NYSE:TMO , XETRA:TN8 ) increased third-quarter revenue by 9% to $12.14 billion, while adjusted earnings per share rose 15% to $6.68. 
Revenue for the three months ended September 2026 increased from $11.12 billion a year earlier, with organic revenue growth, which excludes the effects of acquisitions, disposals and currency movements, reaching 6%. 
Adjusted operating income rose 15% to $2.97 billion, while adjusted operating margin increased to 24.5% from 23.3% in the same period last year. 
The company's generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) diluted earnings per share increased 9% to $4.64, while GAAP operating income rose 17% to $2.26 billion. 
GAAP operating margin improved to 18.6% from 17.4%, indicating that the company retained a larger share of revenue as operating profit. 
Thermo Fisher chief executive Marc Casper said the company's growth strategy and its Practical Process Improvement (PPI) Business System supported its performance during the quarter. 
The company launched several products during the period, including a mass spectrometer designed for isotope ratio analysis, an electron detector for advanced materials research and a new autoimmune screening test cleared by the US Food and Drug Administration. 
Thermo Fisher also partnered with Mayo Clinic to launch Precure, an initiative combining data from more than one million patient samples with its proteomics technologies to support disease research, earlier detection and precision medicine. 
In South Korea, the company opened its first artificial intelligence and automation innovation centre to help customers improve research and development productivity. 
Thermo Fisher also opened a highly automated distribution centre in Kentucky to improve supply chain speed and flexibility across North America. 
The company completed the previously announced sale of its microbiology business during the quarter as part of its capital deployment strategy. 
Thermo Fisher said it would provide updated financial guidance for 2026 during its third-quarter earnings conference call. 
Shares were down around 2% in early Wednesday morning trading.

Lubrizol Enters Crop Care Formulation Market With ZYRA Product Family 
October 21, 2026 Lubrizol ,  ZYRA 
21 October 2026, Ohio : Ohio-based specialty chemicals company Lubrizol has entered the crop care formulation segment of agriculture with the launch of ZYRA, a new family of formulation technologies aimed at manufacturers of pesticides, plant nutrition products, seed treatments and biologicals, the company announced on October 13, 2026.
Lubrizol, headquartered in Wickliffe, Ohio, and part of Berkshire Hathaway, is positioning ZYRA as a response to three pressures facing agrochemical and biologicals formulators: growers and regulators demanding better-performing, more efficient products; regulatory restrictions narrowing the pool of co-formulants manufacturers can use; and the practical challenge of keeping a formulation stable as it scales from laboratory testing to full commercial production.
The ZYRA family is built on five distinct platforms. ZYRAsperse covers hyperdispersants used for wetting, grinding and stabilizing active ingredients in high-load formulations. ZYRAflow consists of rheology modifiers designed to keep particles suspended in a product even at low use rates. ZYRAmul provides emulsifiers for emulsion and suspo-emulsion formulations. ZYRAwet supplies wetting agents and humectants that manage how a spray wets out and covers a leaf surface. ZYRAfix rounds out the line with binders and film formers that control spray retention, adhesion, dust-off and flow characteristics.
The products are aimed squarely at formulators rather than growers directly, covering crop protection, plant nutrition, seed treatment and biological products. Lubrizol says each ZYRA grade comes with supporting technical studies, application guidance and formulation starting points, backed by a four-stage support process covering problem identification, formula building, performance testing against industry benchmarks, and support through commercial-scale production. The products are commercially available immediately; Lubrizol has not disclosed specific country or regional rollout sequencing beyond noting that it operates more than 100 facilities and offices worldwide.

Eduardo Pedreira, President of Lubrizol Surface Sciences, said agriculture represents an important long-term growth opportunity for the company, while Fernando Vinagre, Lubrizol’s Global Business Director for Agriculture, is leading the newly formed agriculture business line. Lubrizol, founded in 1928, employs more than 7,000 people globally. The company has not disclosed R&D investment figures or performance benchmarks specific to the ZYRA line.

TEMPE, Ariz., October 21, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )--Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR), a leading provider of outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services, today announced additional investments in South Korea for capacity expansion initiatives with NVIDIA. With this latest commitment, Amkor's multi-year agreements with NVIDIA in Arizona and South Korea total $3 billion. The initiatives support growing demand for next-generation AI and accelerated computing platforms. 
Advanced packaging technologies are essential to enabling the performance, power efficiency and integration required for next-generation computing systems. The prepayments align Amkor's manufacturing capacity with NVIDIA's long-term growth plans and support increasing demand for advanced packaging solutions. 
"Our partnership with NVIDIA underscores the critical role advanced packaging plays in enabling next-generation AI platforms," said Kevin Engel, president and chief executive officer of Amkor Technology. "These investments build on our global manufacturing footprint and strengthen our ability to support customers through our operations in both the United States and South Korea." 
"Growing demand for accelerated computing is increasing the need for advanced packaging capacity," said Debora Shoquist, executive vice president, operations of NVIDIA. "Our work with Amkor helps us scale production of current and next-generation platforms while strengthening the resilience of our global supply chain." 
This collaboration further strengthens Amkor's role as a strategic manufacturing partner for NVIDIA and reinforces the companies' shared commitment to supporting the continued expansion of AI infrastructure. 
Amkor will also exhibit at NVIDIA GTC Washington, D.C. from Nov. 30 - Dec. 3, where the company will showcase its advanced packaging and test capabilities and engage with customers, policymakers and industry leaders. 
About Amkor Technology, Inc. 
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR) is the world's largest U.S. headquartered OSAT and is a global leader in outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services. With a strong track record of innovation, a broad and diverse geographic footprint and solid partnerships with lead customers, Amkor delivers high-quality solutions that enable the world's leading semiconductor and electronics companies to bring advanced technologies to market. The company's comprehensive portfolio includes advanced packaging, wafer-level processing, and system-in-package solutions targeting applications for smartphones, data centers, artificial intelligence, automobiles and wearables. The company counts Serum Institute of India, the vaccine maker led by billionaire Adar Poonawalla, as a minority investor.
“SCHOTT Poonawalla has invited investment banks to make pitches for the proposed IPO next week. These are early days, but as of now, the intent is to raise around $400 million,” one of the persons cited above said, cautioning that the issue size and valuation have not been finalised and could change depending on market conditions.
A second person confirmed the development and said the proposed issue would likely comprise a combination of fresh shares and an offer for sale.

“The IPO provides a window for investor Serum Institute of India to further dilute part stake if deemed fit,” a third person said.
A fourth person also confirmed the listing plans.
All four people spoke to Moneycontrol on condition of anonymity.
An email query to SCHOTT Poonawalla remained unanswered at the time of publication. TPG and Serum Institute of India declined to comment.
A spokesperson for SCHOTT Pharma said, “As a matter of principle, we do not comment on market speculation or potential future transactions.”
Germany-based SCHOTT Pharma, which specialises in drug containment and delivery solutions, holds a 50% stake in SCHOTT Poonawalla, while TPG Growth holds 35%. The company was originally a 50:50 joint venture between SCHOTT Pharma and Serum Institute of India.
On May 6, 2025, SCHOTT Pharma announced a binding agreement with TPG to sell a 35% stake in the joint venture to the private equity firm. Novo Holdings joined TPG Growth as a co-investor.
Moneycontrol was the first to report , on November 28, 2024, that TPG Growth and Serum Institute of India were in talks over a stake sale.
Read More: Adar Poonawalla-led Serum Institute seals 30%-40% stake sale in SCHOTT Poonawalla to TPG Growth; target firm valued around $800 mn 
“SCHOTT Poonawalla is a unique asset and a clear market leader with an over 50 percent market share in injectable packaging and hence TPG saw an opportunity,” the report said, adding that the company's equity valuation was estimated at around $800 million.
Manipal Health Enterprises, Sai Life Sciences and Dr Agarwal's Health Care are among the healthcare companies backed by TPG that have made their stock market debuts in India.
In India's packaging sector, SCHOTT Poonawalla's listed peers include EPL Ltd, AGI Greenpac, Uflex Ltd, TCPL Packaging and Jindal Poly Films.
Hyundai Motor India, LG Electronics India, Orkla India and Tenneco Clean Air India are among the multinational companies that have launched IPOs in India in recent years. The Indian arms of Pernod Ricard and Carlsberg are also in the pipeline.
Earlier this week, the Rs 2,534-crore IPO of power transmission and drive solutions company Bonfiglioli Transmissions, entirely an offer for sale by its Italian promoter, was subscribed 46 times.
Lens on SCHOTT Poonawalla 
SCHOTT Poonawalla's product portfolio includes cartridges for auto-injector pens, prefillable syringes for a range of biologic drugs, vials and ampoules. It also offers regulatory services to biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies and contract development and manufacturing organisations (CDMOs).
Through its association with SCHOTT Pharma, the company draws on decades of expertise in pharmaceutical packaging, spanning drug administration, clinical trials, regulatory processes and commercial filings.
Speaking about TPG's entry into SCHOTT Poonawalla in May 2025, SCHOTT Pharma CEO Andreas Reisse had said: “India continues to be one of the most dynamic and strategically important manufacturing hubs for SCHOTT Pharma. Welcoming TPG to the partnership marks an exciting step forward in our collaboration. SCHOTT Pharma’s innovation capabilities and pure-play focus on injectables will be complemented by TPG’s local market expertise, relationships, and experience from its strong presence in the Indian healthcare sector. As we continue to expand our local production capacities and leading role in the Indian market, we are confident that this step will further enhance our global footprint and deliver exceptional value to our customers.”

1.1 Silicon-carbon Anode Materials for Solid State Battery Market Summary
Silicon-carbon anode materials for solid state batteries are high-capacity anode materials developed for solid-state and semi-solid lithium battery systems. They are typically based on nano-silicon, silicon oxide, graphite, and porous carbon, and are improved through composite structure design, surface coating, and interface stabilization. The materials are mainly used in automotive power batteries, high-end consumer electronics batteries, and next-generation high-safety energy storage batteries.
The market is still in an early commercialization stage as solid state batteries move from sample validation and pilot projects toward small-scale production. Demand for silicon-carbon anode materials is increasing as automakers, battery manufacturers, and material companies accelerate joint development programs. Compared with conventional graphite anodes, silicon-carbon systems offer much higher theoretical capacity, but they also face challenges such as volume expansion, interfacial side reactions, initial efficiency loss, and batch-to-batch consistency.
According to the new market research report "Global Silicon-carbon Anode Materials for Solid State Battery Market Growth 2026-2032", published by LP Information, the global Silicon-carbon Anode Materials for Solid State Battery market size is projected to reach US$111 million by 2032, at a CAGR of 18.0% during the forecast period.
According to LP Information, the global key manufacturers of Silicon-carbon Anode Materials for Solid State Battery include Group14 Technologies, Sila Nanotechnologies, Amprius, etc. In 2025, the global top three players had a share of approximately 31.65% in terms of revenue.
To read the full report or request a free sample report, please use the link: https://www.lpinformationdata.com/reports/1866822/silicon---carbon-anode-materials-for-solid-state-battery 
1.2 Industrial Chain
The upstream segment mainly includes metallurgical-grade silicon, silane, graphite, and porous carbon, with representative suppliers such as Elkem, Hemlock, and East Hope Group. Raw material purity, particle size distribution, carbon structure, and supply stability directly affect capacity performance, swelling control, cycle life, and batch consistency, while also forming the basis for cost control and mass production.
The midstream segment focuses on silicon-carbon composite structure engineering, interface stabilization, swelling suppression, surface coating modification, and particle morphology optimization. The main challenge is to balance high capacity with long cycle life while controlling initial efficiency, tap density, and processing compatibility. Stable mixing, heat treatment, coating, and classification processes directly affect yield, customer qualification time, and unit manufacturing cost.
Downstream demand mainly comes from automotive power batteries and consumer electronics lithium batteries. Power battery customers focus on longer driving range, fast charging capability, safety, and long-term cycling performance, while consumer electronics customers emphasize volumetric energy density and thinner product design. Silicon-carbon anodes help battery makers improve energy density and create differentiated performance for solid state batteries, premium vehicles, and high-end devices.
1.3 Influencing Factors
Drivers:
The core growth driver is rising demand for high-energy-density batteries. Longer-range electric vehicles, fast-charging platforms, and thinner high-end consumer electronics are pushing anode materials from conventional graphite toward silicon-carbon systems. As solid state battery development and demonstration projects accelerate, battery makers are increasing validation demand for high-capacity, low-swelling, and long-life anode materials, supporting order growth and market expansion.
Challenges:
The main barrier is process stability and cost pressure. Silicon materials tend to expand and trigger interfacial side reactions during charge and discharge, which raises requirements for coating, structure design, and battery system matching. If batch consistency, initial efficiency, and cycle life cannot meet customer requirements steadily, qualification cycles will be extended and production expansion and profitability will be constrained.
Trend:
Future development will focus on higher capacity, lower swelling, and better adaptation to solid state battery systems. Material suppliers will use nano-structure design, porous carbon frameworks, elastic coating layers, and interface modification to improve cycling stability, while developing customized products for different solid electrolytes and cell processes. Companies with materials design, scale-up engineering, and joint customer validation capabilities will gain stronger competitiveness.

Broadcom-TOPPAN JV Opens Singapore FC-BGA Substrate Facility for AI Chip Production
Article By : Stephen Las Marias 
Category : Packaging 
2026-10-21 
(0) Comments
Ask question of embedded
AST's 95,000-square-meter plant will produce large-body, high-layer-count substrates for AI computing and networking chips. 
Advanced Substrate Technologies (AST), a joint venture between TOPPAN Holdings Inc. and Broadcom Inc., has opened a manufacturing facility in Singapore for high-end flip-chip ball grid array (FC-BGA) substrates. It is the first facility of its kind in Singapore and TOPPAN Group’s first outside Japan.
Located in the Jurong Lake District, the facility will complement TOPPAN’s main production hub in Niigata, Japan. It is designed to manufacture large-body, high-layer-count substrates used in advanced semiconductor devices, including AI computing and networking chips.
“AST’s ability to deliver large-body, high-layer-count substrates at TOPPAN’s exacting standard is helping meet a real bottleneck in AI and networking chip production. We are grateful for the longstanding support and partnership of the Singapore government in this venture. This investment reflects both TOPPAN and Broadcom’s long-term commitment to Singapore as a critical hub in our global manufacturing network and strengthens the resilience of the semiconductor supply chain,” said Yoshiyuki Iida, CEO of AST, in a statement.
【Download】Transforming Healthcare with High Performance and Adaptive Computing 
Construction began in March 2024. AST has since recruited more than 200 engineers and skilled technicians, alongside operational staff. The site also includes R&D capabilities and will work with Singapore technology institutions on future substrate requirements.
The approximately 95,000-square-metre plant incorporates solar panels and water-recycling technologies. AST is targeting the start of high-value manufacturing by late 2026, with recruitment continuing across engineering and technical roles.
“Singapore continues to be an attractive destination and gateway to the global semiconductor industry for us, especially with a strong ecosystem of innovation, capabilities and resources. TOPPAN looks forward to continuing to drive advanced semiconductor packaging forward as artificial intelligence accelerates across the board,” said Satoshi Oya, President and COO of TOPPAN Holdings.
Singapore’s Economic Development Board (EDB) and JTC Corp. supported the project. EDB said the facility would expand the country’s advanced substrate capabilities and create jobs, while JTC highlighted the need for infrastructure to support next-generation semiconductor manufacturing.
As TOPPAN’s largest customer for FC-BGA substrates, Broadcom supported the facility’s development to secure additional capacity for its AI computing and networking products.
“AST’s FC-BGA substrate capacity in Singapore gives us meaningful flexibility and differentiation as demand for AI and networking silicon continues to climb. This facility, brought online three months early, strengthens our supply chain resilience by delivering vital relief while the industry is constrained by substrate shortages. Thanks to the exceptional execution by TOPPAN and AST, alongside the continued partnership of the Singapore EDB, this facility will deliver the next generation of large-body, high-layer-count substrates that Broadcom requires to further scale global AI infrastructure,” said Charlie Kawwas, President of Broadcom’s Semiconductor Solutions Group, in a press release.
AST plans to scale production with TOPPAN and Broadcom as demand for advanced substrates grows across AI, networking and next-generation computing.

Asahi Kasei Secures Top-Tier Carbon Verification for Acrylonitrile
George Orwell 21-Oct-2026 
Asahi Kasei’s Tongsuh Petrochemical secures independent high-level carbon footprint verification for acrylonitrile, strengthening transparency and supporting lower-carbon chemical supply chains.
Asahi Kasei has strengthened its sustainability credentials in the global chemicals market after its South Korean subsidiary, Tongsuh Petrochemical, secured “Reasonable Assurance” verification for the product carbon footprint (PCF) of acrylonitrile (AN) . The verification provides a high level of confidence in the reported emissions data, addressing growing customer demand for independently validated environmental information and lower-carbon chemical materials. 
Tongsuh Petrochemical, a wholly owned subsidiary of Asahi Kasei, manufactures acrylonitrile at its Ulsan production facility in South Korea. Socotec Certification Japan conducted the independent audit, examining the methodology, source data, reporting procedures, production processes, and supporting documentation used to calculate the product’s carbon footprint for fiscal 2025. The assessment covered the product lifecycle from raw material procurement through manufacturing. 
The “Reasonable Assurance” classification represents a high level of verification and exceeds the requirements associated with “Limited Assurance.” This milestone strengthens the credibility of Tongsuh Petrochemical’s environmental disclosures and gives customers more reliable information to assess emissions associated with their chemical purchases. 
Acrylonitrile is an important chemical intermediate used in the production of acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) resins, acrylamide, acrylic fibres, and precursor materials for carbon fibre. These downstream applications serve industries including automotive, electronics, textiles, water treatment, and advanced materials. As manufacturers face increasing pressure to reduce emissions across their supply chains, independently verified product-level carbon data can become an important consideration in supplier selection. 
Tongsuh Petrochemical has been advancing lower-carbon acrylonitrile production for several years. In 2021, the company obtained ISCC PLUS certification, which supports the traceability of bio-based and circular raw materials. Since 2022, it has also produced and marketed acrylonitrile using biomass-derived propylene through a mass-balance approach. This method enables certified alternative feedstocks to be allocated to products within an established accounting framework. 
Asahi Kasei plans to continue reducing greenhouse gas emissions associated with acrylonitrile production through improvements in its proprietary catalyst technologies and manufacturing processes. The company is also expanding its use of biomass-based feedstocks to strengthen its portfolio of lower-carbon chemical products. 
The latest verification could help Asahi Kasei differentiate its acrylonitrile offering as industrial customers increasingly prioritise measurable sustainability performance alongside product quality, availability, and cost. By combining alternative feedstocks with independently verified environmental data, the company aims to support customer decarbonisation strategies and reinforce its position as a sustainability partner across global chemical supply chains. 
Product Impact and Chemical Commodity Price Impact 
The verification strengthens Asahi Kasei’s credibility in the lower-carbon acrylonitrile market, potentially improving its appeal to automotive, electronics, acrylic fibre, and carbon fibre manufacturers seeking traceable emissions data. Biomass-derived propylene may support differentiated, sustainability-focused product offerings, although adoption will depend on availability, certification requirements, and cost competitiveness. For commodity prices tracked by ChemAnalyst, the immediate impact on acrylonitrile prices is likely to be limited because the announcement does not indicate additional capacity, supply disruptions, or changes in demand. Any premium for verified lower-carbon acrylonitrile would depend on customer willingness to pay, feedstock costs, and broader market conditions.

Citrini Research Names Charles River, Revvity in AI Drug Thesis
The firm's case rests on faster drug candidate design leading to more laboratory testing, an increase it has not established.
By John Kim Published Oct 20, 2026, 7:01 PM EDT 
Save Share 
A gloved hand slides a sample plate into a laboratory instrument. / TokenPost.ai Citrini Research has singled out Charles River Laboratories and Revvity in an AI drug discovery thesis, arguing that faster candidate design could create more work for laboratory testing and research equipment providers.
The firm developed the thesis after testing Anthropic’s Claude Science. Its experiment produced protein binders for laboratory testing, an early research result rather than a completed treatment.
Charles River Laboratories provides drug-testing services. Revvity supplies research instruments and software. Citrini sees both companies as potential beneficiaries if AI helps researchers design candidates more quickly and more of those candidates move into physical experiments.
That increase in laboratory work is the premise of the thesis, not an observed rise in demand. Designing candidates faster would still leave researchers with the task of testing them. Citrini began exploring life sciences in June.
