Dow boosted as markets rotate from tech shares
AFP 
October 20, 2026 3 min read 
CL=F 
-3.21% 
^DJI 
-1.09% 
Shares of industrial company 3M soared nearly six percent after it released earnings, lifting the Dow (Steve DYKES) Wall Street stocks mostly rose Tuesday, greeting a pullback in oil prices as investors steered funds towards industrial equities amid lingering caution over artificial intelligence shares. 
Comments from Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari describing US-Iran talks as "ongoing" pressured crude prices, despite no concrete changes in a conflict that has dented energy supplies for more than seven months. 
Saudi Arabia on Monday postponed a major investment conference due to repeated attacks from Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis. 
International benchmark Brent oil futures finished down 0.7 percent at $108.79 a barrel after earlier hitting $111.99 a barrel. 
Wall Street stocks began meekly following losing sessions in leading European and Asian markets. But US equities picked up momentum as the day progressed, especially the blue-chip Dow index led by strong results from industrial company 3M. 
A more than one percent rise in the Dow showed a "rotation" from tech shares, said Briefing.com analyst Patrick O'Hare. 
"We still have some lingering softness in the tech trade and specifically the AI space so we're not getting a completely broad market rally," O'Hare said. 
"But a lot of stocks outside the tech sector are doing reasonably well today with oil prices having come down and entry trades remaining relatively well behaved." 
Tech shares have lately been volatile, with analysts pointing to worries over AI profitability and the hefty debt financing of some companies. 
The sector is also vulnerable after having outperformed the market for much of 2026. 
"There's some nervousness that perhaps the growth rates won't be as strong as people have assumed which is to say you could have really good news but it just might not be good enough to satisfy high expectations," O'Hare said. 
Earlier, AI worries hit Asian exchanges. 
Seoul and Tokyo again bore the brunt of the selling as chip giants SK hynix, Samsung and Kioxia took another beating owing to a sharp exit from a sector that saw blistering gains in the first half of this year. 
South Korea's Kospi stocks index sank nearly four percent, with SK hynix off 4.2 percent and Samsung down three percent. 
Further weighing on sentiment was the data center infrastructure firm Elice, whose shares collapsed more than 30 percent on their trading debut. 
The negative sentiment carried over to equity trading in Europe. 
The euro rose against the dollar but remained under pressure as violent protests in France and Italy have pushed up government bond yields. 
Story Continues 
The yield on France's 10-year government bond rose to 4.94 percent Tuesday, more than 150 basis points above the comparable German government bond, considered the European benchmark of creditworthiness. 
The resulting spread between the two yields reached the greatest level since 2011. 
Among individual companies, General Motors slumped 6.8 percent despite reporting better profits than expected. However, the automaker pointed to a recent uptick in commodity costs due to the US-Iran war, clouding its profit outlook.

Safran SkyNaute inertial navigation system selected for Airbus A220
20 October 2026 - 21:27 
Facebook 
X 
WhatsApp 
LinkedIn 
According to Safran , its SkyNaute inertial navigation system has been selected for the Airbus A220, marking its first application on a commercial airliner. The company said the system combines inertial and satellite navigation technologies and is designed to maintain accurate navigation when GNSS signals are unavailable, jammed or spoofed.
Safran press release:
SkyNaute, the inertial navigation system developed by Safran Electronics & Defense, is entering commercial aviation on board the Airbus A220. By combining inertial navigation with hybridized satellite navigation (GNSS) data, it ensures that the aircraft maintains a precise and reliable trajectory in all circumstances.
Already selected for military aircraft, helicopters and drones operated by several European armed forces, SkyNaute demonstrates the full strength of Safran’s dual-use technologies. It now brings commercial air transport a decisive advantage from the defense world: resistance to interference. SkyNaute maintains a highly accurate trajectory even when GNSS signals are unavailable, jammed or spoofed. This capability has become essential for civil aviation, which faces a growing number of such disruptions in several regions of the world. This performance relies on proven technologies, first and foremost the hemispherical resonator gyroscope (HRG) patented by Safran Electronics & Defense. With no mechanical parts subject to wear, this sensor offers unmatched compactness and high resilience in harsh environments.
SkyNaute’s reduced weight, size and power consumption mean simpler installation and weight savings on board for airlines, while meeting the most stringent safety requirements of commercial air transport.
“ Seeing SkyNaute take its place on board the Airbus A220 is a source of immense pride for our teams: for the first time, our inertial navigation system will fly on an airliner. This is a strong signal for French industrial expertise. We sincerely thank Airbus for its trust,” said Benjamin Declety, Head of the Avionics Global Business Unit at Safran Electronics & Defense.
This expertise is rooted in Montluçon, in central France, where the HRG is fully developed and industrialized. In June 2026, Safran Electronics & Defense announced a €120 million investment to expand and modernize the site, tripling its HRG production capacity from 10,000 to 30,000 units per year by 2032.
With this selection, SkyNaute confirms its ability to adapt to aircraft with very different integration constraints. It has already been installed on helicopters subject to strong vibrations and wide temperature variations, on military aircraft exposed to shocks and jamming attempts, and on drones, which require high navigation accuracy and strong resistance to electromagnetic interference.

The company returned $600 million to shareholders during the quarter, including $400 million in dividends and $200 million in share repurchases. Through the first nine months of 2026, 3M returned $4.4 billion to shareholders, including $3.2 billion of buybacks and $1.2 billion of dividends. 
Growth and operational actions 
Brown said 3M's performance reflected initiatives aimed at improving sales-force effectiveness, product development, pricing, productivity and supply-chain execution. The company launched 87 new products in the quarter, up 24% from a year earlier, and said it remains on track to exceed 350 launches for the full year.

Target the Red-Hot Spin-Off and Merger Space With These ETFs 
Year-to-date sales from products introduced within the past five years rose 34% from the prior year to nearly $3 billion, according to Brown. New-product vitality reached the mid-teens, compared with 11% in 2024. 
Story Continues 
The company also reported $140 million of cross-selling wins booked to date and an additional $120 million pipeline, exceeding its original three-year goal of $100 million. Brown said pricing actions fully offset material and oil-cost pressures. 
→ Luxury's Middle Market Is Cracking—These 3 Stocks Could Win 
Gross margin increased 230 basis points year over year, supported by procurement savings, improved asset utilization, lower downtime and quality improvements. Cost of poor quality improved by 40 basis points and overall equipment effectiveness improved by 20 basis points, Brown said. 
3M has closed 16 manufacturing sites and distribution centers so far this year and plans action on 10 additional locations over the next 12 months. Brown said the actions should support additional gross-margin improvement beyond 2027. 
Business-group performance 
Chief Financial Officer Anurag Maheshwari said order trends grew at a high-single-digit rate in the third quarter, led by industrials, safety, data centers, semiconductors and aerospace. Backlog increased by a high-teens percentage from a year earlier. 
Safety and Industrial: Organic sales increased 7%, with double-digit growth in electrical markets as the division expanded data-center customer penetration. Safety, industrial adhesives, abrasives and industrial specialties collectively grew at a high-single-digit rate. Auto aftermarket sales rose in the mid-single digits. 
Transportation and Electronics: Sales rose 0.5%, as growth in semiconductors, aerospace, commercial branding and automotive outside consumer electronics was about 5%. Consumer electronics declined in the mid-teens, while auto was down in the mid-single digits on softer builds. 
Consumer: Sales were flat, improving sequentially. U.S. point-of-sale growth exceeded 2%, though inventory reductions at several major retailers caused U.S. sell-in to decline in the low single digits. International consumer sales grew in the mid-single digits. 
Geographically, U.S. and Canada sales grew about 7%, while Latin America delivered high-single-digit growth. Europe expanded for a second consecutive quarter, and India posted another quarter of double-digit growth. China declined by a high-single-digit percentage, primarily due to weak consumer electronics demand. 
Data-center strategy and Amazon agreement 
Brown highlighted 3M's Expanded Beam Optical, or EBO, technology, which uses a patented ferrule designed to enable faster installation, durability and higher-density optical connections in AI infrastructure. The company previously announced a deployment partnership with Microsoft and said it has been engaged in proof-of-concept work with five other global hyperscalers, including Amazon Web Services. 
3M disclosed that it issued Amazon a warrant to purchase up to 3.2 million 3M shares, representing about 0.6% of common stock, contingent on $6 billion in cumulative sales of optical connectivity and other data-center products over seven years, along with other event-based milestones. Brown said there are no volume commitments under the arrangement and that 3M must earn the sales opportunity. 
Brown said EBO revenue is expected to be about $40 million in 2026 and could double, or potentially exceed that level, next year. The company has doubled internal manufacturing capacity to more than 10 million ferrules annually. It also signed a contract manufacturing agreement with Genius Electronic Optical Company, or GSEO, and acquired a 4.7% stake in the supplier. 
Brown said GSEO could provide manufacturing capacity at multiples of 3M's internal output per month, helping the company meet potential demand. He added that supply diversity will remain important as hyperscalers evaluate the technology. 
Separately, 3M said data-center revenue is expected to reach about $700 million this year, compared with roughly $550 million last year. That revenue includes electrical connections, optical connections, copper products and other products used inside and outside data centers. 
Updated outlook 
3M reaffirmed expectations for organic growth of more than 3.5% for 2026 and projected organic growth of just over 4% in the fourth quarter. Management cited order momentum, backlog levels and easier comparisons in the final quarter. 
The company raised its adjusted EPS outlook to a range of $9.10 to $9.15, from a prior range of $8.95 to $9.10 on its updated reporting basis. The forecast implies annual adjusted earnings growth of 11% to 12%. 
Maheshwari said 3M now expects oil-related inflation of $185 million for the year, compared with its prior estimate of $150 million to $175 million. The company expects pricing to fully offset the higher cost, although the pass-through is expected to dilute margin rate by about 20 basis points. Full-year adjusted operating margin is projected to be about 24.6%, while free cash flow is expected to be approximately $4.8 billion and the adjusted tax rate about 20%. 
For 2027, 3M plans to provide formal guidance in January. Maheshwari said the company expects margin to exceed its Investor Day target of 25.4% on the updated basis, supported by volume growth, supply-chain productivity and transformation actions.

3M is a diversified technology and manufacturing company headquartered in St. Paul, Minnesota. Founded in 1902 as Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing Company, it developed from a mining venture into a global enterprise known for applying materials science and engineering to a broad range of industrial, commercial and consumer applications. 
The company develops and manufactures products including adhesives, abrasives, filtration systems, personal protective equipment, medical and dental supplies, electrical and electronic materials, automotive components, reflective materials and workplace safety solutions.

BASF to expand Taiwan semiconductor materials site
October 20, 2026 | By Mary Bailey 
BASF SE (Ludwigshafen, Germany) signed a Letter of Intent with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), underscoring its long-term commitment to supporting the growth of Taiwan’s semiconductor ecosystem . Through this investment, BASF’s Electronic Materials business is expanding its Kuanyin site in Taoyuan with additional production capacity for advanced semiconductor materials, enhanced quality analysis capabilities, and an expanded Innovation Center. The investment is designed to support increasing global demand for leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing technologies, including advanced nodes below 2 nanometers, while strengthening supply chain resilience and customer proximity.
“Taiwan is a global hub for semiconductor innovation and manufacturing, with leading-edge process technologies and a highly integrated industry ecosystem. Setting the strategic base for BASF’s global Electronic Materials operations in Taiwan in 2025 reflected the strategic importance of Taiwan within the global semiconductor ecosystem and reinforced our confidence in the market’s long-term growth potential,” said Gops Pillay, President, Global Operating Division of BASF.
As the semiconductor industry progresses toward process nodes below 2 nanometers, demand for advanced, high-purity specialty chemical formulations continues to rise. Through the expansion of its Kuanyin site, BASF will strengthen its Innovation Center and broaden its technical and analytical capabilities for leading-edge semiconductor technologies supporting the AI era. The investment will deepen collaboration with key industry partners, enabling the joint development of next-generation materials while reinforcing Taiwan’s position as a global semiconductor innovation hub.
The investment will further strengthen BASF’s local manufacturing, quality assurance and technical service capabilities in Taiwan, enabling the company to provide customers with a more reliable supply of advanced semiconductor materials, faster technical support, and closer collaboration. At the same time, it will enhance supply chain resilience and reinforce BASF’s role as a trusted long-term partner to the semiconductor industry.
“The signing of this Letter of Intent marks another important milestone in BASF’s long-term commitment to the semiconductor industry,” said Jens Liebermann, Senior Vice President, Global Electronic Materials business and Chairman of BASF Taiwan. “As semiconductor technologies continue to advance, innovation in materials must keep pace with our customers’ evolving needs. By strengthening our local manufacturing, innovation, and technical service capabilities, we are deepening collaboration with our customers and accelerating the development of materials solutions for future technology generations, while further enhancing supply chain resilience.”
As a trusted materials partner to the global semiconductor industry, BASF’s Electronic Materials business has maintained a strong presence in Taiwan for more than two decades. The business provides high-performance process chemicals and customized formulation solutions for the advanced semiconductor and display industry as well as specialized metal systems for consumer electronics applications.

HyProMag USA deploys third mobile system
Several technology and recycling firms in the United States and Canada have collaborated to invest in mobile systems to process printed circuit boards and hard drives.
“The deployment of our third Inserma system as a mobile processing unit represents an important step in the development of the Dallas-Fort Worth project,” says Julian Treger, CEO of CoTec Holdings.
Photo courtesy of Intelligent Lifecycle Solutions 
By
Brian Taylor, Senior Editor 
Published October 20, 2026
Listen to article 
/ 
A coalition of firms in the United States and Canada, some with ownership stakes in each other, have now deployed three mobile hard disk drive (HDD) separation system designed to recover rare earth element (REE) and magnet materials from discarded electronic components.
Canada-based Mkango Magnetic Materials Ltd. says HyProMag USA LLC, in which it owns a stake, has announced the deployment of its third Spanish-made Inserma Anoia S.L. HDD separation system to be used as a mobile processing unit, “expanding HyProMag USA’s processing and customer engagement capabilities across the U.S.”
Adds Mkango, “The deployment further strengthens HyProMag USA’s partnership with Intelligent Lifecycle Solutions (ILS) and supports the expansion of a scalable nationwide platform for the recovery and recycling of rare earth magnets from end-of-life HDDs.”
ILS is based in Nevada and has processing capacity there and in South Carolina, according to Mkango.
Also involved is HyProMag USA co-owner CoTec Holdings Corp., a Canada-based firm that says it “integrates breakthrough technologies with strategic assets to unlock secure, sustainable, and low-cost supply chains.” 
Mkango says feedstock inventories currently under contract and in storage, together with active procurement programs undertaken by the companies involved, “continue to strengthen the feedstock platform and are expected to support initial commissioning and ramp-up activities” at a planned HyProMag USA Texas Hub facility in the Dallas-Fort Worth scheduled to open in 2028.
The Canadian company says Delaware-based HyProMag USA also has completed commercial sales of recovered printed circuit board (PCB) material to downstream smelter partners, generating revenue that supports the acquisition and retention of magnet-bearing feedstock inventory.
“The deployment of our third Inserma system as a mobile processing unit represents an important step in the development of the Dallas-Fort Worth project,” says Julian Treger, CEO of CoTec Holdings.
“Together with continued progress in feedstock sourcing and commercial PCB recovery, it strengthens our operating platform and expands our ability to engage directly with customers across multiple end markets,” adds Treger.
Remars Graham Davy, Managing Director of ILS , “The focus of the ILS team has been on demonstrating that HDDs can be efficiently processed into separate, marketable material streams. The mobile unit allows us to work directly with customers at their facilities, supporting trial programs, demonstrating material recovery performance and creating opportunities to secure additional feedstock supply.”
The companies say they are tapping into diversified feedstock channels “across industrial, health care, government and IT asset disposition sectors.”

GE HEALTHCARE LAUNCHES CELL DIVE FOR MORE PRECISE CELL BIOMARKER ANALYSIS
September 26, 2019
Developed by scientists for scientists – first patent issued 2009 for this product Flexibility of system allows for custom biomarker panel design and whole slide imaging Precise image registration enables spatial and quantititative biomarker analysis
(Paris, France and Seattle, Washington) September 26, 2019 - GE Healthcare launches Cell DIVE™ multiplexed imaging , an anti-body based solution that builds on years of research and development to transform immuno-oncology.
“Cell DIVE multiplexed imaging is another example of our commitment to furthering access to life-changing biotherapeutics and diagnostics, ” says Emmanuel Abate, General Manager Genomics and Cellular Research, GE Healthcare Life Sciences. “These are exciting days in immuno-oncology and we are early in our understanding in how a patient’s biomarker profile contributes to a therapeutic outcome.”
This technology was developed by scientists for scientists. The seminal work started in 2008 and the first patent was issued in 2009. Over the last decade, Cell DIVE has been evaluated globally through multiple collaborators resulting in a library of publications, presentations, and research . The milestone paper, Gerdes et al, (2013) in PNAS describes the ‘quantification and visualization of heterogeneous patterns of mTOR/MAPK signaling proteins’ – tackling challenges in tumor heterogeneity. All of this work brings us to the present moment with 400 validated commercially-available antibodies and a robust solution reaching the market.
“The flexibility of an open system that allows for custom biomarker panel design moves us closer to a definitive diagnostic tool,” says Prachi Bogetto, Diagnostics Segment Leader, GE Healthcare Life Sciences. “This flexible solution also supports whole slide, region of interest and tissue microarray (TMA) imaging.”
At its core, scientists will iteratively probe, image, and de-stain to capture thousands of spatial cellular data points from just one tissue image. With our extensive list of validated antibodies, scientists can customize their own panels and have the flexibility to stain and image as they need. Scientists can have confidence knowing that our gentle protocol won’t harm the tissue sample. No stripping of antibodies or complicated sample prep required. GE Healthcare continued its commitment to quality by ensuring this technology produces high quality image data through accurate registration and stitching technology.

“ABB delivered record order intake, and improved operational performance with strong cash flow and return on capital. We advanced our leading position in direct current technology and today we progressed on M&A with a new electrification joint venture with Mitsubishi Electric.”
Morten Wierod, CEO 
CEO summary
Our third quarter order intake reached a record $12 billion, nudging up sequentially; a stronger outcome than the historical pattern of seasonal decline. Year-on-year, orders grew 40% (40% comparable), driven by strong growth in two of our three business areas with a positive development across the majority of customer segments. Most notably so in the data center segment where we saw a triple-digit increase. Revenues were strong, yet order intake was even stronger, yielding a book-to-bill of 1.24.
Overall, we progressed according to plan. We converted strong revenue growth of 14% (14% comparable) into a 24% increase in Operational EBITA which reached $2 billion with margin expanding 160 basis points to 20.8%. We also materially improved Income from operations by 15% with a margin of 19.0%. Earnings per share remained virtually stable, reflecting increased Net finance expenses mainly due to the non-cash revaluation of the deal contingent FX hedge linked to the announced Rotork acquisition. We continue to deliver strong Return on capital employed which improved to 29.9%.
This was yet another solid cash flow quarter. Free cash flow of $1.6 billion was supported by robust earnings combined with disciplined management of Trade net working capital, which more than compensated for higher capex spend. This supported a sustained solid Free cash flow margin of around 14%, on a 12-month rolling basis. At $3.7 billion year-to-date, we are well positioned to surpass last year’s annual level of $4.6 billion.
In the current strong market environment it is essential to maintain focus and discipline, and we incrementally scale capacity to support our strong delivery track record. We already trend at a higher capex level of around $1 billion and do not expect it to rise further in the mid-term. Our investment approach is deliberate: incremental capacity expansion, productivity through automation, and selectively leveraging third-party assembly; balancing capturing of near-term demand with long-term resilience.
A significant milestone was the launch of the Infinitus Direct Current (DC) portfolio, enabling AI data center customers to achieve higher power density and improved energy efficiency. Our portfolio comprises five building blocks that can be combined into complete systems tailored to specific architectures. This includes a Solid State Transformer commercially available in the second half of 2027. We are able to partner with our customers from source to rack across the full spectrum of DC architectures. The portfolio enables acceleration of adoption of DC architectures in data centers and other energy-intensive industries.
Our partnership with Ferrari Hypersail demonstrates our commitment to advancing DC technologies and promoting their broader adoption across industries. The project – a 100-foot, renewable-powered full-foiling monohull yacht - is conceived as an operational proving ground for next-generation microgrid architecture. Its focus on energy management, marine electrical systems, and energy storage closely aligns with our expertise in these areas. The vessel is designed to operate as a fully self-sufficient system, integrating 800 VDC architectures. The engineering challenge central to this partnership – real-time orchestration of renewable generation, storage, and power distribution – mirrors the critical dynamics of emerging industrial microgrids.
It is also good to see our M&A activities bearing fruit. Following the Rotork announcement in July, we today announced that we will acquire a controlling 51 percent stake in a joint venture (JV) to be formed with Mitsubishi Electric’s low voltage power distribution business, with an option for full ABB ownership in the mid-term. This deal will make us the low voltage market leader in Japan, one of the world’s largest electrification markets, allowing us to benefit from the broad electric power trends including any local data center build-out. It also opens doors to the Asia-Pacific region. The Mitsubishi Electric business to be contributed to the JV generated around JPY 102 billion (~$640 million) in revenues in its fiscal year 2025, with a low double-digit EBITDA margin. We expect the joint venture to improve to at least a 20 percent Operational EBITA margin within 5 years. Similar to our successful GEIS acquisition, the profitability improvement will be driven by expanding sales through combined channels, introducing ABB products and technology to Mitsubishi Electric’s customer base and optimizing manufacturing. We acquire a controlling 51% stake in the newly carved out company as well as full ownership of Mitsubishi Electric’s JV-related sales operations outside of Japan for a total consideration of around JPY 79 billion (∼$495 million). These sales operations outside of Japan represent approximately 15% of revenues. The transaction values the combined businesses at a total enterprise value (EV) of about $890 million. Combined, this translates to valuation multiples of EV/Sales ∼1.4 and EV/EBITDA of ∼11.1 based on reported fiscal year 2025. The latter reduces into the mid- to high single-digit range when assuming realization of expected synergies. We see long-term returns well above cost of capital.
Morten Wierod , CEO center 
Outlook
In the fourth quarter of 2026 , we expect comparable revenue growth to be broadly similar to the third quarter and Operational EBITA margin to sequentially soften although less than historical pattern. This excludes the positive impact of ∼CHF240 million related to the sale of properties already completed in Q4.
In full-year 2026, we expect a positive book-to-bill, and comparable revenue growth in the ”low teens” range, year-on-year. The reported Operational EBITA margin should improve by at least 270 basis points year-on-year.

Sumitomo Chemical works with Tata
20th October 2026
Submitted by:
Andrew Warmington
Sumitomo Chemical has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with India’s Tata Electronics to explore a possible collaboration in semiconductor fabrication. The company will examine specific measures aimed at establishing a stable supply system for materials, possibly including a semiconductor chemicals facility in India.
Sumitomo Chemical’s ICT & Mobility Solutions sector is one of its growth drivers and the semiconductor materials business has been designated as a priority area within it. The business offers advanced photoresists and semiconductor chemicals, being particularly known for high-purity chemicals.
In recent years, Sumitomo Chemical has expanded its semiconductor chemicals capacity in Japan and South Korea, while establishing a new base in Texas. Earlier this year, it acquired Asia Union Electronic Chemical, with facilities in Taiwan and Nevada. It has also begun operations at advanced high-purity chemical centres in Japan and South Korea to develop new processes and recycling technologies.
Another Japanese player, Nissan Chemical, has separately established a wholly-owned subsidiary in Zhangjiagang in China’s Jiangsu province. This will make anti-reflective coatings for the photoresists and multilayer materials used in semiconductors. The company said that demand for semiconductors in China has continued to expand, driven by ongoing digitalisation and other factors, whilecustomer demand for supply chain resilience has grown.

title: AdapTronics wins Infineon’s humanoid robotics startup challenge - Electronics Weekly

content_text:
AdapTronics wins Infineon’s humanoid robotics startup challenge
by 
David Manners 
20th October 2026 
in 
Business , News 
0 
AdapTronics from Italy has won the Infineon Startup Challenge 2026 focused on key technologies for humanoid robots. COSMOKE of Korea was runner up and TECHiFAB from Germany third.
The three winning teams are pictured above.
AdapTronics won with an innovative gripping technology for humanoid robots. “The challenge gave us valuable access to technology experts, industry insights and a strong innovation network. We look forward to further advancing our solution and exploring new opportunities for collaboration,” says Lorenzo Agostini, founder and CEO of AdapTronics.
COSMOKE from South Korea was in second place with its magnetic tactile sensing technology for physical AI – COSKIN – which enables humanoid robots to perceive touch, pressure, and physical interactions.
TECHiFAB from Germany came third with its In-Memory Computing based approach to real-time motor control for robotic actuators. This is physical AI by definition and is designed to enable faster, more energy-efficient and safer control while improving performance directly within the drive train of humanoid robots.
Over 100 startups from 29 countries participated in the challenge, 15 were selected to pitch their solutions enabling the next generation of humanoid robots and physical AI applications to an international jury
The programme provided access to Infineon technologies, expert mentoring, business coaching, and an international innovation network
Following four months of intensive collaboration, development and mentoring, 15 selected startups out of more than 100 applicants presented their solutions at the Infineon Startup Challenge Demo Day, held during the Electronic Based Systems Conference (EBSCON) in Graz, Austria.
The challenge brought together startups from Europe and Asia, investors, industry experts and technology leaders to advance innovation in robotics and physical AI.
Participants developed solutions that enable humanoid robots to better perceive and interact with their environment, manipulate objects, and perform precise movements.
The winners were selected by an international jury comprising experts from industry, venture capital, startup ecosystems, and technology innovation.
“Strategic collaboration with startups creates a win-win situation, combining novel ideas with industrially proven semiconductor technologies and thereby accelerating innovative, market-ready applications,” says Infineon svp Sören Jehmlich, “the Startup Challenge is a key pillar of our innovation culture.”
The solutions presented during the challenge reflect the technologies required for the next generation of humanoid robots, from tactile sensing to dexterous gripping and precise motor control.
To support the startups in developing and validating their concepts, Infineon provided access to dedicated hardware and software platforms, including Environmental Sensing Kits, Artificial Skin Kits, Motor Control Kits, Visual Feedback Kits, and in-house AI development software, enabling teams to accelerate prototyping and transform innovative ideas into scalable applications.
“Humanoid robots are the most complex form of physical AI and highly relevant for Infineon,” said Dirk Geiger, Senior Director & Team Lead Humanoid Robotics at Infineon. “They combine power, sensing, real-time connectivity, safety and security with software and AI compute, turning machines into autonomous systems. No single company can master this complexity alone. With the Startup Challenge, we gave startups early access to our hardware stack as well as our software and system offering and brought them together with our partners and application experts. The solutions shown prove how quickly ideas can become building blocks for scalable humanoid platforms and give valuable insight into where the technology is heading.”
The Infineon Startup Challenge is part of the global Infineon Startup Co-Innovation Program, in which Infineon collaborates with startups as a technology and development partner.
As the winner of the Infineon Startup Challenge 2026, AdapTronics will now join the Infineon Startup Co-Innovation Program to further develop and scale its solution together with Infineon.
The collaboration will officially kick off at the Startup Night in Munich in November, where Infineon showcases successful startup partnerships and highlights the value of startup-driven innovation.
Infineon continues to engage with other promising participants for future technological and business collaboration. By combining the agility and creativity of startups with Infineon’s technological expertise and global capabilities, the program supports the development of scalable applications and accelerates innovation in humanoid robotics and physical AI.

content_text:
AI worries weigh on ABB shares despite record orders
By Thomson Reuters 
Oct 20, 2026 | 1:10 AM 
By John Revill
ZURICH, Oct 20 (Reuters) – ABB dropped nearly 6% on Tuesday as market nervousness about the sustainability of investments in artificial intelligence weighed on the Swiss engineering company, which is a major supplier to data centres.
Record new orders and an increase in its full-year ​sales guidance failed to appease institutional buy-side investors who were looking for more, analysts said, ‌as AI-linked stocks fell more broadly.
On South Korea’s stock market, which has become one of the clearest measures of AI sentiment, traders sold heavily on Tuesday as concern mounted over rising costs.
While European semiconductor stocks also fell, ABB shares fell more than peers. The stock, which reached its highest level to date of 89.14 Swiss francs ($108.13) in June, dropped to 70.72 ‌Swiss francs ​on the Swiss exchange after the results.
“Operationally ABB remains strong, but ⁠waning AI enthusiasm is creating headwinds,” ⁠said Marco Estermann, an analyst at Luzerner Kantonalbank.
“Ahead of the third quarter there was a risk that even results exceeding expectations would not be enough to support the share price.”
During its third quarter, ABB said its revenue rose 14% to $9.70 billion, slightly below analysts’ forecasts of $9.74 billion in a ​company-gathered consensus.
Operational earnings before interest, tax and amortisation jumped 24% to $2.03 billion in the three months to the end of September, slightly ahead of analyst forecasts for $2.0 billion.
Another analyst said fears had increased about ⁠the number of companies that will survive in the artificial ⁠intelligence sector, concerns that drove selling in US cloud company CoreWeave last week.
Andreas ​Lipkow, chief analyst at broker CMC Markets, said concerns were increasing about high valuations and the financing of the ​AI boom, with questions raised whether the massive investments will pay off.
Research firm Gartner ‌Inc expects that by 2030, 80% of neocloud providers will cease independent operations because they will fail to generate enough revenue to meet their debts building and managing data centres.
“There is a feeling of insecurity and uncertainty in the market that even good numbers may not be good enough,” said ZKB analyst Florian Sager.
“People ⁠are worrying about the huge debts that the neoclouds are taking on to build their projects. Investors question whether these companies get the revenues they need in the future to survive,” he said.
ABB however remained bullish ⁠on the future of data centres ‌and CEO Morten Wierod said demand for its services had not slowed.
Orders ⁠surged 40% to $12 billion in the three months ended September 30, with ​data centres ‌the biggest driver. The company raised its full-year sales outlook and also announced ​a pending $495 ⁠million investment in a joint venture with Mitsubishi Electric.
“We see a continued acceleration in the market when we’re looking at the demand for the build-out of data centres,” Wierod told reporters.
“Data centres will be a growth market for many years,” he added, saying the value of ABB data centre orders for the third quarter had been the highest yet.
($1 = 0.8244 Swiss francs)
(Reporting by John Revill, additional reporting by Oliver HirtEditing by Linda Pasquini, ​Jochelle Mendonca and Barbara Lewis)

Click to view 
October 20, 2026
France – French aircraft manufacturer AURA AERO has officially inaugurated its new flight testing and electric propulsion development facility at Rochefort–Charente-Maritime Airport on 9 October 2026. The site will support the development and validation of electric and hybrid-electric aircraft technologies, including propulsion systems for its planned ERA regional aircraft, while expanding the manufacturer's civil and military aerospace development capabilities. 
The Rochefort facility occupies infrastructure previously developed for VoltAero, comprising approximately 2,412 square metres of building space on a 7,400-square-metre site with direct runway access. AURA AERO's establishment at the airport follows its acquisition of VoltAero's assets earlier in 2026. 
The facility will support aircraft prototyping, engineering and flight testing, with the manufacturer's X-VOLT hybrid-electric demonstrator serving as a flying testbed for the validation of propulsion technologies before their integration into future aircraft. 
AURA AERO returned X-VOLT, formerly VoltAero's Cassio S demonstrator, to flight at Rochefort in September 2026. The manufacturer reported that X-VOLT and its fully electric INTEGRAL E prototype had accumulated more than 350 hybrid-electric and electric flights between them. 
The 9 October inauguration included flight demonstrations by X-VOLT and an INTEGRAL aircraft. The manufacturer intends to use the site for continued technology development and testing, including applications supporting civil and military aviation. 
For the pilot training market, AURA AERO is developing the two-seat INTEGRAL E electric aircraft for ab initio instruction, Upset Prevention and Recovery Training (UPRT) and other training applications. The aircraft remains in the certification process, with the manufacturer's current product roadmap indicating availability from December 2027. 
AFM previously reported that AURA AERO opened its US headquarters and North American aircraft delivery and customer support facility at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University's Research Park in Daytona Beach, Florida, in November 2025. The 11,000-square-foot facility supports the company's INTEGRAL aircraft family and its wider international manufacturing plans. 
X-VOLT is equipped with Safran ENGINeUS electric motors, allowing AURA AERO to evaluate propulsion components under actual flight conditions. The technologies will contribute to the development of ERA, a proposed 19-seat hybrid-electric regional aircraft designed around eight electric motors and two turbogenerators, with its first flight currently targeted for late 2027. 
About AURA AERO 
AURA AERO is a French aircraft manufacturer founded in 2018 and headquartered at Toulouse-Francazal Airport, specialising in general aviation training aircraft, electric propulsion and hybrid-electric regional aircraft development. Its aircraft portfolio includes the EASA-certified INTEGRAL R two-seat training and aerobatic aircraft, the INTEGRAL S, the developing all-electric INTEGRAL E and the ERA regional aircraft, alongside military and unmanned aviation programs.

Solvay Reduces 2026 Outlook After Middle East Conflict Impacts Q3 Earnings
Solvay's Financial Performance and Outlook
Oct 19 (Reuters) - Solvay cut its 2026 forecast after the Middle East conflict and a peroxide plant shutdown at Sadara in Saudi Arabia hit third-quarter earnings.
Revised Financial Guidance
The chemicals group now sees full-year EBITDA of €720 million to €740 million, slightly below the company-compiled consensus of €775 million, and free cash flow of between €120 million and €150 million.
Previous vs. Current Forecasts
• Solvay previously forecast 2026 underlying EBITDA of €770 million to €850 million and free cash flow of at least €200 million 
Q3 Earnings Breakdown
• The group posted preliminary third-quarter underlying EBITDA of €173 million, missing consensus by 7%, and sales in line at €1.03 billion
Impact of Middle East Conflict
• It said the Middle East conflict reduced quarterly underlying EBITDA by about €25 million, including nearly €15 million linked to the shutdown of the peroxide plant at the Sadara complex in Saudi Arabia
Mitigation Strategies
• Solvay said it was pursuing options to limit the shutdown's financial impact, citing joint-venture contractual provisions that could allow it to recover lost profit

Solvay reports preliminary Q3 2026 results and updates full-year 2026 guidance
Solvay S.A. 
October 19, 2026 4 min read 
SOLB.BR

Solvay S.A. Press release Inside information - Regulated information 
Brussels, October 19, 2026 - 6pm CEST 
During Q3 2026, Solvay's financial performance was affected by the Middle East conflict and the shutdown of the peroxide plant at the Sadara complex in Jubail, Saudi Arabia. 
Preliminary Q3 2026 figures: 
underlying net sales of €1.03 billion 
underlying EBITDA of €173 million 
Free cash flow to Solvay shareholders from continuing operations of €54 million 
2026 full-year guidance updated as follows (excluding potential revenue or recovery measures from Sadara for the remainder of 2026): 
Underlying EBITDA between €720 million and €740 million 
Free cash flow to Solvay shareholders from continuing operations between €120 million and €150 million. 
During Q3 2026, the Group continued to operate in a challenging market environment. Performance was affected by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which had a negative impact of approximately €-25 million on underlying EBITDA in Q3 2026 (following already recorded c. €-20 million in Q2 2026). This impact was primarily due to the continued shutdown of the Peroxide plant at the Sadara complex in Jubail, Saudi Arabia, which accounted for close to €-15 million in Q3 2026. As a result, based on preliminary figures (subject to completion of the quarter-end closing process), the Group recorded Q3 2026 underlying net sales of €1.03 billion, underlying EBITDA of €173 million and Free cash flow to Solvay shareholders from continuing operations of €54 million. 
Solvay' operations in Jubail are conducted through a joint venture with Sadara (which is a joint venture majority-owned by Saudi Aramco). Solvay is exploring all available avenues to mitigate the financial impact of the shutdown, as the joint venture contractual framework includes mechanisms designed to recover lost profitability. 
In light of these developments, Solvay has reviewed its full-year 2026 guidance. Excluding potential revenue or recovery measures from Sadara for the remainder of 2026, the updated guidance is: 
Underlying EBITDA between €720 and €740 million 
Free cash flow to Solvay shareholders from continuing operations between €120 million and €150 million, net of c. €90 million of transformation expenses 
Solvay remains fully committed to its transformation and continues to focus on cash generation and achieving its cost savings targets. 
Due to the ongoing quiet period, Solvay will not comment further ahead of the publication of its Q3 2026 results on November 4.

ABL Texcell Diagnostics Strengthens the Foundations of a Stable Shareholder Base and Pursues Its Growth Strategy
Business Wire 
October 19, 2026 5 min read 
ABLD.PA 
Its principal shareholder, ABL Luxembourg, intends to prioritize long-term investors in connection with any potential future disposals of significant blocks of shares 
WOIPPY, France, October 19, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )--Regulatory News: 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics (Euronext Paris: ABLD – ISIN: FR001400AHX6), a company specializing in molecular diagnostic solutions, healthcare software and services supporting clinical research, informs the market of the principles communicated by its principal shareholder, Advanced Biological Laboratories S.A., a Luxembourg-based diagnostics company ("ABL Luxembourg"), regarding the future management of its shareholding. 
Following a recommendation by the Board of Directors of ABL Texcell Diagnostics, ABL Luxembourg has indicated that, should it consider any future disposal of significant blocks of shares in the Company, it intends to prioritize investors with a long-term investment horizon who would agree, where the terms of the proposed transaction allow, to a minimum twelve-month holding commitment, or lock-up. 
This approach is intended to foster a stable and long-term shareholder base, consistent with the Company's development strategy. It reflects ABL Luxembourg's current intention and does not constitute a commitment to sell shares or the announcement of any specific transaction. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics notes that previous block disposals were carried out by ABL Luxembourg in its capacity as a shareholder and not by the Company. As these transactions involved existing shares, they did not result in the issuance of any new shares, any dilution for existing shareholders or any proceeds being received by ABL Texcell Diagnostics. 
Furthermore, according to information provided by ABL Luxembourg, a final tranche of 10,000 ABL Texcell Diagnostics shares remains on loan to Alumni Capital. The return of these shares is expected by the end of October 2026. Subject to its effective completion, this return will mark the termination of the relevant share loan arrangement. No additional shares may be lent to Alumni Capital under this agreement. 
These principles reflect both the recommendations of the Board of Directors of ABL Texcell Diagnostics and the position expressed by ABL Luxembourg, in accordance with the respective powers and responsibilities of the governing bodies of each company. In this context, Dr Chalom Sayada acts in his respective capacities as Chief Executive Officer of ABL Texcell Diagnostics and as co-founder and principal shareholder of ABL Luxembourg. 
Story Continues 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics remains fully focused on the execution of its growth strategy. This strategy is based on the development of its molecular diagnostics and sequencing activities, the expansion of its services supporting biopharmaceutical development, the strengthening of its international presence, the implementation of synergies arising from recently completed strategic transactions and the selective assessment of external growth opportunities. 
Dr Chalom Sayada, Chief Executive Officer of ABL Texcell Diagnostics, stated: "The forthcoming completion of the share loan arrangement and the position expressed by ABL Luxembourg in favor of long-term investors contribute to creating a more stable shareholder environment for ABL Texcell Diagnostics. The Company can therefore remain fully focused on its operational priorities: developing its activities, accelerating its international expansion, leveraging the complementary nature of its expertise and pursuing sustainable growth for the benefit of all its shareholders". 
Forward-Looking Statements 
This press release contains forward-looking statements based on the information, assessments and assumptions available as of its date. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that may result in actual results or events differing from those expressed or implied herein. 
The intentions expressed by ABL Luxembourg do not constitute an irrevocable commitment or the announcement of any specific transaction. ABL Texcell Diagnostics undertakes no obligation to update these forward-looking statements, except as required by applicable laws or regulations. 
Main translation choices: "disposals of significant blocks of shares" clearly attributes any future transactions to ABL Luxembourg; "existing shares" and "no dilution" preserve the key investor message; and "current intention" avoids presenting the shareholder's position as an irrevocable undertaking. 
About ABL Texcell Diagnostics (ABLD) 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics (ABLD) is an international company that specializes in innovative molecular biology tests and global solutions for its customers: 
Molecular polymerase chain reaction (PCR) detection – UltraGene, and 
Genotyping by DNA sequencing – DeepChek®. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics markets its entire product range globally through its own sales team and a network of exclusive distributors active on all continents. ABL Diagnostics' customers are academic clinical pathology laboratories, private reference laboratories and researchers willing to implement innovative and robust microbiological content in constant expansion. 
Following the acquisition of TEXCELL's operations, ABL Texcell Diagnostics is expanding its activities in the life sciences sector by integrating expertise and services dedicated to virology, biosafety testing and biopharmaceutical development support. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics has been marketing the products and services of its sister company CDL Pharma since the second half of 2025 through an intra-group strategy agreement. 
An expanding portfolio of microbiology products: 
HIV – Drug resistance testing, including a whole genome kit. 
SARS-CoV-2, Tuberculosis, Hepatitis B and C – Advanced Detection Solutions. 
Microbiome and taxonomy – 16s/18s RNA-based analyses. 
Other viral and bacterial targets – Comprehensive molecular assays. 
Integrated Solutions 
Real-time syndromic PCR tests 
Nadis® – Patient Medical Record used in more than 200 hospitals in France for the management of HIV and hepatitis. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics, headquartered in Woippy, is a public limited company listed on compartment B of the regulated market of Euronext in Paris (Euronext: ABLD – ISIN: FR001400AHX6). These molecular biology products generate recurring revenues and cover one of the largest portfolios of applications in microbiology.

Three teams secure places in the WTA Finals Indian Wells doubles field
Press Releases 
3m read
19 Oct 2026
1w ago
Kristina Mladenovic, who has twice won the event, has secured her place with partner Guo Hanyu
Cristina Bucsa is celebrating her debut qualification with Nicole Melichar-Martinez, who will be making her fifth WTA Finals appearance
Defending WTA Finals champion Elise Mertens has qualified with the highly experienced Zhang Shuai
Tickets are available here for this year's WTA Finals at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden
The WTA announced Monday that three doubles teams -- Guo Hanyu & Kristina Mladenovic , Cristina Bucsa & Nicole Melichar-Martinez and Elise Mertens & Zhang Shuai -- have qualified for the WTA Finals Indian Wells, leaving three qualification places remaining to compete on tennis' ultimate stage. 
The teams will join PIF Doubles WTA World No. 1 Katerina Siniakova & trailblazer Taylor Townsend, along with Canada’s Gabriela Dabrowski & Brazilian Luisa Stefani, in the doubles draw. Siniakova and Townsend, along with Dabrowski and Stefani, secured their participation earlier this season.
Following a knee injury, Aleksandra Krunic and her partner Anna Danilina (who currently occupy the No. 3 position on the PIF Race to the WTA Finals Leaderboard) have unfortunately been forced to withdraw from this year’s event.
Kristina Mladenovic is returning to the WTA Finals for the first time since 2019, when she secured her second title at the event after winning her first WTA Finals crown in 2018 (both with Timea Babos).
WTA
She and partner Guo Hanyu, who will be making her debut at the event, have won two titles this season, kicking off the year with a triumph at the WTA 250 ASB Classic (Auckland) before enjoying success on the grass of The Championships, Wimbledon.
Cristina Bucsa and Nicole Melichar-Martinez will also be making their debut as a team at the WTA Finals having enjoyed an impressive 2026 season on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz.
Bucsa, who will be stepping out at the WTA Finals for the first time, and Melichar-Martinez (making her fifth appearance, earning a runner-up finish in 2023) won the WTA 500 Guadalajara Open presented by Santander and also enjoyed success at the WTA 1000 level, contesting the title match at the Internazionali BNL d'Italia (Rome) and making the semifinals at the BNP Paribas Open (Indian Wells).
WTA
Elise Mertens and Zhang Shuai have qualified for the WTA Finals for the first time as a team, but they have no shortage of experience at the event, with a combined total of nine previous appearances between them. Mertens is a two-time champion, winning the title in 2022 and 2025 (both with Veronika Kudermetova) while 2026 marks Zhang Shuai’s third appearance.
Their season has been highlighted by winning the Australian Open, ensuring their qualification through the Grand Slam rule, while they also enjoyed a semifinal run at the WTA 1000 Miami Open presented by Itaú and a further quarterfinal appearance at the WTA 500 VANDA Pharmaceuticals Berlin Tennis Open.
The WTA Finals Indian Wells features the Top 8 singles and doubles teams on the PIF Race to the WTA Finals Leaderboard https://www.wtatennis.com/rankings/race-singles (with the 8th spot going to the singles player and doubles team that have won a Grand Slam if ranked No.8 to No.20). This showcases the world’s best singles players and doubles teams competing in a round-robin format with the singles champion lifting the WTA Finals Billie Jean King Trophy and the doubles champions earning the WTA Finals Martina Navratilova Trophy. The prestigious season-ending tournament celebrates the best of the WTA on and off the court, delivering an unrivaled fan experience that blends sport, entertainment and culture.
Tickets are available here https://www.wtatennis.com/tournaments/wta-finals/tickets for this year's WTA Finals at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden, one of the sport's premier destinations and tournament locations.

[FEATURED]
MODULAR LOGO SYSTEM UNIFIES MAXON’S CREATIVE SOFTWARE layout
 
Motion designer Casey Gu creates the Maxon One Brand Expression Film to introduce a unified visual identity across Maxon’s suite of creative tools. The project translates a modular logo system into motion, establishing a visual connection between products spanning 2D and 3D design, motion graphics, and visual effects. Rather than treating each product as an isolated identity, the film explores how distinct visual characteristics can coexist within a shared brand framework.
 
Led by Leo Hageman, Director of Brand & Creative, the new identity brings together Maxon One, Cinema 4D, Red Giant, ZBrush, Redshift, Universe, Capsules, Cinebench, Cineware, and Moves through a consistent geometric language. Its modular, honeycomb-inspired forms provide the structural basis for this relationship, creating continuity across a diverse range of tools while maintaining room for individual product identities.
all images ©Casey Gu  
 
motion design balances abstract geometry with brand motifs
 
For motion designer Casey Gu, the central challenge was translating the modular visual system into motion while balancing abstraction with product recognition. Using geometric forms, unique transitions, and rhythmic movement, Casey developed a visual narrative that highlights the signature features of each tool while maintaining a consistent visual language across the ecosystem.
 
The animated sequences extend the logo system beyond static marks, using movement to express both individual product identities and their relationships within the broader suite. Shared geometric elements establish continuity, while variations in composition and motion reflect the different functions of each tool. Together, these elements create a flexible visual framework that connects Maxon’s products without diminishing their individual identities.

Qualcomm Showcases V2X Technology at 2026 Gangneung ITS World Congress
Demonstrations include scalable V2X, ADAS integration and global V2X solutions

Qualcomm showcases V2X-based traffic safety technologies and solutions at the 2026 Gangneung ITS World Congress. (Photo: Qualcomm) 
Qualcomm announced on Oct. 19 that it will showcase traffic safety technologies and solutions based on vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communications at the 2026 ITS World Congress in Gangneung, South Korea.
The ITS World Congress is an event focused on intelligent transportation system policies, technologies and services. It addresses future mobility issues, including connected vehicles, autonomous driving, smart infrastructure and artificial intelligence (AI). This year’s event runs from Oct. 19 to 23 at Gangneung Olympic Park in Gangwon Province.
Qualcomm will demonstrate seven technologies during the event and exhibit real-world applications. These include scalable V2X, advanced driver assistance system (ADAS)-based V2X, smart infrastructure, global V2X solutions and products developed by partners using Qualcomm technologies.
V2X enables vehicles to exchange wireless data directly with other vehicles, road infrastructure, pedestrians, motorcycles and other surrounding objects. Using radio signals, the technology can identify potential hazards and warn drivers even in blind spots or adverse weather conditions where visibility is limited. Conventional camera and radar sensors have been limited to detecting obstacles directly ahead or objects within their line of sight.
Scalable V2X allows communication capabilities and data processing levels to be adjusted flexibly according to driving conditions and vehicle performance.
ADAS-based V2X combines onboard sensor systems with V2X communications. Rather than simply warning drivers of potential hazards, the technology enables vehicles to initiate automatic emergency braking (AEB) or steering control.
Qualcomm Korea President Kim Sang-pyo delivers a keynote speech titled “Accelerating Innovation in Traffic Safety.” (Photo: Qualcomm) 
Smart infrastructure refers to intelligent road environments equipped with communication modules and detection sensors installed in traffic lights, electronic road signs, streetlights and base stations.
Global V2X refers to V2X solutions based on worldwide standards.
Kim Sang-pyo, president of Qualcomm Korea, delivered a keynote speech titled “Accelerating Innovation in Traffic Safety.”
“Qualcomm has led mobile communications technology for more than 40 years and has worked with numerous partners to advance the V2X ecosystem, from standardization to commercialization,” Kim said. “We are supporting the development of safe and intelligent transportation systems that reflect real-world road conditions in South Korea.”

Paul van Gerven 
Editor at Bits&Chips

Elon Musk’s Terafab is expected to receive its first ASML EUV lithography system in mid-2027, according to journalist Tim Culpan , citing sources familiar with the matter. The scanner could arrive before the research fab near Austin is ready to accommodate it. Semianalysis expects equipment installation to begin later that year.

The reported delivery suggests Terafab will initially use conventional EUV equipment despite Musk’s public enthusiasm for free-electron laser light sources. Introducing an alternative light source would likely add too much process development and equipment qualification work.
Separately, Terafab’s planned volume-production site is being developed in Grimes County, Texas. Semianalysis forecasts that the first phase will begin operating in late 2029 and reach volume production by mid-2030. The fab reportedly plans to adopt Intel’s 14A process.

Qualcomm showcased vehicle-to-everything (V2X) technology that consolidates vehicles, road infrastructure, and pedestrians in real time at the 2026 Gangneung Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) World Congress, which opened on the 19th.
Kim Sang-pyo, Qualcomm Korea president/Courtesy of Qualcomm Korea 
Qualcomm said on the 19th it will exhibit V2X-based traffic safety solutions and related products at the event being held in Gangneung through the 23rd.
V2X is a technology in which a vehicle communicates with other vehicles, road facilities such as traffic lights, and pedestrians to understand surrounding traffic conditions. Unlike cameras or radar, it can also deliver risk information from areas not directly visible, helping prevent accidents that can occur in blind spots at intersections or beyond sensor detection ranges.
At this event, Qualcomm is introducing extended V2X, V2X linked with advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), smart road infrastructure, and global V2X solutions. It is also exhibiting partner products that apply Qualcomm technology.
In particular, it is presenting use cases that combine vehicle sensors and communication technology to identify the movements of surrounding vehicles and pedestrians and issue early warnings of dangerous situations. The company said this can supplement the limitations of existing vehicle sensors and improve road safety and traffic operations efficiency.
On the day, Kim Sang-pyo, president of Qualcomm Korea, delivered a keynote speech on the theme of accelerating traffic safety innovation. Kim said, "For more than 40 years, Qualcomm has contributed to the development of the global ecosystem from V2X standardization to commercialization and real-world road deployment, based on the technological expertise accumulated in the mobile consolidation field."
Kim added, "In Korea, we are also supporting the establishment of safe and intelligent transportation systems through interoperability verification that reflects actual road environments," and said, "Going forward, we will enhance road safety and expand the possibilities of future mobility based on consolidation technology."
Meanwhile, the congress, hosted and organized by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Gangneung City, and ITS KOREA, is being held under the theme of "A world united beyond mobility." Government, industry, and academic stakeholders from various countries are participating to discuss policies and technologies related to intelligent transport systems and to conduct demonstrations of advanced transport technologies.

HYPROMAG USA DEPLOYS MOBILE INSERMA SYSTEM, EXTENDING HDD PROCESSING TO CUSTOMER SITES ACROSS THE UNITED STATES 
Feedstock platform continues to build ahead of Dallas-Fort Worth commissioning, with commercial PCB sales to smelter partners generating revenue that supports magnet acquisition 
LONDON / VANCOUVER: 19 October 2026 – Mkango Magnetic Materials Ltd. (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) (“Mkango”) is pleased to announce that HyProMag USA LLC (“HyProMag USA”) has announced the deployment of its third Inserma Anoia S.L. (“Inserma”) hard disk drive (“HDD”) separation system as a mobile processing unit, expanding HyProMag USA's processing and customer engagement capabilities across the United States. The deployment further strengthens HyProMag USA's partnership [1] with Intelligent Lifecycle Solutions (“ ILS”) and supports the expansion of a scalable nationwide platform for the recovery and recycling of rare earth magnets from end-of-life HDDs. 
Feedstock inventories currently under contract and in storage, together with active procurement programs, continue to strengthen the feedstock platform and are expected to support initial commissioning and ramp-up activities for Phase 1 at the planned Dallas-Fort Worth facility (the “Texas Hub”) in 2028. HyProMag USA has also completed commercial sales of recovered printed circuit board (“PCB”) material to downstream smelter partners, generating revenue that supports the acquisition and retention of magnet-bearing feedstock inventory. 
Julian Treger, Chief Executive Officer of CoTec Holdings Corp. (“CoTec”), commented : “The deployment of our third Inserma system as a mobile processing unit represents an important step in the development of the Dallas-Fort Worth project. Together with continued progress in feedstock sourcing and commercial PCB recovery, it strengthens our operating platform and expands our ability to engage directly with customers across multiple end markets. These milestones provide increasing confidence in our ability to support commissioning activities and establish a long-term domestic supply of recycled rare earth materials.” 
Graham Davy, Managing Director of ILS, commented: “The focus of the ILS team has been on demonstrating that HDDs can be efficiently processed into separate, marketable material streams. We have continued to build feedstock inventories, completed commercial sales of recovered PCB materials to smelter partners for HyProMag USA and expanded our capabilities through the deployment of a mobile Inserma system. The mobile unit allows us to work directly with customers at their facilities, supporting trial programs, demonstrating material recovery performance and creating opportunities to secure additional feedstock supply.” 
Key Highlights 
● Processing capability expanded: HyProMag USA's third Inserma HDD separation system has been deployed as a mobile processing unit to support customer qualification programs, secure on-site recovery campaigns and future feedstock growth opportunities across the United States. 
● Commissioning readiness advanced: Feedstock inventories currently under contract and in storage, together with active procurement programs, are expected to support initial commissioning and ramp-up of Phase 1 activities at the Texas Hub in 2028. 
● PCB revenue supports magnet acquisition: Commercial sales of recovered PCB material to smelter partners have generated revenue within the HDD processing flow sheet, partly offsetting the cost of acquiring and retaining magnet-bearing feedstock for future rare earth recycling operations. 
● Feedstock channels diversified: Sourcing activities continue to expand across industrial, healthcare, government and IT asset disposition sectors. 
● Secure processing platform: R2v3-certified operations, ISO-certified management systems and documented chain-of-custody procedures support secure handling of data-bearing equipment. 
● Data center market focus: Mobile processing capability enables on-site recovery programs within hyperscale data centers and secure IT asset disposition environments. 
● Inserma testing: A next generation Inserma system designed specifically for the high-capacity HDDs used in hyperscale data centers, including helium filled units, is currently being tested, with early results indicating processing times of under three seconds per drive and successful processing of modern high-capacity data center formats. 
● Partnership network expanding: Relationships across the data center, electronics recycling and rare earth magnet value chain continue to support platform growth. 
Expanding Feedstock Access 
To support continued growth in feedstock volumes, HyProMag USA has deployed its third Inserma HDD separation system as a mobile processing unit to complement existing operations in South Carolina and Nevada. Unlike the fixed installations currently operating through the ILS partnership, the system has been configured for mobile deployment and is intended to support customer trials, feedstock development programs and on-site processing campaigns across the United States. 
Feedstock inventories currently under contract and in storage, together with active procurement programs, continue to strengthen the feedstock platform and are expected to support initial commissioning and ramp-up activities at the Texas Hub. Feedstock sourcing activities continue to expand beyond HDDs into industrial, healthcare, government and IT asset disposition sectors, increasing confidence in the scalability of HyProMag USA's feedstock platform and supporting future supply requirements for the Texas Hub. 
Commercial PCB Recovery 
ILS has completed commercial sales for HyProMag USA of recovered PCB material to downstream smelter partners. The sales validate an additional revenue stream within the HDD processing flow sheet and show that value can be recovered from secondary material streams. Magnet-bearing materials are being retained as feedstock inventory for future rare earth recycling operations. Revenue from recovered PCB material partly offsets the cost of acquiring magnet-bearing feedstock, improving the economics of building the inventory required to support Texas Hub operations. 
Secure Recovery and Chain of Custody 
ILS operates under internationally recognized recycling and management standards, including R2v3 certification and ISO-certified management systems, supporting responsible recycling practices, operational controls and continuous improvement initiatives. The recovery process is supported by documented chain-of-custody procedures designed to provide traceability from collection through processing and final disposition. These controls support the requirements of data center operators, IT asset disposition providers, enterprise customers and government organizations seeking secure and auditable management of end-of-life electronic equipment. 
Building Strategic Partnerships 
HyProMag USA continues to expand relationships across the electronics recycling, data infrastructure and rare earth magnet value chain. Working alongside data center operators, IT asset disposition providers, recyclers, technology companies and downstream processing partners, HyProMag USA is developing an integrated platform for the collection, recovery and recycling of magnet-bearing materials. HyProMag USA is evaluating additional feedstock pathways, including industrial and transportation-related material streams, with pilot programs and commercial opportunities under review. 
About ILS 
Intelligent Lifecycle Solutions (“ILS”) provides secure recovery, processing and recycling services for end-of-life electronic equipment. Through its operating facilities in South Carolina and Nevada, ILS supports the recovery of valuable materials from electronic waste streams while maintaining robust data security and chain-of-custody protocols. 
About HyProMag USA 
HyProMag USA is developing advanced rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing operations to establish a secure domestic U.S. supply chain for neodymium iron boron (“NdFeB”) magnets, essential components for AI infrastructure, defense systems, robotics, electric vehicles, and advanced electronics. Leveraging the revolutionary Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap (“HPMS”) technology, developed over 15 years with over US$100 million in R&D investment, HyProMag USA delivers faster magnet-to-magnet short-loop recycling that uses 88% less energy and reduces carbon emissions by 85% compared to conventional methods. HPMS accepts a wide range of magnet-bearing feedstocks – including end-of-life EV motors, data-center and industrial equipment, consumer electronics, and manufacturing scrap – enabling recovery of magnet-grade material without chemical processing. 
Ownership 
HyProMag USA LLC is owned 50:50 by CoTec Holdings Corp. (TSXV: CTH; OTCQX: CTHCF) (“CoTec”) and HyProMag Limited. HyProMag Limited is 100% owned by Maginito Limited which is owned on a 79.4%/20.6% basis by Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) and CoTec. 
About Mkango Magnetic Materials Ltd. 
Mkango is listed on the AIM and the TSX-V Stock Exchanges. Mkango’s corporate strategy is to become a market leader in the production of recycled rare earth magnets, alloys and oxides, through its interest in Maginito Limited (“Maginito”), which is owned 79.4 per cent by Mkango and 20.6 per cent by CoTec Holdings Corp. (“CoTec”), and the Remloy business acquired by its wholly owned German subsidiary, to develop new sustainable sources of neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium to supply accelerating demand from electric vehicles, wind turbines and other clean energy technologies. 
Maginito holds a 100 per cent interest in HyProMag Limited and a 90 per cent direct and indirect interest (assuming conversion of Maginito’s convertible loan) in HyProMag GmbH, focused on short loop rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing in the UK and Germany, respectively, and a 100 per cent interest in Mkango Rare Earths UK Ltd (“Mkango UK”), focused on long loop rare earth magnet recycling in the UK via a chemical processing route. 
Maginito and CoTec are also expanding Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap (“HPMS”) recycling technology into the United States via the 50/50 owned HyProMag USA joint venture company. 
Remloy has developed a plant in Bitterfeld, Germany, which recycles end-of-life rare earth magnets via a melting process (medium loop rare earth magnet recycling) to produce NdFeB alloy powders for the bonded and hot deformed magnet markets, complementary to HyProMag’s short loop recycling process, to produce sintered magnets, and to Mkango UK’s long loop recycling process, to produce mixed rare earth carbonates and oxides. 
Mkango currently owns 100% of the advanced stage Songwe Hill rare earths project in Malawi and the proposed Pulawy rare earths separation plant in Poland. On grant of the large-scale mining licence the Government of Malawi may elect to take a free 10% interest in the entity holding that licence. The Songwe and Pulawy projects and HyProMag GmbH have been selected as Strategic Projects under the European Union Critical Raw Materials Act. Songwe has also received Development Funding from the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (“DFC”), the U.S. Government’s development finance institution, securing US$4.6 million in reimbursable funding for Front End Engineering and Design. Mkango Rare Earths Limited (“MKAR”) has signed a Business Combination Agreement with Crown PropTech Acquisitions (“CPTK”) to list the Songwe Hill and Pulawy rare earths projects on NASDAQ via a SPAC merger (the “Proposed Business Combination”) under the name Mkango Rare Earths Limited.

Qualcomm Technologies is taking aim at the transport safety market with communications technology linking vehicles and road infrastructure. The company said it will showcase V2X-based transport safety technologies and solutions at the 2026 Gangneung ITS World Congress in Gangneung Olympic Park. Qualcomm will run seven demos covering expanded V2X, ADAS-based V2X, smart infrastructure and global V2X, alongside partner products.

Kim Sang-pyo (김상표), president of Qualcomm Korea, delivers a keynote speech titled "Accelerating Transportation Safety" at the "2026 Gangneung ITS World Congress." [Photo: Qualcomm] 
Qualcomm Technologies is moving to target the transport safety market with communications technology linking vehicles and road infrastructure. Qualcomm said on Oct. 19 it is taking part in the "2026 Gangneung ITS World Congress" at Gangneung Olympic Park and will showcase V2X-based transport safety technologies and solutions, referring to vehicle-to-everything communications.
The ITS World Congress is the world’s largest event where government, industry and academia officials and technology experts gather to discuss intelligent transport system policies, technologies and services. This year’s theme is "One World Beyond Mobility." The agenda includes vehicle connectivity, autonomous driving, smart infrastructure, traffic management, mobility services, AI and data-based systems, and policies and standards.
Qualcomm will run seven demos during the event. Exhibits include expanded V2X, advanced driver assistance systems, or ADAS-based V2X, smart infrastructure and global V2X. Partner products incorporating Qualcomm solutions and products will also be shown. In each demo, the company said it will present use cases in which V2X complements vehicle sensors and connects vehicles, road infrastructure and road users in real time to improve safety and efficiency.
V2X is a technology that enables vehicles, road infrastructure, motorcycles and vulnerable road users such as pedestrians to communicate directly in real time. Cameras and radar can struggle to identify danger when visibility is blocked, but V2X allows vehicles and their surroundings to exchange information even in non-line-of-sight conditions. That is why it can warn in advance of hazards in blind spots and outside sensor detection range. V2X has moved beyond proof-of-concept, and real-world deployments are increasing in many parts of the world. Several countries have built road infrastructure applying V2X, and vehicles equipped with V2X functions have been released and are being used on actual roads.
Kim Sang-pyo (김상표), president of Qualcomm Korea, will deliver a keynote speech titled "Accelerating Transportation Safety." Kim said, "Based on experience leading mobile connectivity innovation for more than 40 years, Qualcomm has led the development of the global ecosystem with various partners from standardisation of V2X technology to commercialisation and real-road deployment." He added, "In Korea as well, we are supporting the building of safer and more intelligent transport systems based on interoperability verification that reflects real road environments," and, "We will continue to enhance road safety and expand new possibilities for future mobility through forward-looking connectivity solutions."
