content_text:
Equipment giants are vying for advanced packaging
半导体行业观察 2026-10-19 10:59 
Today, the competition among equipment vendors centering on hybrid bonding is essentially an early strategic layout for the dominance of the future 3D integrated manufacturing process. 
In early October, a piece of news in the capital market drew widespread attention: over concerns that ASML may enter the hybrid bonding equipment market and the demand for HBM-related equipment will be postponed, Bank of America downgraded the investment rating of Besi, a Dutch packaging equipment manufacturer, on October 6, driving its share price down 5.39% on the same day; the next day, as UBS further downgraded its rating, Besi's share price fell another 8.49%, with a cumulative drop of about 13.4% in just two trading days. In fact, ASML delivered the TWINSCAN XT:260 lithography system for advanced packaging as early as 2025, and news of its R&D of hybrid bonding equipment came out this year, further expanding its business beyond traditional lithography.
Overview of Besi's stock price trend (Source: Yahoo)
Meanwhile, Applied Materials and Lam Research are also accelerating their layout. In the first week of October alone, Applied Materials successively announced deepened cooperation with Besi and Intel, with R&D scope covering hybrid bonding, TCB, chip-to-panel, Foveros 3D packaging and other technologies. Leveraging technologies such as etching, deposition and copper electroplating, Lam Research continues to expand its equipment layout in the fields of TSV and 3D interconnection. In March this year, Reuters reported that both Lam Research and Applied Materials showed acquisition interest in Besi.
It can be seen that the three giants of front-end equipment are extending to advanced packaging along different technical routes. On the one hand, the front-end equipment giants are actively extending to advanced packaging, and on the other hand, the traditional leading packaging equipment manufacturers have become the targets of cooperation, investment and even potential mergers and acquisitions. The originally relatively clear division of labor between front-end and back-end in the semiconductor equipment industry is undergoing subtle changes. Advanced packaging is becoming a new battlefield that semiconductor equipment giants are vying to enter. 
The Three Front-End Equipment Giants Are Surrounding Advanced Packaging 
In fact, a closer look shows that although Applied Materials, Lam Research and ASML are all extending to the advanced packaging field, the three have chosen different entry methods.
Applied Materials pays more attention to material engineering and process integration, and builds comprehensive solutions covering multiple manufacturing links by cooperating with professional packaging equipment manufacturers; Lam Research relies on etching, deposition and copper interconnection technologies to compete for more and more key process steps in the 3D integration process; ASML has begun to try to extend its accumulated nanoscale motion control, precision alignment and measurement technologies in the lithography field to hybrid bonding equipment.
These three routes are complementary to each other, and may gradually form direct competition as technology evolves.
Applied Materials: Join hands with Besi to build a complete process chain
First of all, talking about Applied Materials, its layout in advanced packaging has actually lasted for many years.
As early as 2020, Applied Materials and Besi established a joint R&D project in Singapore, combining its own technologies in etching, planarization, thin film deposition, wafer cleaning, metrology and inspection, and particle control with Besi's capabilities in precision chip mounting, interconnection and assembly.
The representative achievement of the cooperation between the two parties is the Kinex integrated Die-to-Wafer (D2W) hybrid bonding system. Different from traditional packaging equipment that mainly focuses on chip mounting and connection, Kinex attempts to integrate pre-bonding processes such as surface treatment, cleaning, activation and alignment into a more compact manufacturing flow.
Kinex (Image source: Applied Materials)
This design has practical significance.
In the hybrid bonding process, the two chips or wafers to be connected must not only achieve extremely high-precision geometric alignment, but also ensure the flatness, cleanliness and material state of the bonding surface. Even if the bonding equipment itself has excellent positioning accuracy, if the previous process causes particle pollution, abnormal copper pad depression or unstable surface state, it may still lead to connection defects. The cooperation between Applied Materials and Besi is essentially an attempt to combine traditional front-end material engineering with back-end precision assembly technology to improve the final yield through cross-process collaboration.
It is worth noting that Applied Materials does not limit technical cooperation to Besi alone. Previously, it also cooperated with EV Group (EVG), an Austrian wafer bonding equipment manufacturer, to develop wafer-to-wafer bonding solutions.
The cooperation upgrade on October 1 this year further expanded the R&D boundary of both parties. According to the official announcement, Besi will become an innovation partner of Applied Materials' EPIC R&D center located in Silicon Valley. In the future, the two parties will not only continue to promote D2W hybrid bonding, but also jointly research TCB process scaling, chip-to-chip, chip-to-panel and new integration architectures for optical interconnection. The EPIC center is planned to have a maximum investment scale of about 5 billion US dollars, and the investment will be gradually rolled out as customer projects advance. An important goal of this center is to enable chip manufacturers, equipment suppliers and material enterprises to participate in joint R&D at an earlier stage, shortening the cycle for new processes to move from the laboratory to mass production.
From the perspective of industrial significance, this means that Applied Materials is trying to incorporate advanced packaging, which was previously a relatively independent back-end manufacturing link, into its broader material engineering R&D system.
Just five days later, Applied Materials announced the deepening of cooperation with Intel, covering R&D of next-generation transistors, on-chip interconnection and Foveros 3D advanced packaging.
These two cooperations seem to target different enterprises, but their technical logic is connected. In 3D stacking, there are complex interactions between interconnection density, power supply paths, heat dissipation structures and material stress between chips. The performance optimization of next-generation chips is increasingly difficult to achieve by relying solely on one link among advanced process, metal interconnection or packaging.
Therefore, for Applied Materials, the real strategic value may not only be to obtain more orders for hybrid bonding equipment, but to participate in the definition of next-generation chip manufacturing processes earlier through the joint development of front-end and back-end processes. As Prabu Raja from Applied Materials asserted: Advanced packaging is no longer just the physical assembly of the back-end, but a material engineering revolution that requires wafer-level precision and cleanliness.
Lam Research: From Etching, Deposition to 3D Interconnection 
Compared with the cooperation model between Applied Materials and Besi, Lam Research's layout in the advanced packaging field highlights its existing process and equipment advantages. Lam Research has accumulated a large number of high-aspect-ratio etching, thin film deposition and metal interconnection technologies in the past in the manufacture of logic chips, DRAM and 3D NAND.
With the continuous 3D development of advanced packaging, these technologies are gaining more application scenarios. For example, in 3D stacked chips, Through-Silicon Vias (TSVs) undertake vertical electrical connections between different chip layers. To make deep and narrow vias in silicon wafers, high-aspect-ratio etching technology is required, and the via sidewall morphology, etching uniformity and defect control should be guaranteed as much as possible.
Lam Research's Syndion deep reactive ion etching equipment is designed for deep hole etching requirements including TSV. But etching the via is only the first step. After forming the insulating layer, barrier layer and seed layer, the via needs to be filled by metal deposition to form a reliable electrical connection. If voids, seams or other defects occur during the copper filling process, it may affect resistance, heat dissipation and long-term reliability.
The SABRE 3D copper electroplating platform that Lam Research highlighted in July this year is developed around the manufacturing needs of complex metal interconnection in advanced packaging. The company emphasizes that as the interconnection structure of advanced packaging becomes more and more refined, the requirements for metal filling uniformity and void control in the manufacturing process are continuously increasing. SABRE 3D provides metal filling capabilities for structures such as TSV, wafer-level packaging and redistribution layers through electrochemical deposition processes.
In addition, Lam Research has also deployed the VECTOR TEOS 3D dielectric material deposition equipment, as well as related wet and deposition processes for large-sized substrates.
It is worth noting that the attraction of advanced packaging to Lam Research is not just hybrid bonding itself. From traditional 2.5D packaging to 3D chip stacking, and then to panel-level packaging, more and more manufacturing steps require high-precision etching, thin film deposition and metal interconnection processes, which are the fields that Lam Research has long been deeply engaged in.
Therefore, Lam Research's competitive logic is not necessarily to directly replace Besi to manufacture bonding equipment, but to obtain more value in the advanced packaging industry chain by expanding the coverage of key process equipment.
However, the company's interest in bonding equipment is also worthy of attention. In March 2026, Reuters, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that Besi has attracted the attention of potential acquirers due to its hybrid bonding technology, and both Lam Research and Applied Materials are on the relevant list.
For Lam Research, if it wants to further expand into direct bonding equipment, leveraging professional equipment enterprises that already have a customer base and mass production experience may help it establish market position faster than relying entirely on internal R&D.
However, up to now, public reports have not confirmed that the relevant acquisition transaction has finally been reached. This also reveals some information: the next round of competition in the advanced packaging equipment industry may be accompanied by equity investment, strategic cooperation and even industrial integration in addition to technology R&D and product upgrading.
ASML: From Lithography to Hybrid Bonding, Directly Challenging Besi? 
It can be seen that the advanced packaging business of Applied Materials and Lam Research mainly stems from the horizontal extension of their existing material engineering capabilities. However, ASML's potential entry may have a more direct impact on the traditional hybrid bonding equipment market.
As the exclusive global supplier of EUV lithography equipment, ASML's core technical accumulation is concentrated in the fields of high-precision optics, motion control, wafer positioning, deformation compensation and nanoscale overlay accuracy.
In the past, these technologies were mainly used to accurately transfer increasingly tiny circuit patterns to the wafer surface. However, in hybrid bonding, there is also a very critical problem to be solved: how to accurately align the metal interconnection structures on two wafers or different chips and maintain stability during the bonding process. Therefore, there is a certain degree of commonality between ASML's original technical capabilities and hybrid bonding equipment. 
In fact, ASML has already entered the advanced packaging market through dedicated lithography equipment. At the annual general meeting of shareholders held in April 2026, ASML disclosed that the company has delivered the first TWINSCAN XT:260 i-line lithography system, which is specially designed for 3D integration and advanced packaging applications. Different from EUV scanners, which are mainly used for advanced logic processes, the XT:260 targets special patterning requirements in advanced packaging. ASML pointed out in its demonstration materials that the micro-bump process requires a large depth of focus, while hybrid bonding puts forward higher requirements for pattern resolution. This means that as the interconnection density of advanced packaging continues to increase, lithography itself has begun to become an important link affecting the evolution of packaging technology.
The TWINSCAN XT:260 launched by ASML last year is an i-line scanner that can process 270 wafers per hour. In view of the growing demand for AI chips, ASML plans to shift its business focus from pure front-end chip production equipment to packaging and bonding technologies in the next 10 to 15 years. (Image source: ASML)
But ASML is obviously not satisfied with only providing advanced packaging lithography equipment.
In March this year, South Korean media The Elec reported that ASML has started the overall architecture design of hybrid bonding equipment and has been in contact for cooperation with long-term suppliers such as Prodrive Technologies and VDL ETG. These enterprises previously participated in the supply of precision motion systems, drive devices and mechanical structures for ASML's lithography equipment. If ASML tries to transfer its accumulation in high-precision motion platforms to bonding equipment, it may further narrow the technical distance between lithography equipment and hybrid bonding equipment.
Moreover, there is another point worthy of attention that ASML has already published related patents.
The international patent WO2026098870A1 published on May 15, 2026 is titled "Bonding Apparatus", with the applicant being ASML Netherlands BV. The patent relates to a bonding device for two semiconductor substrates, focusing on discussing how to improve the alignment problem that may occur in the bonding process through state control of the substrate support surface. The patent document points out that factors such as internal stress of the wafer, support surface state and flatness may cause alignment deviation during bonding. This is obviously related to ASML's long-term research on wafer deformation compensation, position measurement and precision motion control technologies.
Of course, patent layout does not mean that mass-produced equipment is already mature. ASML has not yet publicly confirmed the commercial delivery time, customer certification progress or mass production performance of its hybrid bonding equipment. But this potential competition has begun to affect the market's expectations for traditional equipment enterprises. On October 6, Bank of America downgraded Besi's investment rating, which mentioned the competitive risk that ASML may enter the hybrid bonding market in the future.
For Besi, this risk is worthy of attention. In the traditional advanced packaging equipment market, Besi's important advantages come from long-term accumulation in precision mounting, assembly processes and hybrid bonding technology. Once ASML officially enters, it may form a new competitive force with its experience in nanoscale positioning, precision measurement and large-scale complex equipment system engineering.
However, from having key technical capabilities to developing competitive commercial equipment and then passing the mass production certification of wafer fabs, there is still a considerable long process of technology and commercialization.
Whether ASML can really challenge Besi ultimately depends on the alignment accuracy, throughput, yield, equipment stability, cost and customer certification progress of the equipment, and cannot be judged solely based on patents or supply chain news.
Why Has Hybrid Bonding Become the Focus of Competition? 
An important background for front-end equipment giants to enter advanced packaging one after another is that chip interconnection technology is changing.
In traditional 2.5D and 3D packaging, chips usually establish electrical connections through Micro-bumps. Thermal Compression Bonding (TCB) achieves reliable connection between solder and metal pads by applying temperature and pressure. This process is widely used in the field of high-performance computing and memory chips, but with the increase of chip stacking layers and the improvement of interconnection density, traditional micro-bump structures are gradually facing higher requirements in terms of pitch, connection height, parasitic effect and thermomechanical reliability.
Hybrid bonding provides another technical route. It combines direct dielectric bonding with metal interconnection to reduce the dependence on traditional solder bumps, thus making it possible to achieve smaller interconnection pitch, higher connection density and more compact chip stacking structure.
In May 2026, Imec, the Belgian microelectronics research center, and EV Group announced that they had achieved a 200nm copper interconnection pitch in wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding research. The research team achieved a post-bond copper pad overlay deviation of less than 40nm for all test chips on 300mm wafers.
Transmission electron microscope image of the daisy chain structure on a 200nm hexagonal pad grid with hybrid pads of the same size and 25% designed copper density. (Image source: imec/IEEE)

To make deep and narrow vias in silicon wafers, high-aspect-ratio etching technology is required, and the via sidewall morphology, etching uniformity and defect control should be guaranteed as much as possible.
Lam Research's Syndion deep reactive ion etching equipment is designed for deep hole etching requirements including TSV. But etching the via is only the first step. After forming the insulating layer, barrier layer and seed layer, the via needs to be filled by metal deposition to form a reliable electrical connection. If voids, seams or other defects occur during the copper filling process, it may affect resistance, heat dissipation and long-term reliability.
The SABRE 3D copper electroplating platform that Lam Research highlighted in July this year is developed around the manufacturing needs of complex metal interconnection in advanced packaging. The company emphasizes that as the interconnection structure of advanced packaging becomes more and more refined, the requirements for metal filling uniformity and void control in the manufacturing process are continuously increasing. SABRE 3D provides metal filling capabilities for structures such as TSV, wafer-level packaging and redistribution layers through electrochemical deposition processes.
In addition, Lam Research has also deployed the VECTOR TEOS 3D dielectric material deposition equipment, as well as related wet and deposition processes for large-sized substrates.
It is worth noting that the attraction of advanced packaging to Lam Research is not just hybrid bonding itself. From traditional 2.5D packaging to 3D chip stacking, and then to panel-level packaging, more and more manufacturing steps require high-precision etching, thin film deposition and metal interconnection processes, which are the fields that Lam Research has long been deeply engaged in.
Therefore, Lam Research's competitive logic is not necessarily to directly replace Besi to manufacture bonding equipment, but to obtain more value in the advanced packaging industry chain by expanding the coverage of key process equipment.
However, the company's interest in bonding equipment is also worthy of attention. In March 2026, Reuters, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that Besi has attracted the attention of potential acquirers due to its hybrid bonding technology, and both Lam Research and Applied Materials are on the relevant list.
For Lam Research, if it wants to further expand into direct bonding equipment, leveraging professional equipment enterprises that already have a customer base and mass production experience may help it establish market position faster than relying entirely on internal R&D.
However, up to now, public reports have not confirmed that the relevant acquisition transaction has finally been reached. This also reveals some information: the next round of competition in the advanced packaging equipment industry may be accompanied by equity investment, strategic cooperation and even industrial integration in addition to technology R&D and product upgrading.
ASML: From Lithography to Hybrid Bonding, Directly Challenging Besi? 
It can be seen that the advanced packaging business of Applied Materials and Lam Research mainly stems from the horizontal extension of their existing material engineering capabilities. However, ASML's potential entry may have a more direct impact on the traditional hybrid bonding equipment market.
As the exclusive global supplier of EUV lithography equipment, ASML's core technical accumulation is concentrated in the fields of high-precision optics, motion control, wafer positioning, deformation compensation and nanoscale overlay accuracy.
In the past, these technologies were mainly used to accurately transfer increasingly tiny circuit patterns to the wafer surface. However, in hybrid bonding, there is also a very critical problem to be solved: how to accurately align the metal interconnection structures on two wafers or different chips and maintain stability during the bonding process. Therefore, there is a certain degree of commonality between ASML's original technical capabilities and hybrid bonding equipment. 
In fact, ASML has already entered the advanced packaging market through dedicated lithography equipment. At the annual general meeting of shareholders held in April 2026, ASML disclosed that the company has delivered the first TWINSCAN XT:260 i-line lithography system, which is specially designed for 3D integration and advanced packaging applications. Different from EUV scanners, which are mainly used for advanced logic processes, the XT:260 targets special patterning requirements in advanced packaging. ASML pointed out in its demonstration materials that the micro-bump process requires a large depth of focus, while hybrid bonding puts forward higher requirements for pattern resolution. This means that as the interconnection density of advanced packaging continues to increase, lithography itself has begun to become an important link affecting the evolution of packaging technology.
The TWINSCAN XT:260 launched by ASML last year is an i-line scanner that can process 270 wafers per hour. In view of the growing demand for AI chips, ASML plans to shift its business focus from pure front-end chip production equipment to packaging and bonding technologies in the next 10 to 15 years. (Image source: ASML)
But ASML is obviously not satisfied with only providing advanced packaging lithography equipment.
In March this year, South Korean media The Elec reported that ASML has started the overall architecture design of hybrid bonding equipment and has been in contact for cooperation with long-term suppliers such as Prodrive Technologies and VDL ETG. These enterprises previously participated in the supply of precision motion systems, drive devices and mechanical structures for ASML's lithography equipment. If ASML tries to transfer its accumulation in high-precision motion platforms to bonding equipment, it may further narrow the technical distance between lithography equipment and hybrid bonding equipment.
Moreover, there is another point worthy of attention that ASML has already published related patents.
The international patent WO2026098870A1 published on May 15, 2026 is titled "Bonding Apparatus", with the applicant being ASML Netherlands BV. The patent relates to a bonding device for two semiconductor substrates, focusing on discussing how to improve the alignment problem that may occur in the bonding process through state control of the substrate support surface. The patent document points out that factors such as internal stress of the wafer, support surface state and flatness may cause alignment deviation during bonding. This is obviously related to ASML's long-term research on wafer deformation compensation, position measurement and precision motion control technologies.
Of course, patent layout does not mean that mass-produced equipment is already mature. ASML has not yet publicly confirmed the commercial delivery time, customer certification progress or mass production performance of its hybrid bonding equipment. But this potential competition has begun to affect the market's expectations for traditional equipment enterprises. On October 6, Bank of America downgraded Besi's investment rating, which mentioned the competitive risk that ASML may enter the hybrid bonding market in the future.
For Besi, this risk is worthy of attention. In the traditional advanced packaging equipment market, Besi's important advantages come from long-term accumulation in precision mounting, assembly processes and hybrid bonding technology. Once ASML officially enters, it may form a new competitive force with its experience in nanoscale positioning, precision measurement and large-scale complex equipment system engineering.
However, from having key technical capabilities to developing competitive commercial equipment and then passing the mass production certification of wafer fabs, there is still a considerable long process of technology and commercialization.
Whether ASML can really challenge Besi ultimately depends on the alignment accuracy, throughput, yield, equipment stability, cost and customer certification progress of the equipment, and cannot be judged solely based on patents or supply chain news.
Why Has Hybrid Bonding Become the Focus of Competition? 
An important background for front-end equipment giants to enter advanced packaging one after another is that chip interconnection technology is changing.
In traditional 2.5D and 3D packaging, chips usually establish electrical connections through Micro-bumps. Thermal Compression Bonding (TCB) achieves reliable connection between solder and metal pads by applying temperature and pressure. This process is widely used in the field of high-performance computing and memory chips, but with the increase of chip stacking layers and the improvement of interconnection density, traditional micro-bump structures are gradually facing higher requirements in terms of pitch, connection height, parasitic effect and thermomechanical reliability.
Hybrid bonding provides another technical route. It combines direct dielectric bonding with metal interconnection to reduce the dependence on traditional solder bumps, thus making it possible to achieve smaller interconnection pitch, higher connection density and more compact chip stacking structure.
In May 2026, Imec, the Belgian microelectronics research center, and EV Group announced that they had achieved a 200nm copper interconnection pitch in wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding research. The research team achieved a post-bond copper pad overlay deviation of less than 40nm for all test chips on 300mm wafers.

Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany to Acquire Silence Therapeutics, Strengthening Rare Disease Pipeline with Innovative siRNA Asset 
We enter into a definitive agreement to acquire biotechnology company Silence Therapeutics, focused on siRNA-therapies in areas of high unmet need. 
Subscribe
Share 
Icons revealed to the left 
19 Oct 2026 
| 
Darmstadt, Germany 
Purchase price of $20 per ADS in cash represents an enterprise value of $1.1 billion and an equity value of approximately $1.3 billion 
Silence Therapeutics is a UK-headquartered biotechnology company with a potentially best-in-class Phase 3-ready investigational siRNA therapy for rare disease, polycythemia vera (PV) 
Planned acquisition will strengthen the position of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany in rare diseases, a high-value growth driver, and advance its Healthcare ambition to become a leading Global Specialty Innovator 
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, a leading science and technology company, today announced its entry into a definitive agreement to acquire Silence Therapeutics plc (Nasdaq: SLN), a global clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in London, UK, focused on pioneering the design and development of siRNA (short interfering RNA) therapies in areas of high unmet need.
The purchase price of $20 per ADS in cash, with each ADS representing three ordinary shares of Silence Therapeutics (or $6.6667 per ordinary share), represents an enterprise value of $1.1 billion and an equity value of approximately $1.3 billion. The consideration represents an 82% premium to Silence Therapeutics’ 30-day volume-weighted average price of $10.99, as of the close of trading on October 16, 2026, the last trading day prior to the transaction announcement. The transaction is subject to satisfaction of customary closing conditions.
“The planned acquisition of Silence Therapeutics will strengthen our capabilities to serve patients with targeted specialty and rare diseases,” said Kai Beckmann, Chairman of the Executive Board and Group CEO of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. “Following the acquisition of SpringWorks Therapeutics last year, we continue to transform our pipeline toward areas of high specialization and unmet medical need, with an ongoing commitment to external innovation. The proposed transaction follows our strategic priority to address attractive end markets also through M&A, creating value over the mid- to long-term.”
The transaction, once completed, will add Divesiran ─ a potentially best-in-class, phase 3-ready siRNA investigational therapy, in development for phlebotomy-dependent polycythemia vera (PV) ─ to Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany’s pipeline. Divesiran is dosed subcutaneously once every 3 months.
PV is a chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm ─ a type of rare blood cancer ─ characterized by the excessive production of red blood cells, which can be associated with a higher rate of death from cardiovascular and thrombotic events.
Divesiran is designed to selectively silence TMPRSS6, a gene involved in regulating hepcidin, the body’s key regulator of iron metabolism. By increasing hepcidin levels, Divesiran aims to limit iron availability for red blood cell production, helping to control hematocrit levels and potentially reducing the need for frequent therapeutic phlebotomies.
Divesiran met its primary endpoint in the Phase 2 SANRECO study with an 88% responder rate versus 19% for placebo (p “The planned acquisition of Silence Therapeutics marks a significant step forward in our strategy to become a Global Specialty Innovator in Healthcare,” said Danny Bar-Zohar, member of the Executive Board and CEO Healthcare at Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. “Silence Therapeutics’ primary siRNA pipeline asset, Divesiran, is supported by promising Phase 2 efficacy data, a potentially best-in-class, once-every-three-month dosing schedule, and a safety profile that appears manageable, with the added advantage of targeting a well-defined, homogeneous patient population. The planned acquisition also provides an entry point into hematology through a biologically validated mechanism of action. With this transaction, we are advancing our efforts to build a differentiated, sustainable pipeline as we bring more medicines to more patients, faster.”
“We are pleased to have reached this agreement with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, which follows a competitive sale process and delivers significant, immediate and certain value to our shareholders,” said Iain Ross, Interim Principal Executive Officer and Chairman of the Silence Therapeutics’ Board. “This transaction follows potentially best-in-class Phase 2 polycythemia vera data for Divesiran and reflects the important progress we have made advancing our differentiated siRNA pipeline. It also provides a new home for our innovative programs within Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, placing Divesiran with a company that has the scale, resources and commercial capabilities to accelerate its Phase 3 development and bring this potentially best-in-class siRNA therapy to patients in need. We are incredibly grateful to our employees for their dedication and contributions in building Silence Therapeutics into the company it is today.”
The transaction has been unanimously approved by Silence Therapeutics’ Board of Directors and Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany’s relevant corporate bodies and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to satisfaction of customary closing conditions, including receipt of required regulatory approvals and approval by Silence Therapeutics’ shareholders. In connection with the transaction, certain securityholders of Silence Therapeutics holding securities representing approximately 14% of Silence Therapeutics’ voting power have entered into a voting and support agreement with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, under which the securityholders have agreed among other things, to vote their voting securities of Silence Therapeutics in favor of the transaction. Silence Therapeutics is a UK company, with ADSs, each representing three of its ordinary shares, listed on NASDAQ. As is customary for similar transactions, the transaction will be effected through a UK scheme of arrangement.
The planned acquisition will be funded through proceeds from new debt.
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany is committed to leveraging advanced technologies and data science to accelerate the discovery and delivery of breakthrough medicines. This acquisition is another step forward in its broader strategy to enhance research productivity and the output of its pipeline sustainably, focusing on indications that can be derisked through proper preclinical and early clinical testing to ensure that more patients gain access to effective treatments.
Silence Therapeutics employs approximately 80 people and operates from locations in the UK, the US and Germany.
A&O Shearman is acting as legal counsel to Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany.

About Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany 
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, a leading science and technology company, operates across life science, healthcare and electronics. More than 62,000 employees work to make a positive difference to millions of people’s lives every day by creating more joyful and sustainable ways to live. From providing products and services that accelerate drug development and manufacturing as well as discovering unique ways to treat the most challenging diseases to enabling the intelligence of devices – the company is everywhere. In 2025, Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, generated sales of € 21.1 billion in 65 countries.
The company holds the global rights to the name and trademark “Merck” internationally. The only exceptions are the United States and Canada, where the business sectors of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, operate as MilliporeSigma in life science, EMD Serono in healthcare and EMD Electronics in electronics. Since its founding in 1668, scientific exploration and responsible entrepreneurship have been key to the company’s technological and scientific advances. To this day, the founding family remains the majority owner of the publicly listed company.
All Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, press releases are distributed by e-mail at the same time they become available on the EMD Group website. In case you are a resident of the USA or Canada, please go to www.emdgroup.com/subscribe to register for your online, change your selection or discontinue this service.
No Solicitation and No Offer 
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, its directors and executive officers are not soliciting proxies from the shareholders of Silence Therapeutics in connection with the transaction. Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany is making this communication for informational purposes only and does not intend to file any communication relating to the transaction on a proxy statement on Schedule 14A with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

PILLAR has delivered a powerful share price run over the past few years, and the latest jump has pushed the discussion firmly onto what investors are really paying for. With a move like that already on the board, the question now is whether PILLAR's current earnings are enough to support where the stock trades today. 
PILLAR has returned about 424.9% over the past 5 years, which puts a lot of pressure on its earnings profile to justify that kind of long haul performance. 
The business model relies heavily on how efficiently it can convert revenue into sustainable profit. This can shape what investors are willing to pay for each unit of its earnings over time.

Does PILLAR Look Pricey on Earnings? 
The P/E ratio is a useful yardstick for PILLAR because it links what you pay directly to the profits the business is already generating. Right now the stock trades on about 24.9x earnings, while the wider Chemicals group sits closer to 13.0x and direct peers cluster around 17.7x. 
That gap suggests investors are paying a premium for PILLAR compared with both its sector and similar companies. The tailored fair multiple implied by its own profile comes in lower than where the shares trade today, so on this framework the stock screens as overvalued. Was the White House chief of staff behind the ouster of the shortest-serving press secretary?
by Shin Sang-yoon 
Published : Oct. 18, 2026 - 10:59:06
View Korean Original
Link copied!
Politico reports Susie Wiles arranged the Fox News interview that accelerated Katie Zacharia's dismissal
Critics say Zacharia's selection bypassed Wiles, fueling speculation of a White House power struggle
Katie Zacharia, who stepped down as White House press secretary just five days after being appointed. [EPA] 
White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles effectively set a trap that led to the ouster of Katie Zacharia, who became the shortest-serving White House press secretary in history after resigning just five days into the job amid controversy over misrepresenting her legal credentials, according to media reports.
Wiles arranged the television interview widely seen as the decisive blow to Zacharia's tenure, the reports said. They also raised allegations that Zacharia was caught up in an internal White House power struggle.
According to Politico, the US political news outlet, Wiles was involved in arranging Zacharia's appearance on Fox News. The report, citing two White House sources, was published Saturday (local time).
Zacharia appeared on Fox News on Thursday — three days after she began her duties as the new White House press secretary. The program was hosted by Sean Hannity, a presenter with close ties to President Donald Trump. Hannity pressed her hard on two issues: her having presented herself as a lawyer despite failing the bar exam, and the widespread criticism her first press briefing had drawn.
Zacharia struggled to respond. She offered an unconvincing explanation, saying she had consulted a legal expert who told her it was acceptable to call herself a lawyer. She appeared on another Fox News program the following morning but again failed to handle the questions smoothly. She was dismissed that same afternoon — five days after her appointment.
Politico, citing two White House sources, reported that the person who arranged the Hannity interview was none other than Wiles and White House communications official Daniel Alvarez.
While the interview could have appeared to offer Zacharia a chance to put the controversy behind her — given Hannity's prominence among Trump's hardcore MAGA base — analysts say it was in effect a scheme engineered to bring about her downfall.
Zacharia's selection as White House press secretary had been Trump's own decision, made with little consultation with Wiles, sparking talk inside the White House of a "Wiles bypass." Critics say the episode was a symbolic sign of Wiles' diminishing standing at a time when Trump was already said to be considering replacing his chief of staff.
One source told Politico that Zacharia's appearance was "a deliberate hit" — that Wiles had pushed her into the Hannity interview knowing she would not survive it. White House Communications Director Steven Cheung rebuffed the account, calling it "pure speculation and an uncreative work of fiction." He added that Zacharia "took on a very important role and will continue to support the president as she transitions to a new position. She is a great colleague and a remarkable talent."
Fox News also issued a statement, saying the interview had been Hannity's own decision and that "Wiles and Alvarez had nothing to do with the booking."

Public records show that Schmalz was founded in 1910 and has long specialized in vacuum automation and ergonomic handling systems. Its product portfolio covers vacuum components, gripping systems, and automated handling solutions, with business extending across multiple global markets.
FAIRINO, meanwhile, focuses on the R&D and manufacturing of collaborative robots. Leveraging proprietary intellectual property and localized service networks, it is advancing its international layout. This signing marks an upgrade from product-level adaptation to a long-term ecosystem synergy. Jingce Electronic's Semiconductor Backlog Jumps 98% YoY; Advanced Packaging Equipment Fully Deployed
Add preferred source 
Chinese semiconductor inspection equipment maker Jingce Electronic said its semiconductor business has become the core support of its operating results, with semiconductor backlog of approximately CNY 3.609 billion (approximately $541.1 million), up 98% year-on-year, accounting for nearly 70% of total backlog. First-half 2026 revenue was CNY 1.812 billion (approximately $271.7 million), up 31.19% year-on-year, with net profit attributable to the parent of CNY 75.03 million (approximately $11.2 million), up 171.21%. The company's bright-field optical defect inspection equipment has completed 28nm production-line acceptance and 14nm production-line delivery, and it has newly won 14nm orders from a leading Chinese customer; its main products including film thickness, OCD and e-beam equipment have completed 7nm process delivery and acceptance. In advanced packaging and glass substrates, core metrology equipment has been introduced into production lines, and its TGV solution offers sub-micron to micron-level measurement capability, with multiple units delivered cumulatively. The company will continue to advance product finalization and mass-production adaptation, seizing opportunities in the localization of China's semiconductor equipment.
Key Elements 
Jingce Electronic 300567.SZ HBM TGV Advanced Packaging Semiconductor Equipment OCD Equipment E-beam Equipment Glass Substrate Panel-Level Packaging Shanghai Jingce Shanghai Jingji Microelectronics 14nm 7nm BFI Hubei Xingchen KLA Lasertec Hitachi High-Tech Tokyo Electron Advantest 
China's semiconductor inspection equipment maker Jingce Electronic (300567.SZ) said on October 16 that its semiconductor business has become the core support of its operating results. As of the disclosure date of its 2026 interim report, semiconductor backlog totaled approximately CNY 3.609 billion (approximately $541.1 million), up 98% from a year earlier and accounting for nearly 70% of the company's total backlog.
In an investor relations activity, the company disclosed that total backlog currently stands at approximately CNY 5.589 billion (approximately $837.9 million). The company said it is seizing the critical window for import substitution in semiconductor equipment, increasing R&D investment and product deployment in advanced processes, and that its main semiconductor products have all achieved large-scale mass production, with delivery capability greatly enhanced.
First-Half Results: Orders Lead, Revenue Yet to Catch Up
In the first half of 2026, Jingce Electronic posted revenue of CNY 1.812 billion (approximately $271.7 million), up 31.19% year-on-year, and net profit attributable to the parent of CNY 75.0349 million (approximately $11.2 million), up 171.21%. However, semiconductor segment revenue in the same period was CNY 644 million (approximately $96.5 million), up 14.55% year-on-year—a growth rate far below the 98% growth in backlog. The semiconductor segment's gross margin was 48.75%, roughly flat from a year earlier, but net profit attributable to the parent was CNY 49.963 million (approximately $7.5 million), down 31.40% year-on-year. The company explained that this was because it raised its stake in core semiconductor asset Shanghai Jingji Microelectronics, which remains in a period of heavy investment, dragging results down by about CNY 30 million (approximately $4.5 million).
First-half R&D investment was CNY 391 million (approximately $58.6 million), up 22.27% year-on-year and equal to 21.59% of revenue; of that, R&D investment in semiconductor metrology and inspection was CNY 227 million (approximately $34.0 million), up 36.30% year-on-year, showing the company continues to concentrate resources on front-end metrology and inspection and advanced processes.
The structure of the backlog is as follows:
Business segment Backlog (CNY 100 million) YoY change Share 
Semiconductor 36.09 +98.00% ~64.6% 
Display 12.28 -14.68% ~22.0% 
New energy 7.52 +117.22% ~13.5% 
Total 55.89 +54.89% 100% 
Shares are calculated by dividing each segment's backlog by the total, rounded to one decimal place; the total may not equal 100% due to rounding.
Comparing the semiconductor backlog of CNY 3.609 billion with semiconductor revenue of CNY 644 million, the backlog is about 5.6 times first-half revenue. On one hand, this shows high visibility for future revenue; on the other, it means whether orders convert into revenue depends on the pace of customers' production-line construction and acceptance—backlog does not equal realized revenue. Display backlog in the same period was CNY 1.228 billion (approximately $184.1 million), down 14.68% year-on-year, as the traditional display business continued to contract; new energy backlog was CNY 752 million (approximately $112.7 million), up 117.22% year-on-year, but from a still-small base. Semiconductors have become the main engine driving the company's growth.
The company also announced a preliminary major asset restructuring plan on July 16, 2026 to acquire the remaining 41.17% stake in its controlled subsidiary Shanghai Jingce Semiconductor Technology Co., Ltd. by issuing shares, convertible bonds and paying cash; upon completion, Shanghai Jingce will become a wholly owned subsidiary. As of mid-October, the audit, valuation and legal due diligence had not been completed.
Advanced Processes: 14nm Bright-Field Inspection Orders Land
On advanced processes, Jingce Electronic's bright-field optical defect inspection (BFI) equipment has completed 28nm process production-line acceptance and 14nm process production-line delivery; in the first half of 2026 it newly won 14nm process orders from a leading Chinese customer and completed delivery before the report disclosure date. The company said this marks a further breakthrough in the application of this product category in the advanced-process market.
The company noted that its main products—the film thickness series, OCD equipment and e-beam equipment—have completed delivery and acceptance for the 7nm advanced process, with products for more advanced processes under development; its unpatterned dark-field defect inspection equipment (Vega series) for the 28nm process has completed R&D, with the next-generation product still in development. More than 90% of the semiconductor business's orders and revenue come from front-end metrology and inspection, while back-end inspection remains in the market-introduction stage.
Advanced Packaging Metrology and Inspection Deployment
In advanced packaging metrology and inspection, Jingce Electronic's core products—including the film thickness series, OCD equipment, e-beam equipment and bright-field optical defect inspection equipment—have all been introduced into advanced packaging production lines. The company's advanced packaging business mainly advances in step with customers' development cadence.
At present, the company's equipment for 2.5D and 3D advanced packaging covers high-aspect-ratio structure measurement after TSV etching, HBM wafer topography measurement, hybrid bonding surface roughness measurement, and integrated copper dishing measurement after TSV copper-fill CMP, among others; multiple tools have completed customer delivery and entered practical application. The chart below summarizes the measurement items corresponding to these process steps:
The company's interim report also noted that its wafer appearance inspection equipment has been used for inspection of patterned silicon wafers and unpatterned glass wafers in CMOS image sensor, AR/VR, Logic, MEMS, Memory, RF and Power processes, as well as advanced packaging processes such as FOWLP, WLCSP, Bumping and Chiplet, and has completed small-batch shipments. The company is also positioning itself in high-density advanced packaging through Hubei Xingchen, in which it invested in March 2024; Hubei Xingchen has built a 12-inch advanced packaging R&D line, with a mass-production line under construction.
However, advanced packaging is not yet the mainstay of Jingce Electronic's semiconductor business. The company's interim report shows that front-end metrology and inspection account for more than 90% of semiconductor orders and revenue, while back-end inspection and advanced packaging remain in a deepening market-introduction stage with relatively low shares. In other words, this wave of order growth comes mainly from front-end metrology and inspection; advanced packaging and glass substrates are future options, not today's revenue mainstay.
Glass Substrate Deployment Continues
In glass substrates and panel-level advanced packaging, the company has established a dedicated product lineup, with multiple units of related equipment delivered cumulatively. Its TGV (through-glass via) solutions cover key measurement and inspection items including hole diameter, position, top and bottom surface hole diameter, waist hole, roundness, taper and in-hole structure; they now offer sub-micron to micron-level measurement capability and have completed sample prototyping and inspection validation with multiple customers.
The company said it is continuing to optimize equipment and finalize products in line with different customers' materials, hole types and process requirements. It will subsequently advance process validation, product finalization and mass-production adaptation of TGV-related equipment in line with downstream customers' process maturity and production-line construction pace, focusing on enhancing capabilities in large-size panels, high-precision measurement, multi-layer structure inspection and mass-production efficiency.
Glass substrates are seen as a candidate material for next-generation advanced packaging substrates. TechInsights' 2026 advanced packaging outlook notes that glass substrates and panel-level packaging are accelerating, with 2026 a critical year for defining related processes; however, Yole Group estimates that glass core substrate revenue will reach about $275 million by 2030 (best case), and the market is still at a commercial starting point. This means the long-term direction for glass substrates is clear, but the near-term market size remains small, and their revenue contribution to Jingce Electronic will take time.
The difficulty of TGV measurement lies in the fact that a single panel contains millions of through-glass vias, and any hole-diameter deviation, positional shift or micro-crack can affect subsequent metal filling and reliability. Measurement systems must measure top, waist and bottom hole diameters hole by hole, and monitor position, roundness, taper and panel thickness uniformity; glass is brittle and prone to cracking, and cracks during processing that are not detected early can grow into fatal defects downstream.
Metrology and Inspection: A Key Segment Where China's Market Share Remains Low
Semiconductor metrology and inspection equipment is central to yield control in advanced processes. According to CSET statistics, the global process control equipment market was about $15.7 billion in 2025, with KLA at 56.8%, Applied Materials at 11.2%, Lasertec at 6.4% and Hitachi High-Tech at 6.2%; Chinese domestic vendors combined accounted for only 0.7%. In other words, this segment—dominated by American, Japanese and European vendors—is one of the areas with the greatest room for import substitution in China's semiconductor equipment.
China accounts for about one-third of global demand for metrology and inspection equipment. Citing QYResearch data in its interim report, Jingce Electronic noted that the global semiconductor metrology and inspection equipment market was about $17.232 billion in 2025, with the Chinese market at about $5.581 billion, or 32.39%, expected to rise to $10.366 billion by 2032, or 34.84% of the global total.
On policy, Reuters reported in December 2025 that China requires wafer fabs to use at least 50% domestic equipment when adding new capacity (according to sources); Japan, meanwhile, has since July 2023 placed 23 categories of advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment under export controls, including inspection equipment. This policy tug-of-war is precisely the backdrop for the rapid growth of Chinese metrology and inspection equipment orders.
Japanese Equipment Makers' China Revenue Is Shrinking
This wave of localization has already had a clear impact on Japanese equipment makers. Nikkei Asia reported in June 2026 that Japan's top five equipment makers—Tokyo Electron, Advantest, SCREEN, Disco and Kokusai Electric—posted combined China revenue of ¥1.47 trillion (approximately $9.4 billion) in fiscal 2025 (ended March 2026), down 12% year-on-year, the first annual decline. Front-end processes were hit hardest, with combined China revenue at Tokyo Electron, SCREEN and Kokusai Electric falling nearly 20%; back-end packaging and test equipment held up relatively well, with Advantest up about 20% and Disco up nearly 10%.
Tokyo Electron's China revenue share fell from 50% in April-June 2024 to 27% in January-March 2026; ASML's China revenue share also fell to 19% in the first quarter of 2026, down 8 percentage points from a year earlier.
For the Japanese market, the significance of this news goes beyond one Chinese company's orders. Japanese vendors still hold important positions in metrology and inspection: Lasertec has strengths in photomask inspection and Hitachi High-Tech in CD-SEM (critical-dimension scanning electron microscopy), and together the two account for about 12.6% of the global process control market. But Chinese domestic vendors currently account for only 0.7% combined; if localization policy continues to advance, this market—dominated by KLA, Applied Materials and Japanese and European vendors—will be one of the areas with the greatest room for import substitution in China.
Localization Opportunities
Jingce Electronic said it will actively seize opportunities in the localization of glass substrates and panel-level advanced packaging. As AI chips' demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) continues to expand and penetration of 2.5D and 3D advanced packaging rises, demand for related metrology and inspection equipment is warming in tandem.
The rapid growth of the company's semiconductor backlog reflects downstream customers' capex momentum in advanced packaging and advanced processes. At CNY 3.609 billion, semiconductor backlog is already close to 70% of the company's total backlog, showing that its business focus has clearly tilted toward semiconductors.
Overall, Jingce Electronic's order growth has two supports: first, a rising share of local equipment procurement by Chinese wafer fabs in mature and advanced processes; second, metrology and inspection demand driven by advanced packaging and HBM. Key things to watch going forward include the speed at which the backlog converts into revenue, when the drag from Shanghai Jingji Microelectronics' investment will narrow, and the actual timing of volume ramp-up in new businesses such as glass substrates.

Besi was down 2.66% at €159.05, while ASML Holding rose 1.11% to €1,480.40, as of 08:02 ET (12:02 GMT). 
The report said ASML filed 27 bonding patent families between December 2022 and November 2024, most for die-to-wafer bonding, and the true count is likely higher because later filings are not yet public. 
Besi has led die-to-wafer bonding and is the only supplier with tools in volume production, SemiAnalysis said. Everyone else is still trying to get a first tool qualified.

Logic accounts for most of Besi's hybrid bonding business, concentrated at TSMC and Intel, both of which ASML has worked with for more than two decades. 
Besi's HBM prospects are also weakening, SemiAnalysis said, as Korean challengers catch up and HBM adoption of die-to-wafer bonding is expected to slip to 2029 or beyond. 
ASML's design differs from conventional machines, where a bond head picks each die off a diced wafer and places it. 
Instead, each die moves on its own holder around a track past inspection, cleaning, plasma activation and measurement stations before reaching a bonding station, where a chuck lifts the bottom wafer to meet it. 
SemiAnalysis said ASML could gain an edge in alignment accuracy and particle control, the two factors that set bonding yield, but still needs to solve challenges around feed-forward metrology, die-to-wafer contact, modifying non-bonding tools and keeping the loop clean. It expects ASML to price its tools at a premium to peers. 
The Elec reported in March that ASML had started architecture design of a hybrid bonder with Prodrive Technologies and VDL ETG. 
Die-to-wafer hybrid bonding has moved slowly because the industry lacks mature tools combining alignment accuracy and throughput, SemiAnalysis said, keeping cost per die high. It runs in volume only in logic, where AMD has shipped hybrid-bonded V-Cache since 2022.

Bioprocess Technology Market to Reach USD 134.06 Billion by 2035 – Credence Research
by Cision 
October 16, 2026 
Reading Time: 8 mins read 
in DACH , GREEN , PRIVATE EQUITY , UK&IRELAND 
Share on Facebook Share on Twitter 
LONDON, Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — The “ Bioprocess Technology Market – Growth, Share, Opportunities & Competitive Analysis, 2025–2035 ” report has been added to the Credence Research Inc. market intelligence offering.
The global bioprocess technology market was valued at USD 55.63 billion in 2025 and is estimated at USD 60.75 billion in 2026. Revenue is projected to reach USD 134.06 billion by 2035, representing a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 9.19% over the 2025–2035 market-value interval. North America held the largest regional share at 40.0% in 2025, while Asia Pacific is expected to record the fastest growth at 10.38% annually. These revenue forecasts and market shares are Credence Research estimates.
Key Takeaways 
The market increases from USD 55.63 billion in 2025 to USD 134.06 billion in 2035 at a stated 9.19% CAGR.
North America contributed 40.0% of global 2025 value; Asia Pacific has the highest modeled regional growth rate at 10.38%.
Consumables and accessories represented 62.0% of product revenue in 2025.
Downstream processing represented 54.0% of process revenue in 2025.
Fed-batch technology represented 58.0% of technology revenue in 2025.
Scope & Segmentation – Bioprocess Technology Market 
Production equipment, consumables and process technology used to culture cells and purify biologic drug substances, including bioreactors, media, filters, chromatography systems, resins, membranes and analytical instruments. Finished biologic sales, fill-finish equipment and contract manufacturing service revenue are excluded to avoid conflating tools with their end products.
By product: Instruments; Consumables and accessories.
By process type: Upstream processing; Downstream processing.
By technology: Batch; Fed-batch; Continuous processing.
By application: Monoclonal antibodies; Recombinant proteins; Cell and gene therapy products; Antibiotics; Others.
By geography: North America; Europe; Asia Pacific; Latin America; Middle East and Africa.
Download sample and detailed segmentation – https://www.credenceresearch.com/report/bioprocess-technology-market 
Why This Report Matters 
Maps the commercial drivers of this market without treating forecasts as verified transaction totals.
Separates leading applications and products from the regional opportunities and access constraints that affect revenue.
Assesses supplier competition, recent regulatory or product developments and likely implications for business planning.
Market Overview 
Bioprocess equipment and consumables are critical inputs for making antibodies, vaccines, recombinant proteins and advanced therapies. Unlike the revenue of finished biological medicines, this market measures instruments and materials purchased to manufacture them.
Plant builders invest in bioreactors and purification systems when new capacity comes online, while validated commercial facilities buy media, bags, membranes, resins and reagents repeatedly. Product mix is therefore unusually sensitive to capacity utilization and whether a manufacturer operates stainless steel or single-use systems.
Market Insights 
Consumables and accessories represent 62.0% of product value, creating recurring revenue after instruments have been installed.
Downstream processing accounts for 54.0% of process revenue because purification and filtration have high cost per batch.
Fed-batch remains dominant with 58.0% of technology value; continuous processing is the fastest-growing technology category at a modeled 12.56% CAGR.

Market Drivers 
Growing commercial biologic capacity 
Biopharmaceutical companies and contract development and manufacturing organizations are expanding capacity for antibody and cell therapy pipelines. The commissioning of additional sites requires upfront investment in bioreactors, filtration and process monitoring, while each subsequent batch consumes materials that deliver recurring revenue for suppliers.
Shift toward intensification and single-use workflows 
Single-use bioreactors shorten turnaround between products and reduce cleaning validation requirements. Intensified perfusion and connected purification can raise output per unit of capacity, but changes to commercial processes require regulatory comparability evidence. Manufacturers often adopt these tools most readily in new plants rather than retrofit fully validated facilities.
Market Trends and Opportunities 
Suppliers increasingly offer complete upstream and downstream product ranges. In September 2025, Thermo Fisher completed its approximately USD 4 billion acquisition of Solventum’s filtration and purification business, adding membranes and related technologies.
Process analytical technology, including inline sensors and automated control, may reduce deviation risk and support more efficient batch release. Regulatory incentives can help, although equipment qualification and implementation remain facility-specific.
Regional Analysis 
Credence Research estimates the following 2025 revenue shares. All five regional figures are proprietary research-model allocations rather than independently audited sales totals.
North America | 40.0% share in 2025 
Established biologics capacity and broad pipelines support recurring demand for resins, media and filters. U.S. manufacturers are also evaluating advanced manufacturing designation and process intensification.
Europe | 29.0% share in 2025 
Biologics manufacturing hubs in Switzerland, Germany, Ireland and Denmark support equipment replacement and specialized upstream and downstream consumables.
Asia Pacific | 23.0% share in 2025 
New CDMO plants and biosimilar capacity in South Korea, China, India and Singapore are driving 10.38% annual modeled growth.
Latin America | 4.5% share in 2025 
Vaccine, insulin and biosimilar localization programs expand demand for fermentation, filtration and purification tools, especially in Brazil and Mexico.
Middle East and Africa | 3.5% share in 2025 
Local biomanufacturing initiatives create opportunities for modular systems, while workforce and validation constraints limit implementation scale.
Market Challenges 
A change in resins, membrane materials or equipment may require new process validation and regulatory submissions. For established products, switching can be uneconomical despite the potential for productivity gains.
Capital-intensive instrument orders can fluctuate with biotechnology funding and construction schedules. Specialized operators and quality staff remain scarce, while single-use plastic waste and supply dependence create operational constraints.
Future Outlook 
Bioprocess spending is expected to grow fastest where new CDMO capacity meets expanding portfolios of complex biologics. Consumables should preserve repeat sales even if capital project timing varies.
The strongest technology providers will combine dependable supply, process documentation, training, high-value purification tools and automation support.
Competitive Landscape 
Competition among full-line suppliers centers on the breadth of validated components and integrated production workflows. Thermo Fisher, Danaher, Sartorius and Merck KGaA supply combinations of cell culture, filtration and purification products.
Eppendorf, Bio-Rad, Agilent and specialized equipment firms compete in process development, analytics and particular hardware categories. Lonza and Roche are major manufacturing operators and equipment customers, rather than primarily direct competitors as process-tool vendors.

Dec. 31, 2024: The FDA finalized its Advanced Manufacturing Technologies Designation Program guidance, which describes an early-engagement pathway for qualifying technologies. 
Sept. 2, 2025: Thermo Fisher completed its acquisition of Solventum’s purification and filtration business for approximately USD 4.0 billion in cash.

content_text:
DGR Job Fair in Nagpur Offers Over 1,300 Employment Opportunities for Ex-Servicemen
Posted On:
16 OCT 2026 6:26PM by PIB Mumbai
Nagpur, 16 October 2026 
 
The Directorate General Resettlement (DGR), under the Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare (DESW), Ministry of Defence, organised an Ex-Servicemen (ESM) Job Fair at Nagpur on 16 October 2026, reaffirming its commitment to enabling meaningful second careers for veterans and strengthening the industry–veteran employment ecosystem. 
The Job Fair witnessed enthusiastic participation from over 480 Ex-Servicemen and 42 leading national and multinational companies, offering more than 1,300 employment opportunities across diverse sectors. The event provided a focused platform for connecting the skills, experience and leadership of trained Armed Forces personnel with the evolving talent requirements of industry. 
The event was inaugurated by Maj Gen Varun Malhotra, General Officer Commanding, UMANG Sub Area, who attended as the Military Chief Guest. Shri Amitabh Sinha, Chairman, CII Vidarbha Zonal Council, graced the occasion as the Corporate Guest of Honour. Maj Gen SBK Singh, SM, Director General Resettlement, and Brig Ranjan Keron, ADG, DRZ South, were also present. 
Senior military officers and corporate representatives interacted with participating veterans, discussing employment prospects, industry expectations and the competencies required in the civilian workforce. The interactions underscored the significant value that Ex-Servicemen bring to organisations through their leadership, discipline, integrity, technical proficiency, problem  solving abilities and experience in managing people and resources under demanding conditions. 
Prominent recruiters included Solar Group, Delhivery, Eros Group, Haldiram, JSR Dynamics and SBI Life, among other reputed organisations. Their participation reflected the growing scope for employing veterans across sectors and the importance of sustained industry engagement in expanding resettlement opportunities. 
The Job Fair went beyond employment facilitation to strengthen the connection between military experience and corporate requirements. It enabled employers to engage directly with a disciplined, skilled and experienced talent pool, while providing veterans with opportunities to explore new professional pathways and apply their capabilities in the civilian domain. 
DGR continues to advance the resettlement of retiring and retired Armed Forces personnel through employment facilitation, skill development, entrepreneurship promotion and partnerships with industry. These initiatives aim to ensure that the transition from military to civilian life is supported by dignified employment, sustainable livelihoods and opportunities for continued contribution to nation-building. 
DGR calls upon corporate organisations, industry associations and employers across sectors to deepen their engagement with Ex-Servicemen and recognise the immense potential of this proven talent pool. Stronger partnerships between government, industry and the Armed Forces can translate military experience into productive civilian employment thus benefiting veterans, their families, employers and the nation.

CC Securities Announcement: Chemours Investors with Losses have Rights in Pending Securities Fraud Class Action – BFA Law Reminds Shareholders of Upcoming Deadline
Chemours has been sued for securities fraud after its stock plummeted 18.63% because Chemours allegedly misrepresented the strength of demand for its Opteon products.
October 16, 2026 06:18 ET 
  | Source:
Bleichmar Fonti & Auld 
Bleichmar Fonti & Auld 
NEW YORK, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Leading securities law firm Bleichmar Fonti & Auld LLP announces that a class action lawsuit has been filed against The Chemours Company (NYSE:CC) and certain of the company’s senior executives for securities fraud after a significant stock drop resulting from potential violations of the federal securities laws.
If you invested in Chemours, you are encouraged to obtain additional information by visiting: https://www.bfalaw.com/cases/chemours-class-action-lawsuit .
Key Details of the Chemours ($CC) Class Action: 
Lead Plaintiff Deadline: December 7, 2026
Alleged Misconduct: Securities fraud alleging Chemours misrepresented the strength of demand for its Opteon products
Stock Drop: August 5, 2026 – 18.63% Stock Drop
Court: U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware
Action: Contact BFA Law to discuss your rights
Investors have until December 7, 2026 to ask the Court to be appointed to lead the case. The complaint asserts securities fraud claims under Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 on behalf of investors in Chemours securities. The class action is pending in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware. It is captioned Darcy v. The Chemours Company , No. 26-cv-1299.
Why is Chemours Being Sued for Securities Fraud? 
Chemours offers a range of industrial and specialty chemical products, including Opteon, a set of refrigeration chemicals with a reduced ozone-depletion footprint. In late 2020, Congress enacted the U.S. AIM Act, which directed the EPA to oversee the transition to alternative refrigerants that present a lesser impact to the ozone layer.
According to the complaint, Chemours stated that continued adoption of the AIM Act drove sustained growth for its Opteon products. Chemours stated that the “sustained double-digit” Opteon expansion would be “driven by the continued regulatory adoption” of the AIM Act. What’s more, Chemours provided 2026 net sales guidance of 3% to 5% growth and 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $800M – $900M, driven by “higher . . . demand” in its Opteon segment.
As alleged, Chemours failed to disclose that customers were already oversupplied with Opteon products because of the AIM Act transition, leading to an “oversupplied channel heading into 2026.”
Why did Chemours’s Stock Drop? 
On August 4, 2026, Chemours announced Q2 2026 financial results, revealing an approximately 1% year-over-year decrease in net sales and cutting 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance by about 11% (to $775M – $825M from $800M – $900M). Chemours also revealed that customers had “built additional inventory” of Opteon products the prior year, that aftermarket channels had been filled, and that Chemours was selling into an “oversupplied channel heading into 2026.”
On this news, Chemours’s stock dropped $3.34 per share, or 18.63%, from a closing price of $17.93 per share on August 4, 2026, to $14.59 per share on August 5, 2026.
