title: ASML Is Building a Hybrid Bonding Tool, Sending More Chills to Besi - SemiAnalysis
query: ("Besi" OR "BE Semiconductor Industries") (Korea OR Korean) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
ASML Is Building a Hybrid Bonding Tool!
Sherry Zhang , Gerald Wong , Steven Lee , and Dylan Patel 
Oct 15, 2026 
∙ Paid
138
17
Share
ASML has not announced anything yet, but its patent filings, a news report and its own roadmap all suggest so. We believe it will start with a die-to-wafer (D2W) hybrid bonding (HB) tool. This is harder to build than wafer-to-wafer but is where ASML could gain an edge. We see the move as a natural extension of ASML’s vertical integration, and one that should strengthen its customer ties. 
In this article we unpack the tool’s design end to end, starting with patent filings. What makes it unique is that it runs on a track . That changes how the tool and the dies move: each die rides its own holder past the process stations, and the tools get closer at each station to process the dies. The track’s independent shuttles also lift station utilization, save on duplicate tooling, and enable heterogeneous integration. 
We believe ASML could gain an edge in alignment accuracy and particle control for Hybrid Bonding. These are the two factors that set bonding yield. And ASML has expertise in solving the same problems in lithography. 
Despite the advantages, ASML still needs to solve challenges around feed-forward metrology, the die-to-wafer contact, the modification of the non-bonding tools so they can process dies on the track, and keeping the whole loop clean. 
We expect advanced logic, where D2W already runs in volume, to adopt ASML’s D2W HB tool first. This is bad news for Besi . Logic accounts for most of Besi’s HB business today concentrated at TSMC and Intel. ASML has been working with both for more than two decades and just announced a joint photomask initiative in September. We won’t be surprised to see a similar move in the back end process. Besi’s HBM prospects are also weakening. Korean challengers are catching up, in addition to an HBM adoption that we expect to slip to 2029 or beyond. 
ASML is Building a Hybrid Bonder 
We did a deep dive on hybrid bonding in 2024, and we still see it as the most transformative innovation in semiconductor manufacturing since EUV. Wafer-to-wafer (W2W) hybrid bonding (HB) is already in volume in image sensors and 3D NAND, and DRAM makers will be next. Die-to-wafer (D2W) HB is moving slower , because the industry still lacks mature tools that combine satisfying alignment accuracy and throughput (our check indicates upper bound in current applications is only one wafer per hour), which keeps cost per die high. Today D2W runs in volume only in logic: AMD has shipped hybrid-bonded V-Cache since 2022, and TSMC’s SoIC bonds at about 6um pitch today and targets 4.5um around 2029. The market expected HBM to become the big D2W volume driver from 2028. However, our view is different: we believe HBM will not adopt D2W HB before 2029 , if at all. 
Besi has led D2W and is the only supplier with tools in volume production. Everyone else is still trying to get a first tool qualified. But we believe the situation will soon change, because ASML is building a D2W hybrid bonding tool. Management hasn’t announced anything yet. But the company filed 27 bonding patent families between December 2022 and November 2024, most of them D2W, and the true count is likely higher because filings made after November 2024 are not yet public. The Elec also reported in March that ASML had started the architecture design of a hybrid bonder with Prodrive Technologies and VDL ETG. 
In the anchor filing ( WO2025201788A1 ), ASML drew how its bonding flow works. Interestingly, the system looks nothing like a traditional D2W bonder (see Advanced Packaging Part 5 for how those work). Instead of a bond head picking each die off a diced wafer and placing it, ASML moves single dies on independent holders around a track (Fig 1). Each die passes inspection, cleaning, plasma activation and metrology (topography, leveling and alignment) stations before it reaches the bonding station where the chuck lifts the bottom wafer up to meet the die. We unpack the design in the sections below. 
Fig 1: ASML’s track-based D2W bonder, SA annotated and simplified 
Source: ASML; SemiAnalysis Wafer Fabrication Equipment Model 
ASML could be building a W2W hybrid bonding tool as well. According to a patent analysis by Inha University , ASML is likely building W2W HB equipment on its TWINSCAN platform, leaning on its wafer overlay accuracy. We focus on the D2W machine in this note, because it is the harder tool to build and the one where ASML could gain a real edge. 
…as Part of its Vertical Integration Initiative 
We believe this is a continuation of ASML’s effort to integrate vertically and tighten customer relationships. ASML bought Cymer for its light source in 2013, HMI for e-beam inspection in 2016 and Berliner Glas for optics modules in 2020. It shipped its first back-end product, the XT:260 i-line packaging scanner, in 3Q25. And most recently, ASML announced joint initiatives with TSMC , Intel Foundry and Samsung to move the industry from 6-inch to 12-inch photomasks for High NA EUV. 
Building a bonder would be a natural next step. In fact, ASML’s own roadmap already puts bonding inside the front-end flow. Its 2024 Investor Day listed W2W and D2W hybrid bonding for NAND, DRAM and logic (Fig 2). And a July 2024 filing shows how the bonder and the scanner would work together by sharing die position data. Today a scanner printing on a bonded wafer must pre-align and coarse-align every die before it can expose. In ASML’s design the bonder already knows where it put each die and hands that map (a “coordinate system” in the filing) to the scanner, which checks a few marks and exposes. Customers get faster lithography on bonded wafers, and ASML gets to sell the bonder and the scanner as a pair. 
Fig 2: ASML’s map of front-end 3D integration 
Source: ASML Investor Day, 14-Nov-2024 
We expect advanced logic to be the first adopter. Logic is where D2W HB already runs in volume, and where the alignment requirement keeps tightening. TSMC calls overlay “always the biggest challenge” for SoIC. As its HB pitch moves from 6um to 4.5um by 2029, the placement accuracy requirement will tighten further. ASML is strong in alignment, as we will elaborate below, so an edge here should help it win logic customers first. Advanced logic dies are also among the most expensive chips, so logic customers can afford a premium tool. We expect ASML to price its tools at a premium to peers. 
In the next three sections, we discuss (1) the tool’s track system - the most unusual thing about it compared with what is on the market; (2) how ASML’s strengths in alignment, particle control and motion could make its HB tool superior; and (3) the challenges ASML or its supply chain partners still need to resolve to build a working tool. Let’s dive in.
What’s Unique About the Tool 
One of the most interesting things about the tool is that it runs on a track . ASML names SuperTrak CONVEYANCE (Fig 3) as an example in its patent filing , so we assume it uses that track and we base our analysis on the track’s published design. 
The fundamental difference from a traditional bonder is where the die lives. In a Besi-type tool, the die is prepared elsewhere, and a bond head picks it up only for the final placement. In ASML’s design, each die sits on its own holder from the moment it leaves the carrier and stays there until the bonding step . The process stations are built around the track: the die stops in front of a station, the station cleans, activates or measures it in place, and the die moves on. 
Fig 3: SuperTrak CONVEYANCE track (HORIZON10 platform) 
Source: Company website 
Now let’s go through the process step by step . For illustration, we took the patent drawing and labelled every station in Fig 4. A gripper takes the die off its carrier and sets it on an empty substrate holder (206), which carries it along the track (202). The die stops in turn at the inspection, cleaning, plasma activation, topographic inspection, leveling, coarse alignment, position adjustment and fine alignment stations (210 to 226). At each stop the die stays on its holder, and the station does its work. Note the reversal here: in the patent it is the station’s sensor or head that moves in to reach the die, not the die that is carried into the tool as in today’s flow. After these steps the die arrives at the bonding station (228). 
This bonding station deserves a closer look . The first thing to note is that the final placement is done by the holder (206) and the chuck (234), not the track: SuperTrak’s spec sheet puts the shuttles’ repeatability at about 10um, nowhere near the 50nm placement accuracy the bond needs. Next, zoom in on the right-hand part of Fig 4 for the bonding work. The chuck lifts the bottom wafer to within tens of microns of the die, the holder’s actuators adjust the die’s position, the die is pressed onto the wafer to form the bond, and the holder releases it. The empty holder then starts another loop. 
Fig 4: Patent WO2025201788A1 Fig. 2 (left) and Fig. 6 side view (right), SA annotated 
Source: ASML; SemiAnalysis Wafer Fabrication Equipment Model 
This design has three major benefits:
First, independent shuttles lift the utilization of every station . The number of stations per step can be set from that step’s cycle time: a three-second cleaning step gets three stations, and a 1.2-second bond step gets one, so every station stays busy. The patent asks for exactly this, to “occupy all process stations simultaneously”. 
Second, capacity is added by adding a station rather than a second tool, as long as the equipment chamber has room for it. That saves duplicate tooling and budget . 
Last but not least, the design suits heterogeneous integration : a new die type is a new software recipe, so mixed chiplets could share one line. 
That said, the track brings its own challenges around the non-bonding stations and the cleanliness of the whole loop. We come back to them later.
How ASML May Gain an Edge 
Before that, let’s look at how ASML could bring its existing strengths to the HB tool.
First, a reminder of why alignment accuracy and cleanliness matter so much in hybrid bonding. As we elaborated before , a single 1um particle between two full-thickness wafers can unbond an area around 10mm across , resulting in a defective bond (Fig 5). So particle control is extremely important for HB. Alignment matters for two reasons: placement accuracy sets bond yield directly, and alignment time weighs far more on D2W throughput than on W2W because it compounds with the die count. These two hurdles are what make hybrid bonding almost a front-end process. 
Fig 5: A small particle opens a void and an open contact in hybrid bonding 
Source: SemiAnalysis 
We believe ASML can tackle both with decades of experience solving the same two problems in lithography.
For alignment, we believe ASML can reuse its wafer-alignment sensor technology. Based on its patent filings , the bonding system puts a tiny diffraction grating on each die and reads the die’s position from the light the grating scatters. The principle is the same as ORION , the wafer-alignment sensor on every new TWINSCAN since 2017. ORION was built to read marks that CMP and etch have tilted or deformed (Fig 6), and a mark on a bonding die goes through the same CMP and plasma activation as the copper pads next to it, so it carries the same asymmetry. We believe the same sensor family can serve the D2W bonder. 
Fig 6: A symmetric and a tilted alignment mark. Process steps shift the apparent center; ORION’s multi-color readout was built to see through that 
Source: ASML, Aligning lithography to the nanometer, Dec-2021 
Its sensing and motion capabilities also provide it with more room in total alignment error budget. Its NXT:2100i holds 0.9nm overlay on a single machine. And ASML can already measure the distortion of a W2W bonded wafer and correct the next lithography layer for it, bringing post-bond overlay from 40-60nm down to below 4nm (Fig 7). These are litho numbers, not bond results. But they mean ASML’s sensor and stage errors sit more than an order of magnitude below the 50nm a bonder needs. Higher stage precision leaves more room in a bonder’s error budget for the other factors: die shift on the holder, thermal drift and movement during contact. 
Fig 7: ASML metrology plus scanner correction brings post-bond overlay to 2.5-3.9nm 
Source: ASML Investor Day, 14-Nov-2024 
Prodrive Technologies and VDL ETG are the likely component suppliers to help ASML’s bonder move fast on motion. Prodrive makes the linear motors and drives for ASML’s EUV maglev stages and has also built Hanwha Semitech’s SHB2 Nano bonder. VDL ETG builds ASML’s frames and modules (Fig 8). 
Fig 8: Prodrive’s linear motor (left) and VDL ETG’s wafer handler module (right) 
Source: Company websites 
On cleanliness, the requirements for ASML’s EUV systems are more strict as a bonder’s. Few tool makers have fought particles at the nanometer scale for as long as ASML. EUV scanners move reticles and wafers in vacuum and keep reticle particle adders at a level “ compatible with HVM requirements for sub-10nm node lithography ”. We believe ASML has thought about the bonding surfaces too: its bonding apparatus filing adds a tool that cleans the substrate supports and a sensor that watches their flatness, particle load and distortion. 
That said, contaminants in a bonder differ from those in a scanner. Most are dicing debris on die edges and particles landing on freshly activated, hydrophilic surfaces. We look for more detail on how ASML handles these bonder-specific contaminants in future filings.
After the paywall we discuss the challenges ASML needs to tackle to build a working tool, and how its tool will impact on Besi’s business prospects.
Open Questions ASML Needs to Solve

Cell therapy weekly: stem cell therapy for osteoarthritis
15 Oct 2026 
Written by Megan Giboney

News

The week in cell therapy 
This week: a new manufacturing facility for Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) grade small molecules opened in Bristol, UK, a collaboration leveraging cGMP Next-Generation Sequencing-based viral safety testing to advance a stem cell therapy for osteoarthritis was announced, and a pre-clinical CAR-T portfolio was sold for €8 million.
The news highlights:
New UK facility boosts GMP small molecule manufacturing for cell therapies 
Collaboration to advance stem cell therapy for osteoarthritis 
Early-stage CAR-T portfolio sold for €8 million 
New UK facility boosts GMP small molecule manufacturing for cell therapies
Bio-Techne Corporation (MN, USA) has announced the opening of its new purpose-built 10,000-square-foot GMP manufacturing facility in Bristol, UK, strengthening the company’s global GMP manufacturing infrastructure.
The facility has five ISO-8 multifunctional cleanrooms and two ISO-7 cleanrooms dedicated to small molecule manufacturing and product handling.
“As the cell therapy field continues to mature, success increasingly depends on the ability to manufacture therapies consistently and at scale,” said Kim Kelderman, President and Chief Executive Officer of Bio-Techne. “Our investment in Bristol demonstrates Bio-Techne’s commitment to providing customers with the GMP materials, manufacturing expertise, and supply chain reliability needed to accelerate development and ultimately bring transformative therapies to patients worldwide.”
Read more 
Collaboration to advance stem cell therapy for osteoarthritis
Charles River Laboratories (MA, USA) and Magellan Stem Cells (Victoria, Australia) have announced a partnership to advance the development and commercialization of Magellan’s lead proprietary allogeneic, off-the-shelf stem cell therapy candidate (Zelestrocel) for osteoarthritis.
Magellan has recently completed Phase I/II trials for Zelestrocel and is now moving toward a Phase III study. The company has also built manufacturing capacity directly into its development process, having obtained GMP certification from Australia’s Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) for its production site in Melbourne.
Under the agreement, Charles River will provide cGMP Next-Generation Sequencing-based viral safety testing for Zelestrocel to support regulatory readiness.
“As we prepare for the next stage of Zelestrocel’s development, having access to advanced testing technologies and collaborating with experienced partners is critical to our success,” said Magellan Stem Cells CEO Julien Freitag.
Read more 
Early-stage CAR-T portfolio sold for €8 million
Lakefront Biotherapeutics (formerly Galapagos NV; Mechelen, Belgium) has announced the completed sale of its early-stage cell therapy portfolio to Armed Cell Therapeutics (Brussels, Belgium). Under the deal terms, Lakefront will receive €8 million upfront, with the possibility of earning up to $230 million in future milestone payments plus a modest royalty on sales.
The divested assets include a range of multi-targeting and armed CAR-T constructs engineered to enhance the potency and persistence of CAR-T therapies while addressing treatment resistance in hematological cancers and solid tumors.
“I’m pleased we were able to complete this sale of the early-stage cell therapy programs as it provides a path to continue to advance these assets on behalf of patients. Additionally, it offers Lakefront shareholders the opportunity to benefit from their potential future progress by the experienced team at Armed Cell Therapeutics,” said Sooin Kwon, Chief Business Officer of Lakefront. “Lakefront continues to be in an enviable position with a rich legacy of innovation, an exciting newly established pipeline of T-cell engagers and a strong cash balance.”

LEHIGH VALLEY, Pa. , Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Air Products (NYSE: APD ) will feature gas supply solutions and technologies designed to improve productivity, optimize costs, and support future growth for laser cutting, 3D printing, and welding applications at FABTECH 2026 from October 21-23 at the Las Vegas Convention Center in Nevada.
Application specialists will be on hand at booth #C4249 throughout the conference to speak with attendees about solutions to the challenges they face in their day-to-day operations and how Air Products can provide industry leading support and expertise in addition to supplying industrial gases.
Whether a customer process utilizes nitrogen, oxygen, argon, helium, hydrogen or carbon dioxide, Air Products' experts can provide insight on selecting the right supply solution for a specific process or operation, from cylinders and microbulk systems, to bulk supply and intelligent gas management.
FABTECH 2026 is North America's largest metal forming, fabricating, welding and finishing event for sheet metal manufacturing. More than 31,000 attendees and 1,400 exhibitors are expected at this year's event.
For more information about Air Products' full range of high performance and industry standard gases and related technologies for laser cutting applications visit Air Products' visit Advanced Gas Supply System for Laser Cutting  webpage.
About Air Products 
Air Products (NYSE:  APD ) is a world-leading industrial gases company in operation for over 85 years focused on serving energy, environmental, and emerging markets and generating a cleaner future. The Company supplies essential industrial gases, related equipment and applications expertise to customers in dozens of industries, including refining, chemicals, metals, electronics, manufacturing, medical and food. As the leading global hydrogen supplier, Air Products develops, engineers, builds, owns and operates some of the world's largest hydrogen projects. Through its sale of equipment businesses, the Company also provides turbomachinery, membrane systems and cryogenic containers globally.
Air Products had fiscal 2025 sales of $12.0 billion from operations in approximately 50 countries. For more information, visit  airproducts.com  or follow us on  LinkedIn ,  X ,  Facebook  or  Instagram .

Air Products to Highlight Gas-based Technologies for Laser Cutting, 3D Printing and Welding at FABTECH 2026
PR Newswire 
October 15, 2026 2 min read 
APD 
LEHIGH VALLEY, Pa., Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Air Products (NYSE: APD) will feature gas supply solutions and technologies designed to improve productivity, optimize costs, and support future growth for laser cutting, 3D printing, and welding applications at FABTECH 2026 from October 21-23 at the Las Vegas Convention Center in Nevada. 
(PRNewsfoto/Air Products) Application specialists will be on hand at booth #C4249 throughout the conference to speak with attendees about solutions to the challenges they face in their day-to-day operations and how Air Products can provide industry leading support and expertise in addition to supplying industrial gases. 
Whether a customer process utilizes nitrogen, oxygen, argon, helium, hydrogen or carbon dioxide, Air Products' experts can provide insight on selecting the right supply solution for a specific process or operation, from cylinders and microbulk systems, to bulk supply and intelligent gas management. 
FABTECH 2026 is North America's largest metal forming, fabricating, welding and finishing event for sheet metal manufacturing. More than 31,000 attendees and 1,400 exhibitors are expected at this year's event. 
For more information about Air Products' full range of high performance and industry standard gases and related technologies for laser cutting applications visit Air Products' visit Advanced Gas Supply System for Laser Cutting  webpage. 
About Air Products 
Air Products (NYSE:  APD ) is a world-leading industrial gases company in operation for over 85 years focused on serving energy, environmental, and emerging markets and generating a cleaner future. The Company supplies essential industrial gases, related equipment and applications expertise to customers in dozens of industries, including refining, chemicals, metals, electronics, manufacturing, medical and food. As the leading global hydrogen supplier, Air Products develops, engineers, builds, owns and operates some of the world's largest hydrogen projects. Through its sale of equipment businesses, the Company also provides turbomachinery, membrane systems and cryogenic containers globally. 
Air Products had fiscal 2025 sales of $12.0 billion from operations in approximately 50 countries. For more information, visit  airproducts.com  or follow us on  LinkedIn ,  X ,  Facebook  or  Instagram .

Prodrive Technologies participates in SEMICON West 2026, held at the Moscone Center in San Francisco from Oct. 13 to 15. (Photo: THE ELEC) 
Dutch company Prodrive Technologies plans to open an office in South Korea between late 2026 and early 2027 to strengthen support for local customers, including Hanwha Semitech, and expand its presence through sales activities.
At SEMICON West 2026, held at the Moscone Center in San Francisco on Oct. 13, Prodrive said it was recruiting local employees in preparation for the office opening. “We expect to open around the end of this year or early next year,” the company said. It is considering Dongtan and Pangyo as potential locations.
The Korean office will handle sales and customer support, with a small team being recruited. Prodrive is also building a new manufacturing facility in Malaysia. It operates production sites in the Netherlands, Boston in the US, and China, as well as sales offices in Japan and Israel. The company employs approximately 2,300 people worldwide.
Prodrive develops modules and provides system integration services for semiconductor equipment manufacturers. Rather than selling finished equipment directly to chipmakers, it designs and integrates equipment modules to meet manufacturers’ requirements. Its core products include precision stages, motion controllers, motors, actuators and high-speed cameras used in applications requiring high-precision control. It also produces equipment for front-end metrology and inspection and back-end hybrid bonding.
In South Korea, Hanwha Semitech collaborated with Prodrive to develop a hybrid bonder. Earlier this year, the second-generation hybrid bonder, SHB2 Nano, was manufactured and assembled at Prodrive’s Netherlands facility before being brought to South Korea. Prodrive also supplies linear motors and servo drives for magnetic levitation systems used in ASML’s extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography equipment.
“The Korean office will be responsible for sales and customer support,” a Prodrive representative said. “We have no plans to establish manufacturing facilities in Korea because we can support Korean customers from Malaysia, China and Europe.”

The 2nd largest aircraft equipment company in the world launches a new facility in Africa’s largest manufacturing country
Chinedu Okafor 
15 October 2026 10:30 AM
The world’s second-largest aerospace equipment manufacturer, Safran, via its Moroccan subsidiary, has launched a new facility in a country now recognized as Africa’s largest manufacturing country . 
Safran Morocco HQ Located near Casablanca airport [image:safran group] 
Safran has inaugurated a 5,700-square-meter extension of its facility in Temara, Morocco, strengthening the country's position as Africa’s largest manufacturing hub.
The expansion is expected to create 400 new jobs and bring operational activity to nearly two million production hours by 2026.
Safran’s Temara site now covers 31,400 square meters and produces about 93,000 electrical harnesses annually for major aircraft manufacturers.
Morocco and Safran are collaborating on Africa’s largest aircraft-engine assembly hub, with plans for a €350 million investment and almost 900 direct jobs by 2030.

Morocco’s Safran Electrical & Power, commemorating 20 years of operation in the North African country , inaugurated a new 5,700-square-meter extension.
The new facility serves as an extension to its industrial site in the coastal city of Temara, located just south of Rabat in the Rabat-Salé-Kénitra region.
As presently constituted, the facility’s workforce is upwards of 1,600 employees, while operational activity at the location is projected to approach two million production hours by 2026.
ADVERTISEMENT
Per the information provided by the facility, the extension is also intended to create 400 additional jobs, bolstering Morocco’s growing aerospace sector . 
Safran’s expansion is against the backdrop of Morocco’s new designation as Africa’s top manufacturing country, a title it took from South Africa at the start of the year.
“This anniversary and this new extension demonstrate the confidence Safran has placed in Morocco and its talent for the past twenty years,” said Serge Pons, executive vice president and general manager of Interconnection Systems Eurasia at Safran.

“Thanks to the commitment of our teams, the Témara site has become an essential part of our industrial network. This new milestone will enable us to support the growth of our activities and prepare for the challenges of tomorrow’s aerospace industry,” Serge Pons added.
ADVERTISEMENT
The latest expansion adds 5,700 square meters to Safran’s facility in Temara, bringing its total area to 31,400 square meters.
Safran’s presence in Temara dates back to 2005, when the group integrated Gespec into its operations, as seen on MoroccoWorldNews .
The new space was designed to aid the company in handling more civil and military aerospace projects while increasing its production of electrical cables and equipment used by major aircraft manufacturers.
The multinational aerospace company disclosed that the plant currently produces close to 93,000 electrical harnesses each year.
In 2025, Morocco unveiled plans to build a new aircraft-engine assembly hub in partnership with Safran Group.
ADVERTISEMENT
The project was touted as Africa’s largest aircraft-engine assembly hub; a site intended to become the world’s second-largest LEAP-1A production hub, after Safran’s flagship Villaroche plant in France.
It was also set to be constructed within the Midparc industrial zone in Nouaceur.
Included in the €350 million investment were a final assembly plant for LEAP-1A engines, the same model powering Airbus A320neo aircraft, and a facility for engine maintenance and repair.
The project was projected to create nearly 900 direct jobs by 2030, with the assembly plant handling up to 350 engines annually and the maintenance facility servicing 150 engines per year.
Airbus expansion in Morocco 
ADVERTISEMENT
Very recently, it was reported that Airbus plans to establish a third factory in Morocco and launch a helicopter-maintenance operation that could serve West Africa.
Morocco is making giant strides to become a major aviation manufacturing hub 
BI Africa 
The proposed factory would cover approximately 6,900 square metres and form part of an industrial expansion described as increasing the group’s Moroccan footprint by 30%.
Airbus already operates two factories in the country, employs more than 1,300 people and works with approximately 100 local suppliers, according to its Morocco representative, Mickaël Bertrand.
Airbus’ existing Moroccan operations produce cockpit components, fuselage structures, floor panels, wing elements and cabin fittings.
ADVERTISEMENT
Its Airbus Atlantic Maroc Composites business also manufactures components for A320 cockpits, ATR baggage compartments and business- and first-class seating.
These activities connect Moroccan factories to international aircraft production rather than limiting their customers to the domestic aviation market.
Chinedu Okafor

Vestas Secures 92 MW Wind Turbine Orders in Germany in Partnership with BBWind
By Kavitha 
15th October 2026

Vestas has announced new wind turbine orders totalling approximately 92 MW across three onshore wind projects in Germany, in collaboration with BBWind Projektberatungsgesellschaft mbH. The orders, included in the company’s third-quarter (Q3) order intake, cover the supply of 13 wind turbines and include 20-year Active Output Management (AOM) 5000 service agreements.
The projects, located in Borken and Raesfeld, will feature Vestas’ V172-7.2 MW and V162-5.6 MW turbine models, supporting the continued expansion of Germany’s onshore wind energy capacity.
The first order covers the 42 MW Borken Kierit wind project, developed by Windenergie Kierit GmbH & Co. KG in association with BBWind Projektberatungsgesellschaft mbH. Vestas will supply five V172-7.2 MW turbines and one V162-5.6 MW turbine for the project. Deliveries are scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027, with commissioning expected to commence in the second quarter of 2028. The agreement includes a 20-year AOM 5000 service contract to support long-term turbine performance and operational reliability.
The second agreement involves the 29 MW Raesfeld Lanzenhagen wind project, developed by Windenergie Lanzenhagen GmbH & Co. KG in collaboration with BBWind. The project will feature four V172-7.2 MW wind turbines, with deliveries planned to begin in the first quarter of 2028 and commissioning scheduled to commence in the fourth quarter of 2028. The contract also includes a 20-year AOM 5000 service agreement.
The third order covers the 22 MW Borken Deepschlatt wind project, developed by Windenergie Deepschlatt GmbH & Co. KG alongside BBWind. Vestas will deliver three V172-7.2 MW wind turbines, with deliveries expected to begin in the first quarter of 2028 and commissioning scheduled to start in the third quarter of 2028. The project will also benefit from a 20-year AOM 5000 service agreement.

Across the three projects, Vestas will supply 12 V172-7.2 MW turbines and one V162-5.6 MW turbine, representing a combined turbine capacity of approximately 92 MW. The long-term service agreements are designed to support operational efficiency, turbine availability, and reliable electricity generation throughout the projects’ operating lives.
The latest orders highlight continued investment in Germany’s onshore wind sector and reinforce Vestas’ collaboration with BBWind in developing renewable energy infrastructure.
The projects are expected to contribute to Germany’s renewable energy expansion by increasing wind power generation capacity, strengthening domestic clean electricity supply, and supporting the country’s broader energy transition and decarbonisation objectives.

Dow Partnership Advances Recyclable Polymer Technology
Award honors Northwestern-Dow collaboration to make crosslinked polymers recyclable
Oct 15, 2026 Brian Sandalow 
The Problem
Conventional crosslinked polymers found in car tires, rubber bands, and other everyday items are durable, but their permanent crosslinks prevent them from being recycled.
Our Idea
Researchers developed crosslinks that remain strong during use but can break and reform during reprocessing, allowing the material to be recycled multiple times.
Why It Matters
The approach could make widely used crosslinked polymers recyclable using improved industrial processes.
Our Team
Professor John Torkelson; PhD graduates Boran Chen (PhD ’24), Logan Fenimore (PhD ’25), Yen-Wen Huang (PhD ’26), and Mathew Suazo (PhD ’26); Dow researchers Evelyn Auyeung (PhD ’14), Stephanie Barbon, Hayley Brown, and Colin Li Pi Shan.
Northwestern Engineering’s John Torkelson and eight collaborators from Northwestern University and the Dow Chemical Company have been selected to receive the 2027 Cooperative Research Award in Polymer Science and Engineering from the American Chemical Society’s (ACS) Division of Polymeric Materials: Science and Engineering (PMSE). An award symposium in their honor will be held at the Spring 2027 National ACS Meeting in New Orleans. The award recognizes outstanding cooperative research among industrial, academic, and national laboratory scientists. 
Along with Torkelson, Walter P. Murphy Professor of Chemical and Biological Engineering and Materials Science and Engineering at the McCormick School of Engineering, honorees include four researchers who conducted the work as PhD students in his group : Boran Chen (PhD ’24), Logan Fenimore (PhD ’25), Yen-Wen Huang (PhD ’26), and Mathew Suazo (PhD ’26). In addition, recipients include four collaborators from Dow: Evelyn Auyeung (PhD ‘14), Stephanie Barbon, Hayley Brown, and Colin Li Pi Shan.
The collaboration, supported through Dow’s University Partnership Initiative , has spanned nearly seven years to address a persistent problem in polymer recycling: how to give crosslinked polymers the durability that makes them useful without making them permanently unrecyclable.
For Torkelson, who joined Northwestern in 1983, the recognition also reflects a research direction he has pursued for decades. 
“Sometimes the most important thing to do is to work on things that people think can’t be done,” said Torkelson, an expert in polymer science and engineering, particularly sustainable and recyclable polymers, polymer processing, and polymer nanotechnology, who has been energized by the success of the partnership.
The project began with skepticism. The team’s first paper demonstrating its reprocessable polyethylene networks was rejected. The team then submitted the manuscript to another journal, where it received strong reviews and was later recognized as one of the journal’s most popular papers of 2022. That paper became the foundation for much of the research now being recognized by the ACS PMSE award and pursued toward commercial application.
The research has since produced more than 20 publications and multiple patent filings. Torkelson sees its development from a small-scale university experiment to commercialization research as an example of what sustained relationships between universities and companies can accomplish.
Making crosslinked polymers recyclable
Crosslinked polymers are everywhere, from rubber tires and rubber bands to foam mattresses. Crosslinks tie long polymer chains together, creating some of the most robust materials.
That durability, however, creates a recycling problem. Unlike thermoplastics, whose molecular chains can move past one another when heated, conventionally crosslinked materials cannot return to a flowing melt state that allows them to be reshaped.
“Once it’s made, you can never take a rubber band back into a melt state, Torkelson said.
His group developed a different approach. They created crosslinks that remain robust under normal use conditions but become dynamic at the elevated temperatures used during reprocessing. At those temperatures, the bonds forming the crosslinks can dissociate, allowing the material to be reshaped. As the material cools, the bonds reform.
The approach has been demonstrated with polyethylene and polypropylene, which together account for more than half of the roughly 1 trillion pounds of polymers and plastics produced globally each year. Currently, less than 10 percent of that total is recycled, Torkelson said.
The new method is designed as a relatively simple modification of an existing industrial process. Permanently crosslinked polyethylene is already manufactured by adding an initiator to polyethylene. Torkelson’s approach adds a small amount of a dynamic crosslinker to that process.
“Industry doesn’t have to develop a whole new process to accommodate this,” Torkelson said. “We can modify the existing process.”
That alignment can eliminate the need for new machinery and reduce the amount of process development required before adoption. Torkelson said the approach might require adjustments to some processing conditions, but it remains a relatively small variation on technology already used commercially.
The research could have implications beyond recycling. In recently published work, Huang and Torkelson found that converting polyethylene into the group’s crosslinked systems also made the material more resistant to wear. In tests, the materials exhibited more than a one-third reduction in wear, measured through volume or mass loss, compared with the polyethylene from which they were derived.
Because everyday wear of plastics can produce microplastics, Torkelson said the increased durability raises another possibility for the research.
“The crosslinks just lead to more durable materials that will actually wear less,” he said. “This even has an implication for potentially mitigating microplastic formation.”
From the university lab and commercial research
Much of the project’s development has depended on the complementary capabilities of Northwestern and Dow.
At Northwestern, Torkelson’s group develops ideas, studies their underlying science, and demonstrates them at laboratory scale. Dow brought expertise and facilities needed to test whether those concepts could move toward larger-scale manufacturing and commercial applications.
“This was a case where they have real expertise in terms of large-scale processing, and we do everything at the university at small scale,” Torkelson said. “I’ve learned a lot from Dow. They have learned a lot from us.”
What began as a three-year Dow project supporting one graduate student expanded as the results accumulated. Fenimore, who had received a National Science Foundation fellowship, also joined the effort. Torkelson said Dow typically supports university projects for about three years before moving to new research questions, but the polymer work continued beyond that initial period with funding for two graduate students.
This was a case where they have real expertise in terms of large-scale processing, and we do everything at the university at small scale. I’ve learned a lot from Dow. They have learned a lot from us. John Torkelson 
Dow has since conducted commercialization research based on the Northwestern technology at facilities in Lake Jackson, Texas, and Shanghai, China.
One area Dow has explored is molded footwear. Such products offered a relatively small consumer application through which the company could test the technology and its recyclability. Torkelson said Dow researchers demonstrated that a used crosslinked product could be cut into pieces, reprocessed, and used to make a new product. Waste material created during injection molding could similarly be fed back into the manufacturing process rather than discarded.
The partnership also provided an education that extended beyond Torkelson’s laboratory.
Chen, Fenimore, Huang, and Suazo carried out the bulk of the university research, Torkelson said, while gaining exposure to industrial research and the process of moving a scientific idea toward application.
The 2027 honor marks the first time the Cooperative Research Award has recognized the graduate students who performed much of the university research in addition to faculty and industrial researchers. For Torkelson, their inclusion in the Cooperative Research Award is particularly meaningful.
The four researchers have since moved into industry and academic research. Huang joined Dow, Suazo joined AOC Formulations, and two are pursuing postdoctoral research, including Fenimore at the National Institute of Standards and Technology and Chen at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.
While Torkelson cautioned that not every university-industry research project will produce the same results, he said this collaboration has proven mutually beneficial for a relatively modest industrial investment.

This audio is auto-generated. Please let us know if you have feedback .
Dive Brief:
Applied Materials , an equipment, services and software supplier for chipmakers, has opened its multibillion-dollar Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization Center to collaborate with industry on next-generation technologies.
Leading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and research universities will work at the center to develop advanced chipmaking processes, as well as to move technologies from early-stage research to high-volume manufacturing faster, Applied Materials said.
The 600,000-square-foot facility is located at the company’s campus in Sunnyvale, California, and has near four acres of advanced cleanroom space. Applied Materials said it expects capital spending to reach $5 billion as new customer projects begin.
Dive Insight:
The news comes several months after Applied Materials announced it had partnered with South Korea-based SK Hynix to accelerate memory innovation and address semiconductor-related challenges at the EPIC Center. The agreement was reached as technology firms navigate a global shortage of memory chips driven by surging artificial intelligence demand.
According to Applied Materials, the EPIC Center will “reinvent” the standard research and development model in the semiconductor industry. The standard model typically involves handing off foundational materials research, equipment and process development, and process integration and pilot produciton from one siloed environment to the next.
“The EPIC Center is designed to remove these handoffs, putting the people who invent the materials, build the equipment, and make the chips together in a state-of-the-art facility purpose-built for commercialization,” the company said. “The technologies the AI era demands are too complex and too consequential for any one company to invent alone.”
Applied Materials said it expects the center’s operating model to provide chipmakers early access to advanced materials and equipment, shorter learning cycles and a faster path to volume production. 
Materials innovation has “outgrown serial development” and “demands coordinated development and integrated solutions,” Prabu Raja, president of Applied Materials’ semiconductor products group, said in a statement. “EPIC is the only place where materials, process technology and equipment will be innovated in parallel, which increases the success rate of new materials and technologies.”
Partners in the EPIC Center “span the AI technology stack” and include TSMC, Intel, SK Hynix, Micron, Samsung Electronics, Broadcom and Advantest, along with Arizona State University, Stanford University, University of California, Berkeley and other institutions. More companies and organizations are expected to join the center over time.
Applied Materials reported $7.01 billion in Q1 revenue , above the midpoint of its guided range, citing increased demand for leading-edge logic, high-bandwidth memory and advanced packaging.

Tosoh Takes Full Control of HDI Monomer Producer Nanyo Kasei
George Orwell 15-Oct-2026 
Tosoh will acquire Asahi Kasei's 50% stake in Nanyo Kasei, securing full ownership and strengthening HDI monomer supply for derivatives production.
Tosoh Corporation has moved to strengthen its control over the supply chain for hexamethylene diisocyanate (HDI) monomer by acquiring the remaining 50% stake in Nanyo Kasei Co., Ltd. from Asahi Kasei Corporation. The transaction will transform the existing joint venture into a wholly owned subsidiary of Tosoh, supporting the company's efforts to secure raw material supplies and strengthen its downstream HDI derivatives business. 
Established in 1980, Nanyo Kasei was formed through equal investments by Nippon Polyurethane Industry Co., Ltd., now part of Tosoh Corporation, and Asahi Kasei Corporation. The joint venture was established specifically to manufacture HDI monomer, an important chemical intermediate used in the production of HDI-based derivatives. 
Under the existing arrangement, Tosoh and Asahi Kasei supply raw materials and other inputs to Nanyo Kasei. The company manufactures HDI monomer, which is subsequently purchased by both shareholders for their respective manufacturing operations. Following the acquisition, Tosoh will gain full ownership of the production facility and greater control over its operations and output allocation. 
The strategic move is primarily aimed at ensuring a stable supply of HDI monomer, a critical feedstock for Tosoh's downstream derivatives business. By bringing Nanyo Kasei entirely under its ownership, Tosoh expects to strengthen supply-chain coordination, improve procurement certainty and support the consistent operation of its HDI derivatives manufacturing activities. 
The acquisition is particularly significant because Tosoh's new HDI derivatives plant commenced commercial operations in September 2026. Securing reliable access to HDI monomer will be important for maintaining production continuity at the new facility and supporting the company's downstream business requirements. Full ownership of Nanyo Kasei is expected to give Tosoh greater flexibility in aligning monomer production with the demand generated by its derivatives operations. 
HDI is widely used to manufacture aliphatic polyisocyanates, which serve as curing agents in polyurethane coatings. These products are valued for their weather resistance, durability, colour stability and long-term performance. They are used in automotive refinishing, industrial coatings, protective finishes and other applications requiring high-performance surface protection. 
Although the acquisition strengthens Tosoh's control over an important upstream asset, its immediate effect on the wider HDI market will depend on production volumes, operating rates, demand conditions and the availability of competing supplies. The announcement does not specify any additional production capacity or a planned increase in HDI monomer output. 
Overall, the transaction represents a strategic vertical-integration move, positioning Tosoh to better coordinate HDI monomer procurement with its expanding derivatives operations while reinforcing supply reliability for its downstream customers. 
Product and Chemical Price Impact 
Tosoh's acquisition is expected to improve HDI monomer supply security for its downstream derivatives business, particularly following the September 2026 startup of its new derivatives plant. However, the deal does not confirm additional production capacity or increased market supply, limiting the likelihood of an immediate price impact. Greater operational integration could improve procurement efficiency and reduce supply disruptions for Tosoh. HDI monomer and HDI-based polyisocyanate prices may remain influenced by feedstock costs, plant operating rates, demand from automotive and industrial coatings, and competing suppliers. Any broader price softening would depend on increased output rather than ownership changes alone.

The firm also raised adjusted EBITDA estimates for Albemarle to $3.2 billion in 2027 and $2.9 billion in 2028. Roberts noted that regulatory delays at CATL's Jianxiawo lithium mine in China could further tighten supply. Albemarle has fallen 31% year to date amid weaker lithium prices, but the company's low-cost position and improved balance sheet are seen as key advantages.
Key Elements 
Albemarle Corp Mizuho Securities John Roberts Benchmark Minerals Contemporary Amperex Technology NYSE LSEG 
Albemarle Corp (ALB) climbed 4% in premarket trading Wednesday after Mizuho Securities lifted its rating on the world's largest lithium producer, betting that surging demand for utility-scale battery storage will tighten the market and push prices higher.
Analyst John Roberts upgraded the stock to Outperform from Neutral while keeping his $130 price target, a level he had trimmed from $140 about two weeks earlier, implying roughly 33% upside from Tuesday's close. The Charlotte, North Carolina-based company has fallen 31% year to date as lithium prices weakened, but the firm now sees a more favorable supply-demand balance taking shape.
The gain did not hold. By Wednesday's close the stock was 0.4% lower at a fresh year-to-date low. Earlier in the week, Chinese lithium carbonate futures posted their steepest one-day fall since March, closing down 11.8% at 104,740 yuan a metric ton on Oct. 12 after the European Union proposed capping imports of Chinese hybrid vehicles at about 350,000 units a year. Spot battery-grade carbonate in China was assessed at 115,400 yuan a metric ton that day, down 5.7%.
"We are raising ALB rating to Outperform as strong Battery Energy Stationary Storage (BESS) demand has tipped market balance into favorable territory," Roberts wrote in a note to clients. "ALB is the lowest-cost lithium producer and its improved balance sheet provides downside resilience while providing flexibility to invest as project returns improve."
The catalyst is accelerating deployment of grid-scale energy storage systems, which is consuming global lithium supply faster than previously expected. Albemarle's own numbers make the same point: on its August earnings call, the company raised its 2026 forecast for global stationary-storage battery production to 900-1,100 gigawatt-hours, about 100 GWh above its prior range, and said storage would account for roughly 30% of global lithium demand this year — nearing parity with light-duty electric vehicles. Global lithium consumption was up 45% year over year through May, and the company described inventories as low and the physical market as tight.
Revised forecasts from industry consultant Benchmark Minerals project lithium carbonate prices reaching $22,500 per metric ton by 2027 and $19,500 per metric ton by 2028, substantial upward revisions from earlier estimates of $18,375 and $14,500, respectively.
Mizuho noted that the surge in stationary storage requirements lifted projected 2027 demand by about 10%, while expected global supply and inventory drawdowns remained essentially unchanged. That widening gap prompted the firm to raise its price forecasts for Albemarle's core Energy Storage segment to $21,000 per metric ton in 2027 and $19,000 per metric ton in 2028.

Note: Per metric ton.
Reflecting higher realization assumptions, Mizuho boosted its adjusted EBITDA estimates for Albemarle to $3.2 billion in 2027 and $2.9 billion in 2028, up from $2.4 billion and $2.5 billion previously. As the industry's lowest-cost producer, the company is well positioned to convert higher market prices into expanding operating margins and stronger cash flow generation.
Earnings Sensitivity to Lithium Prices 
Albemarle's own 2026 outlook, published in August, shows how much of its earnings power hinges on where lithium settles:
Lithium price assumption ($/kg LCE) FY2025 average (~$10) Q1 2026 average (~$20) 2021-2025 average (~$30) 
Net sales $4.1-4.3 billion $5.7-6.0 billion $7.5-7.8 billion 
Adjusted EBITDA $0.9-1.0 billion $2.4-2.6 billion $4.2-4.4 billion 
Mizuho's 2027 EBITDA estimate sits roughly 30% above the midpoint of the $20/kg scenario, reflecting its $21,000 a metric ton realization assumption for the energy storage segment and the volume growth expected as the CGP3 plant at the Greenbushes joint venture ramps to full capacity in the first quarter of 2027. Management said on the same call that 2027 volumes should return to a 240,000-260,000 metric ton trajectory.
Supply Constraints Could Add Fuel
Roberts also flagged that lithium demand could intensify further if regulatory hurdles delay the resumption of Contemporary Amperex Technology's upstream production. The reference is to Jianxiawo, a lepidolite mine in Jiangxi province that is China's largest lithium operation by capacity, with nameplate capacity approaching 150,000 metric tons of lithium carbonate equivalent a year. Its permitting saga has dragged on for more than a year:
The same consultancy now expects the mine to produce 32,000 metric tons LCE in 2026, half its previous forecast, while keeping its 2027 estimate at about 99,000 metric tons. The environmental review could stretch into 2027, and authorities are also inspecting other Jiangxi mines that were expected to produce about 108,000 metric tons LCE this year. The Chinese battery giant is a major player in the lithium supply chain, so any slowdown removes supply from an already tightening market.
"Lithium remains a volatile, capital-intensive commodity, but the near-term supply/demand outlook has tightened as demand continues to exceed expectations while new supply is constrained by long project lead times and reduced industry capital spending," the analyst wrote.
Mizuho's call aligns with broader Street sentiment. Of the 23 analysts covering Albemarle, 15 hold a buy or strong buy rating, while eight maintain a hold, according to LSEG data. Investors will likely watch whether accelerating stationary storage deployment can offset ongoing volatility in consumer electric vehicle adoption over the coming quarters. The next checkpoint is Nov. 4, when Albemarle reports third-quarter results; management has guided for sequential declines in both net sales and adjusted EBITDA, citing lower volumes and softer pricing.

Fair Value Estimate 
: $2,050.00

Morningstar Economic Moat Rating 
: Wide
Morningstar Uncertainty Rating 
: High
What We Thought of ASML Holding’s Earnings
Last quarter, ASML Holding ASML announced plans to expand low-NA EUV and immersion DUV capacity by 30% in 2027 and another 30% in 2028. These plans seem already outdated, as management has acknowledged this might not be enough to meet customer demand.
Why it matters: ASML’s backlog keeps growing, with 2027 fully booked and significant order intake already for 2028. In our view, the most important disclosure from these earnings was that ASML is having first conversations with customers for 2029 and 2030 orders. DRAM makers seem the most open to talking about 2029-30 already.
While we still see some upside to our 2028 revenue and EPS forecast as ASML tries to expand capacity beyond 30% with its existing footprint, we believe most of it is already priced in. What could push the stock higher is order visibility that confirms 2029 and 2030 as “growth years.”
The bottom line: We maintain our wide Morningstar Economic Moat Rating and EUR 1,800 fair value estimate.
After 28% sales growth in both 2027 and 2028, reaching EUR 56 and EUR 71.5 billion respectively, we model a return to low-double-digit growth in 2029 and 2030, with sales reaching EUR 88 billion in 2030. Should management confirm the first 2029 orders over the next six months, our 2029-30 forecast would gain credibility, and the stock price could converge toward our fair value estimate.
Our bull case would require 2029 to book as quickly and as fully as 2028 has. If customers place orders at a fast pace in the coming months, sales growth in 2029-30 could exceed our low-double-digit forecast.
Key stats: Beyond expanding capacity, ASML continues to aggressively develop upgrades to low-NA EUV and immersion DUV output. Installed base management revenue reached EUR 3.3 billion, EUR 400 million higher than expected, thanks to the upgrade business, as customers look to extract more productivity from their machines. Upgrades were the main driver of the 57.5% gross margin this quarter, above guidance of 55.0%-57.0%.

title: The Maxon Fall 2026 Release Delivers Bigger Worlds, Faster Workflows, and More Creative Control - USA Today

content_text:
The Maxon Fall 2026 Release Delivers Bigger Worlds, Faster Workflows, and More Creative Control
Maxon Computers
New Cinema 4D Scatter and Liquid FX, integrated UV workflows in ZBrush, faster Redshift interaction, art-directable VFX in Red Giant, and MCP-powered Autograph workflows give artists more capability, speed and control. 
BAD HOMBURG, GERMANY / ACCESS Newswire / October 14, 2026 / Maxon , maker of powerful, approachable software solutions for creators working in 2D and 3D design, motion graphics, visual effects and visualization, today announced its Fall 2026 ecosystem release , which introduces the 2027.0 releases of Cinema 4D, ZBrush, Redshift, Red Giant and Autograph, bringing substantial new creative capabilities and workflow improvements across the Maxon toolset. In the 2027.0 release, Maxon is delivering new ways to populate and simulate complex 3D worlds, more complete production workflows inside ZBrush, faster rendering feedback in Redshift, new art-directable VFX capabilities, and deeper creative automation and cross-application workflows in Autograph through Model Context Protocol (MCP) support and first direct connection with Cinema 4D.
“We’re continuing to do what we’ve always done: listen to our artists and bring the best tools we can to them,” said David McGavran, CEO of Maxon. “Everything we build adds to what came before it, so the possibilities keep getting bigger. A few years ago, you couldn’t simulate a beer in Cinema 4D. Now you can pour it, foam it, spray it and make it look almost as satisfying as the real thing. That’s the kind of progress we want artists to feel: faster workflows, fewer barriers and more of the real world available to create.”
Build Bigger, Richer Worlds in Cinema 4D 
Cinema 4D 2027.0 delivers an all new Scatter System , one of the product’s most requested capabilities, giving artists a procedural way to populate environments with vegetation, rocks, debris, crowds and other objects while maintaining precise creative control.
The new Scatter Generator and Scatter Tag support distribution, filtering, clustering and transform controls, while integration with Cinema 4D’s MoGraph toolset lets artists use familiar Fields and Effectors to shape, animate and influence scattered objects. The updates give artists a more approachable path to building dense, believable environments without relying on complex workarounds or separate scattering tools.
Cinema 4D’s unified simulation system now also includes Liquid FX , adding automatically generated foam, spray and bubbles to liquid simulations. These secondary effects respond to the underlying liquid behavior, adding the visual detail that makes pours, splashes, waterfalls and other fluid effects feel more convincing without requiring artists to construct separate complex simulations.
The release also deepens the connection between Cinema 4D and Redshift – including ACES 2.0 alignment improvements – streamlines everyday workflows, and introduces a range of quality-of-life upgrades designed to make routine production work faster and less prone to error.
An End-to-End Sculpting Pipeline in ZBrush, from iPad to Desktop 
Artists have been asking for ways to do more of their production workflow without needing to leave the ZBrush environment – and now they can.
A new UV Editor lets artists create, edit and refine UVs directly inside ZBrush, with professional workflow support including UDIMs and texel density controls. Built using proven Maxon technology from Cinema 4D, the editor reduces the back-and-forth between applications while artists are still iterating on a sculpt, helping them move more quickly from sculpting and painting into texturing and downstream production.
New Selection Sets tackle another everyday pain point by allowing artists to save and recall Polygroups, masks, Polypaint, morph targets and UV configurations rather than repeatedly rebuilding them by hand. For complex iterative work, that means less time recreating selections and more freedom to explore different ideas.
ZBrush for iPad continues to become a more complete professional sculpting environment with Spotlight, bringing reference, projection, painting and image-driven sculpting workflows to iPad. New non-destructive 3D Layers enable artists to experiment freely on the iPad with sculpting, polypaint and masking on a layer, giving more control over sculpting changes, detail blending, and creative iteration.
Rendering in Redshift Means Less Time Waiting, More Time Creating 
Cinema 4D and Redshift 2027.0 give artists speed where it matters most: while the creativity is flowing.
A reworked memory architecture uses available memory more efficiently across an increasingly wide range of hardware, while major interactivity improvements shorten the time between making a change and seeing the rendered result. For artists, that means less lag time between an idea and the visual feedback needed to refine it. Change a light, material or scene element and understand its impact on the environment more quickly for a more fluid creative experience.
Redshift also continues to feel more native inside Cinema 4D. Artists can more easily drag Cinema 4D objects, Cloners and particle systems directly into material workflows and access their properties in the Node Editor, simplifying tasks that previously required more steps. Creative flexibility is further enhanced through a new procedural system for generating fur, fibers, textiles, and knitted materials directly at render time, while support for NVIDIA RTX Spark brings Redshift workflows to a wider range of power-efficient mobile devices and production environments.
Red Giant Introduces Art-Directable Visual Effects 
Red Giant 2027.0 brings powerful updates to VFX artists, motion designers, and content creators, making visual effects faster, more intuitive, and more art-directable across creative workflows.
Scene Light , a new AI-powered, depth-aware relighting tool, lets artists place lights into existing live-action footage and CG imagery directly in After Effects. Artists can add realistic interactive light from effects such as muzzle flashes, explosions, and environmental sources, or make broader changes such as day-for-night treatments, without relying on extensive masking and manual color adjustments. Lights remain fully art-directable within the compositing workflow.
Maxon Noise for Universe brings the procedural noise patterns familiar to Cinema 4D and Redshift into video and compositing workflows. Long requested by the community, Maxon Noise gives motion designers and VFX artists GPU-accelerated tools for building textures, animated maps, transitions and abstract effects directly within their existing workflows.
Real Lens Flares becomes more flexible and physically grounded with Custom Schmutz, which lets artists use their own still or animated textures for lens grime, splashes and imperfections, alongside expanded Light Source Types for creating flares appropriate to different real-world lighting sources rather than treating every source like sunlight.
Chromatic Displacement also comes to Autograph, extending the Red Giant toolset available inside Maxon’s free motion graphics and compositing application, while new Custom UI support in Maxon Studio allows Capsules to expose richer Red Giant controls including color wheels, curves, gradients and text controls.
New Autograph MCP Server Gives Artists a Productivity Boost 
Autograph 2027.0 now supports an MCP Server that can be switched on to bridge AI agents to Autograph’s own tools, helping artists navigate the software and increase creative output.
The new MCP Server opens Autograph to agentic AI workflows, allowing supported AI tools to assist with tasks inside the application, answer questions about how to use Autograph, or automate portions of a creative workflow, all through natural language prompting. The integration is designed to work with Autograph’s native tools and workflows, giving artists the ability to continue editing and directing the work inside the application.
Autograph also now has its first direct connection with Cinema 4D: artists can copy and paste 3D elements directly from Cinema 4D into Autograph, including animated elements, cameras, lights, nulls and compatible primitives. This brings the applications closer together as a unified 3D and compositing workflow, letting artists combine Cinema 4D scenes and Redshift renders with Autograph’s native 3D workspace without rebuilding key scene information by hand.
Listen. Build. Deliver. 
The Maxon 2027.0 release continues a year of development across Maxon’s tools. Throughout 2026, Maxon has shipped new capabilities, platform support, performance improvements and workflow refinements as they became ready rather than asking artists to wait for one annual product drop.
“We’re focused on giving artists more of what they need to create, removing friction from the parts of the process that slow them down, and improving the technology underneath the tools they use every day,” said McGavran.
Availability 
The new releases of Cinema 4D, ZBrush, Redshift, Red Giant and Autograph will be available beginning October 14, 2026.
About Maxon 
Maxon makes powerful, yet approachable software solutions for content creators working in 2D and 3D design, motion graphics, visual effects and visualization. Product lines include the award-winning Cinema 4D suite of 3D modeling, simulation and animation technology; the diverse Red Giant lineup of editing, motion design and filmmaking tools; the leading-edge Redshift renderer; ZBrush, the industry-standard digital sculpting and painting solution; and Autograph, Maxon’s motion graphics and compositing application.

Tosoh to acquire Asahi Kasei’s stake in HDI monomer JV, taking full ownership
October 14, 2026 | By Mary Bailey 
Tosoh Corp. (Tokyo) has decided to acquire all shares (50%) of Nanyo Kasei Co., Ltd. (Tokyo), a joint venture with Asahi Kasei Corp. (Tokyo). The deal will make Nanyo Kasei a wholly owned subsidiary of Tosoh.
Nanyo Kasei was established in 1980 through equal investment by Nippon Polyurethane Industry Co., Ltd. (now Tosoh) and Asahi Kasei to manufacture hexamethylene diisocyanate (HDI) monomer .
Currently, Tosoh and Asahi Kasei supply raw materials and other inputs to Nanyo Kasei, which manufactures the HDI monomer. Each company then purchases the monomer for its own operations. Tosoh will acquire the 50% of Nanyo Kasei shares held by Asahi Kasei.
Through the full acquisition, Tosoh aims to secure a stable supply of HDI monomer and support the stable operation of its HDI derivatives business. The transaction will also contribute to the stable procurement of HDI monomer for Tosoh’s new HDI derivatives plant, which began commercial operations in September 2026.
Tosoh expects the impact of the transaction on its consolidated financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, to be minimal.

CELEBRATING SUCCESS: The 2025 HEY Business Awards winners
By Rick Lyon, Co-Editor
Judges have had their say on the best and the brightest businesses across the region.
A total of 27 different organisations remain in the running for the prestigious annual accolades at the Hull & East Yorkshire Business Awards, with the leading figures at the helm of three of the category contenders also competing for the coveted Entrepreneur of the Year title.
It is the third edition of the awards under the tenure of talent champion Simon Jones and events specialist Jane Smallwood, and the level of support generated has surpassed even that garnered for last year’s silver anniversary celebration.
And with the quality of entries also praised, the gala celebration promises to be another great night under the guidance of top television host Gethin Jones, when it is held next month.
Simon said: “Our partnership numbers are incredible this year, the highest we’ve seen since taking the awards on, and we see that as a real show of confidence in what we’re delivering.

Judging of the nominations has been made more rigorous, moving from a desktop exercise with independent representatives of the business community, to in-person interviews and site visits by a far wider supporting cast.
Jane said: “Since taking the awards baton on from Reach Plc, who remain our media partner, we’ve refreshed the judging process – taking it from a paper exercise to a deep dive with face-to-face meetings. We feel it enhances the credibility of the accolades, and this is reflected in the quality of our contenders.”
Headline partner is For Entrepreneurs Only, with three new principal partners also involved in 2026 – BAE Systems, H&H and Siemens Gamesa.
Winners will be crowned at the Doubletree by Hilton Hotel Hull on Thursday, November 19. There will be a dozen awards presented, including the Lifetime Achievement Award, with packages of support tailored to the individual category, again part of the deeper focus on a richer event, taking it beyond the night.

Charles River partners with Magellan Stem Cells on cell therapy
The partnership focuses on biologics quality control as well as viral and release testing under cGMP standards.

Charles River will supply viral safety assessments using NGS for cell and gene therapy. Credit: Gorodenkoff/Shutterstock.com. 
Charles River Laboratories International (CRL) has collaborated with Australian biotechnology firm Magellan Stem Cells to advance the development and clinical progress of Magellan’s regenerative medicine candidate, Zelestrocel.
The partnership focuses on biologics quality control as well as viral and release testing under current good manufacturing practice (cGMP) standards.

Magellan recently completed Phase I/II clinical studies evaluating Zelestrocel, an off-the-shelf, allogeneic stem cell therapy designed to treat osteoarthritis.
The company is now preparing to initiate a pivotal Phase III clinical programme.
Charles River global manufacturing corporate senior vice president Kerstin Dolph said: “Working with organisations at the forefront of innovation allows us to expand our GMP testing capabilities and help accelerate the delivery of safe, compliant therapies to patients.
“We are excited to support Magellan as they work towards advancing Zelestrocel from the clinic to potential commercialisation.”
To support the therapy’s progress towards international regulatory standards, Charles River will provide viral safety assessments using next-generation sequencing (NGS) for cell and gene therapy (CGT).
The testing protocols comply with regulatory benchmarks from the European Medicines Agency (EMA), the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), GMP standards, and International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) Q5A and Q5B guidelines.
Charles River expanded its sequencing capabilities through the acquisition of Pathoquest, a company specialising in biopharmaceutical quality control and characterisation.
Magellan COO Nick Bliesner said: “Charles River’s GMP NGS capabilities provide an innovative approach to viral safety testing that supports both product quality and regulatory readiness. This collaboration strengthens our ability to advance Zelestrocel toward commercialisation with confidence.”
Magellan manufactures the cell therapy internally at its Melbourne facility, which holds GMP certification from the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA).
It is one of only four cell therapy manufacturing centres in Australia to hold GMP certification.
The sequencing work also aligns with Charles River’s Alternative Methods Advancement Project (AMAP), an initiative guided by a scientific advisory board chaired by Dr Namandjé Bumpus to reduce animal testing by implementing new approach methodologies (NAMs).
In addition, Charles River operates nine CGMP-compliant International Organization for Standardization-6 (ISO-6) cleanroom suites, offers cell bank release within eight to ten weeks, and has produced more than 2,000 cell and viral banks.
In August this year, CRL and Medigen Vaccine Biologics (MVC) entered into a collaboration to support the characterisation and validation of the virus seed bank for MVC’s next-generation multivalent enterovirus vaccine.

Tosoh to take full control of PU monomer producer
14 Oct 2026
Share: 
Acquisition from Asahi Kasei to support supply to newly commissioned HDI derivatives plant
Tokyo – Tosoh Corp. is to acquire Asahi Kasei's 50% interest in Nanyo Kasei, taking full ownership of the Japanese producer of hexamethylene diisocyanate (HDI) monomer.
Nanyo Kasei was established in 1980 as a 50:50 joint venture between Asahi Kasei and Nippon Polyurethane Industry, now part of Tosoh, to manufacture HDI monomer.
Under the current arrangement, Tosoh and Asahi Kasei supply raw materials and other inputs to Nanyo Kasei and subsequently purchase the HDI monomer produced by the company.
In a 13 Oct statement, Tosoh said the acquisition would enable it to “secure a stable supply of HDI monomer” and support the stable operation of its HDI derivatives business.
In particular, the group said the transaction would support HDI monomer supply to its new HDI derivatives plant, which started commercial operations in September.
The acquisition is scheduled to close by the end of March 2027.

ASML says it's getting order interest through 2030 as profit smashes expectations
Published Wed, Oct 14 2026 1:14 AM EDT Updated Wed, Oct 14 2026 4:45 AM EDT 
Arjun Kharpal @/in/arjunkharpal/ @ArjunKharpal 
WATCH LIVE 
Key Points
ASML said some customers are "expressing an interest" in placing orders with the company in 2029 and 2030, providing investors with a view into longer-term demand.
The Dutch chip giant said it is looking at ways to increase capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase it had previously forecast as demand remains strong.
The company also raised the lower end of its sales forecast for 2026.
In this article
ASML 
TSM 
Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT 
ASML said Wednesday that some of its customers are expressing interest in placing orders for its critical semiconductor tools for 2029 and 2030 as the company reported third-quarter profit that beat expectations.
The comments will likely comfort investors who have been looking to assess the longer-term demand outlook for ASML's lithography machines.
"Our customers continue to increase their short- and medium-term equipment demand forecasts with us, driven primarily by their views on the size and duration of AI-related investments," CEO Christophe Fouquet said in a press release. 
"In light of their demand visibility, some customers are expressing an interest in placing orders with us for 2029 and even 2030."
ASML is the only company in the world that produces extreme ultraviolet lithography machines, a key tool used by the likes of TSMC to make the world's most advanced semiconductors. 
Investors closely watch the Dutch company's earnings for signs of AI-related chip demand. 
watch now 
VIDEO 3:47 03:47 
ASML races to expand capacity on strong AI-driven demand
Squawk Box Europe 
Fouquet said current supply planned for 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet the demand of its customers. The company is "investigating ways" to increase capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase it had previously forecast. 
ASML has now updated its guidance three times this year, upping its full-year forecast for the second time in July, and on Wednesday it raised the lower end of its sales forecast for 2026. 
The company now expects net sales of between 44 billion euros and 45 billion euros ($49.3 billion to $50.4 billion). The previous lower end of the forecast was for 43 billion euros.
ASML also said it expects fourth-quarter net sales of between 14.2 billion euros and 15.2 billion euros. The upper end of the range is ahead of LSEG consensus estimates of 14.2 billion euros. 
ASML's stock was around 2% higher in early trade in Europe. Shares of the company have rallied 56% this year. 
ASML shares year-to-date
During the quarter, Samsung and TSMC, the world's two biggest chipmakers, committed to using ASML's High NA extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines. High NA EUV is ASML's next-generation tool, which analysts see as key to the Dutch firm's future growth.
For the third quarter, here's how ASML did versus LSEG consensus estimates:
Net sales: 11.66 billion euros versus 11.72 billion euros expected
Net profit: 4.96 billion euros versus 4.1 billion euros expected 
ASML sticks to China forecast 
The semiconductor equipment maker said it expects China sales to account for 20% of its total business, sticking to a prior forecast.
While ASML holds an effective monopoly on EUV machines, a July report from The Information suggested an unnamed Chinese company had begun manufacturing an immersion deep ultraviolet lithography (DUV) machine, citing people familiar with the matter.
ASML dominates the manufacturing of DUV machines, which are less advanced than EUV. China has been ramping up its domestic semiconductor supply chain, with some investors concerned it could challenge the European and U.S. dominance. However, analysts raised questions about China's ability to ramp up its own DUV technology. 
ASML meanwhile has faced challenges in China over the last few years. The company is restricted from selling EUV and some DUV tools to China.

Consensus is for the semiconductor equipment giant to record $12.47 in earnings per share (EPS), which would represent about a 94.5% increase on a year-over-year basis.
