ASML stock's year-to-date surge has not deterred options traders from betting on continued gains ahead. 
According to Barchart, the put-to-call ratio on contracts expiring Oct. 16 sits at 0.88x currently, indicating a bullish skew (a reading below 1.00x is typically characterized as in favor of the bulls). 
And the upper price on those options contracts is set at $1,783, signaling potential upside of about 4.58% in the semiconductor stock through the end of this week. 
On the flip side, however, the technical setup heading into ASML earnings is not constructive; the company slipped through its 50-day and 100-day moving averages (MAs) today, indicating bears are taking control across multiple timeframes. 
ASML Shares Continue to Ride the AI Wave 
For long-term investors, the bull case extends beyond an earnings beat. As chipmakers continue to expand their manufacturing capacity, ASML shares stand to benefit from improving visibility into future demand. 
The giant's planned 30% increase in low-NA EUV production capacity for 2027 further supports the argument that the ongoing AI investment cycle could translate into sustained business growth. 
ASML shares historically close each of the final three months of a calendar year in the green, a seasonal pattern that makes it even more attractive for the near term. 
Plus, a small 0.53% dividend yield serves as the cherry on top for prospective buyers. 
Wall Street Also Remains Bullish on ASML 
Investors could also take heart in the fact that Wall Street remains bullish on ASML stock for the remainder of 2026.

Strong operational performance at Oyu Tolgoi copper and Pilbara iron ore 
MELBOURNE, Australia, October 13, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )--Rio Tinto Chief Executive Simon Trott said: "We delivered strong operational performance in the third quarter. Oyu Tolgoi copper production increased 29% year-to-date, with the operation running at a ~450 kt annualised rate in the quarter, and global iron ore sales are up 3% year-to-date. The Simandou iron ore mine hit an annualised production run-rate of ~10 Mtpa (100% basis) in the quarter as the project continues to ramp up. 
"We are finishing the year with momentum, with significant opportunities to accelerate improvements in safety, productivity and reliability through implementation of our operating system. We remain on track for a $1.8 billion annualised productivity benefit run-rate by the end of 2026. Our major projects remain on schedule and budget, underwriting our growth profile to 2030. 
"We made further significant steps in decarbonising our business in the third quarter, with our Pacific Aluminium smelter repowering arrangements now well progressed. 
"Today, we announce that we have achieved more than $2 billion1 of capital release year-to-date, as we actively manage our portfolio with discipline to maximise long-term value, as part of the $5 to 10 billion capital release program." 
Executive Summary 
Operational excellence: ~1% YTD increase in copper equivalent (CuEq2) production, driven by growth from Oyu Tolgoi copper and Pilbara iron ore. 
Copper: Oyu Tolgoi production increased by 27% YoY in Q3 and 29% YTD. At Kennecott, we successfully completed the rebuild of the flash converting furnace at end-August ahead of plan. 
Iron ore: Q3 global iron ore sales were 90.8 Mt, up 3% YoY, while Pilbara sales increased 2% YoY. Simandou hit an annualised production run-rate of ~10 Mtpa (100% basis) in Q3 as the project ramps up and remains on track to reach a 60 Mtpa production run-rate during H2 20283. 
Aluminium : Consistent, stable performance across the full operating system. Pacific smelter repowering arrangements are now well progressed, following the Tomago and Bell Bay power agreements in Q3. 
Lithium : Production up 33% YTD despite adverse weather impacting Q3 operations. Fenix 1B ramp-up continues to progress well.

Infrastructure Projects in Sask. Receive More Than $73.5 Million in Funding
by MBC News | Oct 13, 2026 
Ten projects will improve water, wastewater, sewer and drainage infrastructure across Saskatchewan, including a La Ronge project aimed at supporting new housing development. 
Communities across Saskatchewan are set to receive more than $73.5 million in joint federal and provincial funding for infrastructure projects aimed at supporting housing and community growth.
The investment includes $40.1 million from the federal government and $33.4 million from Saskatchewan through the Provincial and Territorial Agreement stream of the Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund. Ten water supply and wastewater infrastructure projects will receive support.
“Strong, reliable infrastructure is essential to the health, growth and long-term success of communities across Saskatchewan,” Rural Development Secretary of State Buckley Belanger said. “By working together with our partners, we are helping communities address critical infrastructure needs while supporting new housing, economic opportunities and a strong quality of life for residents.”
Government Relations Minister Eric Schmalz said infrastructure investment is an important part of supporting growth across Saskatchewan.
“People raise their families and businesses in Saskatchewan because of our strong economy, our vibrant people and our commitment to long-term, sustainable growth,” Schmalz said. “We are excited that these projects are moving forward so residents can benefit from modern, reliable infrastructure that make our communities strong and safe now and for generations to come.”
La Ronge project to support new housing
In La Ronge, sanitary sewer infrastructure along Bedford Drive and Louis Road will be extended to support the construction of two residential apartment buildings.
The project will include 860 metres of sewer main connecting the development sites to a nearby sewage pumping station and is expected to enable approximately 124 new housing units.
The project is receiving $643,800 from the federal government, $536,446 from Saskatchewan and $429,254 in municipal funding.
“This funding from the Government of Canada and the Province of Saskatchewan through the Canada Housing and Infrastructure Fund, combined with the Town of La Ronge’s contributions, will help realize a significant housing project for the community that will go a long way in alleviating the existing housing shortage,” La Ronge Mayor Joe Hordyski said.
Hordyski said the development will also provide accommodations for people coming to work in the community, including those connected to the new long-term care facility and regional RCMP detachment.
Yorkton receives major investment
In Yorkton, funding will support the first phase of the Water Pollution Control Plant Renewal Project.
The project will increase the wastewater treatment capacity of the H.M. Bailey Water Pollution Control Plant’s Headworks facility. It will receive $20 million federally, $16.665 million provincially and $13.335 million from the municipality.
“This is a significant day for Yorkton. This funding represents the largest grant our city has ever received and allows us to begin the Water Pollution Control Plant Renewal Project, the largest infrastructure project in Yorkton’s history,” Yorkton Mayor Aaron Kienle said.
Projects across Saskatchewan
The funding will support infrastructure work in 10 Saskatchewan communities.
In Arcola, the work includes new municipal wells, a water treatment plant and related water infrastructure, while Big River will expand its municipal water and sanitary sewer systems. Estevan will see an expansion of its wastewater pumping, storage and sewer infrastructure.
Shellbrook will upgrade its existing water treatment plant, while Swift Current will construct a new water transmission main aimed at improving capacity and reliability.
Meanwhile, Warman will undertake drainage improvements in areas prone to surface flooding.
Naicam will develop an infrastructure master plan to guide decisions through 2050, while the RM of St. Louis No. 431 will study options for upgrading or expanding the Bellevue lagoon.
The remaining projects include the sewer extension in La Ronge and the first phase of Yorkton’s Water Pollution Control Plant renewal.

Source: Rivian 
Doug Field, the engineer who ran Tesla’s Model 3 program and later Ford’s entire EV operation, is now president of Mind Robotics, the industrial robotics startup Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe spun out of Rivian last year.
He lands at a company that has now raised more than $1 billion in under a year, and he’ll run product, engineering, and operations alongside Scaringe.
Field’s next job is robots
Field’s résumé reads like a tour of the most ambitious hardware programs in the industry. He was Tesla’s SVP of Engineering through the Model 3 launch, ran Apple’s car effort inside its Special Projects Group, and then spent nearly five years at Ford as chief EV, digital and design officer.
We reported in April that Ford was folding Field’s EV group into manufacturing as he left the company . Ford didn’t replace him with an outside hire, and his department ended up under COO Kumar Galhotra. Five months later, he has his next job.
Advertisement - scroll for more content 
In Mind’s announcement, Scaringe called Field “a remarkable leader with a track record of delivering new technologies in successful products,” adding that’s “exactly what Mind needs as we deploy robots into real factories and beyond.”
Field called the combination of AI and robotics “one of the most important—and difficult—engineering challenges of our time.”
A $1 billion war chest and a factory to practice in
Mind Robotics first surfaced as part of Rivian’s Q3 2025 earnings report , with a $115 million seed round led by Eclipse. The money has piled up fast since then:
$115 million seed, led by Eclipse (late 2025)
$500 million Series A, co-led by Accel and Andreessen Horowitz (March 2026)
$400 million round led by Kleiner Perkins (May 2026), which Reuters reported valued Mind at $3.4 billion
That’s roughly $1 billion for a company that hasn’t shown a product publicly. Mind says it’s building foundation models plus “purpose-built” robot hardware for dexterous manufacturing work. It hasn’t said whether any of that hardware is humanoid.
Mind’s real edge is its access. Rivian is a major shareholder and its launch customer, which gives the startup a live, high-volume auto plant to collect training data and deploy robots in. And that plant is busy: the R2 is ramping in Normal, Illinois, and Rivian delivered 19,248 vehicles in Q3 alone.
The Tesla comparison is unavoidable
Field’s hire puts Mind on a direct collision course with the program Tesla now uses to justify much of its valuation: Optimus.
Tesla’s track record there isn’t great. Elon Musk predicted about 10,000 Optimus robots built in 2025, with roughly 1,000 doing useful work in Tesla factories by year-end. In January, he admitted none were doing “useful work.” Tesla then ended Model S and Model X production at Fremont to convert those lines for Optimus, and it has pushed back the Optimus V3 reveal repeatedly . In July, Musk said production would be “extremely slow at first” .
Mind is taking a quieter route. No stage demos, no unit targets. Just robots trained on a real assembly line, with a customer that already owns a stake in the company.
Electrek’s Take
This is a smart hire.
Field is a hardware industrialization guy. That’s his whole career: taking a product that works in a lab and making it work at volume. The Model 3 got to mass production on his watch. It was messy, and he took a leave at the height of “production hell” in 2018 before leaving Tesla, but the car shipped and became the best-selling EV in the world for years.
Top comment by Belafonte 
Liked by 7 people 
Field also led the effort to build zonal architecture at Ford. That failed miserabaly and then he tried downplaying it by saying zonal architecture doesn't matter. 
This guy hasn't had any success in the past ten years and has actively advocated against the very technology that has kept Rivian afloat recently. Not a lot of confidence this hire will work out for Rivian.
View all comments 
His record since then is more mixed. The Apple car was canceled after he left. At Ford, Model e lost more than $5 billion in 2024 alone, and the company has since scaled back its EV ambitions. But the low-cost Universal EV Platform and the $30,000 midsize pickup coming out of Louisville in 2027 are his team’s work, and that’s the most promising thing Ford has going in EVs.
So why does Mind need him? Because foundation models are the easy part to fundraise on. Getting robot hardware reliable enough to run shifts in a car plant is where everyone, Tesla included, has struggled.
It also tells us how serious Scaringe is about this. He’s running Rivian through the most important launch in its history, plus Also and now Mind. Bringing in a president with Field’s profile is how you keep Mind from becoming a side project while focusing your needed attention on Rivian.

Boeing delivers 57 aircraft in September as orders surge to 165 jets
Deliveries reached their highest monthly level of 2026, with Turkish Airlines accounting for 100 orders and the 737 MAX leading production
Ricardo Meier 
October 13, 2026 17:58 
Boeing delivered 57 aircraft in September 2026, its highest monthly total of the year, an increase of 11.8% from the 51 jets delivered in August and 3.6% above the 55 recorded in September 2025. 
The U.S. aircraft manufacturer also secured 165 gross orders during the month, compared with just 15 in August. The increase was largely driven by Turkish Airlines, which ordered 100 Boeing 737 MAX passenger jets.
According to figures released on October 13, Boeing delivered 43 737 MAX aircraft, eight 787 Dreamliners, two 777 freighters and four 767s during September.
The company has delivered 475 aircraft in the first nine months of 2026, compared with 440 during the same period last year, an increase of 8%. The total includes 363 737 MAX jets, the highest number delivered by the program during the first nine months of any year.
September also brought Boeing's third-quarter deliveries to 161 aircraft, narrowly above the 160 recorded during the corresponding quarter of 2025.
Boeing 737 MAX 10 Aviation Capital Group 737 MAX leads deliveries
The 737 MAX accounted for approximately 75% of Boeing's September deliveries, with 43 aircraft handed over to airlines and leasing companies.
Southwest Airlines was the largest individual recipient, taking nine jets, followed by United Airlines with five and VietJet Air with four.
Flydubai and Norwegian Air each received three aircraft, while Singapore Airlines and Virgin Australia took one each.
Leasing companies accounted for another significant portion of the deliveries. AerCap received six 737 MAX jets, followed by Aviation Capital Group and Dubai Aerospace Enterprise with three each.
CDB Leasing took two aircraft, while Bank of Communications Leasing, Everbright Financial Leasing and SMBC Aviation Capital received one each.
Boeing also delivered eight 787 Dreamliners, comprising seven 787-9s and one 787-10.
United Airlines received four 787-9s, while SMBC Aviation Capital took two and Qatar Airways received one. Korean Air was the recipient of the month's only 787-10.
Freighter deliveries included two 777Fs, one each for Air China Cargo and FedEx Express, and a 767-300F for UPS.
The remaining three aircraft were 767-2Cs delivered to Boeing's defense business for completion as KC-46A Pegasus aerial refueling tankers.
Turkish Airlines Boeing 737 MAX jets | Boeing Turkish Airlines dominates new orders
Boeing recorded 165 gross orders in September, more than ten times the 15 aircraft booked in August and above the 96 gross orders registered in September 2025.
The 737 MAX accounted for 132 orders, led by Turkish Airlines with 100 aircraft. Lufthansa ordered another 20 jets, while Biman Bangladesh Airlines placed an order for six. The remaining six were attributed to unidentified customers.
The 787 Dreamliner generated 23 orders, including five 787-10s for Biman Bangladesh Airlines .

Boeing reported no order cancellations in September.
The manufacturer accumulated 618 net orders during the first nine months of 2026, although this figure differs from gross orders because it accounts for cancellations and other adjustments.

Boeing's 475 deliveries through September included 367 aircraft from the 737 family, 62 Dreamliners, 26 767s and 20 aircraft from the 777 family.
The 737 total includes 363 MAX aircraft, with the remaining deliveries attributed to other variants of the family.
The manufacturer is working to increase 737 MAX production toward 47 aircraft per month, although Boeing Chief Executive Kelly Ortberg acknowledged in September that the production increase has taken longer than expected.
Boeing ended September with an official backlog of 6,371 aircraft, compared with 6,156 at the end of August, an increase of 215.
Despite its higher order intake, Boeing remained behind Airbus in deliveries during September. The European manufacturer handed over 72 aircraft, compared with Boeing's 57.

content_text:
Slow-Release Alkalinity Turns Slag Cement Into a Stronger, Greener Binder
by 
October 13, 2026 
in 
Technology 
Reading Time: 6 mins read
0 
Slow-Release Alkalinity Turns Slag Cement Into a Stronger, Greener Binder
Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on Linkedin Share on Reddit Share on Telegram 
Concrete is everywhere, and so is its carbon problem. Producing ordinary Portland cement releases roughly 0.83 tons of carbon dioxide for every ton of cement made, and global cement production now accounts for around 7.5 percent of all human-caused carbon emissions. As construction industries worldwide scramble to decarbonize, a family of low-carbon binders known as sulfate-activated cementitious materials has attracted intense attention. These materials replace the bulk of cement with industrial wastes such as granulated blast furnace slag, steel slag, and Bayer red mud, using sulfates like gypsum under mildly alkaline conditions to awaken the latent reactivity of the waste glass. Now, a new study published in Case Studies in Construction Materials by Jixiang Wang, Ninghui Sun, Dongmin Wang, and Bo Liu reveals a surprisingly subtle chemical principle that governs whether these green binders turn out strong or weak: the speed at which alkalinity is released, not just how much is supplied.
Sulfate-activated slag cements are environmentally attractive for several reasons. They require no high-temperature calcination, they can incorporate very high levels of industrial by-products, and their main hydration products, needle-like ettringite crystals and low-calcium aluminum-containing C-A-S-H gel, give the hardened paste excellent resistance to sulfate and chloride attack. Their modest hydration heat also helps avoid the thermal cracking that plagues massive concrete pours. These traits make them promising candidates for marine engineering, construction in saline-alkali environments, and subgrade stabilization. Yet one stubborn flaw has kept them from widespread adoption: at early ages, their hydration is sluggish. Slag barely reacts in pure water, and a dense protective layer of C-A-S-H rapidly forms on particle surfaces, choking off further reaction. The result is prolonged setting times and disappointing early strength.
Previous work showed that adding an alkaline boost, for instance quicklime or Portland cement clinker, can break the slag glass structure open and accelerate early strength gain. But the system is notoriously sensitive to alkali content and type, and too much alkali can actually reduce strength. What remained missing was a mechanistic, microscopic understanding of how different alkaline activators reshape slag dissolution kinetics, hydration product formation, and microstructural evolution. To close this gap, the team designed an elegant comparative experiment using three clinker-based activators arranged along a gradient of mineralogy and hydraulic reactivity. Ordinary Portland cement clinker, rich in highly reactive C3S and C3A phases, served as the fast, high-alkalinity benchmark. High-belite clinker, dominated by the slow-hydrating C2S phase, represented a lower-carbon, moderate-reactivity alternative. And fully hydrated cement paste powder, containing no unreacted clinker at all, acted as a pure chemical control that simply releases calcium hydroxide to supply alkalinity, cleanly separating chemical activation from any physical contribution of active clinker hydration.
The researchers blended each activator at 5 percent into a mix of 80 percent blast furnace slag and 5 percent gypsum, keeping a constant water-to-binder ratio of 0.40, and then deployed an impressive battery of techniques: isothermal calorimetry to track heat release over five days, in situ X-ray diffraction with Rietveld refinement to quantify evolving phases within the first twelve hours, pore solution extraction followed by ICP-OES analysis, thermodynamic modeling with PHREEQC, thermogravimetric analysis, scanning electron microscopy, low-field nuclear magnetic resonance for real-time pore structure monitoring, autogenous shrinkage measurements, and standard compressive strength testing. The reference mix without any activator remained unset even after three days of curing, underscoring how essential alkaline activation is to this system.
The strength results told a striking story. Even the weakest activated system, the one using fully hydrated paste powder, exceeded 8 megapascals at three days, while the reference only began to harden after a week. But the standout performer was the high-belite clinker system, which achieved the highest compressive strength at every curing age tested. This was puzzling at first, because the three activators should theoretically deliver comparable total alkalinity, roughly 1.65 percent calcium hydroxide from the ordinary clinker and 1.58 percent from the high-belite clinker upon complete hydration. Since the chemistry of supply was similar, the difference had to lie in the timing and kinetics of alkalinity release, driven by the intrinsic mineralogy of each clinker.
The calorimetry and in situ XRD data unraveled this paradox. In the ordinary clinker system, the heat flow curve showed four distinct stages, including a weak early peak from the very reactive C3A and a pronounced shoulder from rapid C3S hydration starting around six hours. Once C3S hydration began, slag consumption and C-A-S-H gel formation accelerated dramatically, confirming that a timely supply of hydroxide ions depolymerizes the slag glass network. In the high-belite system, the main reaction peak appeared roughly four hours later, but when it arrived it burned hotter, ultimately producing the greatest cumulative heat release and the highest degree of slag reaction by twelve hours. Pore solution analysis showed why: the ordinary clinker rapidly pushed the pH above 12, while the high-belite clinker raised alkalinity more gradually, maintaining a moderate, sustained supersaturation rather than a chemical jolt.
That difference in timing proved decisive for how ettringite, the system’s key crystalline hydration product, grew. Electron microscopy revealed that in the fast-release systems, the rapid pH spike created extreme local supersaturation, triggering burst-like homogeneous nucleation. Thousands of tiny ettringite crystals formed almost simultaneously, but with limited growth space and ionic supply they stayed small and poorly interlocked, producing a loose, porous microstructure. In the slow-release high-belite system, moderate and persistent supersaturation allowed thermodynamically controlled crystal growth instead. Ions deposited in an orderly fashion onto existing nuclei, developing large, well-defined needle-like and prismatic crystals that bridged pores and built a robust load-bearing skeleton. In other words, the strength advantage came not from making more hydration product, but from shaping its crystallization kinetics.
Low-field nuclear magnetic resonance captured the pore structure consequences in real time. In the ordinary clinker system, the dominant relaxation peak first shifted toward shorter times as pores refined, then reversed and coarsened dramatically, with the maximum relaxation time climbing from 2.76 milliseconds at twelve hours to 8.96 milliseconds at forty-eight hours, even higher than the fresh paste. This coarsening coincided with rapid ettringite precipitation driven by locally excessive alkalinity. The high-belite system, by contrast, showed sustained pore refinement throughout the observation window with essentially no coarsening, and the fully hydrated paste control showed pronounced coarsening at later ages. Autogenous shrinkage measurements reinforced the picture: all pastes expanded slightly, with the ordinary clinker system showing roughly 1.05 percent strain, about double that of the high-belite system, and the team concluded that excessive early ettringite-driven expansion generates internal microcracks that undermine strength development.
Synthesizing these results, the authors propose a clear regulatory mechanism. The hydrolysis of clinker-based activators provides the alkaline environment, around pH 12, needed for slag dissolution, but the rate and stability of alkalinity development play the decisive role. Highly reactive clinkers dump calcium hydroxide quickly, paradoxically suppressing early slag dissolution and promoting concentrated burst nucleation of fine ettringite, which yields a loose microstructure, elevated expansion, internal stresses, and restricted strength. Slow-release activators maintain a moderate, persistent supersaturation that favors oriented crystal growth, dense pore filling, and a homogeneous, stable matrix, while the activator’s own hydration still exceeds that of the slag and boosts early strength.
The implications reach well beyond the laboratory. Because sulfate-activated slag systems inherently expand slightly, precise microstructural control is especially critical for their engineering use, and this study demonstrates that selecting an activator with the right hydration reactivity can balance nucleation against growth, avoiding premature localized ettringite formation and detrimental expansion. High-belite clinker, itself a lower-carbon product with a dominant slow-hydrating phase, now emerges as a particularly attractive partner for slag-based binders. The researchers caution that their work covered a limited set of activators and testing durations, and they call for future studies to span broader activator systems, quantitative models linking hydroxide release kinetics to microstructural evolution, and long-term durability plus full life-cycle environmental assessment. Still, the core lesson is already compelling for anyone watching the cement industry’s decarbonization race: in green cement chemistry, as in many other fields, patience beats brute force, and a slow, steady supply of alkalinity builds a stronger material than a fast one ever can.

content_text:
AVL and VisIC reveal GaN-based EV traction inverter
Tuesday 13th October 2026
Demonstrator vehicle uses D³GaN power modules in an advanced electric drivetrain 
VisIC, a developer of high-power GaN chips, and AVL, a mobility technology company, have worked together on integrating VisIC's D³GaN power module technology into AVL's vehicle demonstrator.
The demonstrator combines a high-speed e-axle, advanced power electronics and vehicle control technologies, with a GaN traction inverter using VisIC power modules. The overall project brings together technology from AVL, NXP Semiconductors and VisIC Technologies. 
It builds on a two year collaboration between AVL and VisIC. In earlier Dyno WLTC testing at AVL facilities in Germany, an inverter based on VisIC's GaN-on-Silicon D³GaN technology is claimed to have achieved 99.67 percent efficiency at 10 kHz and more than 99.8 percent at 5 kHz on AVL's e-motor test bench. The companies reported an improvement compared with comparable SiC inverters and a reduction of inverter energy losses of more than 60 percent under the tested conditions.
The inverter development used VisIC's D³GaN technology, NXP driver, AVL's PI850e Inverter Development Platform and AVL control software.
According to the company, integration into the vehicle demonstrator now enables the technology to be evaluated within a complete electric drivetrain environment and illustrates how the efficiency advantages of GaN can translate from semiconductor and inverter performance into vehicle-level benefits.
EV traction inverters operate across a wide range of speed, torque and load conditions. VisIC say its D³GaN technology is designed to combine low switching and conduction losses with high power density for high-power automotive applications.
The benefits can be particularly important during partial-load operation where reducing switching losses can improve inverter efficiency and reduce cooling requirements. Current 400V battery technology is especially attractive for PHEV and Range extended HEV cars. At vehicle level, this creates the potential for a more compact power-electronics system, improved drivetrain efficiency and increased driving range.
"Bringing D³GaN from the test bench into a fully operational vehicle is an important milestone for high-power GaN," said Tamara Baksht, VisIC Technologies' CEO. "The AVL demonstrator shows that GaN is no longer limited to discussing future potential. We can demonstrate the technology in the traction inverter of a real electric vehicle and show automotive manufacturers what higher efficiency, lower losses and higher power density can mean at system level."
"Integrating a GaN traction inverter into a vehicle demonstrator is an important step in understanding the opportunities and challenges of bringing this technology into future automotive applications," said Mathias Deiml, technical lead GaN Inverter Development, AVL Software and Functions. "The project combines semiconductor innovation with system-level development expertise and allows to push forward the state of the art regarding efficiency and advanced functionality."
The collaboration between AVL and VisIC Technologies is also intended to support the development of scalable GaN solutions for future EV architectures. The companies previously announced plans to extend the GaN-on-Silicon platform toward 800V GaN power modules, addressing the growing adoption of higher-voltage battery and drivetrain systems.

Veolia Sues Milwaukee Sewerage District Over $700M Jacobs Contract
A judge has paused contract finalization until the lawsuit is resolved
By Annemarie Mannion 
Photo courtesy of the Milwaukee Metropolitan Sewerage District
Jacob Solutions won a $700M operations and maintenance contract for the Milwaukee Metropolitan Sewerage District, but Veolia Milwaukee has filed a lawsuit seeking to keep the contract from being finalized. 
October 13, 2026
The Milwaukee Metropolitan Sewerage District awarded a $700-million , 10-year operations and maintenance contract on Sept. 28 to Dallas-based Jacobs Solutions , but its longtime contractor, Veolia Milwaukee , has filed a lawsuit against the agency seeking a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction before the contract is executed.
The lawsuit , filed in September in U.S. district court in Milwaukee, alleges that the agency's competitive procurement process, which took place over two years, was predetermined and unfairly structured to favor Jacobs for the new operations and maintenance contract, planned to start in March 2028.
U.S. District Judge Brett Ludwig this month paused finalization of the contract until the lawsuit is resolved.
In the lawsuit, Veolia states it has managed district operations and maintenance since 2008 in what it terms the largest public-private water partnership in North America. The scope includes operation and maintenance of two water reclamation facilities with combined capacity of 630 million gal per day, a 361-mile collection system, biosolids production and the 500-million gal Deep Tunnel storage system. Veolia's current contract is valued at $500 million. 
Veolia's complaint argues that the district's RFP process did not actually select the winning bidder based on the stated criteria. Instead, it claims the request was used to give the appearance of competition while implementing a decision the defendant had already made or was predisposed to make. Additionally, the company alleges that advocacy groups and elected officials began campaigning against it in early 2026 and sought to influence the procurement.
Common Ground of Southeastern Wisconsin, a non-partisan advocacy group, notes on its website that it investigated allegations of mismanagement of the wastewater management system by Veolia and that it interviewed current and former employees of the company and district, reviewed hundreds of pages of public records and consulted experts, stakeholders and public officials. Former district Director of Intergovernmental Relations Steve Jacquart, who served in the position for 19 years, later identified himself as the first whistleblower and joined Common Ground’s campaign, and other former agency and company employees then came forward with allegations about the firm’s management of the wastewater system. 
Common Ground alleges that Veolia failed to properly maintain equipment, falsified water quality reports, performed inaccurate sewage dumps, failed to provide safe worker conditions, did not maintain proper staffing levels and employed unqualified persons. Also, the organization alleged district staff did not properly monitor Veolia’s management of facilities.
Trading Arguments 
Responding to those allegations in May, Veolia Senior Vice President Adam Lisberg said in a statement that the "company stands firmly behind the performance and integrity of our team, operating an extremely complex system under rigorous regulatory oversight to meet [agency], state and federal standards," according to Urban Milwaukee . 
He added that “Veolia encourages all employees to report any workplace concerns, even anonymously, whether directly to their supervisors or through additional channels we’ve established to report issues without fear of retaliation.” 
The district has denied Veolia’s allegations that it manipulated its procurement process to favor Jacobs Solutions.
In response to the lawsuit, rhe district says the RFP established four criteria for evaluating proposals: pricing (60%); company’s overall approach (25%); staffing, training and corporate culture (10%); and regional partnership (5%). 
The district confirms that its ad hoc committee recommended Jacobs on Aug. 17, giving the firm 96.8 points compared to Veolia's 84.9. It also acknowledges substantial differences in proposed sewer-cleaning prices. For one category, Jacobs proposed $5.54 per linear foot compared with Veolia's $54. The distrct says it evaluated Jacobs' rates against recent bids for similar work and found its pricing reasonable.
The Jacobs overall bid was $54 million lower than Veolia’s.
At a meeting in 2025, Veolia asserts that district Executive Director Kevin Shafer told the committee it would compare proposal pricing line-by-line specifically to screen out unrealistic, below-market rates: "So if someone undercuts one or overcuts one, we'll compare line items, then to make sure that we feel comfortable with whoever we select," he said.
Wisconsin law does not allow an unsuccessful bidder to recover damages for losing a public contract, meaning its only meaningful remedy is to stop the award before the contract is signed and work begins, Veolia notes.
The district argues that Veolia's lawsuit should be dismissed because procurement decisions involve discretionary governmental functions protected under Wisconsin law. It says Veolia has failed to identify a law that the district violated, that Wisconsin law does not prohibit public input into government procurement decisions and that no law requires the district to restart the procurement process. 
Jacobs Solutions' bid for the contract also did not go entirely smoothly after its relationship with Palantir Technologies became a point of controversy . 
Jacobs initially proposed using Palantir's technology but later agreed to remove the company following objections from community organizations about the tech firm's work with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), including providing data used in immigration enforcement. 
The district serves 29 communities across a 423-square-mile area in southeastern Wisconsin. 
Jacobs said in a statement that it "appreciates the confidence and trust the Milwaukee Metropolitan Sewerage District, its commissioners and the ad hoc committee have placed in us, and we look forward to the work ahead, working side by side with MMSD."

ETEL Announces Metis HP—A New High-Precision XY Air Bearing Stage for Step-and-Scan Semiconductor Applications
Heidenhain Corporation 
October 13, 2026 2 min read 
Heidenhain Corporation HEIDENHAIN Metis HP Stage 
HEIDENHAIN Metis HP Stage SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- ETEL , the leading supplier of high-performance motion control components and complete motion platforms, is proud to introduce the METIS HP, a new full air bearing planar platform designed for the most demanding step‑and‑scan semiconductor applications, including direct laser writing and high‑resolution optical inspection systems. With this new product, ETEL further strengthens its position as a leader in high-precision motion control by delivering a solution that combines exceptional speed and stability, outstanding dynamic straightness, and projected tool‑point measurement capability. 
"Building on ETEL's long‑standing expertise in high‑precision platforms, the METIS HP provides the trajectory quality required for advanced optical processes," said Stéphane Pellegrini, Product Manager at ETEL. "Its remarkable speed stability and dynamic straightness ensure consistent performance even at high scanning velocities. Supporting panel sizes up to 600 mm × 600 mm, the METIS HP addresses the growing need for next‑generation maskless lithography with large‑area substrates." 
At the core of the METIS HP is a multi‑degree‑of‑freedom (mDoF) HEIDENHAIN encoder, ensuring accuracy without thermal drift. This architecture enables projected tool‑point measurement. ETEL controllers can emulate a transistor-transistor logic (TTL) position signal for use as a trigger event. This innovative solution is a very compelling alternative to the classical interferometer used as an advanced trigger generator. With the METIS HP, there is no need for a mirror to be added on the carriage, no air lensing effect or air perturbation, and a lower cost. 
The METIS HP delivers outstanding performance, including ±150 nm accuracy over the full XY stroke after mapping, ±150 nm dynamic straightness at speeds up to 1 m/s, and dynamic capabilities reaching accelerations up to 20 m/s². These capabilities minimize turnaround time, thereby increasing machine throughput for step-and-scan applications. 
High-end inspection applications for advanced packaging require rapid and precise focal-distance adjustments. With its high-bandwidth 4-DoF module providing fine control over the Z, tip, tilt, and theta axes, METIS HP is the optimal platform for these demanding inspection tasks. 
The METIS HP is now available for OEM integration. For further information, visit ETEL's website at https://www.etel.ch/contact/ . Or visit ETEL at the HEIDENHAIN Booth 1639 during SEMICON West, taking place October 13-15, 2026, in San Francisco.

content_text:
AVL and VisIC Bring High-Power GaN Traction Inverter Technology to the Road
News provided by
VisIC Technologies
13 Oct, 2026, 15:00 IDT
Share this article
Share this article
The demonstrator vehicle showcases VisIC D³GaN power modules in an advanced AVL electric drivetrain, taking high-power GaN from test bench validation to a complete vehicle environment. The same D³GaN platform expends to power AI data centers and physical AI to benefit from high efficiency, compact size and reliability. 
The potential of the efficient evaluated D³GaN semiconductor platform in modern time is hard to overestimate. 
NESS ZIONA, Israel , Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- VisIC Technologies , a developer of high-power gallium nitride (GaN) semiconductor solutions, and AVL , one of the world's leading mobility technology companies, are advancing their collaboration with the integration of VisIC's D³GaN power module technology into AVL's vehicle demonstrator .
The vehicle provides a real-world development platform for evaluating next-generation electric propulsion technologies and demonstrates the potential of high-power GaN in one of the most demanding EV applications: the traction inverter. Evaluated under demanding conditions for power electronics, the demonstrator combines a high-speed e-axle, advanced power electronics and vehicle control technologies, with a GaN traction inverter using VisIC power modules. The overall project brings together technology from AVL, NXP Semiconductors and VisIC Technologies. 
The program marks an important step in the evolution of GaN for electric mobility, moving VisIC's D³GaN technology from laboratory and dynamometer testing into a fully operational vehicle platform.
From Record Efficiency to a Complete Vehicle 
The demonstrator builds on collaboration between AVL and VisIC Technologies started in 2024. In earlier Dyno WLTC testing at AVL facilities in Germany, an inverter based on VisIC's GaN-on-Silicon D³GaN technology achieved 99.67% efficiency at 10 kHz and more than 99.8% at 5 kHz on AVL's e-motor test bench. The companies reported an improvement compared with comparable SiC inverters and a reduction of inverter energy losses of more than 60% under the tested conditions.
The inverter development used VisIC's D³GaN technology, NXP driver, AVL's PI850e Inverter Development Platform and AVL control software.
Integration into the vehicle demonstrator now enables the technology to be evaluated within a complete electric drivetrain environment and illustrates how the efficiency advantages of GaN can translate from semiconductor and inverter performance into vehicle-level benefits.
Why GaN Matters in Real-World Mobility 
EV traction inverters operate across a wide range of speed, torque and load conditions. VisIC's D³GaN technology is designed to combine low switching and conduction losses with high power density for high-power automotive applications.
The benefits can be particularly important during partial-load operation where reducing switching losses can improve inverter efficiency and reduce cooling requirements. Current 400V battery technology is especially attractive for PHEV and Range extended HEV cars. At vehicle level, this creates the potential for a more compact power-electronics system, improved drivetrain efficiency and increased driving range.
The AVL demonstrator therefore provides more than a showcase of peak efficiency. It illustrates how GaN technology can operate as part of a complete high-performance EV drivetrain.
Automotive-Evaluated GaN for AIDC and Physical AI Power 
Evaluated in the demanding automotive environment, VisIC's D³GaN platform delivers the efficiency, power density and reliability required for next-generation power conversion. These same capabilities make the platform an excellent fit for AIDC infrastructure, where rapidly growing AI workloads require compact, highly efficient and scalable power supplies with lower energy losses and reduced cooling demand.
The platform is equally well suited to physical AI applications—including robotics, autonomous systems and intelligent industrial equipment—where power electronics must combine fast dynamic response, high efficiency, compact size and dependable operation under demanding conditions. Automotive validation therefore provides a strong foundation for deploying D³GaN across the emerging AI power ecosystem.
"Bringing D³GaN from the test bench into a fully operational vehicle is an important milestone for high-power GaN," said Tamara Baksht, VisIC Technologies' CEO . "The AVL demonstrator shows that GaN is no longer limited to discussing future potential. We can demonstrate the technology in the traction inverter of a real electric vehicle and show automotive manufacturers what higher efficiency, lower losses and higher power density can mean at system level." 
"Integrating a GaN traction inverter into a vehicle demonstrator is an important step in understanding the opportunities and challenges of bringing this technology into future automotive applications," said Mathias Deiml, Technical Lead GaN Inverter Development, AVL Software and Functions . "The project combines semiconductor innovation with system-level development expertise and allows to push forward the state of the art regarding efficiency and advanced functionality." 
"This project demonstrates how strong collaboration can accelerate the development of emerging technologies for e-mobility," said Dr. Thomas Frey, Head of Segment E-Mobility & E-Drive System, AVL Software and Functions. "By combining VisIC's semiconductor expertise with AVL's capabilities in inverter development and vehicle integration, we have established a platform for assessing the future potential of GaN technology in electric powertrains." 
Building Toward 800V GaN 
The collaboration between AVL and VisIC Technologies is also intended to support the development of scalable GaN solutions for future EV architectures. The companies previously announced plans to extend the GaN-on-Silicon platform toward 800V GaN power modules , addressing the growing adoption of higher-voltage battery and drivetrain systems.
VisIC's GaN-on-Silicon approach also provides a potential manufacturing scalability advantage because the technology can leverage established silicon semiconductor manufacturing infrastructure. The companies have previously highlighted compatibility with 200 mm and 300 mm silicon foundries as part of the technology's path toward high-volume production.
With the AVL vehicle demonstrator, the companies are taking another step toward bringing high-power GaN into mainstream electric propulsion, demonstrating that GaN has the potential to become a practical alternative for the next generation of EV traction inverters.
About VisIC Technologies 
VisIC Technologies develops high-power GaN semiconductor solutions for power-electronics applications including electric vehicles, renewable energy, data centers, AI infrastructure and industrial systems. Its proprietary D³GaN technology is designed to provide high efficiency, power density and scalable manufacturing for demanding power-conversion applications.

Mkango Magnetic Materials Ltd. (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) said HyProMag USA has secured power capacity with Oncor Electric Delivery Company for its planned Texas rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing hub.
The power allocation covers the initial cutting and finishing operation and the proposed Phase 1 development , with a pathway to additional capacity for Phase 2 through a substation upgrade.
HyProMag USA expects the electricity supplied to the facility to come predominantly from renewable energy sources .
PegasusTSI has started a contractor-selection process for the cutting and finishing facility, while Weston Solutions is progressing permitting activities.
The first stage is targeted for commissioning during the first half of 2027 .
That operation will not initially manufacture magnet blocks from recycled material in Texas. Instead, it is designed to cut, finish and qualify NdFeB magnet blocks supplied from other HyProMag Group operations .
The facility is intended to establish US finishing capability, customer qualification processes and workforce training ahead of the larger integrated development.
HyProMag USA plans to operate to recognised magnetic-material and quality standards, including ASTM A977/A977M and systems aligned with ISO 9001.
The larger Phase 1 Texas Hub is targeted for completion in mid-2028 . It is designed to produce approximately 550 tonnes per annum of sintered NdFeB magnet blocks and finished magnets , together with around 484 tonnes of co-products, giving approximately 1,034 tonnes per annum of total payable production .
A subsequent Phase 2 expansion envisages approximately 1,048 tonnes per annum of NdFeB magnet blocks and cylinders plus 478 tonnes of co-products, taking total payable production to approximately 1,526 tonnes per annum .
Importantly, those figures are design capacities rather than current production or confirmed future output .
CoTec chief executive Julian Treger said securing power, advancing permitting and commencing contractor selection further de-risk the project and support the goal of establishing a domestic US rare earth magnet supply chain.
For investors, the significance is that the Texas Hub is moving from engineering and planning towards site infrastructure, permitting and contractor procurement .
The next tangible milestones are the award of construction contracts, permitting progress and successful commissioning of the initial cutting and finishing operation in H1 2027 , followed by execution of the larger integrated Phase 1 development targeted for 2028.

Integrated Power Services Acquires Bold Renewables to Expand Solar Services
October 13, 2026 
Staff 
Solar 
From: Mercom India 
Integrated Power Services (IPS), a provider of power management lifecycle services, has acquired Colorado-based Bold Renewables , a solar inverter maintenance and field services company, effective October 9, 2026.
The financial terms of the acquisition were not disclosed.
Headquartered in Windsor, Bold Renewables provides original equipment manufacturer (OEM) field services, spare parts, and preventive maintenance for Advanced Energy central solar inverters under the Solaron, NX, TX, and PV Powered brands.
The company supports approximately 14,000 legacy solar inverters with a combined installed capacity of over 4 GW across more than 3,000 solar sites in the U.S. and Canada.
Bold holds the original OEM design drawings, blueprints, and firmware for these inverter platforms. It provides proprietary spare parts, technical support, preventive maintenance, and field services through technicians across North America. The company reports an average inverter uptime of 99%. Its customers include independent power producers, utilities, solar asset managers, site owners, and operations and maintenance service providers.
Following the acquisition, Bold will join IPS’ Motion division within its renewable energy services group, alongside ENA Electronics and IPS Folcroft.
The combined platform is expected to align solar and wind power electronics expertise, field service, engineering, component repair, logistics, and inventory resources to provide more complete support for renewable energy customers.
Headquartered in Greenville, South Carolina, IPS provides repair, field services, and replacement solutions for power infrastructure across North America, the United Kingdom, and the Caribbean.
IPS’s Motion and Electrification divisions provide lifecycle services for power management ecosystem, including battery energy storage systems, transformers, and switchgear, across fleets comprising equipment from multiple manufacturers.
In the first half of 2026, corporate M&A activity in the solar sector increased to 57 transactions, compared to 50 transactions in 1H 2025, as per Mercom’s 1H and Q2 2026 Solar Funding and M&A Report .
In March 2026, ABB, a Switzerland-based industrial conglomerate specializing in electrification and automation, announced the acquisition of Gamesa Electric’s power electronics business in Spain from renewable energy developer Siemens Gamesa.

Transfer Membrane Market Sees 2026 PVDF Launch as High-Sensitivity Protein Detection Gains Attention
10-13-2026 11:34 AM CET | Health & Medicine 
Press release from: DataM Intelligence 4 Market Research LLP 
Transfer Membrane Market
The Transfer Membrane Market is seeing renewed product competition following Tailin's June 2026 launch of its ImmutailinTM PVDF blotting membrane, designed for high protein-binding capacity, chemical resistance, and sensitive protein detection. The product targets Western blotting and related laboratory applications, where membrane performance directly affects protein retention and detection quality. The launch highlights continued product differentiation in research consumables, with manufacturers focusing on improved sensitivity and reliability to support increasingly demanding protein analysis workflows.

CoTec Holdings Corp. Notes HyproMag USA Secures Power and Advances Project Readiness for Texas Rare Earth Magnet Recycling and Manufacturing Hub
Investing News Network 
October 13, 2026 
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 13, 2026 / CoTec Holdings Corp. ( TSXV:CTH )(OTCQX:CTHCF) ("CoTec" or the "Company") notes the press release issued today by its joint venture, HyProMag USA, LLC ("HyProMag USA"), providing an update on development activities for its Texas Hub rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing project in Dallas-Fort Worth, Texas (the "Texas Hub"). Following the commencement of formal power supply discussions announced on June 22, 2026, i HyProMag USA has secured electrical power capacity with Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC ("Oncor") for the Texas Hub development and expects the facility's electricity requirements to be supplied predominantly from renewable energy resources.
Key Highlights 
Power capacity secured: Power capacity secured with Oncor for both cutting and finishing operations and the Phase 1 development, with a pathway through a sub-station upgrade to provide power for Phase 2.
Contractor selection and permitting underway: Pegasus TSI, Inc. ("Pegasus") has commenced contractor selection for cutting and finishing operations and Weston Solutions, Inc. ("Weston") is advancing permitting activities.
Cutting and finishing operations targeted for H1 2027: Targeted commissioning of cutting and finishing operations in H1 2027 with the processing of neodymium iron boron ("NdFeB") magnet blocks, initially supplied from HyProMag Group operations, to produce finished magnets.
Phase 1 development: Phase 1 development is targeted for completion in mid-2028 and is designed to produce approximately 550 tonnes per annum ("tpa") of NdFeB magnet blocks and finished magnets and approximately 484 tpa of co-products, representing approximately 1,034 tpa of total payable production.
Phase 2 development: Phase 2 development envisions expansion to approximately 1,526 tpa of total payable production.
Renewable energy supply: Electricity supply expected to be sourced predominantly from renewable energy resources.
Julian Treger, Chief Executive Officer of CoTec Holdings Corp. , commented: "Securing power with Oncor, advancing permitting activities through Weston Solutions and commencing contractor selection are important milestones for the Texas Hub. Initial cutting and finishing operations in 2027 are expected to establish U.S. magnet finishing and qualification capabilities aligned with internationally recognized magnetic material and quality standards, while the full Phase 1 development will deliver integrated recycling and magnet manufacturing capacity. Together, these activities further de-risk the project and demonstrate continued progress towards establishing a domestic and sustainable rare earth magnet supply chain in the United States." 
Cutting and Finishing Operations 
Cutting and finishing operations in 2027 comprise the initial magnet finishing and qualification facility, enabling production and qualification of finished NdFeB magnets using magnet blocks supplied from HyProMag Group operations. The facility is designed to process NdFeB magnet blocks and support qualification of finished magnets in accordance with ASTM A977/A977M, the national classification standard for magnetic materials, together with quality management systems aligned with ISO 9001 and customer-specific quality, performance and traceability requirements. The objective is to establish qualification capabilities that meet the requirements of U.S. customers and establish a strategic training facility for the finishing of NdFeB magnets in advance of the main Texas Hub developments.
Permitting and Contractor Selection 
Weston is advancing permitting activities for the Texas Hub, while HyProMag USA's engineering partner Pegasus has commenced a Request for Quotation ("RFQ") process for the selection of a general contractor for cutting and finishing operations. Pegasus and BBA USA Inc. are HyProMag USA's U.S.-based engineering, procurement and construction management firms.
Phase 1 and Phase 2 Development 
Phase 1 represents the first integrated recycling and magnet manufacturing stage of the Texas Hub and is designed to produce approximately 550 tpa of sintered NdFeB magnet blocks and finished magnets, together with approximately 484 tpa of co-products, representing total payable production of approximately 1,034 tpa. Upon completion of Phase 2, the Texas Hub is expected to produce approximately 1,048 tpa of sintered NdFeB magnet blocks and cylinders, together with approximately 478 tpa of co-products, representing total payable production of approximately 1,526 tpa.
About HyProMag USA 
HyProMag USA is developing advanced rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing operations to establish a secure domestic U.S. supply chain for NdFeB magnets, essential components for AI infrastructure, defense systems, robotics, electric vehicles, and advanced electronics. Leveraging the revolutionary Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap ("HPMS") technology, developed over 15 years with over US$100 million in R&D investment, HyProMag USA delivers faster magnet-to-magnet short-loop recycling that uses 88% less energy and reduces carbon emissions by 85% compared to conventional methods. HPMS accepts a wide range of magnet-bearing feedstocks - including end-of-life EV motors, data-center and industrial equipment, consumer electronics, and manufacturing scrap - enabling recovery of magnet-grade material without chemical processing.
Ownership 
HyProMag USA LLC is owned 50:50 by CoTec and HyProMag Limited. HyProMag Limited is 100% owned by Maginito Limited, which is owned 79.4% by Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) and 20.6% by CoTec.
For more information on HyProMag USA, please visit www.hypromagusa.com 
About CoTec 
CoTec Holdings Corp. ( TSXV:CTH )(OTCQX:CTHCF) is redefining the future of resource extraction and recycling. Focused on rare earth magnets and strategic materials, CoTec integrates breakthrough technologies with strategic assets to unlock secure, sustainable, and low-cost supply chains.
CoTec's mission is clear: accelerate the energy transition while strengthening strategic mineral supply chains for the countries we operate in. By investing in and deploying disruptive technologies, the Company delivers capital-efficient, scalable solutions that transform marginal assets, tailings, waste streams, and recycled products into high-value critical minerals.
From its HyProMag USA magnet recycling joint venture in Texas, to iron tailings reprocessing and reclamation in Québec, to next-generation copper and iron solutions backed by global majors, CoTec is building a diversified portfolio with long-term growth, rapid cash flow potential, and high barriers to entry. The result is a differentiated platform at the intersection of technology, sustainability, and strategic materials.

Vestas Completes Taiwan's First V236-15.0 MW™ Offshore Wind Turbine Hub Assembly Ahead of Schedule; Achieves Milestone in CIP's Fengmiao 1 Project
Oct. 13 2026
Vestas Completes Taiwan's First V236-15.0 MW™ Offshore Wind Turbine Hub Assembly Ahead of Schedule; Achieves Milestone in CIP's Fengmiao 1 Project
Share
Vestas has completed the assembly of Taiwan's first V236-15.0 MW™ offshore wind turbine hub , marking a milestone in the introduction of next-generation offshore wind technology to Taiwan. The achievement was supported by steady progress on the CIP's 495 MW Fengmiao 1 Offshore Wind Farm (渢妙一期) , the first project in Taiwan's Round 3 offshore wind zonal development to secure full financing and commence construction.
Since entering Taiwan in 2000, Vestas has established a strong presence in both onshore and offshore wind, employing more than 500 people locally. The successful assembly combined the company's global technological expertise with the capabilities of its Taiwan team, which has developed specialized skills in quality management, testing and safety procedures for critical turbine components. The hub was delivered ahead of schedule, with safety and quality remaining top priorities.
Vestas Asia-Pacific President Purvin Patel said, "Completing Taiwan's first V236 hub assembly is an important milestone for Vestas. It demonstrates that our Taiwan team can deliver safely, to a high standard of quality and on schedule. The skills and experience gained through this work will also serve as an important foundation for the continued development of Taiwan's offshore wind industry."
The V236-15.0 MW™ is Vestas' flagship offshore wind turbine platform, designed to support standardized, large-scale production and improve project execution efficiency. Upon completion of Fengmiao 1, Vestas' cumulative offshore wind capacity delivered in Taiwan is expected to reach approximately 1.7 GW, reinforcing the company's long-term commitment to Taiwan's offshore wind sector and its contribution to the country's energy security.
【About Vestas】 
Vestas is a global leader in sustainable energy solutions, specializing in the design, manufacturing, installation, and servicing of onshore and offshore wind turbines. The company has installed more than 207 GW of wind power capacity across 88 countries worldwide and currently services wind turbines with a combined capacity of more than 165 GW.

Syensqo expands circular Fomblin portfolio with UL validation
Syensqo is investing at its Spinetta Marengo manufacturing site in Italy to boost recycling capabilities and increase fluorine recovery
By ICN Bureau | October 13, 2026 
Syensqo expands its portfolio of certified circular specialty materials. (Photo: Syensqo) 
Syensqo has expanded its portfolio of circular high-performance fluids with UL Environmental Claim Validation for Fomblin Y, reinforcing its push to recover and reuse fluorine while reducing dependence on virgin raw materials.
 
The validation, secured under UL 2809 in September 2026, builds on the certification Syensqo obtained in 2025 for selected high-performance elastomers and lubricant fluids. 
 
Around 40% of the fluorine allocated to the newly certified Fomblin Y products comes from post-industrial recycled (PIR) hydrofluoric acid (HF), using a mass balance accounting approach.
 
The move comes as Europe seeks to strengthen the security of supply of critical raw materials. Fluorspar, the primary mineral source of fluorine, is classified as a critical raw material under the European Union’s Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA). By recovering fluorine from post-industrial waste, Syensqo aims to reduce dependence on virgin resources and support more resilient European supply chains.
 
Alongside the expanded certification, Syensqo is investing at its Spinetta Marengo manufacturing site in Italy to boost recycling capabilities and increase fluorine recovery.
 
The investment is designed to improve the availability of recycled raw materials for the company’s specialty polymers portfolio, as demand grows for circular high-performance fluorinated elastomers and fluids across industries.
 
“Our customers are increasingly looking for high-performance materials that enable them to use resources more efficiently while strengthening the resilience of their supply chains. 
 
"The expansion of our certified Fomblin portfolio, together with our investment in recycled fluorine recovery at Spinetta Marengo, demonstrates how we are responding to this demand at an industrial scale. By recovering and reusing fluorine locally, we can reduce reliance on virgin resources while helping build a more circular and resilient European fluorine value chain," said Tom Wood, Vice President, Head of Product and Asset Management at Syensqo.
 
The expanded UL validation for Fomblin Y marks another step in Syensqo’s efforts to integrate recycled raw materials into high-performance fluorinated products while meeting the stringent requirements of industrial applications.
 
The company says the approach enables customers to increase the use of recycled raw materials without compromising the performance and reliability needed in demanding operating environments.
 
Under Syensqo’s mass balance system, 40% by weight of the fluorine in the Fomblin
 Y molecule is allocated as recycled fluorine. Because fluorine accounts for more than 65% of the polymer’s total mass, this translates into an allocated recycled content of 25% by weight in the final molecule.
 
The expanded portfolio and investment at Spinetta Marengo underline Syensqo’s strategy of combining material performance with greater resource efficiency, as Europe looks to strengthen circularity and reduce its exposure to critical raw material supply risks.

Engineers considering hydraulic replacement should provide their required force, stroke, speed, motion profile and operating environment to Electromate. Asahi Kasei Acquisition Pays Off With FDA Approval for Novel Herpes Drug 
Asahi Kasei’s Hovilpri is now approved for treating lesions caused by herpes simplex virus infection. This daily pill came from the $919 million acquisition of AiCuris Anti-Infective Cures.
By Frank Vinluan on October 12, 2026 10:44 am 
Share 
Share Options 
Share a link to this article
Copy Link 
Copy Link

X 
Patients with lesions caused by herpes simplex virus have a new FDA-approved treatment option, an oral antiviral drug from Asahi Kasei.
The late Friday regulatory decision covers the treatment of adults whose lesions do not respond to the three oral antivirals that make up the current standard of care. Asahi Kasei’s once-daily pill, known in development as pritelivir, will be commercialized under the brand name Hovilpri.
In people with healthy immune systems, herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection is often asymptomatic or causes mild disease. But in people with weakened immune symptoms — those who have undergone a transplant procedure, or patients with HIV, cancer, or autoimmune disorders — HSV infection can occur more frequently and with greater severity. While oral antivirals are available to treat HSV, viral mutations can lead to resistance to these older drugs. There are alternative treatment options, but they require intravenous dosing.
Sponsored Post 
The Power Behind Enterprise EHR Software for Large Healthcare Systems  
Enterprise EHR boosts scalability, interoperability, and governance for large healthcare systems. 
By Malvika Tarnekar, Director of Product Strategy, PrognoCIS by Bizmatics Inc 
Hovilpri gives patients the choice of an oral drug with a different mechanism of action. This small molecule is designed to inhibit a complex of enzymes key to the synthesis of viral DNA. The drug was developed to treat both types of HSV, HSV-1 and HSV-2.
The regulatory submission for Hovilpri was based on the results of a Phase 3 study that showed statistically significant superiority in lesion healing up to day 28 compared to the physician’s choice of treatment. The most common adverse reaction reported for the study drug was headache.
“Today’s approval delivers the first FDA-approved treatment for refractory mucocutaneous HSV lesions with a novel mechanism of action in nearly 30 years and marks an important advancement for immunocompromised adults,” Stacy Wheeler, CEO of Asahi Kasei Therapeutics in the U.S. and Europe, said in a prepared statement. “Hovilpri offers a new oral treatment option for adult patients with a persistent, difficult-to-treat disease.”
Hovilpri was originally developed by AiCuris Anti-Infective Cures, a Germany-based biopharmaceutical company acquired by Asahi Kasei for €780 million (about $919 million). In the February acquisition announcement, Tokyo-based Asahi Kasei said the deal strengthens the company’s presence in severe infectious disease. It added that HSV patients addressed by Hovilpri are commonly seen in transplant centers and specialized hospital settings where the company has established commercial relationships and infrastructure.
Sponsored Post 
The Hidden Administrative Tasks Draining Small Practices 
Small practices play a critical role in healthcare delivery, but they cannot continue to absorb ever-increasing administrative demands without consequences. 
By Michael Blackman, MD, MBA Chief Medical Officer, Greenway Health® 
Asahi Kasei has been expanding its portfolio and pipeline via business deals. In 2020, the company closed the 8.3 billion Danish krone (about $1.3 billion) acquisition of Veloxis Pharmaceuticals , a company that develops and sells therapies for organ transplant patients. The Japanese company’s 11.8 billion Swedish krona (about $1.18 billion) acquisition of Calliditas Pharmaceuticals in 2024 brought a portfolio that includes Tarpeyo, which has FDA approval for treating the rare kidney disorder immunoglobulin A nephropathy.
The Aicuris acquisition brought more than Hovilpri. Asahi Kasei gains royalty income from Prevymis, a cytomegalovirus drug whose global rights Aicuris had licensed to Merck. The Japanese company also gets an experimental antisense oligonucleotide that Aicuris has advanced to Phase 1 testing as a treatment for BK virus infection in kidney transplant patients.

ARKAY has announced the inauguration of a next-generation acrylic acid purification unit at its Carling site in France, strengthening its competitive position in Europe's market while advancing decarbonization. The nearly 150 million Euro investment is one of the company's largest industrial projects in France and contributes to its ambitious climate investment program. 
The new unit improves the energy efficiency of the purification process by 25% and reduces the carbon intensity of the Carling site by 20%. Its innovative technology also optimizes resource and waste management while significantly lowering solvent consumption. These improvements enhance efficiency to reinforce Arkema's position in the low-carbon acrylic materials market. 
The Carling facility is a leading acrylic production site, manufacturing acrylic monomers used in performance coatings, adhesives, water treatment and other advanced materials. The project, decided in 2023, received partial funding from the French State under the France 2030 program, operated by ADEME, and from the European Union's NextGenerationEU initiative. 
The cumulative investments could reach €400 million over 2022-2030, under the company's decarbonization plans, while making its industrial hubs the driving forces of future. Arkema's investment also aligns with its strategy to strengthen its Specialty Materials segment and its increasing focus on reducing emissions across the industry.

Lithium futures tumble 10% in China after E.U. deal cuts hybrid car exports
Less than 1 min read 
ALB SQM LAR SGML 
Albemarle ALB and other lithium stocks traded sharply lower pre-market Monday after lithium carbonate futures prices in China plunged to a nearly 10-month low, as an agreement to limit hybrid car exports to the European Union added to concerns over demand prospects for the battery material. 
In pre-market trading, Albemarle ALB down 4.2%, SQM SQM down 4.2%, Lithium Argentina LAR down 3.2%, Sigma Lithium SGML down 1.9%, Atlas Lithium ATLX down 1.7%, Lithium Aericas LAC down 0.8%. 
The most active lithium carbonate contract on the Guangzhou Futures Exchange fell to its weakest since December 17, 2025, before settling down 11.8% to 104,740 yuan/ton ($15,649), marking its steepest daily decline since March. 
China and the European Union reached an agreement that could cut Chinese exports of hybrid cars to the bloc by more than half, the European Trade Commission said Friday. 
Lithium prices have been on a downward trajectory since hitting a 33-month high at 209,880 yuan on May 13 on concerns about demand from electric vehicles and larger-scale energy storage systems. 
Lithium's supply-demand balance is shifting in a bearish direction, Goldman Sachs analysts said in a note, forecasting that both the Chinese and global markets will move from a deficit to nearly balanced in Q4 followed by surpluses in the next two years. title: Aicuris acquisition delivers new drug for Asahi Kasei - pharmaphorum
query: "Asahi Kasei" ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Aicuris acquisition delivers new drug for Asahi Kasei
News
Asahi Kasei's $920 million takeover of German biotech Aicuris in April has paid off with FDA approval for the herpes simplex virus (HSV) drug at the heart of the deal. 
The oral drug, called Hovilpri (pritelivir), has been cleared for treating adults with weakened immune systems who have sores on the skin or mucous membranes – such as lips, nostrils, eyes, and genitals – that are caused by HSV and have not responded to standard nucleoside analogue therapies like acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir.
Hovilpri, which acts as a helicase-primase inhibitor, represents the first FDA approved HSV therapy with a novel mechanism of action in nearly 30 years, according to Asahi Kasei. It also provides an oral alternative to intravenously administered antivirals used to treat immunocompromised adults with refractory HSV infection, with or without resistance to current drugs.
There are two types of HSV infection – HSV-1 and HSV-2 – which cause common infections like cold sores and genital herpes. Most people are exposed to the virus in childhood and recover from the primary infection, although in many cases the virus lies dormant.
HSV is a major threat to immunocompromised people, as the virus can quickly reactivate and cause lesions that release contagious virus particles.
The FDA approval of Hovilpri draws on the pivotal, open-label PRIOH-1 study, which enrolled 101 immunocompromised adults and compared the drug with investigator's choice of available treatments for up to 28 days until all mucocutaneous lesions healed, which was extended up to 42 days if lesions were improving, but not completely healed, after 28 days.
The primary endpoint was the proportion of participants with all lesions healed during the treatment period up to 28 days, which was achieved in 63% of patients receiving Hovilpri, compared with 34% of patients receiving one of the other medications.
The study recruited adults who had weakened immunity due to a wide range of causes, including haematopoietic stem cell transplants (HSCT) for serious illnesses, various forms of cancer, HIV infection, autoimmune diseases, and solid organ transplantation.
Asahi Kasei said that it expects to launch Hovilpri in the US before the end of the year, but has not released pricing details as yet.
Aicuris , which now operates as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Asahi Kasei, previously developed another antiviral used for HSCT patients, MSD-marketed Prevymis (letermovir), which is used to prevent infection with cytomegalovirus (CMV).
It is also developing AIC468, which aims to prevent and treat BK virus infections in kidney transplant recipients.
Asahi Kasei has a long history in the anti-infectives arena, with products like antifungal Cresemba (isavuconazonium sulfate) and aminoglycoside antibiotic Exacin (isepamicin), and has said that adding Aicuris will help it reach its goal of driving pharma sales to around $1.9 billion) by its 2030 fiscal year.

Airbus Asia Training Centre Welcomes South Korea's Jin Air as 97th Customer
October 12, 2026
Singapore & South Korea – Airbus Asia Training Centre (AATC), the Singapore-based flight simulator training joint venture between Airbus and Singapore Airlines, has welcomed South Korean low-cost carrier Jin Air as a customer for Airbus A320 type rating training. 
Jin Air becomes AATC's 97th customer, according to the training centre's October 2026 announcement, extending its portfolio of airline training customers across Asia-Pacific. 
The training arrangement comes as Jin Air transitions from its historically Boeing-focused fleet toward Airbus A320-family operations. In 2026, the airline began incorporating Airbus A321 aircraft, including an A321-200 previously operated by Asiana Airlines, alongside plans to introduce additional A321neo aircraft. 
Jin Air signed an agreement in August 2026 to merge with Air Busan and Air Seoul, targeting the launch of an integrated low-cost airline under the Jin Air brand on 17 March 2027. The integration will consolidate Airbus and Boeing operations, creating additional flight crew training and fleet standardisation requirements. 
Jin Air has also been investing in domestic simulator capacity, having introduced an A320neo full flight simulator in May 2026 and outlined plans to operate two FFS devices and one flight training device. 
Airbus' September 2026 disclosure identified nine installed FFS devices at AATC, comprising two A320, one A330, four A350, one A380 and one ATR 72-600 simulator, alongside six fixed cockpit training devices. 
About Airbus Asia Training Centre 
The Airbus Asia Training Centre, located in Singapore’s Seletar Aerospace Park, provides pilot type-rating and recurrent training for all Airbus jetliner models. Established in 2015, AATC is part of the Airbus global Flight Training network, serving the Asia-Pacific region and beyond. This 10, 000-square-foot facility is fitted with x10 Full Flight Simulators (FFS), including x2 A320, x2 A330, x4 A350, x1 A380 and x1 ATR. This makes AATC the largest flight crew training facility within the Airbus Training Centre network and the largest operator of A350 FFS worldwide. It also features a ATR 72-600 FFS.
