Department of War Executes White House Strategy for a New Golden Age of Science
Oct. 8, 2026
| 
×
Share
Copy Link 
Email
Facebook
X
LinkedIn
WhatsApp
The Department of War (DoW) today announced a series of initiatives to advance President Donald J. Trump's vision for a New Golden Age of American science. Building on the recommendations in the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios's report Science: A New Golden Age, these initiatives will modernize how the Department supports and evaluates scientific research, bring new talent to work on critical scientific challenges in defense of the nation, and strengthen partnerships across the science ecosystem between discovery, innovation, and national defense to ensure American warfighters are supported with cutting edge technology and capabilities.
"President Trump has made it clear that technological dominance requires us to move faster, safeguard our research, and build right here in America," said Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering. "We are answering that call by dismantling barriers to commercialization, modernizing our labs, and ruthlessly securing taxpayer-funded research from foreign exploitation. The Department of War will continue to turn the President's vision of a new golden age of science into unrivaled capability for our warfighters."
"Maintaining our technological edge requires balancing rapid innovation with responsible program protection," said Joseph Jewell, Ph.D., Assistant Secretary of War for Science and Technology. "As we accelerate how we move concepts from the lab to the field, we are equally committed to safeguarding federally funded research and ensuring domestic investments deliver tangible capabilities. By modernizing our testing facilities, empowering industry through initiatives like the Defense Patent Holiday, and expanding pathways for domestic scientific talent, we are safeguarding our nation's economic vitality and national security, ensuring this new golden age drives lasting domestic strength and unrivaled technological capabilities for our warfighters."
The Department's execution of the White House strategy includes major lines of effort led by the Office of the Assistant Secretary of War for Science and Technology:
1. Revitalizing America's Defense Research Enterprise 
Department of War and National Science Foundation Establish Memorandum of Understanding to Advance Science, Technology, and Innovation: The Department of War and the National Science Foundation (NSF) have established a broad memorandum of understanding (MOU) to pursue mutually beneficial collaborative activities in science, technology, and innovation. The MOU establishes a framework for the Department and NSF to explore and coordinate opportunities that strengthen the nation's research ecosystem, accelerate the transition of promising technologies, and promote collaboration among government, academic, industry, and other research partners. Initial areas of joint interest include X-Labs, the Programmable Cloud Laboratories Network, and AI Forge ($40 million), among other initiatives that advance experimentation, modernize research infrastructure, build the workforce, and push the development of emerging technologies. As part of this effort, the Department of War is dedicating $200M to Programmable Cloud Labs in Fiscal Year 2028 across the Future Years Defense Program (FYDP).
Through this partnership, the Department of War and NSF may identify opportunities for information exchange, joint workshops, research collaboration, pilot activities, and other initiatives consistent with each organization's authorities, priorities, and available resources.
Department of War Advances Metascience-informed Framework to Strengthen the Defense Research Enterprise: Consistent with Science: A New Golden Age and the recommendations of the Defense Research Enterprise Review, the Department of War is establishing a new enterprise-wide framework to measure and improve the performance and effectiveness of its in-house laboratories, Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDCs) and University-Affiliated Research Centers (UARCs).
Implementing Recommendation 14 of the Department's recently published "Defense Research Enterprise Review," the initiative will apply metascience-informed principles to create measures of performance (MOP) and measures of effectiveness (MOE) as metrics.
The initiative reflects a metascience-informed approach to research management: using evidence and rigorous evaluation to improve how research organizations are assessed, governed, and resourced. Rather than impose a single scorecard on organizations with different missions, the Department will develop category-specific measures anchored to each institution's mission, comparative advantages, and enduring technical capabilities.
The framework will be designed to:
Focus on outcomes: Assess whether portfolios achieve mission-relevant results commensurate with their resources and responsibilities
Support independent verification: Use measures that can be audited and substantiated
Measure progress over time: Track long-term performance consistent with the timelines of scientific research and engineering
Respect institutional differences: Enable appropriate comparisons while recognizing that laboratories, warfare centers, medical research organizations, federally funded research and development centers, and university affiliated research centers have distinct missions and operating models
Reduce distorted incentives: Avoid overreliance on narrow activity metrics that can encourage organizations to report volume instead of mission outcomes
Inform leadership decisions: Strengthen the evidence base for portfolio management, resource allocation, and performance improvement
The Defense Research Enterprise Review found that existing enterprise measures, including activity counts and obligation and expenditure rates, remain useful for financial stewardship and oversight but do not independently capture portfolio-level outcomes. The new MOP/MOE framework is intended to complement—not replace—appropriate financial management and program oversight tools.
The Department is launching the framework with a limited pilot across representative research organizations to validate measures before engaging in a broader implementation.
New Department of War Research Center Unites Academic Researchers with Broader Industry, Venture Capital, Non-Profit Ecosystem: The Department of War is catalyzing the university research ecosystem through the new Center for Defense Academic Research's (CeDAR) two complementary initiatives: the Problem-Based Basic Research Consortium (PBR-C) and the Translational Research Initiative for Academia and Defense (TRIAD) Partnership. Through PBR-C, the Department will unite multidisciplinary university research teams and world-class individual investigators to solve pressing scientific challenges, leveraging partnerships with non-profit research foundations, selective international collaborations, and participation from industry and venture capital observers. In parallel, TRIAD pairs transdisciplinary academic research teams with Service laboratories to develop actionable solutions for Combatant Command and Joint Interagency Task Force mission priorities.
2. Investing in America's Scientific Talent to Support the Warfighter 
Expansion of Hands-On Technical Learning: Fulfilling the White House directives to invest in individual researchers and elevate technical apprenticeships, the Department is expanding premier human capital programs. Celebrating its 20th anniversary, the Science, Mathematics, and Research for Transformation (SMART) Scholarship for Service Program welcomed its largest cohort of more than 750 scholars this year.
The DoW's SMART Program provides merit-based scholarships to bachelor's, master's, and doctoral students in STEM fields. In exchange for full tuition, stipends, and internship opportunities, scholars commit to a one-to-one service period as civilian employees with the DoW. Since its inception in 2006, the SMART program has awarded over 6,500 scholarships, with 91 percent of scholars successfully completing the program.
Beginning this fiscal year, the Department of War will explore a talent exchange initiative that would connect the Department of Energy's (DOE's) Genesis Mission Fellowship program to the DoW's SMART and National Defense Science and Engineering Graduate (NDSEG) programs. This partnership enables DoW and DOE scholars to intern with each other's laboratories and industry partners, putting opportunities in academia, government laboratories, and companies under one umbrella.
The Department's flagship SMART and NDSEG programs are producing a new generation of scientific leaders. To date, the two programs boast over 5,000 Ph.D. graduates between them; these graduates have gone on to fill critical roles within the Department, drive innovation in the private sector, and advance the frontiers of knowledge in academia.
Complementing this talent pipeline, the NDSEG program has cultivated the nation's scientific minds since 1989, awarding nearly 4,900 fellowships. The program offers full tuition and a generous stipend for up to three years to individuals pursuing doctoral degrees, with no service obligation. This provides fellows with the flexibility to pursue careers across academia, industry, and government, with 90 percent of graduates entering research and development roles, broadly strengthening the U.S. innovation ecosystem.
The SMART SEED Innovation Award supports SMART scholars as they begin their DoW employment after completing their doctorates. The technical work completed through SEED, which provides funding of up to $155,000 per year for up to three years, aligns with Department missions or critical technology areas.
The Department of War is proud to announce the Fiscal Year 2026 SMART SEED Innovation Award principal investigators:

Since Fiscal Year 2020, SMART SEED awards have invested $41 million in 140 projects, resulting in new patents, publications, and advanced defense technologies. Ultimately, these programs ensure the long-term sustainability of an agile, highly capable STEM workforce equipped to safeguard national security and maintain America's enduring technological edge.
3. Accelerating and Safeguarding American Defense Innovation 
Enforce Robust Research Security and Program Protection: The Department has strengthened its Science & Technology Program Protection and Maintaining Technology Advantage frameworks to support implementation of National Security Presidential Memorandum-33 (NSPM-33). The Department conducts rigorous risk-based reviews of fundamental research, screens against National Defense Authorization Act Section 1286 foreign-risk entity lists, ensures strict compliance with Section 1062 foreign institution limits, and executes mandatory foreign ownership due diligence. This ensures technological advancements made in America can be translated into operational capabilities for the United States and our allies.
Dismantle Commercialization Barriers via the Defense Patent Holiday Initiative: The Department is responding to the White House's mandate to reform intellectual property licensing and open federal innovations to non-traditional builders through the Defense Patent Holiday Initiative. This initiative directly supports White House priorities by rapidly accelerating the transition of Department-funded technologies into the commercial sector. By granting royalty-free licensing windows to federally developed patents, the Department empowers private-sector innovators to commercialize breakthrough defense hardware without navigating months of legal friction.
Leverage R&D to Strengthen Domestic Manufacturing: The Department of War's ManTech Program celebrated its 70th anniversary this year and serves as the Department's primary bridge from prototypes to programs of record, shaping not just what the military designs, but how it is produced affordably, securely, and at scale. The Department's Manufacturing Innovation Institutes (MIIs) include a network of nine active, defense-led institutes across the nation, including the latest addition, the FutureTEX institute in Belmont, North Carolina.
These unified lines of effort strengthen the American innovation pipeline and deliver unmatched capabilities to our warfighters.

NSA Releases Zero Trust Guidance for Protecting Operational Technology Systems
FORT MEADE, Md.—Today, the National Security Agency released a Cybersecurity Information Sheet (CSI), “Hardening Department of War (DoW) Critical Operational Technology (OT) Environments with Zero Trust (ZT) Principles.” 
The guidance recommends using ZT mitigation principles to prevent catastrophic impacts to U.S. national security, economic security, and public health and safety. While primarily intended for National Security Systems (NSS), DoW, and Defense Industrial Base (DIB) network system owners, and the operators responsible for protecting these critical systems, this guidance is also applicable to technical leaders and experts, as well as information technology and OT managers and administrators. 
ZT assumes the occurrence of adversarial breaches and uses a “never trust, always verify” principle. By assuming compromise is possible or already present, ZT continuously verifies users, devices, workflows, and communications. Applying these principles to OT strengthens protection against unauthorized access, lateral movement, and adversarial persistence.
The adoption of ZT principles is essential for enhancing the security of legacy OT, enabling defense-in-depth across critical infrastructure while ensuring adherence with federal guidance. 
While organizations are increasingly integrating super intelligence (SI) into OT to improve efficiency, resilience, and mission effectiveness, this introduces new risk, attack surfaces, and disruption opportunities. Adversaries are leveraging SI capabilities to automate reconnaissance, accelerate exploit development, and conduct cyber campaigns at unprecedented speed and scale, making achieving ZT outcomes on OT systems more critical than ever. Adversarial attacks now extend beyond espionage and reconnaissance, often aiming to deny, degrade, disrupt, deceive, or destroy the United States’ critical infrastructure. The consequences of such attacks vary by sector and can result in significant and widespread damage. Affected sectors may include, but are not limited to, energy, water, agriculture, public health, and government facilities.
Read the report and visit our full library for more cybersecurity information and technical guidance.

Veolia completes $58M Princeton Meadows wastewater treatment facility
Veolia has modernized the Princeton Meadows Wastewater Treatment Facility with a $58 million upgrade, incorporating climate-resilient infrastructure and advanced treatment technologies to serve 11,000 residents and businesses more efficiently.
Oct. 8, 2026
Add Us On Google 
Veolia
Veolia's Princeton Meadows Wastewater Treatment Facility in Plainsboro, NJ (Photo and caption credit: Veolia via PR Newswire). 
Veolia's Princeton Meadows Wastewater Treatment Facility in Plainsboro, NJ (Photo and caption credit: Veolia via PR Newswire).
Veolia has completed a $58 million replacement of the Princeton Meadows Wastewater Treatment Facility in Plainsboro, New Jersey, with the new plant incorporating climate-resilient infrastructure and advanced treatment technologies.
The facility serves approximately 11,000 residents and businesses and includes ultraviolet disinfection, high-efficiency biological treatment and energy-efficient equipment. The plant was built on higher ground outside the original 100-year floodplain to reduce the risk of flooding to critical infrastructure.
The facility treats approximately 475 million gallons of wastewater annually and reuses 32 million gallons of reclaimed water. The site has supplied reclaimed water for irrigation at a Middlesex County golf course since 1971, with approximately 1.4 billion gallons reused over the past 55 years.
The project replaces an aging facility that had operated for more than five decades. Veolia said the new infrastructure is designed to improve treatment performance, withstand extreme weather and meet future environmental requirements.
The project was completed in partnership with the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities, New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection, Middlesex County, Township of Plainsboro and engineering and construction firms including HDR and J. Fletcher Creamer & Son.

Arkema inaugurates its next-generation acrylic acid purification unit in Carling
Download the PDF 
Arkema has inaugurated a new acrylic acid purification unit featuring an innovative process at its Carling site in France. This facility positions the Group among the most competitive players in Europe and contributes to the decarbonization of the European chemical industry. It is part of Arkema’s decarbonization investment program and supports the implementation of its ambitious climate plan.
The inauguration ceremony for the new unit was held in the presence of Thierry Le Hénaff, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Arkema and Stéphane Séjourné, Executive Vice-President of the European Commission for Prosperity and Industrial Strategy.
The ceremony took place on the same day as the Critical Chemicals Alliance General Assembly, which brought together European industrial leaders and policy-makers to discuss the key challenges of sovereignty, competitiveness, and decarbonization.
With an investment of nearly €150 million, this new unit represents one of Arkema’s largest industrial projects in France.
It will contribute to the Group’s ambitious climate plan, underpinned by a dedicated investment program supporting Arkema’s decarbonization, with a cumulative amount that could reach €400 million over the 2022-2030 period.” 
Thierry Le Hénaff, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Arkema.
“Europe must keep its chemical industry. There can be neither industrial sovereignty nor strategic autonomy if we allow the essential building blocks of our economy to leave. Carling is showing the way forward: nearly €150 million invested to produce in Europe, using less energy and generating less carbon, while building on decades of industrial know-how. This is exactly the model we want to promote: decarbonizing without deindustrializing, investing in our regions, and making our industrial hubs the driving forces of our future.” 
Stéphane Séjourné, Executive Vice-President of the European Commission for Prosperity and Industrial Strategy. 
The Carling site is one of the leading acrylic production facilities in Europe. It produces acrylic monomer s used in performance coatings, adhesives, water treatment and other advanced materials.
The new unit improves the energy efficiency of the purification process by 25% and reduces the carbon intensity of the site’s operations by 20%. The innovative technology deployed also helps optimize resource and waste management while significantly reducing solvent consumption.
Thanks to this investment, the Carling plant is positioning itself among the reference sites in the industry, aligned with the highest operational and environmental standards . It also strengthens Arkema’s leadership in the low-carbon acrylic materials market.
This project has been decided in 2023 and has been partly funded by the French State as part of the France 2030 program, operated by ADEME, and funded by the European Union – NextGenerationEU.

Air Liquide to build new Air Separation Unit at its Fairfield facility in New South Wales
PR Newswire 
October 7, 2026 2 min read 
AI.PA 
+1.98% 
MELBOURNE, Australia, Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Air Liquide announces a new investment to build and operate a new Air Separation Unit (ASU) and its related infrastructure at its existing Fairfield Facility located in Yennora, New South Wales - Australia. This will enhance local supply chain reliability for industrial and medical gases across Australia. 
Air Liquide to build new Air Separation Unit in New South Wales The new ASU will produce nitrogen and oxygen, critical gases to support the daily operations and long-term growth of key Australian sectors , including food and beverage processing, healthcare and medical facilities, mining and advanced manufacturing. 
The ASU is expected to start-up in 2028. 
Tim Kehoe, Managing Director of Air Liquide Pacific said: "Expanding our air gas capacity demonstrates Air Liquide's long-term commitment to fueling the growth of Australian industries with essential gases they depend on every day. With the new ASU in New South Wales, we are reinforcing our commitment to serving our customers and enhancing our supply chain resilience." 
Air Liquide Australia 
Air Liquide Australia started its operations in 1957 and currently employs 400+ employees across Pacific. In Australia, Air Liquide operates air separation plants, CO₂ plants and gas filling facilities. Air Liquide provides innovative and customer-focused solutions and services and supports the Australian economy through a unique blend of advanced equipment, processes & systems, supported by a highly engaged and competent workforce. 
Air Liquide is a leader in gases, technologies, and services for numerous economic sectors. As an invisible yet essential cornerstone of industry and healthcare for more than a century, the Group's molecules pave the way for progress by delivering useful and innovative solutions to customers, patients, and society. 
Present in 59 countries with approximately 65,000 employees, the Group serves 4.3 million customers and patients. With revenues close to 27 billion euros in 2025 and solid foundations, Air Liquide combines performance with lasting value creation for all its stakeholders. With "Beyond", its strategic plan through 2030, the Group has set an ambitious roadmap to accelerate its profitable growth trajectory and continue inventing the future. 
Air Liquide is listed on the Euronext Paris stock exchange (compartment A) and is a member of the CAC 40, CAC 40 ESG, EURO STOXX 50, FTSE4Good, and Dow Jones Best-in-Class Europe indexes.

CPHI 2026: Big Thermo Fisher announcements include new manufacturing lines in US and Italy 
As the firm continues to expand its global footprint, we spoke with an executive about what life science companies should consider when choosing research and manufacturing partners.
Josh Abbott , News Editor, BioProcess International October 7, 2026
schedule 3 Min Read 
stock.adobe.com 
link 
Biotech giant Thermo Fisher Scientific made a splash this week at CPHI Milan 2026 with a number of big announcements spanning multiple service areas. The company is expanding its sterile drug product lines in Plainville, Massachusetts, and at its sites in Monza and Ferentino, Italy. 
The expansions will support the development and commercial manufacturing of vials and prefilled syringes. According to the firm, the Plainville expansion includes the introduction of bioprocessing equipment to the site, expanding US-based GMP monoclonal antibody (mAb) manufacturing capacity. 
Thermo Fisher is also expanding its clinical supply storage with a 52,000-square-foot expansion in Bohemia, New York, that will increase clinical label manufacturing capacity. The company is additionally growing its footprint in Japan – doubling that country’s clinical supply storage, distribution, and secondary packaging capacity – with a new facility in Tokyo. 
Related: Revisiting build or buy: What a year of scale-up changed for radiopharmaceutical programs 
“Drug development increasingly depends on decisions and capabilities that span traditional boundaries, from development and manufacturing to clinical supply and clinical execution,” said Mike Shafer, EVP and president of Biopharma Services at Thermo Fisher Scientific. “We’re investing not only in capacity, but in how those capabilities connect. That gives our customers greater continuity as they navigate critical transitions, scale their programs, and prepare for commercialization.” 
These moves, in addition to announcements the company made in the small-molecule space, further cement Thermo Fisher’s standing as a global pharma service provider. BioProcess International spoke with Anil Kane, executive director and global head of technical & scientific affairs at Thermo Fisher, about the challenges and advantages of partnering with a company that operates under an integrated model, offering both contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) and contract research organization (CRO) services. 
“Companies have traditionally selected partners function by function: a CRO for clinical development, a CDMO for manufacturing, another provider for clinical supply,” Kane told us. “Moving away from it requires rethinking how a development program is managed, not just changing vendors.” 
He said that developers might choose to work with multiple specialized service providers to maintain flexibility and retain access to specialized expertise in each area. The trade-off comes in separating elements that are interdependent. 
“A manufacturing decision can affect clinical supply, an analytical issue can push out downstream timelines, and a shift in enrollment assumptions can throw off inventory and manufacturing plans,” he said. “When those activities are managed separately, it can be difficult to see the downstream impact of a decision until it has already caused a delay.” 
Related: Responsible outsourcing: Avoiding common pitfalls in biopharma partnerships 
Nevertheless, he acknowledged that every situation is different. For programs that are already underway, transitioning to an integrated model can create further challenges. 
“If a company is already well into a program, changing partners or governance structures all at once can create unnecessary disruption,” he said. “In those situations, it can make sense to look for natural inflection points in development where greater integration can be introduced without putting the program at risk.” 
For some companies, such an inflection point may be found between phases. Thermo Fisher commissioned a study by the Tufts Center for the Study of Drug Development (CSDD), which Kane cited as illustrating greater financial return for integrated programs in Phase III than in Phase I for both mAb and small-molecule programs. 
But Kane once again stressed that the decision will not be the same for every company in every situation. “Development phase is only part of the equation,” he said. “Integration can also be valuable earlier in development when the science is complex, timelines are compressed, manufacturing and clinical strategies need to evolve together, or a smaller biotech has limited internal resources to coordinate multiple partners.”

COMSOL named Official Multiphysics Partner of Formula E
COMSOL and Formula E have announced a multi-year partnership naming COMSOL the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.
Partners 07 Oct '26 
facebook 
x 
email 
The partnership brings together Formula E, the world’s leading all-electric motorsport Championship, and COMSOL, a global leader in multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering (CAE) software. Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics® to investigate complex technology challenges involving multiple interacting physical effects.
Electric race cars bring together electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid, and battery systems under extreme constraints. As Official Multiphysics Partner, COMSOL will support Formula E with simulation software and expertise to help its technology teams understand how interacting physical phenomena influence multiple aspects of the sport. The partnership will also explore how simulation apps and digital twin solutions can make physics-based insight accessible beyond the traditional modeling workflow. 
Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said: “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another. We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”
Dan Cherowbrier, CTO at Formula E, said: “Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modeling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing.”
Looking ahead, the next generation of Formula E will place even greater demands on performance, efficiency, energy management, and vehicle development as the Championship prepares for the GEN4 era, introducing the fastest and most technologically advanced race car to date. 
At the same time, COMSOL has announced COMSOL Multiphysics version 2027, scheduled for release later this autumn, with new capabilities particularly relevant to advanced engineering workflows, including dedicated electric motor modeling, system-level simulation, agentic modeling, and expanded access for creating simulation apps.
The partnership was announced today at the COMSOL Conference 2026 Boston, where Cherowbrier delivered a keynote talk on the technology and engineering shaping the future of Formula E. To learn more about the partnership, visit COMSOL's website: www.comsol.com/formula-e.

The new glass fiber-reinforced PBT/PET compounds are designed to deliver technical performance that can match conventional grades based on virgin raw materials while helping customers increase recycled content.

title: Peptron Ends Technology Evaluation with Eli Lilly; Stock Plunges Nearly 30% as Definitive Deal Fails to Materialize - BigGo Finance
query: ("Eli Lilly and Company" OR "Eli Lilly") (Korea OR Korean) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Peptron Ends Technology Evaluation with Eli Lilly; Stock Plunges Nearly 30% as Definitive Deal Fails to Materialize
Add preferred source 
Peptron has concluded a two-year technology evaluation of its SmartDepot platform with Eli Lilly. With no announcement of a follow-on commercialization agreement, the stock plummeted nearly 30% in after-market trading. Peptron emphasized that the end of the technology evaluation does not signal the end of the partnership, but there has been no confirmation that Lilly has signed a binding license agreement. The market had held high expectations that SmartDepot could be applied to Lilly's obesity treatments. Peptron is proceeding with domestic patent registrations for its proprietary pipeline candidates PT403 and PT404 and construction of Osong Plant 2, but questions may arise about the prospects for recovering its production facility investment if a definitive agreement fails to materialize.
Key Elements 
Peptron Eli Lilly SmartDepot Choi Ho-il PT403 PT404 Mounjaro Osong Plant 2 Tirzepatide Semaglutide 
Peptron (087010), a developer of long-acting injectable therapies, has concluded a two-year technology evaluation of its SmartDepot platform with global pharmaceutical company Eli Lilly. With no announcement of a follow-on commercialization agreement, the stock plummeted nearly 30% in after-market trading just before the market close.
Peptron announced on the 7th that the technology evaluation period with Lilly ended as of that date. The company stated, "We take seriously the fact that we were unable to announce a follow-on commercialization agreement at the conclusion of the technology evaluation period."
On the Korea Exchange that day, Peptron closed at ₩94,200 (approximately $70), down 27.87% from the previous trading day. In after-market trading, the decline widened further, with the stock falling to ₩91,500 (approximately $68), down 29.94%. Compared with its three-year high of ₩392,500 (approximately $290) reached in November last year, the current price is less than a quarter of that level.
Two Years of Expectations and Anxiety
The collaboration between Peptron and Lilly began on October 7, 2024. The two companies signed a technology evaluation agreement to apply Peptron's long-acting drug delivery platform, SmartDepot, to peptide-based medicines held by Lilly. The initial contract period was approximately 14 months, but it was extended to up to 24 months through a corrective disclosure in December 2025.
SmartDepot is a drug delivery system (DDS) that uses biodegradable polymer-based microspheres to control the rate of drug release in the body. It has drawn attention in the chronic disease treatment market, including obesity and diabetes, because it can convert peptide therapies that require daily or weekly administration into once-monthly injections.
The market had expected that research was underway to apply SmartDepot to Lilly's obesity treatment Mounjaro (active ingredient: tirzepatide) to extend dosing intervals. However, in July, Peptron CEO Choi Ho-il stated at a biotech forum that "when conducting joint research with Company L (Lilly), we are developing a completely different peptide formulation together, and tirzepatide is not included," which sent the stock down to its daily limit. At the time, CEO Choi purchased 10,000 shares of company stock in an effort to stabilize sentiment.
Collaboration Potential Remains, But...
Peptron drew a line, stating that the end of the technology evaluation does not mean the end of its partnership with Lilly. The company said, "Reviews and discussions regarding commercialization collaboration will proceed based on the accumulated joint research and technology evaluation results, comprehensively considering all factors necessary for actual commercialization, including commercial viability, mass production capability, marketability, and intellectual property rights."
Peptron explained that during the joint research process, the scope of research was expanded beyond the initial plan, additional technology evaluations were conducted, and all agreed-upon compensation was received. However, regarding the specific format and timing of follow-on collaboration, the company maintains that it "cannot disclose details."
The market's response has been cold. This is because there has been no confirmation that Lilly has decided to adopt SmartDepot and sign a binding license agreement. The fact that Lilly has also been expanding its collaboration scope with other long-acting drug delivery platform companies, such as Camurus, adds to the uncertainty.
Proprietary Pipeline and Production Investment
Separately from the Lilly agreement, Peptron is accelerating its proprietary pipeline development. The company recently received domestic patent registration decisions in South Korea for PT403 (active ingredient: semaglutide) and PT404 (active ingredient: tirzepatide), once-monthly long-acting obesity treatments currently under development.
The company is also expanding its production base. It is pursuing construction of Osong Plant 2 with an investment of approximately ₩89 billion (approximately $66.5 million), with an investment completion date of February 15, 2028. The market had previously interpreted this investment as a preemptive move to prepare for technology transfer with global pharmaceutical companies and future commercial production demand. However, some observers note that if a definitive agreement with Lilly does not materialize, the prospects for recovering the production facility investment and utilization rates could come under scrutiny.
Impact on Biotech Investment Sentiment
Industry observers believe that Peptron's sharp stock decline could weigh on investment sentiment across South Korea's biotech sector as a whole, beyond the technology evaluation conclusion of an individual company. South Korean biotech stocks have recently shown significant volatility based on expectations for future achievements such as technology exports to global pharmaceutical companies, joint research, and clinical data announcements.
While news of collaboration with major pharmaceutical companies serves as a catalyst that rapidly boosts corporate valuations, delays or failures in definitive agreements can lead to sharp stock corrections, particularly in stocks where expectations have been excessively priced in. One industry insider said, "Going forward, biotech investment sentiment is likely to be reorganized around substantive achievements such as the terms of actual technology transfer agreements, upfront payments and milestones, clinical progress, and commercialization timelines, rather than simple technology evaluation or collaboration announcements."

content_text:
Bayer’s CEO cut manager ranks by 70%. Now comes the hard part
By Diane Brady 
Diane Brady 
Executive Editorial Director 
By Diane Brady 
Diane Brady 
Executive Editorial Director 
October 7, 2026, 5:02 AM ET 
Bayer AG CEO Bill Anderson during the Federation of German Industries (BDI) Day of Industry conference in Berlin on June 22, 2026. Krisztian Bocsi/Bloomberg via Getty Images 
Add Fortune on Google for similar content.
Add us on Google 
Add us on Google 
In today’s CEO Daily: What happens after you flatten your company? 
The big leadership story: Why Oura really pulled its IPO
The markets: Mostly down after the S&P 500 closed at a record high on Tuesday.
Plus: All the news and watercooler chat from Fortune .
Good morning . After you’ve streamlined and transformed and flattened your company, how do you get it to grow again? I recently asked that question to Bayer CEO Bill Anderson, who’s done all of the above at the 163-year-old health science giant. He’s reduced the number of managers from about 16,000 to 4,500 (in a company of 88,000) and replaced hierarchy and annual budgets with 5,000 small teams working on 90-day cycles. So what’s next?
Recommended Video 
“Our ambition, for the last three years, basically, was to survive,” he told me, as we sipped takeout coffee in an empty corner of New York’s Javits Center last month. “How much are we willing to stretch ourselves now and put out a bold ambition for what this company can be and fight for that?”
Good question. Bayer announced plans to invest $2.2 billion in a new Ohio manufacturing site last week. Global COO Sebastian Guth recently wrote in Fortune that the company stopped assigning sales targets. Investors are newly enthusiastic as Bayer’s stock is up 57% over the past year (versus about 21% for BASF and 14% for Novartis) but flat over the past three years (versus 43% and 47% growth, respectively). Anderson has improved profitability and won a Supreme Court ruling that addresses liability claims predating his arrival, but the real test will be whether he can continue to drive revenue and profit growth .
.contents]:contents flex items-center"> 
Anderson has found that giving people more authority doesn’t necessarily increase their willingness to make tough decisions. “We have a nice culture” that’s “a little softer” on things like “courageous authenticity and decisiveness.”
To address that, he started at the top: “The job of the leaders is not to manage people, and it’s not to decide the goals, and then, you know, cascade them. No, forget that. The job of the leaders is to set the vision. That’s very different than telling everyone what to do,” he said. “We are putting 95% of decision making at the bottom, not delegating it down in the hierarchy.” He ranks his priorities in descending order: Mission first, employees second, shareholders third, senior management last. 
What’s oddly heartening is the realization that Anderson doesn’t have all the answers. It shows that transformation is ongoing and hard. “This is not a culture program or a communication program,” said Anderson. “Ninety-nine percent of all corporate transformations are not transformations. They’re just shuffling the boxes around.”

Skyworks readies Si829x gate driver for EV inverter trials
Skyworks’ isolated gate driver shows software control moving deeper into EV power electronics, down to how each switch turns on
By 
Automotive World
October 7, 2026 
Skyworks Solutions’ Si829x isolated gate driver, built for electric vehicle traction inverters, has passed AEC-Q100 automotive qualification and entered pre-production release. Samples, evaluation kits and driver software are available now, allowing automakers and inverter suppliers to start advanced prototyping with the part.
The driver uses ProVCD, a variable current drive in its second generation, to shape gate waveforms cycle by cycle through a digital interface. Skyworks says this cut switching losses by up to 44% against voltage-mode drive in its testing.
Configurability is the commercial pitch. The driver handles silicon carbide and silicon power switches, with parameters set in software so one design can serve several vehicle platforms and chip suppliers.
Skyworks says the part supports functional safety designs up to ASIL D, the highest automotive safety integrity level, subject to system validation. Documentation, including a functional safety manual, is available under a non-disclosure agreement.
In a statement, Mario Battello, Vice President of Product Line Management at Skyworks, said: “Si829x gives customers a qualified path from evaluation to advanced prototypes. The ProVCD™ platform combines software-configurable performance with the safety, isolation and design flexibility needed to standardize inverter designs for EVs, eVTOL, and eAgriculture, and accelerate development for high power motor applications like datacenter cooling and AI power supplies.”
Source: Skyworks

Renishaw Expands Miskin Site as Demand Drives Manufacturing Growth 
October 7, 2026 
This year, engineering technologies business, Renishaw, is celebrating the 15th anniversary of the purchase of its Miskin site in South Wales, and the completion of the first phase of a further £70 million development of the facility. Announced in 2022, this is the largest capital investment project in the company’s history, which will ultimately double the size of the Miskin site, giving the company space to expand manufacturing capacity to meet rising demand for its world-leading precision metrology, additive manufacturing and position measurement products.
Renishaw has been committed to the manufacturing of its own products since its formation and uses many of these products within its machining facilities. Whilst much of its production is performed in the UK, at its Miskin, Stonehouse and Woodchester sites, it has carriedout the assembly of metrology products in Ireland since 1981, and also has a significant operation in Pune, India.
Renishaw completed the acquisition of the 193-acre site, situated to the west of Cardiff, from RobertBosch Ltd in September 2011. It started modest operations in May 2012 with a single production shift, having refurbished around 15% of the 416,000 sq ft (38,675 sqm) total building space, which primarily consisted of two large production halls. By the time of the formal opening of the facility in October 2012 by then First Minister of Wales, employee numbers were around 25, compared to around 950 today. Following the completion of the first development phase (Hall 3), usablespace has grown to 617,000 sq ft (57,350 sqm) and will total 880,000 sq ft (81,765 sqm) once Hall 4 is completed and operational, establishing the Miskin facility as one of the UK’s largest advanced manufacturing sites.
Renishaw has continued to invest throughout its tenure, with around £150 million spent to date on acquiring the site, refurbishing legacy buildings, developing the new halls, and installing advanced manufacturing equipment. The latter currently includes 134 CNC machine tools producing around one million parts per month, three PCB assembly lines, robotic assembly and automated warehousing, with more equipment on order to support customer requirements.
Manufacturing Capacity to Support Future Growth 
The latest phase of development demonstrates Renishaw’s long-term confidence in the UK and its commitment to creating highly skilled jobs and supporting economic growth for years to come.
Hall 3 is used to manufacture Renishaw’s metal additive manufacturing (AM) systems, AGILITY coordinate measuring machines (CMMs) and also houses a multimillion-pound automated storage andretrieval warehousing system. The company is currently experiencing strong demand for its AM systems, notably from the aerospace and defence (A&D) sector, and is also seeing growing demand for its high precision multi-sensor CMMs used to inspect complex components, including applications in the energy and Aerospace & Defence sectors.
Hall 4 was constructed as a shell building, with its future utilisation dependent on sales demand and capacity requirements. Due to exceptional demand for Renishaw’s position encoders from manufacturers of semiconductor equipment,driven by the growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), some of that additional capacity is now required, and Hall 4 will be partially occupied over the coming months. To support customers in this important sector, the company is also increasing its capital expenditure on equipment, especially new machine tools, electronics production and automated assembly.
Steve Oakes, Director of Position Measurement, said, “ Our encoders are used at all stages of the semiconductor production process, from manufacturing silicon wafers to packaging and testing individual devices. The semiconductor sector is highly cyclical, and we are currently seeing a ‘super cycle’, which is driving very high levels of investment across the entire supply chain. ”
A Focus on Sustainability 
Beyond increasing manufacturing capacity, the development of the new halls has been designed to deliver long-term operational and environmental benefits, supporting Renishaw’s wider commitment to achieving Net Zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scopes 1 and 2 by 2028. The company’s long term ambition is for all buildings at the Miskin site to operate at Net Zero, and both new halls have been designed to achieve Net Zero Carbon in Operation.
The high-performance buildings require significantly less energy than conventional industrial facilities, reducing operating costs and carbon emissions from the outset. Enhanced insulation in the walls, roofs and floors delivers thermal performance well beyond current building regulation requirements, while high-performance glazing minimises heat loss and reduces the energy required to maintain comfortable indoor conditions throughout the year.
Heating and cooling are provided by highly efficient electric heat pump systems, which generate multiple units of heating or cooling energy for every unit of electricity consumed. The system delivers approximately four units of heat and six units of cooling per unit of electricity, making it substantially more energy efficient and lower in carbon emissions than conventional gas-fired systems.
A key feature of the Miskin expansion is its extensive use of on-site renewable energy generation, delivering an estimated 200 MWh of clean electricity each year. Where additional electricity is required, renewable energy tariffs are used to further reduce the site’s carbon footprint.
The Miskin expansion has provided valuable opportunities to develop the skills of Renishaw’s apprentices and graduate engineers who have played an active role throughout the project. They have gained first-hand experience of delivering a major industrial development, and project engineering apprentices were embedded within the design teams responsible for the new development, contributing to layout planning, coordinating with multiple business functions, attending regular site visits and supporting the design of office and workshop facilities.
Commitment to The Future 
The expansion of the Miskin site represents a major long-term investment in UK manufacturing, sustainability and skills development. It reinforces Renishaw’s commitment to South Wales and the UK while providing a modern, low-carbon manufacturing environment that showcases the best of British engineering. As the site continues to evolve, the new facilities will play a vital role in supporting innovation, reducing carbon emissions and creating high-quality employment opportunities for years to come.
Jim Long, Director of Group Manufacturing, said, “ The strong growth we are currently seeing has highlighted the importance of in-house manufacturing and the control it gives us in meeting our quality, cost and delivery targets. This commitment to manufacturing is exemplified by the investment that we have made in Miskin over the past 15 years and I would like to thank the many people from across our business who have supported the development of this world-class facility.” 
He continued, “ A key aim of our facilities is to create an attractive and enjoyable working environment that inspires employees while creating a world-class environment that impresses visitors and presents a positive image of manufacturing.” 
Long concluded, “ The significant ongoing investment by our Board to increase our production capabilities demonstrates a huge vote of confidence in our manufacturing operations and people, at an exciting time for the business.”

Tokyo Electron Eyes 1 Trillion Yen Operating Profit on Samsung, SK hynix Spending
Editor 
Park Jung-hwan 
2026.10.07 10:17
Print 
URL Copy 
Fonts Size Down 
Fonts Size Up 
AI Boom Drives Memory Chip Investment, Fueling Record Earnings at Japan’s Top Chip Equipment Maker
A cleanroom equipped with Tokyo Electron semiconductor manufacturing equipment (Tokyo Electron) 
The explosive growth of the artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductor market is reshaping the earnings outlook for Japan’s semiconductor equipment industry. As global Big Tech companies ramp up spending on AI infrastructure, that investment is flowing through to capital expenditures by memory chipmakers such as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, prompting Japanese equipment suppliers to project record earnings.
According to Nikkei on Aug. 6, Tokyo Electron, Japan’s largest semiconductor manufacturing equipment maker, is expected to post consolidated operating profit of 1 trillion yen, equivalent to approximately 8.5 trillion won or $6.35 billion, for the fiscal year ending March 2027, which runs from April 2026 through March 2027. That would represent an increase of about 60% from the previous year and comfortably surpass the company’s previous record of 697.3 billion yen in the fiscal year ended March 2025. The average market forecast also stands at 1.03 trillion yen, supporting expectations that Tokyo Electron could surpass the 1 trillion yen threshold.
Hiroshi Kawamoto, chief financial officer of Tokyo Electron, said, “Customer investment momentum is growing stronger than it was at the time of our full-year earnings announcement,” adding, “Depending on our revenue level this fiscal year, we expect to reach operating profit of 1 trillion yen.” Close ties with Korean chipmakers are cited as a key driver of the company’s strong performance. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, Samsung Electronics accounted for 15.1% of Tokyo Electron’s total revenue, or 368.1 billion yen, overtaking TSMC at 12.9% to become its largest customer.
Behind the strong earnings outlook is aggressive AI investment by major U.S. technology companies, including Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta. The four companies’ combined free cash flow was negative $94.6 billion in the April-June quarter, underscoring the scale of their spending on AI infrastructure. In response to concerns about potential overinvestment, Tokyo Electron has characterized current demand as genuine underlying demand rather than speculative buying.
CFO Kawamoto cited the spread of agentic AI and physical AI, which enables robots to perceive and act in the real world, as reasons for his positive outlook. “The scenario in which demand continues to grow, including through improvements in semiconductor performance, remains intact,” he said.
Tokyo Electron is also working to improve profitability. The company has already completed price increase negotiations with some customers and plans to raise its gross margin from the current level of around 47% to 50% through productivity improvements using robotics and AI.
As semiconductor architectures become increasingly complex, inspection and back-end semiconductor equipment are also emerging as new growth areas. With stacked packaging processes such as those used in high-bandwidth memory (HBM) gaining importance, sales of Tokyo Electron’s “bonders,” equipment used in memory stacking processes, are performing well. Demand for “probers,” equipment used to test semiconductor wafers and chips, is also rising as manufacturers seek to reduce costs associated with defects caused by increasingly complex semiconductor structures.
Other Japanese equipment makers are also benefiting from the same trend. Advantest, a maker of HBM inspection equipment, has seen its revenue roughly double from fiscal 2022 levels, while Disco, which manufactures wafer-dicing equipment, has also reported a significant increase in operating profit. Analysts say that not only rising AI chip production volumes but also the increasing complexity of manufacturing processes is creating opportunities for equipment makers to increase the value of their products and services.
Investment in AI data centers in Japan is also gaining momentum. JERA, Japan’s largest power generation company, is partnering with Dell and others to develop a large-scale AI data center in Chiba Prefecture, while SoftBank and global investment firm Blackstone have signaled investments worth trillions of won in infrastructure in Japan. The expansion of the AI ecosystem, from semiconductor manufacturing to data center construction, is expected to provide a long-term growth foundation for Japan’s semiconductor equipment industry.

Thömus Maxon announces departure of Albin and Forster
The Whoop UCI Mountain Bike World Series has only just wrapped up, but with two teams closing and a saturated rider market, the 2026-27 off-season is already shaping up to be an eventful one.
After eight years with the team, Vital Albin’s time with Thömus Maxon is coming to an end. The Swiss rider’s best World Cup result came last year in Nové Město, where he finished sixth in the XCO, while his best result of 2026 came in Les Gets, where he took seventh in the short track.
Also leaving the team is Lars Forster, who has spent the past four seasons with the Swiss outfit. After joining from Scott-SRAM, Forster claimed an XCO World Cup victory for Thömus Maxon in Leogang in 2023. However, he has struggled to reproduce that form in recent seasons, with 17th in South Korea his best XCO result of 2026.
Where either rider will end up in 2027 remains to be seen, as does who will replace them at Thömus Maxon. With several teams already announcing their departures from the World Series, and a number of riders now looking for new homes, the coming weeks could prove particularly busy for the XC transfer market.

Full Release
European Affiliate, based in Amsterdam, to support upcoming marketing authorization submissions, OCU410 Phase 3 development program, and potential commercialization in Europe
MALVERN, Pa., Oct. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ocugen, Inc. (“Ocugen” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: OCGN), a biotechnology company focused on developing and commercializing novel gene therapies to address blindness diseases, today announced the appointment of Jolanda Crombach, MSc PharmD, as General Manager of the Company’s European affiliate. Ms. Crombach, an accomplished pharmaceutical executive with more than 20 years of industry experience, will lead the Company’s newly established European affiliate, headquartered in Amsterdam, Netherlands.
“As we advance our three Phase 3 modifier gene therapy programs toward regulatory submissions and potential commercialization, establishing a strong presence in Europe is an important component of our growth strategy,” said Shankar Musunuri, PhD, MBA, Chairman, Chief Executive Officer and Co-founder of Ocugen. “Jolanda is ideally suited to lead this important expansion. Her extensive pharmaceutical leadership experience, deep understanding of the European healthcare environment and track record of building organizations will be invaluable as we develop our European operations and prepare to potentially bring transformative, one-time treatment gene therapies to patients.”
Under Ms. Crombach’s leadership, the European affiliate will build the team and infrastructure to support Ocugen’s three late-stage modifier gene therapy programs addressing major blindness diseases, including OCU400 for retinitis pigmentosa, OCU410 for GA secondary to dry age-related macular degeneration, and OCU410ST for Stargardt disease. All three development programs are in Phase 3, with key data readouts expected in 2027 and 2028, followed by global regulatory submissions, including Marketing Authorization Application submissions in Europe.
Ms. Crombach brings a proven track record of building and leading organizations across the European life sciences sector. Most recently, she served as Managing Director and Board Member of Moderna Netherlands, where she built the company’s Netherlands affiliate from the ground up and subsequently led its operations. Prior to Moderna, she held leadership roles spanning commercial, market access, medical, corporate and public affairs at MSD (Merck) and Pfizer. She began her career as a pharmacist and holds a MSc PharmD degree from Utrecht University in the Netherlands.
“I am excited to join Ocugen and contribute to the Company’s mission of developing innovative gene therapies for people living with blindness diseases,” said Jolanda Crombach, General Manager of European Affiliate, Ocugen. “Ocugen has built an innovative pipeline addressing significant unmet needs in ophthalmology, and I look forward to working with the team to establish a strong European organization and help expand access to these potentially transformative gene therapies for patients across Europe.”
About Ocugen, Inc.
Ocugen, Inc. is a pioneering biotechnology company developing gene therapies for blindness diseases. The Company’s breakthrough modifier gene therapy platform has the potential to address significant unmet medical needs across large patient populations through a gene-agnostic approach. Unlike traditional gene therapies and gene-editing technologies that target a single gene mutation, Ocugen’s modifier gene therapies are designed to address the underlying disease biology by restoring balance across multiple gene networks. The Company is currently advancing programs for inherited retinal diseases and other causes of blindness that affect millions worldwide, including retinitis pigmentosa, Stargardt disease, and geographic atrophy, an advanced form of dry age-related macular degeneration. Vestas Powers Up Vietnam's Clean Energy Ambitions with Two New Projects Under PDP8 Totaling 16 Wind Turbines 
Hanoi, Vietnam (ANTARA/PRNewswire)- Vestas has been awarded contracts to supply its 16 new V163 wind turbines from the 4 MW Platform across two new wind farms in central Vietnam. In partnership with a reputable Vietnamese renewable energy developer with a significant portfolio, Vestas will expand proven track record of 1.6 gigawatts in Vietnam and strengthen the company's role in driving the country's wind energy growth.
Included in Vietnam's Power Development Plan 8 (PDP8), these projects are among the first to secure investment licenses and proceed toward execution, supporting the country's clean energy transition and its pathway toward net-zero emissions by 2050. The awards highlight growing momentum in Vietnam's wind sector and demonstrate how advanced turbine technology can help unlock the next generation of projects under PDP8. Through higher hub heights, larger rotors and site-specific solutions, Vestas is helping developers improve project economics and maximise energy production in Vietnam's wind conditions.
The 163 metre rotors will be the largest Vestas model deployed in Vietnam to date. Combined with tailor-made 155-metre hub height tower solutions, they are designed to maximise energy production and project performance for Vietnam's wind conditions. Built on Vestas' proven 4 MW platform, which already accounts for +88 GW of installed capacity globally and 1.6 GW of installed capacity in Vietnam, the solution combines increased energy yield with demonstrated operational performance and track record in the market. The projects will also be backed by 20-year AOM 5000 service and maintenance agreements, delivering long-term business case certainty and optimal operational performance.
"We are honoured by our customer's confidence and proud to be supporting some of the first wind projects moving forward under PDP8. These projects demonstrate that the next generation of wind development in Vietnam can be enabled through innovative, proven technology and tailor-made solutions. With our V163-4 MW platform, 155-metre site specific hub height configuration and deep local expertise, Vestas is delivering a solution specifically designed for Vietnam's evolving market needs. We remain committed to supporting the country's energy security and helping our customers accelerate Vietnam's clean energy transition," Antoine CROIZE, Country Manager, Vestas Vietnam. 
Vestas Backs Vietnam's Local Employment 
The two wind farms will be located near an existing hub of Vestas projects, extending long-term service employment in the region for decades to come.
Vestas' wind turbine components are expected to begin delivery to Vietnam in 2027, with commissioning to follow.
About Vestas 
Vestas is the energy industry's global partner on sustainable energy solutions. We design, manufacture, install, and service onshore and offshore wind turbines across the globe, with more wind power capacity installed through time than anyone else. Through our industry-leading smart data capabilities and unparalleled wind turbines under service, we use data to interpret, forecast, and exploit wind resources and deliver best-in-class wind power solutions. Together with our customers, Vestas' employees are bringing the world sustainable energy solutions to power a bright future.

Gene Therapy Brings Hearing to Children with Inherited Deafness
Research By:
John Greinwald Jr., MD Post Date: October 6, 2026 | Publish Date:
Oct. 12, 2025 
Share on X 
Share on LinkedIn 
Share by Email 
deafness 
gene therapy 
innovation 
As part of a breakthrough clinical trial, experts at Cincinnati Children’s have provided a treatment called Otarmeni (lunsotogene parvec-cwha) that has restored natural acoustic hearing to a pair of siblings 
Key Takeaways
In a clinical trial, a one-time gene therapy restored meaningful hearing in 9 of 12 children with profound deafness caused by inherited variants in OTOF .
The treatment delivers a working copy of the otoferlin gene directly into the cochlea using a dual AAV1 vector.
The NEJM study reporting these findings was co-authored by John Greinwald Jr., MD, Division of Otolaryngology
Two children, a brother and sister, have been treated at Cincinnati Children’s in the second group of clinical trial participants.
To see a 3-year-old boy who was born with profound deafness simply smile and point to the sounds coming from a nearby speaker felt like nothing short of a medical miracle to everyone in the room.
“For us, it was a moment of real amazement, because it’s something that we would have never really expected to happen in our career, for kids to be able to hear without the need of devices,” says John Greinwald Jr., MD, a clinician-scientist with the Division of Otolaryngology at Cincinnati Children’s.
In April 2025, Greinwald provided the boy with a treatment called Otarmeni (lunsotogene parvec-cwha), a novel gene therapy developed by Regeneron. The treatment was made for pediatric and adult patients with severe-to-profound and profound sensorineural hearing loss (any frequency >90 decibel hearing level) associated with molecularly confirmed biallelic variants in the OTOF gene, preserved outer hair cell function, and no prior cochlear implant in the same ear.
The approach for administering the drug is similar to cochlear implant surgery, but the delivery of the drug is technically challenging. The surgical team directly infused Otarmeni into the cochlear fluid space at a controlled rate while the boy was under general anesthesia.
The outcome was profound. Once inside the inner ear, the “dual AAV1 vector system” began entering sensory hair cells, augmenting the cell with a normal OTOF gene that produces otoferlin, a protein that helps pass signals from hair cells to the auditory nerve. Over time, these healthy cells were expected to multiply and transform the boy’s ability to hear. Within several weeks, follow-up examinations revealed dramatic improvement.
“I think this is going to be the dawn of a new age of molecular intra-cochlear therapy,” Greinwald says.
What type of deafness can be treated this way? 
This therapy addresses a specific form of OTOF -related congenital deafness. This occurs when a child is born with malfunctioning variants in both copies of the OTOF gene. Overall, an estimated 1% of congenital deafness cases involve biallelic OTOF variants.
These children cannot hear noises as loud as a running lawnmower a few feet away. And without devices like cochlear implants, their hearing never gets better. Although implanted devices can provide functional levels of hearing, the auditory information is somewhat limited and notably different from natural human hearing.
How Much Improvement Has Occurred? 
By 24 weeks, nine of the first 12 study participants were able to hear down to at least 70 decibels or less, a level that generally avoids the need for cochlear implantation, according to research published in The New England Journal of Medicine. Four patients gained normal to near-normal hearing and four patients had only mild to moderate hearing loss, which allowed them to hear normally with standard hearing aids. Meanwhile, one child did not respond at all to Otarmeni, for reasons that remain unclear.
Since the first 12 patients treated, two children have received this therapy at Cincinnati Children’s—a brother and sister both born with extreme loss of hearing.
The boy, Abdu, was treated in 2025 at age 3. He went from hearing nearly virtually no sounds at all to detecting sounds within four weeks. Now, he is hearing in the normal range and had begun developing speech.
His successful-so-far outcome then led to his 1-year-old sister, Sumaya, receiving the treatment. She also has experienced dramatically improved hearing.
Researchers are still tracking specific details about these and other newer cases. More results are expected to be presented in October 2026 and included in a future medical journal publication.
For more information about the family’s journey, watch this video 
Potential for wider application? 
Up to 50% of childhood deafness traces back to genetic causes. However, because gene therapies act upon specific gene variants, this type of treatment will require modification to address hearing loss related to various gene malfunctions. Further development of customized treatments will be needed.
Impressively, however, the initial study of Otarmeni showed hearing improvement even when participants were up to 16 years old. While early treatment remains ideal, previously it had been assumed that gene therapy for deafness could be successful only if provided during infancy.
In many cases globally, the specific cause of deafness may not be diagnosed until later in childhood, if at all. Meanwhile, developing treatments to target other deafness gene variants will take time. So, the potential to apply treatments beyond infancy offers more families hope.
“This clinical trial might help broaden thinking about which patients may benefit,” Greinwald says. “Although larger and longer studies will be needed to better define the optimal treatment window.”
About the study 
This clinical trial was funded by Regeneron. The results were published on behalf of the CHORD Study Group. Regeneron scientists Jonathon Whitton and Vassili Valayannopoulos served as corresponding authors.
About the Cincinnati Ear and Hearing Center
2001: Center founded by Drs. Dan Choo and John Greinwald.
2001-2009 : Developed the current and accepted algorithms for the medical work up for sensorineural hearing loss in children.
2002-2014: NIH funded laboratories in the fields of developmental biology of the ear, molecular genetics of deafness and CMV related hearing loss.
2004-2006 : Developed one of the first gene arrays (Otoseq) for detecting the genetic cause of deafness in children.
2005-2008: Developed the “Cincinnati Protocol” for determining the size and pathogenicity of the vestibular aqueduct in the inner ear.
2005-2007: Published one of the first papers on cochlear implants in patients with auditory neuropathy.
2007: Published one of the first articles about minimal access surgery in cochlear implants which is now the standard in pediatric patients.
2018-2021: Collaborated with Otonomy Corporation doing pre-clinical work on gene therapy.
2024- present : Collaborating with the Regeneron and Eli Lilly corporations on the first in human gene therapy trials, one of only two places in the world performing simultaneous trials at the same location.
October 2026 : An update about the total cohort of 39 ears treated with Regeneron’s gene therapy will be presented by Greinwald at the American Academy of Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery conference.

Tokyo Electron Korea launches triple-digit hiring across 19 roles for January start 
Applications open until the 18th with January onboarding across multiple engineering and corporate tracks 
입력 2026.10.06. 09:53 
조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 
Tokyo Electron Korea's poster for open recruitment of new and experienced employees for the second half of 2026./Courtesy of Tokyo Electron Korea 
Semiconductor equipment maker Tokyo Electron Korea will conduct open hiring for new and experienced employees in the second half of this year. It will hire in the triple digits across 19 roles, including engineers, sales, and corporate functions.
Tokyo Electron Korea said on Oct. 6 that it will accept applications for new and experienced employees for the second half of 2026 through the 18th. Those accepted will join the company in January next year.
Open roles include field engineers (FE), who install and maintain semiconductor equipment at client sites, and process engineers (PE), who handle process development and evaluation, as well as software and systems engineers, mechanical design, manufacturing and production management, product safety, facilities management, and information technology (IT) support. It will also hire in sales and corporate functions such as strategic planning and human resources.
Work locations, depending on role, are Korea establishments in Hwaseong, Pyeongtaek, and Icheon in Gyeonggi Province; Cheongju in North Chungcheong Province; and Balan in Gyeonggi Province. Staff will also be assigned to the Yongin office, scheduled for completion in January next year.
Starting with this hiring round, the process to verify job fit will also be strengthened. The self-introduction questions were revamped to ask about experience and competencies required for the actual role. For entry-level candidates, the scope of the artificial intelligence (AI) competency test will be expanded, and a simplified AI competency test will be introduced for experienced candidates.
The process will proceed with a document screening followed by first and second interviews, with interviews held in November. On the 13th, it will hold an online recruiting session, "TEL-in Session," with current practitioners participating, and conduct a Q&A on roles and company life.
After joining, new employees will attend a two-week group training program, "TEL-SHIP." Experienced hires will complete the "TEL Culture Program" to learn the company's way of working and organizational culture. A four-week Japanese language training program will also be offered to all new hires.
Tokyo Electron Korea currently has about 2,400 officers and employees. Staff age 34 and under account for about 63% of the total. Last month, it was selected for the sixth time since 2018 as a "Korea Job Best Company" by the Ministry of Employment and Labor (MOEL).
Tokyo Electron Korea said it plans to hire applicants who have the competencies required for the role and an understanding of the semiconductor industry, without limiting to semiconductor-related majors. A Tokyo Electron Korea official said, "Because the semiconductor equipment industry sees rapid technological change, the ability to continuously learn new processes and equipment and apply them to work is important," adding, "Rather than a specific major or the fact of prior experience, we plan to focus on whether applicants can quickly learn new technologies based on the experience and competencies they have built and demonstrate them in the role."

Cognex Acquires RealSense to Expand into Robotic Perception Market
Cognex Corporation has announced a $500 million acquisition of RealSense, aiming to diversify its product offerings and enter the robotic perception market, a key growth area in machine vision.
Jim Tatum 
Oct. 6, 2026
2 min read 
Add Us On Google 
Key Highlights
Cognex's acquisition of RealSense marks a strategic move into the rapidly growing robotic perception market.
The $500 million deal is financed through Cognex's existing cash reserves, with additional investments in employee retention and incentives.
Both companies aim to leverage their combined strengths to serve a broader industrial customer base globally.
Image/Cognex
6ac403f33f45089d8a6f05a5 Cognex Real Sense Image 
Cognex Corporation (Natick, MA, USA) has entered an agreement to buy RealSense (San Francisco, CA, USA) for $500 million.
The deal, announced in a press release Sept. 22, is part of Cognex’s plans to diversify its products and offerings by entering the robotic perception market, according to Cognex CEO Matt Moschner.
"RealSense represents a compelling strategic expansion for Cognex into robotic perception, one of the most attractive adjacent markets in machine vision," Moschner said. 
Nadav Orbach, Chief Executive Officer of RealSense said in the press release that joining Cognex gives RealSense “access to a global industrial customer base and go-to-market reach that would have taken us years to build on our own. This is a combination that makes both businesses stronger.” 
According to the press release, Cognex will acquire RealSense for approximately $500 million, financed entirely from existing cash and investments on its balance sheet. In addition, Cognex also expects to provide a three-year, $56.5 million cash retention program at target for RealSense employees, subject to performance modifiers, and to grant restricted stock units valued at approximately $50 million under Cognex's existing 2023 Stock Option and Incentive Plan dependent on the grant-date share price. 
The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026
“Cognex believes that robotic perception and these robotic systems are the future, a very new style of automation, that's here to stay,” Moschner said. “But we don't view it as an either, but an ‘in addition to.’ What's exciting is both of those things can coexist. We want to serve customers across both of those areas and. And we see that as key to our long-term growth ambition for Cognex.”
